title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄序
仰惟
聖天子御極紀元之初載實天下
開科取士之期
飛龍在天萬物利覩於是雲藩
得遵行故事合雲貴兩省之
士試焉先是巡按雲南監察
===
御史羅玉謀于前巡撫雲南
右副都御史何孟春暨今巡
撫右副都御史王啓集藩臬
議禮聘學職司試事戒脩百
具以協禮典維時鎮守雲南
總兵官黔國公沐紹勛貴州
鎮守太監楊廣巡撫右副都
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄序

仰惟聖天子御極紀元之初載，實天下開科取士之期。飛龍在天，萬物利覩。於是雲藩得遵行故事，合雲貴兩省之士試焉。先是，巡按雲南監察御史羅玉謀于前巡撫雲南右副都御史何孟春暨今巡撫右副都御史王啓，集藩臬議，禮聘學職司試事，戒脩百具，以協禮典。維時，鎮守雲南總兵官黔國公沐紹勛、貴州鎮守太監楊廣、巡撫右副都
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

We reverently reflect that the first year in which the sagely Son of Heaven ascended the throne and inaugurated his reign era was indeed the appointed time for holding examinations and selecting scholars throughout the realm. “The flying dragon is in heaven”: all things benefit from beholding him. Accordingly, the Yunnan provincial administration followed established precedent and assembled the scholars of Yunnan and Guizhou provinces for examination.

Before this, Luo Yu, Investigating Censor on a tour of inspection in Yunnan, consulted with He Mengchun, formerly Grand Coordinator of Yunnan and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Wang Qi, the current Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. They convened the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners for deliberation, ceremonially invited educational officials to conduct the examination, and ordered all necessary preparations to be made in accordance with the ritual statutes. At this time, Mu Shaoxun, Duke of Qianguo and Regional Commander stationed in Yunnan; Yang Guang, the eunuch Grand Defender stationed in Guizhou; and the Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
御史湯沐鎮守署都督僉事
陳珣巡按貴州監察御史陳
克宅咸祗若
德美崇獎士類時戶科右給事中
吳廉監察御史李美刑部郎
中王袍各以公至與議焉期
既屆御史羅玉實主監臨之
===
任考試則學正欒教諭周忠
同考試則學正方田訓導張
嵩詹文慶鄭要提調則雲南
右布政使黃衷參政劉鶴年
監試則雲南按察使陳良珊
僉事潘棠外則左布政使方
璘參政鄧相晁必登參議羅
punctuated:
御史湯沐、鎮守署都督僉事陳珣、巡按貴州監察御史陳克宅，咸祗若德美，崇獎士類。時戶科右給事中吳廉、監察御史李美、刑部郎中王袍，各以公至，與議焉。期既屆，御史羅玉實主監臨之任。
考試則學正欒、教諭周忠，同考試則學正方田、訓導張嵩、詹文慶、鄭要，提調則雲南右布政使黃衷、參政劉鶴年，監試則雲南按察使陳良珊、僉事潘棠，外則左布政使方璘、參政鄧相、晁必登、參議羅
translation_en:
…Censor-in-chief Tang Mu; Chen Xun, the regional military commander serving as Assistant Commissioner-in-chief; and Chen Kezhai, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Guizhou, all reverently followed the example of imperial virtue and honored and encouraged the scholars. At this time, Wu Lian, Right Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue; Li Mei, Investigating Censor; and Wang Pao, Director in the Ministry of Justice, each arrived on official business and took part in the deliberations. When the appointed time arrived, Censor Luo Yu assumed responsibility as Supervising Official.
The Examiners were Luan, School Director, and Zhou Zhong, Instructor. The Associate Examiners were Fang Tian, School Director, and Zhang Song, Zhan Wenqing, and Zheng Yao, Assistant Instructors. The Proctors were Huang Zhong, Yunnan’s Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Liu Henian, Administration Vice Commissioner. The examination invigilators were Chen Liangshan, Yunnan’s Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Pan Tang, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. In addition, there were Fang Lin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Deng Xiang and Chao Bideng, Administration Vice Commissioners; and Luo…, Administration Assistant Commissioner.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
方陶心副使王忠陳璋詹源
姜龍僉事周愚陳卿翁素各
賛翊之自餘印卷以下諸執
事罔不遴具而貴州左布政
使宗璽參政鄭錫文傅習參
議江玠按察使李麟副使劉
瓚僉事王瑞之沈圻亦續食
===
多士迤邐而來廼集提學副
使鄭元僉事夏邦謨所選士
鎖院三試之雲南都指揮胡
章張松方仲外率其屬防範
惟謹御史羅玉且誓于眾曰
以人事
君臣之職也所不盡心于
punctuated: 方、陶心，副使王忠、陳璋、詹源、姜龍，僉事周愚、陳卿、翁素，各賛翊之。自餘印卷以下諸執事，罔不遴具。而貴州左布政使宗璽、參政鄭錫文、傅習、參議江玠、按察使李麟、副使劉瓚、僉事王瑞之、沈圻，亦續食多士，迤邐而來。廼集提學副使鄭元、僉事夏邦謨所選士，鎖院三試之。雲南都指揮胡章、張松、方仲，外率其屬，防範惟謹。御史羅玉且誓于眾曰：「以人事君，臣之職也。所不盡心于
translation_en:
… Luo Fang and Tao Xin, Assistant Administration Commissioners; Wang Zhong, Chen Zhang, Zhan Yuan, and Jiang Long, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; and Zhou Yu, Chen Qing, and Weng Su, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners, each lent their assistance. All other functionaries, from those responsible for printing the examination papers downward, were carefully selected and fully appointed. In Guizhou, Zong Xi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Zheng Xiwen and Fu Xi, Administration Vice Commissioners; Jiang Jie, Assistant Administration Commissioner; Li Lin, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Liu Zan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Wang Ruizhi and Shen Qi, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners, likewise supplied provisions to the many candidates as they made their way here.

The candidates selected by Zheng Yuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner supervising education, and Xia Bangmo, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, were then assembled. The examination compound was locked, and they were examined in three sessions. Outside, Hu Zhang, Zhang Song, and Fang Zhong, Regional Military Commissioners of Yunnan, led their subordinates in maintaining strict security. Censor Luo Yu also pronounced an oath before the assembled officials: “To serve the ruler by securing worthy men is the duty of a minister. Should anyone fail to devote himself wholeheartedly to …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
國事違公徇私拔庸黜賢者神
則臨之殄厥祿誓已退各事
事鑾等精一校讎靡有夙暮
額得士五十五人其不能悉
取者或有矣旣乃刻其文之
純者爲錄以
獻鑾當序諸首惟雲貴古秦黔之
===
===
地而西南之紀也然其風厚
其氣和山水之會萃陰陽之
融結固必有異物出焉往時
如良馬犀象金貝文石或產
于絕域利用中土然皆禹貢
所棄雖勤遠貴異之世猶未
之取迺今則纖無遺矣孰知
punctuated:
國事，違公徇私，拔庸黜賢者，神則臨之，殄厥祿。」誓已，退各事事。鑾等精一校讎，靡有夙暮，額得士五十五人。其不能悉取者，或有矣。旣乃刻其文之純者爲錄，以獻。鑾當序諸首。
惟雲貴，古秦黔之地，而西南之紀也。然其風厚，其氣和，山水之會萃，陰陽之融結，固必有異物出焉。往時，如良馬、犀象、金貝、文石，或產于絕域，利用中土，然皆《禹貢》所棄。雖勤遠貴異之世，猶未之取，迺今則纖無遺矣。孰知
translation_en:
…in affairs of state, whoever acts against the public good for private interests, promotes the mediocre, and rejects the worthy shall be watched over by the spirits, who shall extinguish his emoluments.” Once the oath was concluded, they withdrew, each to perform his duties. Luan and the others devoted themselves single-mindedly to examining the papers, without regard to morning or evening, selecting fifty-five men under the prescribed quota. There may have been others whom they could not include. They then had the finest essays carved on printing blocks to compile a record for presentation to the throne. It fell to Luan to write the preface at its beginning.
Yunnan and Guizhou occupy the ancient lands of Qin and Qian [?] and form the framework of the southwest. Their customs are substantial, their vital energies harmonious. Where mountains and waters converge and yin and yang blend, extraordinary things must surely emerge. In former times, fine horses, rhinoceroses and elephants, gold and cowries, and patterned stones were sometimes produced in remote regions and put to useful purposes in the central lands. Yet all were omitted from the Tribute of Yu. Even in ages that exerted themselves to reach distant regions and prized rarities, these things were still not procured; now, however, not the slightest thing is left out. Who could know…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
瑰瑋俶儻卓犖不羣之士固
彬彬然先後繼出其間皆能
和其聲以鳴
國家之盛邪蓋山川之正氣不
鍾于物而鍾于人太平之景
象不寶異物而寶賢人矧惟
我
===
國家仁覆海隅聲教四訖外夷
子弟亦知嚮義求入大學肆
今餘百五十年學校之設殆
徧天下而雲貴遐土尤切霑
濡至于增學校廣解額實與
夫鼓舞作興之機
皇上稽古右文柄用儒碩羣姦宿
punctuated: 瑰瑋俶儻卓犖不羣之士，固彬彬然先後繼出其間，皆能和其聲以鳴國家之盛邪？蓋山川之正氣，不鍾于物而鍾于人；太平之景象，不寶異物而寶賢人。矧惟我國家仁覆海隅，聲教四訖，外夷子弟亦知嚮義，求入大學。肆今餘百五十年，學校之設殆徧天下，而雲貴遐土尤切霑濡。至于增學校、廣解額，實與夫鼓舞作興之機。皇上稽古右文，柄用儒碩，羣姦宿
translation_en: …that extraordinary, gifted men, outstanding and unlike the common run, have indeed emerged there in cultivated succession, all able to harmonize their voices in proclaiming the flourishing of the state? For the vital essence of its mountains and rivers gathers not in objects but in people; the mark of an age of great peace is to treasure worthy men rather than exotic objects. Moreover, our dynasty’s benevolence extends to the remotest shores, and its civilizing influence reaches in every direction. Even the sons of foreign peoples know to turn toward righteousness and seek admission to the Imperial University. For more than a hundred and fifty years now, schools have been established almost everywhere under Heaven, and the distant lands of Yunnan and Guizhou have received particularly abundant benefits. Increasing the number of schools and enlarging the Provincial Examination quotas truly provide the means to encourage and inspire learning [?]. His Majesty looks to antiquity, honors literary culture, and entrusts authority to eminent Confucian scholars; the host of treacherous men and long-standing…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
弊一切掃除而嘉靖一
詔拳拳以却貢獻禁守臣爲言夷
裔老幼携扶往聽想見
德化之成士以逢掖遊庠序者
苟非暴棄之徒皆欲抱忠貞
以求自効蓋
祖宗豐芑之遺
===
列聖菁莪之化於是爲至宜其人
才之盛物産之嗇而士之投
牒而進者加多於昔也是豈
山川之靈淑能獨使之然哉
夫今玆之選諸士既有以自
見矣由是益加砥礪不爲空
言期於實用上以賛
punctuated: 弊，一切掃除。而嘉靖一詔，拳拳以却貢獻、禁守臣爲言。夷裔老幼携扶往聽，想見德化之成。士以逢掖遊庠序者，苟非暴棄之徒，皆欲抱忠貞以求自効。蓋祖宗豐芑之遺，列聖菁莪之化，於是爲至。宜其人才之盛，物産之嗇，而士之投牒而進者加多於昔也。是豈山川之靈淑能獨使之然哉？夫今玆之選，諸士既有以自見矣。由是益加砥礪，不爲空言，期於實用，上以賛
translation_en:
…abuses were all swept away. A single edict inaugurating the Jiajing reign earnestly addressed the rejection of tribute offerings and prohibitions upon territorial officials. Young and old among the non-Han peoples supported one another as they went to hear it: one can imagine the accomplishment of this moral transformation. Scholars who attend the schools in their broad-sleeved robes, unless they have utterly abandoned themselves, all wish to hold fast to loyalty and integrity and seek to offer their service. Thus the ancestral emperors’ legacy of nurturing future talent, evoked by “Abundant Millet,” and the successive sage emperors’ cultivation of scholars, evoked by “Luxuriant Southernwood,” have now reached their culmination. It is fitting that talent should flourish, though local produce is scant, and that more scholars should submit their registration papers and come forward than in former times. Could the numinous excellence of the mountains and rivers alone have brought this about?

In this year’s selection, you scholars have already had the opportunity to distinguish yourselves. Henceforth, apply yourselves still more diligently to self-cultivation; do not indulge in empty words, but aim at practical service, so that above you may assist…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
休明之治而下求所以異於齊
民我之所應而有司之所求
舉於責無訾焉則亦幾矣脫
或行不掩言名浮于實甘於
卑下而不耻僞爲矯飾以欺
人則科目何賴於賢而吾儒
光大之功用固如是乎哉諸
===
士其慎厥始圖惟厥終無貽
終身之悔可矣
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學
正季鑾謹序
punctuated:
休明之治，而下求所以異於齊民。我之所應，而有司之所求，舉於責無訾焉，則亦幾矣。脫或行不掩言，名浮于實，甘於卑下而不耻，僞爲矯飾以欺人，則科目何賴於賢，而吾儒光大之功用固如是乎哉？諸士其慎厥始，圖惟厥終，無貽終身之悔可矣。
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正季鑾謹序。
translation_en:
…enlightened governance, and, below, seek the means to distinguish themselves from the common people. If, in what we ought to fulfill and what the responsible officials seek, we discharge all responsibilities without grounds for reproach [?], then we will have come close to the ideal. But if conduct does not measure up to words, reputation exceeds substance, and one willingly sinks into baseness without shame, putting on false appearances to deceive others, what reliance can the examination system place upon worthy men? Can this really be how we Confucian scholars serve to extend and illuminate the Way? You scholars should take care at the outset and give thought to the outcome, so that you leave yourselves no cause for lifelong regret.
Preface respectfully written by Ji Luan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試
監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史羅玉〔汝成四川南充縣人辛未進士〕
提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司右布政使黃衷〔子和廣東南海縣人丙辰進士〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政劉鶴年〔惟新四川巴縣人戊辰進士〕
監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司按察使陳良珊〔子珍直隸華亭縣人己未進士〕
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事潘棠〔希召湖廣辰州衛人乙丑進士〕
===
考試官
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正季鑾〔廷用廣西馴象衛籍橫州人壬子貢士〕
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學教諭周忠〔節夫福建閩縣人癸酉貢士〕
同考試官
河南開封府許州儒學學正方田〔仲莘湖廣巴陵縣人丙子貢士〕
江西撫州府臨川縣儒學訓導張嵩〔中夫福建福寧州籍餘姚縣人丙子貢士〕
江西袁州府儒學訓導詹文慶〔用升湖廣江夏縣人己卯貢士〕
浙江湖州府安吉州儒學訓導鄭要〔守約福建龍溪縣人丙子貢士〕
印卷官
punctuated:
嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試

監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史羅玉〔汝成，四川南充縣人，辛未進士〕。

提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司右布政使黃衷〔子和，廣東南海縣人，丙辰進士〕。
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政劉鶴年〔惟新，四川巴縣人，戊辰進士〕。

監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司按察使陳良珊〔子珍，直隸華亭縣人，己未進士〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事潘棠〔希召，湖廣辰州衛人，乙丑進士〕。

考試官
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正季鑾〔廷用，廣西馴象衛籍，橫州人，壬子貢士〕。
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學教諭周忠〔節夫，福建閩縣人，癸酉貢士〕。

同考試官
河南開封府許州儒學學正方田〔仲莘，湖廣巴陵縣人，丙子貢士〕。
江西撫州府臨川縣儒學訓導張嵩〔中夫，福建福寧州籍，餘姚縣人，丙子貢士〕。
江西袁州府儒學訓導詹文慶〔用升，湖廣江夏縣人，己卯貢士〕。
浙江湖州府安吉州儒學訓導鄭要〔守約，福建龍溪縣人，丙子貢士〕。

印卷官
translation_en:
Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination, First Year of Jiajing (1522)

Supervising Official
Luo Yu, Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Yunnan, courtesy name Rucheng, was from Nanchong County, Sichuan, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the xinwei year.

Proctors

Examination Monitoring Officials

Examiners
Ji Luan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Tingyong. Registered with Xunxiang Guard in Guangxi and a native of Hengzhou, he was a tribute student (gongshi) of the renzi year.
Zhou Zhong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Jiefu, was from Min County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the guiyou year.

Fang Tian, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Zhongshen, was from Baling County, Huguang, and was a tribute student of the bingzi year.
Zhang Song, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Zhongfu. Registered in Funing Subprefecture, Fujian, and a native of Yuyao County, he was a tribute student of the bingzi year.
Zhan Wenqing, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Yongsheng, was from Jiangxia County, Huguang, and was a tribute student of the jimao year.
Zheng Yao, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Anji Subprefecture, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Shouyue, was from Longxi County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the bingzi year.

Officials in Charge of Printing Examination Papers

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲南等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨潘鍇〔廷剛浙江仁和縣人知印〕

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
國治而后天下平
夫子喟然嘆曰吾與點也
學問之道無他求其放心而已矣
易
比吉原筮元永貞无咎
進以正可以正邦也
是以明於天之道而察於民之故是興神
===
物以前民用
易之爲書也不可遠爲道也屢遷
書
敬敷五教在寬
恭默思道夢帝賚予良弼
文王不敢盤于遊田以庶邦惟正之供
宅乃事宅乃牧宅乃準兹惟后矣
詩
于以采蘩于沼于沚于以用之公侯之事
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
國治而后天下平。
夫子喟然嘆曰：「吾與點也！」
學問之道無他，求其放心而已矣。

易
比，吉。原筮，元永貞，无咎。
進以正，可以正邦也。
是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物，以前民用。
易之爲書也，不可遠；爲道也，屢遷。

書
敬敷五教，在寬。
恭默思道，夢帝賚予良弼。
文王不敢盤于遊田，以庶邦惟正之供。
宅乃事，宅乃牧，宅乃準，兹惟后矣。

詩
于以采蘩？于沼于沚。于以用之？公侯之事。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
Only after the state is well governed is all under Heaven brought to peace.
The Master sighed deeply and said: “I am with Dian!”
The way of learning is nothing other than seeking to recover one's strayed heart.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
Union brings good fortune. Examine the matter through divination: with fundamental goodness, constancy, and correctness, there will be no blame.
By advancing with correctness, one can set the state right.
Thus, understanding the Way of Heaven and discerning the circumstances of the people, they instituted sacred objects to guide the people's use of them.
The Changes, as a book, must not be kept at a distance; as a Way, it continually shifts.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
Reverently spread the five teachings, doing so with leniency.
Reverent and silent, I pondered the Way; in a dream, the Lord on High bestowed upon me an excellent assistant.
King Wen did not dare indulge in pleasure excursions and hunting; he required the many states to supply only their regular tribute.
Place the right men in charge of your affairs, as your governors, and as your judges: this is what it means to be a sovereign.

Book of Odes (Shijing)
Where do we gather the white southernwood? By the pools and on the islets. For what do we use it? For the sacrificial service of dukes and lords.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
樂只君子德音是茂
既燕于宗福祿攸降公尸燕飲福祿來崇
帝命式于九圍
春秋
公會齊侯于防〔隱公九年〕
公敗齊師于長勺〔莊公十年〕公會齊侯
盟于柯〔莊公十有三年〕
晉人宋人衛人曹人同盟于清丘〔宣公十〕
〔有二年〕
===
遂城虎牢〔襄公二年〕戍鄭虎牢楚公子
貞帥師救鄭〔襄公十年〕
禮記
五者備當上帝其饗
雜帶君朱綠大夫玄華士緇辟二寸再繚
四寸
禮樂之說管乎人情矣
君爲正則百姓從政矣
第貳場
punctuated:
樂只君子，德音是茂。
既燕于宗，福祿攸降；公尸燕飲，福祿來崇。
帝命式于九圍。

春秋
公會齊侯于防〔隱公九年〕。
公敗齊師于長勺〔莊公十年〕。公會齊侯，盟于柯〔莊公十有三年〕。
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人同盟于清丘〔宣公十〕〔有二年〕。
遂城虎牢〔襄公二年〕。戍鄭虎牢，楚公子貞帥師救鄭〔襄公十年〕。

禮記
五者備當，上帝其饗。
雜帶：君朱綠，大夫玄華，士緇，辟二寸，再繚四寸。
禮樂之說，管乎人情矣。
君爲正，則百姓從政矣。

第貳場
translation_en:
Joyful is the noble lord; his virtuous reputation flourishes.
When the feast is held in the ancestral temple, blessings and emoluments descend. The impersonator of the ancestor feasts and drinks; blessings and emoluments come in abundance.
The Lord on High commanded him to serve as a model for the nine regions.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke met the Marquis of Qi at Fang. 〔Ninth year of Duke Yin.〕
The duke defeated the army of Qi at Changshao. 〔Tenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 The duke met the Marquis of Qi and concluded a covenant at Ke. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
Men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao joined in a covenant at Qingqiu. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕
They then fortified Hulao. 〔Second year of Duke Xiang.〕 They garrisoned Hulao in Zheng. Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to rescue Zheng. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang.〕

Book of Rites
When all five are complete and properly arranged, the Lord on High will accept the offering.
For belts with mixed-colored borders: the ruler uses vermilion and green; a grand master uses black with patterned ornamentation; a serviceman uses black. The edging is two cun wide; doubled over, it measures four cun.
The teachings of ritual and music encompass human feelings.
When the ruler is upright, the common people follow his government.

Second Session

策五道
問帝王爲治之要道莫粹於洪範百聖傳
心之要典莫粹於大學善乎儒先有曰
不學書無以議制又曰爲人君而不知
punctuated:
論：講學爲正心之要。

詔誥表內科一道：擬漢勸農桑禁采黃金珠玉詔，景帝後三年。擬唐以楊綰爲國子祭酒誥，大曆五年。擬宋製觀文鑒古圖輔臣賀表，慶曆四年。

判語五條：損壞倉庫財物。守掌在官財物。乘驛馬齎私物。私受公侯財物。官吏聽許財物。

第叁場

策五道

問：帝王爲治之要道，莫粹於《洪範》；百聖傳心之要典，莫粹於《大學》。善乎，儒先有曰：「不學《書》，無以議制。」又曰：「爲人君而不知
translation_en:
Discourse
“Discussing and pursuing learning is essential to rectifying the mind.”

One topic from among imperial edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?]:
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor encouraging agriculture and sericulture and prohibiting the extraction of gold, pearls, and jade: the third year of Emperor Jing’s Later Era.
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Yang Wan as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education: the fifth year of Dali.
Compose a congratulatory memorial from the Song emperor’s chief ministers on the production of the Illustrations for Viewing Cultural Patterns and Examining Antiquity (Guanwen jiangu tu): the fourth year of Qingli.

Five legal judgments:
Damaging property in granaries and storehouses.
Custody and management of government property.
Carrying private goods while riding relay horses.
Privately receiving property from dukes and marquises.
Officials and clerks agreeing to accept property.

Third Session

Five Policy Questions

Question: Of the essential principles by which emperors and kings govern, none is more refined than the Great Plan; of the essential canonical texts transmitting the understanding of the sages, none is more refined than the Great Learning. Well said was the pronouncement of an earlier Confucian scholar: “Without studying the Book of Documents, one has no basis for discussing institutions.” He also said: “To be a ruler of men and yet not know …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
大學無以清出治之原是故唐虞三代
治隆俗美而非後世所及者蓋有堯舜
禹之中湯之敬文之純武之極大本立
而大用著夫豈徒哉洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝
天聰明之至
妙聖神之機當
大業甫定之餘卽
===
聖學緝熈之日於尚書洪範則
親御翰墨詳疏其旨於大學衍義則揭於
殿廡時復睇觀蓋得二書之純以立其本也
審矣其間
聖製之所述
聖政之所施與凡當時侍臣之所論議無非經
世之用千載而下可仰而窺也其脗合
於洪範大學與比隆於唐虞三代者多
矣諸生涵濡
punctuated: 《大學》，無以清出治之原。」是故唐虞三代治隆俗美，而非後世所及者，蓋有堯舜禹之中、湯之敬、文之純、武之極，大本立而大用著，夫豈徒哉！洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，天聰明之至，妙聖神之機，當大業甫定之餘，卽聖學緝熈之日。於《尚書》〈洪範〉，則親御翰墨，詳疏其旨；於《大學衍義》，則揭於殿廡，時復睇觀。蓋得二書之純以立其本也，審矣。其間聖製之所述、聖政之所施，與凡當時侍臣之所論議，無非經世之用，千載而下，可仰而窺也。其脗合於《洪範》《大學》，與比隆於唐虞三代者，多矣。諸生涵濡
translation_en:
…the Great Learning, one has no means of purifying the source from which good government proceeds.” Thus, government flourished and customs were admirable under Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, beyond anything later ages could attain. This was because they possessed the centrality of Yao, Shun, and Yu, the reverence of Tang, the purity of King Wen, and the supreme standard of King Wu. The great foundation was established, and its great efficacy became manifest. Could this have been without cause?
We reverently reflect upon our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao. Possessed of the utmost heavenly intelligence [?], he wondrously exercised the subtle workings of sagely wisdom. As soon as his great enterprise was firmly established, he devoted himself to continuing and illuminating sagely learning. For the “Great Plan” (Hongfan) chapter of the Book of Documents, he personally took up brush and ink and expounded its meaning in detail. As for the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi), he had it displayed in the palace halls and galleries and repeatedly looked it over. Surely he grasped the pure essence of these two works to establish his foundation.
What his sagely writings set forth, what his sagely government put into practice, and all that his attendant officials discussed at the time were applications of learning to ordering the world. Even a thousand years later, one may look up to them and glimpse their achievement. Numerous were the ways in which they accorded with the Great Plan and the Great Learning and equaled the flourishing rule of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. You students have been steeped in…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖化蓋已有年其敬陳之毋忽
問詔令者帝王以心動天下之大幾也幾
動於善則天下應之以善矣堯舜聖者
也其幾動於治天下也一出言即可爲
世法令觀其典謨所載都俞吁咈之間
君臣氣通内外機應天下即形之矣湯
雖聖者自時則有誓矣誓也者終不若
典謨相信之深也周之末則詛矣民不
惟不信且有作慝作怨之刑而上下之
===
心離矣秦尚奚足言哉自漢之興詔多
可紀有聞之而士生色者有聞之而民
伸眉者惟士與民天下元氣元氣理則
百體從令矣仰惟我
皇上即位一詔上以昭天道下以悉人情其録
忠褒節與詩書所載者何所同其愛民
惜財與帝王所行者何所合敬老乃示
民以知孝也優賢乃示民以崇德也皆
慎固邦本之大端培養元氣之首務今
punctuated:
聖化，蓋已有年，其敬陳之，毋忽。

問：詔令者，帝王以心動天下之大幾也。幾動於善，則天下應之以善矣。堯舜，聖者也，其幾動於治天下也，一出言即可爲世法令。觀其典謨所載，都俞吁咈之間，君臣氣通，内外機應，天下即形之矣。湯雖聖者，自時則有誓矣。誓也者，終不若典謨相信之深也。周之末則詛矣，民不惟不信，且有作慝作怨之刑，而上下之心離矣。秦尚奚足言哉！自漢之興，詔多可紀，有聞之而士生色者，有聞之而民伸眉者。惟士與民，天下元氣；元氣理，則百體從令矣。仰惟我皇上即位一詔，上以昭天道，下以悉人情。其録忠褒節，與詩書所載者何所同？其愛民惜財，與帝王所行者何所合？敬老，乃示民以知孝也；優賢，乃示民以崇德也。皆慎固邦本之大端，培養元氣之首務。今
translation_en:
…the sage influence of imperial rule for several years now. Respectfully set forth your views on this matter; do not treat it lightly.

Question: Edicts and commands are the great incipient impulses through which emperors and kings move all under Heaven with their minds. If an impulse tends toward goodness, all under Heaven respond with goodness. Yao and Shun were sages: when their impulses moved toward governing all under Heaven, a single utterance could become a rule or command for the world. Consider what is recorded in their Canons and Counsels: amid their exclamations of approval and dissent, ruler and ministers communicated freely in spirit, and impulses within and beyond the court answered one another; all under Heaven gave outward expression to this [?]. Although Tang was a sage, from his time there were Oaths. Oaths, after all, fall short of the depth of mutual trust found in the Canons and Counsels. By the end of the Zhou, there were imprecations. The people not only lacked trust; there were also punishments for committing evil and stirring resentment, and the hearts of those above and below became estranged. What, then, is there worth saying of the Qin!

Since the rise of the Han, many edicts have been worthy of record. Some made scholars glow with pride on hearing them; others made the people relax their furrowed brows. Scholars and common people are the vital energy of all under Heaven. When that vital energy is properly regulated, all the body's members obey its commands.

We reverently consider the edict issued by our Emperor upon his accession: above, it elucidated the Way of Heaven; below, it fully addressed human feelings. In its recognition of loyalty and commendation of integrity, what does it share with the records of the Book of Odes and Book of Documents? In its love for the people and care for resources, how does it accord with the practices of the ancient emperors and kings? Honoring the aged shows the people how to understand filial piety; favoring the worthy shows the people how to esteem virtue. These are all major means of carefully securing the foundations of the state and foremost tasks in nourishing its vital energy. Now…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
並舉而互言焉宜天下之感動如此其
速也矧察其廢閣也有方考其振舉也
有法即是而之焉三代之治可復也諸
生仰聽之餘不知尚將何以爲
獻請明著于篇毋使隨何之誚嘖嘖
問昔人謂讀書萬卷不讀律致君堯舜終
無術則刑律一節固學者之所當講者
我
朝法律因時以定制緣情以制刑誠萬世所
===
當遵守者也竊以平日所疑者與諸生
議之夫五刑在古所不宥也而舜典許
其贖金至穆王五刑之疑罰鍰有等然
則贖罰固可訓乎抑或别有論也延及
於漢因討西羌兵食不繼建爲入穀贖
罪之法謀國可謂忠矣何以有開利路
傷治化之譏又至於宋因人情冒利犯
禁别爲贖法使人重穀帛免刑罰憫下
可謂切矣何以有貧者不能自免之議
punctuated:
並舉而互言焉，宜天下之感動如此其速也。矧察其廢閣也有方，考其振舉也有法，即是而之焉，三代之治可復也。諸生仰聽之餘，不知尚將何以爲獻？請明著于篇，毋使隨何之誚嘖嘖。
問：昔人謂：「讀書萬卷不讀律，致君堯舜終無術。」則刑律一節，固學者之所當講者。我朝法律，因時以定制，緣情以制刑，誠萬世所當遵守者也。竊以平日所疑者與諸生議之。夫五刑，在古所不宥也，而《舜典》許其贖金；至穆王，五刑之疑，罰鍰有等。然則贖罰固可訓乎？抑或别有論也？延及於漢，因討西羌，兵食不繼，建爲入穀贖罪之法，謀國可謂忠矣，何以有開利路、傷治化之譏？又至於宋，因人情冒利犯禁，别爲贖法，使人重穀帛、免刑罰，憫下可謂切矣，何以有貧者不能自免之議？
translation_en:
…these measures are advanced together and discussed in conjunction. It is fitting that all under Heaven should have been moved so swiftly. Moreover, there are proper means for investigating their neglect and procedures for assessing their revival and implementation. By proceeding along this course, the good government of the Three Dynasties can be restored. Having respectfully heard these pronouncements, what further contributions will you candidates offer? Please set them forth clearly in your essays, lest the reproach concerning Sui He resound insistently.
Question: Someone of old said, “Though you read ten thousand volumes, if you do not read the statutes, you will ultimately lack the means to make your ruler a Yao or Shun.” Penal statutes, then, are certainly a subject that scholars ought to study. Our dynasty’s laws establish institutions suited to the times and prescribe punishments according to the circumstances. They are indeed to be observed for ten thousand generations. I venture to discuss with you candidates some matters that have long puzzled me. In antiquity, the five punishments were not subject to pardon, yet the Canon of Shun permitted their redemption through payments of metal. By the time of King Mu, doubtful cases involving the five punishments carried graded fines measured in huan. Does this mean that redemption payments may properly serve as a precedent? Or is there another interpretation?
Later, under the Han, when campaigns against the western Qiang left military grain supplies insufficient, a law was instituted allowing offenders to redeem their crimes by delivering grain. Such planning for the state may be called loyal; why, then, was it criticized for opening a path to profit and harming governance and moral transformation? Again, under the Song, because people pursued profit and violated prohibitions, a separate system of redemption was established, making people value grain and silk and enabling them to escape punishment. This may be called earnest compassion for those below; why, then, was it criticized on the grounds that the poor could not secure their own exemption?…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
夫刑以繩姦在盛世亦所不免而准贖
一法又非後人之所裁定毫芒輕重之
間世教勸懲所係諸生蓋必有超然之
見矣願一言之
問學之一言其來尚矣至孔門辨之始無
遺義而後世謂之學者尚多可疑焉其
借名於孔門以售己說者類亦多矣至
宋有五星聚奎之祥而諸儒應徵而出
發古人未言之妙啓後學難知之微使
===
無志於斯學者則亦已矣如有志於斯
焉舍是宜無所與論也試舉一二與商
之玉山有講義白鹿洞亦有講義其所
講之義同歟異歟春秋有講義乾卦亦
有講義其所講之義一歟二歟講於東
湖書院者可得指而陳耶講於竹林精
舍者可得舉而言耶嚴陵一講其條目
凡幾和靖一講其名義何居是皆正學
之階梯入聖之門路諸生不欲為吾道
punctuated:
夫刑以繩姦，在盛世亦所不免，而准贖一法，又非後人之所裁定。毫芒輕重之間，世教勸懲所係，諸生蓋必有超然之見矣，願一言之。
問：學之一言，其來尚矣。至孔門辨之，始無遺義，而後世謂之學者，尚多可疑焉。其借名於孔門以售己說者，類亦多矣。至宋，有五星聚奎之祥，而諸儒應徵而出，發古人未言之妙，啓後學難知之微。使無志於斯學者，則亦已矣；如有志於斯焉，舍是宜無所與論也。試舉一二與商之：玉山有講義，白鹿洞亦有講義，其所講之義同歟異歟？春秋有講義，乾卦亦有講義，其所講之義一歟二歟？講於東湖書院者，可得指而陳耶？講於竹林精舍者，可得舉而言耶？嚴陵一講，其條目凡幾？和靖一講，其名義何居？是皆正學之階梯，入聖之門路。諸生不欲為吾道
translation_en:
Punishments serve to restrain wrongdoing and are unavoidable even in a flourishing age; moreover, the provision allowing redemption of punishment was not devised by later generations. The slightest differences in severity bear upon moral instruction and the encouragement of good and deterrence of evil. You candidates surely have discerning views on this; please state them.
Question: The term “learning” has a long history. Only when it was elucidated in the school of Confucius was its meaning fully brought out. Yet much of what later generations called learning remained questionable. There were also many who borrowed the name of Confucius’s school to peddle their own doctrines. In the Song, the auspicious conjunction of the five planets in the Kui constellation occurred, and Confucian scholars emerged in response to this portent. They revealed subtleties the ancients had left unspoken and made accessible to later students refinements difficult to comprehend. Those without aspirations to this learning may leave the matter there; but for those who aspire to it, there should be no basis for discussion apart from these teachings. Let us raise a few examples for consideration. There are lecture expositions from Yushan, and also from Bailudong: are the principles expounded in them the same or different? There are lecture expositions on the Spring and Autumn Annals and also on the Qian hexagram: do they expound one principle or two? Can you identify and set forth what was taught at Donghu Academy? Can you enumerate and discuss what was taught at Zhulin Study Retreat? How many headings were there in the Yanling lecture? What is the significance of the title of the Hejing lecture? These are all steps toward correct learning and paths to sagehood. If you candidates do not wish to pursue the learning of our Way…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之學吾固不得而强聒也如耻爲世俗
之學焉舍是則無所與共圖者盍悉之
以觀脩身用世之具
問蠲貸之令三代之時不聞然則何從而
始也豈後世之寬仁反過於古與自是
有蠲逋貸者有寬逋賦者有除戶調絹
綿者有蠲度支鹽鐵者有减上供饋運
者有免官司債負和買役錢者條目雖
殊而寬貸之仁一也然儒臣建議又多
===
不同夫積久負欠每年帶納一分似爲
便民矣何以有豐年不如凶年之論民
窮賦重盡數蠲除而困尚未甦也何以
有催理九分遷延一分以待蠲放之說
嗚呼蠲貸之典本欲厚民而歲計未免
侵損本欲博愛而小民未必霑恩果何
如而使德澤旁通困窮受惠也其詳言
之以觀經制之策
punctuated:
之學，吾固不得而强聒也。如耻爲世俗之學焉，舍是則無所與共圖者。盍悉之，以觀脩身用世之具？

問：蠲貸之令，三代之時不聞，然則何從而始也？豈後世之寬仁反過於古與？自是有蠲逋貸者，有寬逋賦者，有除戶調絹綿者，有蠲度支鹽鐵者，有减上供饋運者，有免官司債負和買役錢者。條目雖殊，而寬貸之仁一也。然儒臣建議，又多不同。夫積久負欠，每年帶納一分，似爲便民矣，何以有豐年不如凶年之論？民窮賦重，盡數蠲除，而困尚未甦也，何以有催理九分、遷延一分以待蠲放之說？嗚呼！蠲貸之典，本欲厚民，而歲計未免侵損；本欲博愛，而小民未必霑恩。果何如而使德澤旁通，困窮受惠也？其詳言之，以觀經制之策。
translation_en:
…learning, I certainly cannot insist on wearying you with my words. If you are ashamed to pursue merely conventional learning, however, then without this there is nothing we can plan together. Why not explain it fully, so that we may assess your resources for cultivating yourselves and serving the world?

Question: Edicts granting remission and relief are unheard of in the Three Dynasties. When, then, did they originate? Could the generosity and benevolence of later ages actually have surpassed those of antiquity? Since their introduction, some have cancelled overdue loans; some have granted relief on tax arrears; some have abolished household levies of silk cloth and silk floss; some have remitted fiscal levies on salt and iron; some have reduced supplies sent to the court and transport obligations; and some have waived debts owed to government offices, compulsory purchases, and service payments. Although the provisions differ, the benevolence expressed through relief is the same. Yet proposals made by Confucian officials have also differed greatly.

For debts long in arrears, collecting one tenth each year alongside current payments would seem convenient for the people. Why, then, has it been argued that a good harvest year is worse than a bad one? When the people are impoverished and taxation is heavy, even complete remission has not relieved their distress. Why, then, is there talk of pressing for collection of nine tenths while delaying the remaining tenth in anticipation of remission?

Alas! The institution of remission and relief is intended to benefit the people, yet inevitably diminishes annual revenues; it is intended to extend kindness broadly, yet ordinary people do not necessarily receive its blessings. What, then, would enable the benefits of virtuous government to spread everywhere and bring relief to those in distress and poverty? Explain this in detail, so that we may assess your proposals for fiscal administration.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
國治而后天下平
張合
同考試官訓導詹批大學一題人皆能
習之皆能道之下筆處便欠切當
是篇發明經意畧無汎漫之語而
氣格復整豈深於造道者邪
考試官教諭周批講聖經本色語自
===
是難造此作妙矣
考試官學正季批無一句可疵錄之
既有以新一邦之民斯有以新一世之民甚矣
化行自近始也新民之功由一邦而推之於一
世焉其序固如是哉聖經覆言大學之條目至
此蓋謂國於天下雖有遠近之殊而化之所被
初無彼此之間是故提封井井而根本乎諸夏
天子之國政令於是乎出京邑翼翼而表正乎
四方天子之邦聲教於是乎行烝民之生習俗
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
國治而后天下平
張合

同考試官訓導詹批：「大學一題，人皆能習之，皆能道之，下筆處便欠切當。是篇發明經意，畧無汎漫之語，而氣格復整，豈深於造道者邪？」
考試官教諭周批：「講聖經本色語，自是難造，此作妙矣。」
考試官學正季批：「無一句可疵，錄之。」

既有以新一邦之民，斯有以新一世之民。甚矣，化行自近始也！新民之功，由一邦而推之於一世焉，其序固如是哉！聖經覆言大學之條目至此，蓋謂國於天下，雖有遠近之殊，而化之所被，初無彼此之間。是故提封井井，而根本乎諸夏，天子之國，政令於是乎出；京邑翼翼，而表正乎四方，天子之邦，聲教於是乎行。烝民之生，習俗
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Only after the state is well governed is All-under-Heaven at peace.”
Zhang He

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: “Everyone can familiarize himself with a topic from the Great Learning and discuss it, yet when putting brush to paper, writers readily fall short of precision and aptness. This essay elucidates the meaning of the classic without any vague or rambling language, and its force and form are also well ordered. Could its author be someone deeply accomplished in approaching the Way?”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “In expounding the sages’ classic, language true to its essential character is certainly difficult to achieve. This composition is excellent.”

Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: “Not a single sentence can be faulted. Include it.”

Once there are means to renew the people of one state, there are thereby means to renew the people of an entire age. How profound it is that the spread of transforming influence begins with what is near! The work of renewing the people extends from one state to an entire age: surely this is its proper sequence! When the sages’ classic reaches this point in restating the successive stages of the Great Learning, its meaning is that, although the state and All-under-Heaven differ in proximity and distance, the transforming influence that reaches them makes no distinction between the one and the other. Thus, with its territorial boundaries well ordered, it serves as the foundation of the various Xia states: this is the Son of Heaven’s state, from which governmental commands issue. With its capital stately and imposing, it sets an upright example for the four quarters: this is the Son of Heaven’s realm, from which his moral instruction spreads. In the lives of the multitude, customary habits…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
所移未易一也然自新之德出于身而加于民
凡有所觀感者舊染之污以革翕然遵道遵義
之風羣黎之聚氣品所拘未易化也然自明之
德發乎邇而見乎遠凡知所興起者敦睦之俗
自成居然不識不知之域國其有不治耶夫大
道之行有可化之機至仁之推無不準之理由
是薄海之內體國之外天下固大矣皆歸于允
脩之極天之所覆地之所載四海固廣矣舉囿
于昭明之天凡民有行意以之誠心以之正而
===
矯偽之忒不作蕩蕩乎民恊于中之盛也有生
之衆身知所脩家知所齊而親長之愛以流熈
熈乎萬國咸寧之休也天下有不平邪是則舍
近而謀遠其為力也難篤近而舉遠其責效也
易自新之功既至新民之化自成蓋有不期然
而然者矣大學君子可不知所務哉蓋嘗論之
治天下有本身之謂也治天下有則家之謂也
大學言明德新民之序極其體用之全蓋不徒
為入德之門雖堯舜之治亦不過此而後之君
punctuated: 所移，未易一也。然自新之德出于身而加于民，凡有所觀感者，舊染之污以革，翕然遵道遵義之風。羣黎之聚，氣品所拘，未易化也。然自明之德發乎邇而見乎遠，凡知所興起者，敦睦之俗自成，居然不識不知之域。國其有不治耶？夫大道之行，有可化之機；至仁之推，無不準之理。由是薄海之內，體國之外，天下固大矣，皆歸于允脩之極；天之所覆，地之所載，四海固廣矣，舉囿于昭明之天。凡民有行，意以之誠，心以之正，而矯偽之忒不作，蕩蕩乎民恊于中之盛也！有生之衆，身知所脩，家知所齊，而親長之愛以流，熈熈乎萬國咸寧之休也！天下有不平邪？是則舍近而謀遠，其為力也難；篤近而舉遠，其責效也易。自新之功既至，新民之化自成，蓋有不期然而然者矣。大學君子可不知所務哉？蓋嘗論之：治天下有本，身之謂也；治天下有則，家之謂也。大學言明德新民之序，極其體用之全，蓋不徒為入德之門，雖堯舜之治亦不過此，而後之君
translation_en:
…shaped by custom, they are not easily brought into accord. Yet the virtue of renewing oneself proceeds from one's own person and extends to the people. All who witness it and are moved by it cast off the stains of former habits, joining together in a prevailing spirit of following the Way and righteousness. The assembled common people, constrained by their temperaments and dispositions, are not easily transformed. Yet the virtue of making oneself luminous begins nearby and manifests itself afar. Among all who know to rouse themselves, customs of generosity and concord naturally take shape, and they come to dwell in a realm where goodness is practiced without conscious knowledge or awareness. Could the state then fail to be well governed?

Where the Great Way prevails, there is the potential for transformation; when consummate benevolence is extended, its principles apply everywhere. Thus, within the bounds of the seas and beyond the state's territory [?], vast though all under Heaven may be, all turn toward the highest standard of sincere cultivation. Throughout all that Heaven covers and Earth supports, broad though the Four Seas may be, all are enclosed beneath a heaven of radiant illumination. In all the people's conduct, their intentions are thereby made sincere and their hearts rectified, so that the faults of affectation and deceit do not arise. How expansive is the flourishing condition in which the people harmonize with the mean! Among the multitude of the living, all know how to cultivate themselves and regulate their families, and love for parents and elders spreads abroad. How joyful is the blessed condition in which the myriad states are all at peace! Could all under Heaven then fail to be pacified?

Thus, to forsake what is near and scheme for what is distant makes the effort difficult; to attend earnestly to what is near and thereby reach what is distant makes results easy to obtain. Once the work of renewing oneself has reached its fulfillment, the transformation that renews the people comes about of itself: it happens without having been deliberately sought. Can the gentleman who pursues the Great Learning fail to know where to direct his efforts?

I have considered this: governing all under Heaven has a root—one's own person; governing all under Heaven has a model—one's family. The Great Learning sets forth the sequence of making virtue luminous and renewing the people, fully encompassing both its substance and its operation. It is more than merely a gateway into virtue: even the government of Yao and Shun went no further than this. Yet the gentlemen of later ages…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
子卒致慨乎至治之澤何哉大學之道不明而
正心之功未講耳善乎董子之言曰正心以正
朝廷正朝廷以正百官正百官以正萬民森然
孔氏家法也聖君賢相苟欲共成正大光明之
業者尚鑒兹哉
夫子喟然嘆曰吾與點也
趙汝濂
同考試官訓導鄭批場中作此題者率
爲暮春以下數句纏繞於聖人許
===
點之意全形容不出此作於清明
峻潔之中有雍容頓挫之態亦異
乎諸士之撰矣
考試官教諭周批寫出曾點自得及
聖人嘆許氣象宛然在目
考試官學正季批胸次不凡立論自
別
聖人於賢者形於嘆而許之深所以重其志也
蓋聖人不輕以譽人也於曾點而嘆許之深者
punctuated:
子卒致慨乎至治之澤，何哉？大學之道不明，而正心之功未講耳。善乎董子之言曰：「正心以正朝廷，正朝廷以正百官，正百官以正萬民。」森然孔氏家法也。聖君賢相苟欲共成正大光明之業者，尚鑒兹哉！
夫子喟然嘆曰：「吾與點也。」
趙汝濂
同考試官訓導鄭批：場中作此題者，率爲暮春以下數句纏繞，於聖人許點之意全形容不出。此作於清明峻潔之中，有雍容頓挫之態，亦異乎諸士之撰矣。
考試官教諭周批：寫出曾點自得及聖人嘆許氣象，宛然在目。
考試官學正季批：胸次不凡，立論自別。
聖人於賢者，形於嘆而許之深，所以重其志也。蓋聖人不輕以譽人也，於曾點而嘆許之深者，
translation_en:
…gentlemen of later ages nevertheless came to lament the passing of the blessings of perfect government. Why? Simply because the Way of the Great Learning was not understood, and the work of rectifying the mind was not studied. How excellent are Master Dong’s words: “Rectify the mind in order to rectify the court; rectify the court in order to rectify the hundred officials; rectify the hundred officials in order to rectify the myriad people.” Here stands, in imposing order, the inherited teaching of Confucius. May sage rulers and worthy chief ministers who wish together to accomplish an upright and enlightened undertaking take this as their guide!
The Master sighed deeply and said: “I am with Dian.”
Zhao Rulian
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: Those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic were generally entangled in the several sentences beginning “In late spring,” and entirely failed to convey the sage’s intention in approving Dian. This composition, amid its clarity and rigorous purity, possesses a poise and rhythmic variation that also distinguish it from the compositions of the other candidates.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: It portrays Zeng Dian’s inner contentment and the sage’s sigh of approval so vividly that the scene seems to stand before one’s eyes.
Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: His cast of mind is exceptional, and his argument is distinctive.
When the sage’s response to a worthy man takes the form of a sigh and profound approval, it is because he esteems that man’s aspiration. For the sage does not lightly praise others; as for his sigh and profound approval of Zeng Dian…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
其亦有所感哉昔吾夫子當門人言志之餘正
曾點敷陳之際真樂氣象感觸乎與物同體之
天順適襟懷契合乎隨寓而安之妙於是天機
黙應而感嘆隨之心有所樂而口之宣揚自有
不能已者矣妙理潜孚而嘆息繼之中有所悅
而言之吐露蓋有不容遏者矣其意以為人孰
無志也而或失於外馳志非不壯也而每忽於
內重惟爾曾點充然自得崛起於儔伍之中脫
然無累傑出乎風塵之表涵養既熟而動靜從
===
容依稀乎欲盡理還之境較之汲汲於功名之
會者自不侔矣寧容已於嘆賞乎識見既精而
志嚮卓越彷彿乎安土樂天之趣比之規規於
事為之末者有間矣寧容已於稱許乎數言之
間具見心事真實可以激頹風者在是吾不許
點而誰許哉一時之對足知操履真純可以敦
士行者在是吾不與點而誰與哉是則非諸子
不能見曾點之高非曾點不能發聖人之嘆孔
門師弟子雍容交與之氣象於是乎見矣雖然
punctuated: 其亦有所感哉？昔吾夫子當門人言志之餘，正曾點敷陳之際，真樂氣象感觸乎與物同體之天，順適襟懷契合乎隨寓而安之妙。於是天機黙應，而感嘆隨之；心有所樂，而口之宣揚，自有不能已者矣。妙理潜孚，而嘆息繼之；中有所悅，而言之吐露，蓋有不容遏者矣。其意以為：人孰無志也，而或失於外馳；志非不壯也，而每忽於內重。惟爾曾點，充然自得，崛起於儔伍之中；脫然無累，傑出乎風塵之表。涵養既熟，而動靜從容，依稀乎欲盡理還之境，較之汲汲於功名之會者，自不侔矣，寧容已於嘆賞乎？識見既精，而志嚮卓越，彷彿乎安土樂天之趣，比之規規於事為之末者，有間矣，寧容已於稱許乎？數言之間，具見心事真實，可以激頹風者在是，吾不許點而誰許哉？一時之對，足知操履真純，可以敦士行者在是，吾不與點而誰與哉？是則非諸子不能見曾點之高，非曾點不能發聖人之嘆。孔門師弟子雍容交與之氣象，於是乎見矣。雖然，
translation_en:
…was he not also moved by something? Formerly, when the disciples had spoken of their aspirations and Zeng Dian was setting forth his own, the air of genuine joy stirred in our Master that heavenly nature which forms one body with all things. Zeng Dian’s ease of heart accorded with the wondrous capacity to be at peace wherever one finds oneself. Thus the spontaneous workings of Heaven silently responded, and an admiring sigh followed. His heart found joy, and he could not help giving it voice. Subtle principle found a tacit correspondence, and a sigh ensued. There was delight within him, and its expression in words could not be restrained.

His meaning was this: Who lacks aspirations? Yet some go astray in pursuing things outside themselves. Their aspirations are certainly grand, yet they often neglect what is weighty within. You alone, Zeng Dian, are fulfilled and content in yourself, standing above your companions; free and unencumbered, you rise beyond the dust of worldly affairs. Your self-cultivation has matured, and you are composed in both activity and stillness, approaching the state in which desires are exhausted and principle is restored. You are naturally unlike those who eagerly pursue opportunities for achievement and fame. How could I refrain from sighing in admiration? Your discernment is refined and your aspirations lofty, approaching the spirit of being content where one dwells and delighting in Heaven. You stand apart from those narrowly preoccupied with the peripheral details of practical affairs. How could I refrain from praising you? In a few words, the sincerity of your innermost concerns is fully revealed. Here is what can revitalize declining customs. If I do not approve of you, Dian, whom should I approve of? This single reply suffices to reveal the genuineness and purity of your conduct. Here is what can strengthen the conduct of scholars. If I do not commend you, Dian, whom should I commend?

Thus, without the other disciples, Zeng Dian’s loftiness could not have been revealed; without Zeng Dian, the sage’s sigh could not have been elicited. Here we see the gracious ease with which master and disciples engaged with one another in the school of Kongzi. Even so, …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
曾點之志固高矣使人皆潔身遠引獨善廢倫
則天下之事孰與共理哉但世至春秋急於功
利或失身喪節而不能自振者多欲累之也果
心境虚豁而不爲勢利紛華所制則其建立必
有大過人者此可見事業之偉實原於人品之
高惟有壁立之風度斯有孤高之氣節固相須
而難掩者噫曾點豈易及哉
學問之道無他求其放心而已矣
李元陽
===
同考試官學正方 批此題塲中作者多
以學問二字混講枯澁可厭且於
本章說仁義處略不相關此作專
主周易學聚問辨立意發揮殆盡
其起結又能照管仁義深得孟子
立言微旨子可謂究心理學有素
矣
考試官教諭周 批遍觀諸作全非孟
子本意獨此篇體認真切筆力雄
punctuated:
曾點之志固高矣，使人皆潔身遠引，獨善廢倫，則天下之事孰與共理哉？但世至春秋，急於功利，或失身喪節而不能自振者多，欲累之也。果心境虚豁，而不爲勢利紛華所制，則其建立必有大過人者。此可見事業之偉，實原於人品之高。惟有壁立之風度，斯有孤高之氣節，固相須而難掩者。噫！曾點豈易及哉？
學問之道無他，求其放心而已矣。
李元陽
同考試官學正方批：此題塲中作者，多以學問二字混講，枯澁可厭，且於本章說仁義處略不相關。此作專主《周易》學聚問辨，立意發揮殆盡。其起結又能照管仁義，深得孟子立言微旨。子可謂究心理學有素矣。
考試官教諭周批：遍觀諸作，全非孟子本意，獨此篇體認真切，筆力雄
translation_en:
Zeng Dian’s aspirations were certainly lofty. Yet if everyone kept himself unsullied and withdrew far from public life, cultivating his own goodness alone while abandoning human relationships, with whom could one jointly order the affairs of the world? By the Spring and Autumn period, however, people were so intent on achievement and profit that many compromised themselves and forfeited their integrity, unable to recover: desire had ensnared them. If one’s mind were truly open and unencumbered, uncontrolled by power, profit, worldly bustle, and splendor, one’s accomplishments would surely far surpass those of others. This shows that greatness in achievement truly originates in loftiness of character. Only with a bearing as firm as a sheer cliff can one possess an integrity that stands loftily apart. These qualities depend upon one another and cannot readily be concealed. Ah! How could Zeng Dian’s stature be easily attained?
“The way of learning and inquiry is nothing other than seeking to recover one’s strayed mind.”
Li Yuanyang
Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, School Instructor: Most candidates writing on this topic treated the two words ‘learning’ and ‘inquiry’ indiscriminately, producing dry, labored, tiresome writing that scarcely related to the discussion of benevolence and righteousness in this chapter. This composition focuses specifically on the teaching of the Changes of Zhou concerning learning to accumulate knowledge and questioning to discriminate, developing its central conception almost exhaustively. Its opening and conclusion also attend to benevolence and righteousness, deeply grasping the subtle purport of Mencius’s words. You may indeed be said to have long devoted yourself to investigating the Learning of Principle.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Having read through all the compositions, I find that they entirely miss Mencius’s original meaning. This essay alone shows a genuine and precise grasp, with a forceful literary style…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
健非平日養心靜而充之以學者
不能至此
考試官學正季批洗滌舊聞可以式
矣
大賢論為學之要收心之外無餘事也甚矣人
心易放也為學之要亦惟存此而已豈復有他
道哉昔孟子論仁為人心而嘆人失之不求及
此謂夫人不可以不學學莫貴於知要是故天
下事物之理有所當然者焉載諸古訓而可知
===
有所以然者焉布在方冊而可考學不容已也
必須學以聚之或索之文字之間或資諸師友
之論何為所當然而體驗之不遺何為所以然
而講求之匪懈學不可謂不博矣理之所當然
者學雖有知猶或涉於疑似理之所以然者學
雖有得猶或滯於彷彿問不容已也必須問以
辯之或博考乎羣書或延訪乎眾論決其疑於
師匪直資諸人而已辯其義於友非但訪於眾
而已問不可謂不審矣夫學問之事固非一端
punctuated:
健，非平日養心靜而充之以學者，不能至此。

考試官學正季批：洗滌舊聞，可以式矣。

大賢論為學之要，收心之外無餘事也。甚矣，人心易放也！為學之要，亦惟存此而已，豈復有他道哉？昔孟子論仁為人心，而嘆人失之不求。及此，謂夫人不可以不學，學莫貴於知要。是故天下事物之理，有所當然者焉，載諸古訓而可知；有所以然者焉，布在方冊而可考。學不容已也，必須學以聚之。或索之文字之間，或資諸師友之論，何為所當然而體驗之不遺，何為所以然而講求之匪懈，學不可謂不博矣。理之所當然者，學雖有知，猶或涉於疑似；理之所以然者，學雖有得，猶或滯於彷彿。問不容已也，必須問以辯之。或博考乎羣書，或延訪乎眾論，決其疑於師，匪直資諸人而已；辯其義於友，非但訪於眾而已。問不可謂不審矣。夫學問之事，固非一端。
translation_en:
…vigorous. Only someone who habitually nurtures the mind in stillness and enriches it through learning could attain this level.

Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: “It clears away received notions and may serve as a model.”

When the great worthy discussed the essentials of learning, there was nothing beyond gathering back the mind. How readily the human mind goes astray! The essential task of learning is simply to preserve this mind. Could there be any other way? Earlier, Mengzi explained that benevolence is the human mind and lamented that people lose it without seeking it. Here he says that people cannot forgo learning, and that in learning nothing is more valuable than knowing its essentials. Thus, the principles of the affairs and things of the world include what ought to be so, which is recorded in ancient teachings and can be known; they also include the reasons why things are so, which are set forth in books and can be examined. Learning cannot cease: one must learn in order to accumulate this knowledge. One may seek it in written texts or draw upon the discussions of teachers and friends. One investigates what ought to be so and comprehends it through personal experience, overlooking nothing; one investigates why it is so and studies it without flagging. Such learning cannot be called anything but broad.

As for what ought to be so in principle, although learning yields knowledge, one may still be caught between doubt and apparent truth. As for why it is so in principle, although learning yields understanding, one may still remain at the level of vague impressions. Questioning cannot cease: one must question in order to distinguish clearly. One may consult a wide range of books or seek out diverse opinions. One resolves doubts with a teacher, rather than merely drawing upon other people; one clarifies meanings with friends, rather than merely consulting the many. Such questioning cannot be called anything but thorough. Now, the work of learning and questioning certainly has more than one aspect…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
推原其要惟求諸心耳蓋心也者人之神明所
以具衆理者此其體所以應萬事者此其用易
放也或出或入無一定之時易失也于彼于斯
無常止之處必斂之於翼翼之天使既出者而
復入鎮靜自如無時不在可也約之於惺惺之
地使在彼者常在此一真自若無處不然可也
學問之道如此而已豈復有他求哉夫如是則
學問有益於已而心存心存則仁存矣仁存則
內而心之有制外而事之得宜義亦在其中矣
===
學者欲求仁義之理可不先於此心之致力與
抑孟子生丁是時驩謀功利之徒縱横游說之
輩藉此相高可謂月異而歲不同矣一旦憫人
心之陷溺慨道學之不明而揭此以示人有功
於吾道顧不偉哉先儒謂其功不在禹下益信
其然矣
易
進以正可以正邦也
趙汝濂
punctuated:
推原其要，惟求諸心耳。蓋心也者，人之神明，所以具衆理者，此其體；所以應萬事者，此其用。易放也，或出或入，無一定之時；易失也，于彼于斯，無常止之處。必斂之於翼翼之天，使既出者而復入，鎮靜自如，無時不在，可也；約之於惺惺之地，使在彼者常在此，一真自若，無處不然，可也。學問之道如此而已，豈復有他求哉？夫如是，則學問有益於已而心存。心存則仁存矣，仁存則內而心之有制，外而事之得宜，義亦在其中矣。學者欲求仁義之理，可不先於此心之致力與？抑孟子生丁是時，驩謀功利之徒、縱横游說之輩，藉此相高，可謂月異而歲不同矣。一旦憫人心之陷溺，慨道學之不明，而揭此以示人，有功於吾道，顧不偉哉？先儒謂其功不在禹下，益信其然矣。
《易》
進以正，可以正邦也。
趙汝濂
translation_en:
…Tracing these pursuits to their essentials, one need only seek within the mind. The mind is the spiritual intelligence of the human being: its substance consists in possessing the manifold principles, and its function consists in responding to the myriad affairs. It readily wanders, now going out, now coming in, at no fixed time; it is easily lost, now there, now here, with no constant resting place. One must gather it into a state of reverent vigilance [?], so that, having gone out, it returns within, remaining composed and at ease, present at every moment. One must restrain it within a state of wakeful awareness, so that what was there remains always here, its undivided genuineness unchanged, wherever it may be. This is all there is to the way of learning and inquiry. What else could one seek? In this way, learning and inquiry benefit oneself, and the mind is preserved. When the mind is preserved, benevolence is preserved. When benevolence is preserved, the mind is regulated within and affairs are handled fittingly without; righteousness is also contained therein. Can those who seek the principles of benevolence and righteousness fail to begin by devoting their efforts to this mind?
Now Mencius lived at a time when those who eagerly schemed for achievement and profit [?], and those who traveled about advocating diplomatic alliances, used these pursuits to outdo one another. Their devices could indeed be said to change from month to month and differ from year to year. Moved by pity at the engulfing of people’s minds and distressed that the learning of the Way was obscure, he set forth this teaching for others. Was his service to our Way not great indeed? Earlier Confucian scholars said that his achievement was no less than Yu’s; this gives us still greater confidence that they were right.
Book of Changes
“By advancing with correctness, one can set the state right.”
Zhao Rulian

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導鄭批講正邦處嚴整條
暢一結尤見忠愛得士如此進之
可自慶矣
考試官教諭周批因卦變而推治道
誰不知之但有根據而善發揮如
此者少
考試官學正季批得彖傳微意
即卦變晉正之善見治道表正之本彖傳釋利
貞之意也蓋治化之行繫於身也本旣端矣而
===
施之於政焉有不正者哉彖傳之意蓋如此今
夫漸之所以利貞者何所取哉嘗觀諸卦變矣
九居於二昭於渙也今進處於三則變於艮而
得陽位之正矣九居於四著於旅也今進位於
五則變於巽而得陽體之正矣由下僚而晉具
瞻之地何有乎僭躐之嫌從潛邸而履帝位之
尊允協乎歸依之願夫如是則爲世道一新之
會朝廷更化之機邦國豈有不正乎吾知上下
同心以正理而應庶務君臣合德以正法而肅
punctuated:
同考試官訓導鄭批：講正邦處，嚴整條暢；一結尤見忠愛。得士如此，進之可自慶矣。
考試官教諭周批：因卦變而推治道，誰不知之？但有根據而善發揮如此者少。
考試官學正季批：得彖傳微意。
即卦變晉正之善，見治道表正之本，彖傳釋利貞之意也。蓋治化之行繫於身也，本旣端矣，而施之於政，焉有不正者哉？彖傳之意蓋如此。今夫漸之所以利貞者，何所取哉？嘗觀諸卦變矣。九居於二，昭於渙也；今進處於三，則變於艮，而得陽位之正矣。九居於四，著於旅也；今進位於五，則變於巽，而得陽體之正矣。由下僚而晉具瞻之地，何有乎僭躐之嫌？從潛邸而履帝位之尊，允協乎歸依之願。夫如是，則爲世道一新之會、朝廷更化之機，邦國豈有不正乎？吾知上下同心，以正理而應庶務；君臣合德，以正法而肅
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: The passage explaining how to rectify the state is rigorous, orderly, and lucid. The conclusion especially reveals loyalty and devotion. Having obtained such a scholar, one may congratulate oneself on advancing him.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Who does not know how to infer the way of government from transformations of the hexagrams? Yet few ground their arguments so securely and develop them so well.
Comment by Examiner Ji, School Instructor: He has grasped the subtle meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments.
To discern, in the excellence of advancing into a correct position through a hexagram’s transformation, the foundation of government in setting a correct example: this is the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments in explaining “it is beneficial to be steadfast and correct.” For the implementation of government and moral transformation depends on the ruler’s own person. Once the root is upright, how could its application to government fail to be correct? Such, indeed, is the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments.
Now, on what grounds does the hexagram Gradual Progress (Jian) hold that “it is beneficial to be steadfast and correct”? I have examined this through the transformations of the hexagrams. A nine occupying the second position is clearly seen in Dispersion (Huan). Now, advancing to occupy the third position, it changes the trigram to Keeping Still (Gen), attaining the correctness of a yang position. A nine occupying the fourth position is manifest in The Wanderer (Lü). Now, advancing to the fifth position, it changes the trigram to The Gentle (Xun), attaining the correctness proper to its yang nature.
When one advances from a subordinate office to a position upon which all eyes are fixed, what grounds are there for suspecting usurpation or improper advancement? When one leaves the princely residence to assume the exalted imperial throne, this truly accords with the people’s wish to give their allegiance. Thus it becomes an occasion for renewing the ways of the world and an opportunity for the court to reform its government. How could the state fail to be rectified? I know that those above and below will unite in purpose, addressing the manifold affairs of government through correct principles; ruler and ministers will unite in virtue, employing correct laws to bring order to …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
斯民操乾剛之正於崇高之上而左右臣屬咸
以堯舜之道輔之凡紀綱法度之施悉皆光明
正大之宏規也秉陽德之正於宸極之嚴而奔
走百辟咸以仁義之道佐之凡詔令政刑之舉
絕無偏黨反側之夙弊也自一心以推之於萬
幾罔非王道之懿而可以挽回風化矣凡囿於
覆冒者孰有不正乎自朝廷以達之於邦域莫
非天德之純而可以斡旋世道矣凡得於觀感
者焉有不正乎是則先有正己之本而後有正
===
人之用使進若可議則人皆弗信弗從矣雖一
家尚難況欲正其邦耶此筮而得漸者不可不
利於貞也抑進得其正而效可以正邦是固然
矣使玩安忽治而或以匪人間之亦安能保其
終無敝哉是以古昔盛時志同道合都俞吁咈
之間莫非警戒相成之道猶恐憸邪乘隙以撓
正而隄防疎遠無所不至嗚呼是豈得已哉蓋
天下之勢治日常少而天下之人邪佞易親此
保治之策自不容於不謹也
punctuated:
斯民。操乾剛之正於崇高之上，而左右臣屬咸以堯舜之道輔之，凡紀綱法度之施，悉皆光明正大之宏規也。秉陽德之正於宸極之嚴，而奔走百辟咸以仁義之道佐之，凡詔令政刑之舉，絕無偏黨反側之夙弊也。自一心以推之於萬幾，罔非王道之懿，而可以挽回風化矣，凡囿於覆冒者，孰有不正乎？自朝廷以達之於邦域，莫非天德之純，而可以斡旋世道矣，凡得於觀感者，焉有不正乎？是則先有正己之本，而後有正人之用。使進若可議，則人皆弗信弗從矣，雖一家尚難，況欲正其邦耶？此筮而得漸者，不可不利於貞也。

抑進得其正，而效可以正邦，是固然矣。使玩安忽治，而或以匪人間之，亦安能保其終無敝哉？是以古昔盛時，志同道合，都俞吁咈之間，莫非警戒相成之道，猶恐憸邪乘隙以撓正，而隄防疎遠，無所不至。嗚呼！是豈得已哉？蓋天下之勢，治日常少，而天下之人，邪佞易親，此保治之策，自不容於不謹也。
translation_en:
…these people. Holding fast to the rectitude of Qian’s vigorous strength in his exalted position, the ruler receives assistance from all his attendant ministers in accordance with the Way of Yao and Shun. Every application of governing principles, laws, and institutions follows a grand design that is luminous, upright, and impartial. Maintaining the rectitude of yang virtue in the majesty of the imperial throne, he receives support from all the officials who hasten to serve him, in accordance with the Way of benevolence and righteousness. Every decree and every measure of government and punishment is entirely free of the longstanding abuses of partisanship and duplicity. Extending what is in his own heart to the myriad affairs of state, he manifests nothing but the excellence of the kingly Way and can thereby restore moral influence and transform customs. Among all those encompassed by his protection, who would fail to become upright? Extending this from the court throughout the realm, he manifests nothing but the purity of Heaven’s virtue and can thereby turn the course of the age. Among all those moved by observing his example, who would fail to become upright? Thus, first there is the foundation of rectifying oneself, and afterward there is its application in rectifying others. If his advancement were open to reproach, people would neither trust nor follow him. He would find it difficult even to rectify a single household; how much less could he hope to rectify his state? This is why one who obtains the hexagram Jian, Gradual Progress, through divination must heed the benefit of steadfast correctness.

Now, that advancement in accordance with what is right can produce the effect of rectifying the state is certainly true. But if the ruler grows complacent in peace and neglects good government, and unworthy men should intrude, how could he ensure that no deterioration would eventually occur? Thus, in the flourishing ages of antiquity, ruler and ministers shared aspirations and agreed upon the Way. In their exchanges of assent and dissent, all served to admonish one another and bring one another to fulfillment. Still fearing that crafty and wicked men might exploit an opening to subvert rectitude, they took every possible precaution and kept such men at a distance. Alas! Could they have done otherwise? For in the affairs of the world, days of good order are always few, while among its people, the wicked and flattering are easy to grow close to. A policy for preserving good order therefore necessarily demands vigilance.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易之爲書也不可遠爲道也屢遷
封祖裔
同考試官訓導鄭批場中講屢遷處多
牽引下文變動周流四句填實則
此句似無味矣是作融會全節而
句格亦新蓋邃於易者
考試官教諭周批易有至妙不可遠
得士如此吾敢遠而不取乎
考試官學正季批說理之文難乎明
===
暢此可謂易人之所難也
大傳論易切於人由其有變通之妙也蓋易道
有資於人大矣苟少違焉則所具之理何由而
自行於人哉大傳之意蓋如此今夫易之爲書
本爲卜筮而設若可遠也然卦爻森列括盡天
下之理切於民生而不可須臾離焉變象具陳
曲盡古今之事利於日用而不可頃刻違焉不
存於心終爲韋編之陳迹而吾操縱之權無其
本矣豈若他書專爲一事而作者猶可遠乎不
punctuated:
易之爲書也不可遠，爲道也屢遷。
封祖裔
同考試官訓導鄭批：「場中講屢遷處，多牽引下文變動周流四句填實，則此句似無味矣。是作融會全節，而句格亦新，蓋邃於易者。」
考試官教諭周批：「易有至妙，不可遠。得士如此，吾敢遠而不取乎？」
考試官學正季批：「說理之文，難乎明暢，此可謂易人之所難也。」
大傳論易切於人，由其有變通之妙也。蓋易道有資於人大矣，苟少違焉，則所具之理何由而自行於人哉？大傳之意蓋如此。今夫易之爲書，本爲卜筮而設，若可遠也。然卦爻森列，括盡天下之理，切於民生而不可須臾離焉；變象具陳，曲盡古今之事，利於日用而不可頃刻違焉。不存於心，終爲韋編之陳迹，而吾操縱之權無其本矣，豈若他書專爲一事而作者，猶可遠乎？不
translation_en:
“As a book, the Changes must not be kept at a distance; as a Way, it continually shifts.”
By Feng Zuyi.
Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor, comments: “When explaining ‘continually shifts,’ many candidates in this examination draw upon the four following clauses beginning with ‘changing and moving, circulating everywhere’ to supply concrete content. This leaves the present sentence seeming devoid of meaning. This composition integrates the entire passage, and its sentence patterns are fresh as well. Its author evidently has a profound understanding of the Changes.”
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The Changes contains the utmost subtlety and must not be kept at a distance. Having found a scholar like this, would I dare keep him at a distance and fail to select him?”
Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: “In writing that expounds principles, clarity and fluency are difficult to achieve. This may be said to make easy what others find difficult.”
The Great Commentary explains that the Changes is intimately relevant to human beings because it possesses the subtle power of change and adaptation. Indeed, the Way of the Changes offers great assistance to people. If they depart from it even slightly, how could the principles it contains find expression of themselves in human affairs? Such, broadly, is the meaning of the Great Commentary. Now, the Changes as a book was originally established for divination, so it might seem that one could keep it at a distance. Yet its hexagrams and lines stand arrayed in full order, comprehending all the principles under Heaven; they bear directly upon people’s lives and cannot be left behind even for an instant. Its transformations and images are fully displayed, exhaustively encompassing the affairs of past and present; they benefit daily use and cannot be departed from even for a moment. If it is not kept in the heart, it ultimately remains merely a relic of leather-bound writings, while our power to exercise control lacks its foundation. How could it resemble other books, composed solely for a particular purpose, which one might still keep at a distance? If it is not…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
接於目卒為簡策之虚文而吾張弛之方無其
要矣豈若諸書偏於一節而言者猶可忘乎夫
易之不可離者如是其切由道之載於書者莫
測其機如詩理性情書之局於一者也易則變
化無端而未甞少有凝滯如禮謹節文書之偏
於一者也易則通變無方而未甞少有拘泥雖
曰不過卦爻而已耳其中精微之道在此在彼
而動盪之無常可以守經也可以行權也從之
則安外之則危顧可得而遠哉雖曰不過變象
===
而已耳其間玄妙之理或往或来而流行之匪
定可以行已也可以應物也循之則吉悖之則
凶又可得而離哉是則人有百為必玩易而後
善易有萬變須待人而後行聖人言此無非欲
人體易而開物成務之心始慰矣嗚呼六經皆
聖人垂世之典也曷獨於易而不可遠哉蓋易
之為教雖曰廣大悉備總而言之不過曰時而
已時在造化亦不能違而况於人乎人徒知讀
易而不知隨時之義雖常存心目而卒歸於無
punctuated: 接於目，卒為簡策之虚文，而吾張弛之方無其要矣。豈若諸書偏於一節而言者，猶可忘乎？夫易之不可離者，如是其切，由道之載於書者莫測其機。如詩理性情，書之局於一者也；易則變化無端，而未甞少有凝滯。如禮謹節文，書之偏於一者也；易則通變無方，而未甞少有拘泥。雖曰不過卦爻而已耳，其中精微之道，在此在彼，而動盪之無常，可以守經也，可以行權也。從之則安，外之則危，顧可得而遠哉？雖曰不過變象而已耳，其間玄妙之理，或往或来，而流行之匪定，可以行已也，可以應物也。循之則吉，悖之則凶，又可得而離哉？是則人有百為，必玩易而後善；易有萬變，須待人而後行。聖人言此，無非欲人體易，而開物成務之心始慰矣。嗚呼！六經皆聖人垂世之典也，曷獨於易而不可遠哉？蓋易之為教，雖曰廣大悉備，總而言之，不過曰時而已。時在造化亦不能違，而况於人乎？人徒知讀易，而不知隨時之義，雖常存心目，而卒歸於無
translation_en:
…if it is not brought before the eyes, it ultimately becomes empty writing on bamboo slips, and our methods of tightening and relaxing lose their essential guide. Could it be like other books, whose statements concern only a single aspect, and thus be forgotten? That the Changes cannot be set aside is so pressing because the workings of the Way recorded in this book are unfathomable. For example, the Poetry orders human nature and feelings: it is a book confined to one aspect. The Changes, however, transforms without limit and never shows the slightest stagnation. The Rites, for example, attends carefully to ceremonial forms: it is a book devoted to one aspect. The Changes, however, adapts to change without fixed methods and never shows the slightest rigidity. Though it may be said to contain nothing more than hexagrams and their lines, the subtle Way within them is now here, now there, moving without constancy. Through it one may uphold constant principles or exercise discretion. Following it brings security; setting it aside brings danger. How, then, could one keep it at a distance? Though it may be said to contain nothing more than changes and images, the mysterious principles within them now depart, now arrive, circulating without fixed bounds. Through them one may conduct oneself [?] and respond to things. Following them brings good fortune; going against them brings misfortune. How, then, could one depart from them?

Thus, although people undertake a hundred kinds of activity, they must ponder the Changes before they can act well; although the Changes contains ten thousand transformations, it must await people before these can be put into practice. In saying this, the sage wished only that people should embody the Changes; only then would his desire to elucidate things and bring undertakings to completion be satisfied. Alas! The Six Classics are all canonical works handed down to the world by the sages. Why should the Changes alone be something one cannot keep at a distance? Although the teaching of the Changes is vast and comprehensive, taken as a whole it amounts to nothing more than timeliness. Even the processes of creation and transformation cannot contravene the time; how much less can human beings! If people know only how to read the Changes, but do not understand the meaning of adapting to the time, then, though they constantly keep it in mind and before their eyes, it ultimately brings no …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
補也噫使人皆知此義則易具六十四卦亦足
矣而曷用煩辭爲哉於此見聖人憂世之心果
不得已也
書
恭黙思道夢帝賚予良弼
張合
同考試官訓導詹批高宗中興事業都
在恭黙思道上此篇極其形容渾
雄偉麗無不有之録以爲學書者
===
法
考試官教諭周批發明傳意略無費
辭佳作也
考試官學正季批意圓詞贍程式之
文也
極圖治之誠感輔治之兆賢王自敘之辭也夫
天人相與之際微矣賢王圖治甚誠而得賢甚
異感應之理有如是哉昔高宗因羣臣之諫故
作書喻在己之意若曰表正四方固予之責不
punctuated:
補也。噫！使人皆知此義，則易具六十四卦亦足矣，而曷用煩辭爲哉？於此見聖人憂世之心，果不得已也。

書
恭黙思道，夢帝賚予良弼。
張合

同考試官訓導詹批：高宗中興事業，都在恭黙思道上。此篇極其形容，渾雄偉麗，無不有之，録以爲學書者法。
考試官教諭周批：發明傳意，略無費辭，佳作也。
考試官學正季批：意圓詞贍，程式之文也。

極圖治之誠，感輔治之兆，賢王自敘之辭也。夫天人相與之際微矣，賢王圖治甚誠，而得賢甚異，感應之理有如是哉！昔高宗因羣臣之諫，故作書喻在己之意，若曰：「表正四方，固予之責，不
translation_en:
…of any benefit. Alas! If everyone understood this principle, the sixty-four hexagrams of the Changes would themselves suffice; what need would there be for such elaborate explanations? Here we see that the sage’s concern for the world truly left him no alternative.

Book of Documents
“Reverently and silently I pondered the Way; in a dream the Lord on High bestowed upon me an excellent assistant.”
Zhang He

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: “Gaozong’s achievement in restoring his dynasty rested entirely upon reverently and silently pondering the Way. This essay depicts that to the fullest: unity, vigor, grandeur, and elegance are all present. It is recorded as a model for those studying the Documents.”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “It elucidates the meaning of the commentary without a single superfluous expression. An excellent work.”

Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: “Its thought is rounded and its language ample: an exemplary essay.”

To bring sincerity in seeking good government to its utmost, and thereby evoke an omen of assistance in governing—these are the words in which a worthy king recounts his own experience. How subtle is the juncture at which Heaven and humanity interact! The worthy king was profoundly sincere in seeking good government, and the way he obtained a worthy assistant was extraordinary indeed. Such is the principle of stimulus and response!

Formerly, in response to the remonstrances of his assembled ministers, Gaozong composed a written statement to explain his intentions, as if to say: “To serve as a model and rectify the four quarters is indeed my responsibility; not …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
肖先德尤予之懼顧敢易言乎由是斂此身於
整齊嚴肅之中凝神淵默而沉思之不已囿此
身於齊莊恭敬之內戒謹隱微而致念之不忘
如何而可以飭百官如何而可以統萬民凡爲
治道之圖者反覆思惟如有不及而孜孜法祖
之心亦甚切焉如何而可以正宫闈如何而可
以馭四夷凡爲化理之計者往來念慮若有不
逮而拳拳憲天之念亦甚急焉夫惟望治之心
有甚於饑渴故得賢之兆有感於夢寐予當蘧
===
蘧然氣定之時精神感召儼然上帝以良弼而
授我焉栩栩然神遊之表意氣招來宛乎上帝
以賢佐而賚予焉想像之真戀慕恒切雖未見
焉將欲物色以求之也庶輔弼有資而圖治法
祖之心可少慰乎思賢之極景慕何深雖未接
焉將欲弓旌以招之也庶賛襄有賴而思治憲
天之念可少紓乎夫惟賢王求治之心誠故上
天錫賢之事異如此宜自叙之以爲羣臣告也
與雖然君臣相遇自古爲難也商造中微賢人
punctuated: 肖先德尤予之懼，顧敢易言乎？由是斂此身於整齊嚴肅之中，凝神淵默而沉思之不已；囿此身於齊莊恭敬之內，戒謹隱微而致念之不忘。如何而可以飭百官？如何而可以統萬民？凡爲治道之圖者，反覆思惟，如有不及，而孜孜法祖之心亦甚切焉。如何而可以正宫闈？如何而可以馭四夷？凡爲化理之計者，往來念慮，若有不逮，而拳拳憲天之念亦甚急焉。夫惟望治之心有甚於饑渴，故得賢之兆有感於夢寐。予當蘧蘧然氣定之時，精神感召，儼然上帝以良弼而授我焉；栩栩然神遊之表，意氣招來，宛乎上帝以賢佐而賚予焉。想像之真，戀慕恒切，雖未見焉，將欲物色以求之也。庶輔弼有資，而圖治法祖之心可少慰乎？思賢之極，景慕何深，雖未接焉，將欲弓旌以招之也。庶賛襄有賴，而思治憲天之念可少紓乎？夫惟賢王求治之心誠，故上天錫賢之事異如此，宜自叙之以爲羣臣告也與！雖然，君臣相遇，自古爲難也。商造中微，賢人
translation_en:
…to fall short of my forebears’ virtue is what I fear most. How could I dare speak lightly of it? Thus I composed myself in orderliness and solemnity, concentrating my spirit in profound silence and pondering without cease. I held myself within the bounds of dignity and reverence, remaining watchful and cautious even in what was hidden and imperceptible, never letting my attention lapse. How could I bring the hundred officials into proper order? How could I govern the myriad people? I repeatedly pondered every design for good government, as though I might fall short; and my diligent resolve to emulate my ancestors was intensely earnest. How could I set the inner palace in order? How could I control the peoples of the four quarters? I turned over every plan for transforming and governing the realm, as though my efforts might prove inadequate; and my devoted desire to take Heaven as my model was intensely urgent.

Because my longing for good government surpassed hunger and thirst, a portent of obtaining a worthy man came in response during my dreams. When my vital energies were settled and I became aware, my concentrated spirit elicited a response: it was distinctly as though the Lord on High presented me with an excellent counselor. In the vivid realm of my spirit’s wandering, my thoughts and vital energies summoned a response: it was just as though the Lord on High bestowed upon me a worthy assistant. So true was the image, and so constant and earnest my longing, that although I had not yet seen him, I intended to search for him by his appearance. Might I thus obtain the help of a counselor, and find some comfort for my desire to achieve good government and emulate my ancestors? My thoughts of this worthy man were intense, and my admiration profound. Although I had not yet met him, I intended to summon him with bow and banner, the tokens for inviting worthy men to service. Might I thus have someone upon whose assistance I could rely, and find some relief for my desire for good government and to take Heaven as my model?

It was precisely because the worthy king’s desire for good government was sincere that Heaven’s bestowal of a worthy man was so extraordinary. Surely it was fitting that he should recount this himself to inform his assembled ministers! Nevertheless, for ruler and minister to find one another has been difficult since antiquity. The fortunes of the Shang had declined midway through the dynasty, and the worthy man…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
在下傅巖之築所謂若將終身焉者高宗帝賚
之辭其事若跡亦異矣豈賢人之生固自不偶
邪卒之舟楫霖雨麴糵鹽梅之喻致乎中興之
功則夫帝賚之事夫豈偶然之故哉噫湯以伊
尹而開基高宗以傅說而再造後先一轍抑所
謂上下交而德業成者歟
宅乃事宅乃牧宅乃準茲惟后矣
龔瑀
同考試官訓導詹批說周公述夏臣告
===
君之言以戒其君意首尾明盡而
辭莊氣裕有亹亹之風即子之言
他日所用將無疑於子矣
考試官教諭周批書義要如此作
考試官學正季批明贍可誦是好文
字
克安大臣之位斯盡大君之實蓋大臣之位未
易得其安也今既有以安之人君之實有不盡
乎夏臣敘之以告其君其知恤也何如哉且其
punctuated:
在下，傅巖之築，所謂若將終身焉者。高宗帝賚之辭，其事若跡亦異矣。豈賢人之生固自不偶邪？卒之舟楫、霖雨、麴糵、鹽梅之喻，致乎中興之功，則夫帝賚之事，夫豈偶然之故哉？噫！湯以伊尹而開基，高宗以傅說而再造，後先一轍，抑所謂上下交而德業成者歟？
宅乃事，宅乃牧，宅乃準，茲惟后矣。
龔瑀
同考試官訓導詹批：說周公述夏臣告君之言以戒其君意，首尾明盡，而辭莊氣裕，有亹亹之風。即子之言，他日所用，將無疑於子矣。
考試官教諭周批：書義要如此作。
考試官學正季批：明贍可誦，是好文字。
克安大臣之位，斯盡大君之實。蓋大臣之位未易得其安也。今既有以安之，人君之實有不盡乎？夏臣敘之以告其君，其知恤也何如哉！且其
translation_en:
…remained in a humble station, building walls at Fuyan, seemingly prepared to spend his entire life there. Gaozong spoke of Heaven’s bestowing a worthy upon him: both the event and its manifestations were extraordinary. Could it be that worthy men are born destined to find no suitable opportunity? In the end, the metaphors of boats and oars, timely rain, yeast and ferment, and salt and plums found fulfillment in the achievement of dynastic restoration. How, then, could Heaven’s bestowal have been mere chance? Ah! Tang established the dynasty’s foundations with Yi Yin, and Gaozong rebuilt it with Fu Yue. Earlier and later, they followed the same course. Is this not what is meant by superiors and inferiors joining together to accomplish virtuous deeds?
“Set in their proper places your administrators, your governors, and your officers of justice: herein lies being a sovereign.”
Gong Yu
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: The explanation of how the Duke of Zhou recounted a Xia minister’s admonition to his ruler in order to warn his own ruler is clear and exhaustive from beginning to end. The language is dignified, its spirit ample and unhurried, and it has a quality of sustained earnestness. Judging by your words, there will be no doubt about you when you are employed in the future.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: This is how an essay interpreting the Book of Documents should be written.
Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: Clear, rich, and worthy of recitation: this is fine writing.
Only by properly settling the positions of the great ministers can one fully realize the substance of being a great sovereign. For it is no easy matter to settle the positions of the great ministers properly. Once there is a means of doing so, could the true responsibilities of the ruler remain unfulfilled? A minister of Xia set this forth to admonish his ruler. How deeply he understood what called for concern! Moreover, his…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
意以為三宅之官職任既非羣臣之比關係實
為君道之重可不度德以定其位乎是故王之
所與共治天事者有常任焉必其有猷有為足
以剸繁而治劇不愆不忘足以立綱而正紀信
乎其宅乃事矣所與共子天民者有牧夫焉必
其引養引恬為萬姓之歸𡌨克長克君稱斯民
之父母信乎其宅乃牧矣以至準人則與王共
守天法者也務使惟明惟允克種德而民乃依
以簡以寬惟好生而人不犯準亦無不宅焉是
===
則才德之美固各稱其所居信任之專俾各展
其所蘊矣夫然後君人之實斯無負也蓋君道
莫重於理物事既宅則百揆時敘帝載有用熙
之美庶績其凝天工著寅亮之休君人之責不
於是乎塞耶君道有在於安民牧既宅則本以
固邦以寧四方成寵綏之治德惟迪功惟敘四
海訖聲教之同君人之道不於是而盡耶以至
慎罰又人君之所貴也既宅乃準焉則惟察惟
法元命自作足以副配享之實有倫有要天威
punctuated:
意以為三宅之官，職任既非羣臣之比，關係實為君道之重，可不度德以定其位乎？是故王之所與共治天事者，有常任焉，必其有猷有為，足以剸繁而治劇；不愆不忘，足以立綱而正紀，信乎其宅乃事矣。所與共子天民者，有牧夫焉，必其引養引恬，為萬姓之歸𡌨；克長克君，稱斯民之父母，信乎其宅乃牧矣。以至準人，則與王共守天法者也，務使惟明惟允，克種德而民乃依；以簡以寬，惟好生而人不犯，準亦無不宅焉。是則才德之美，固各稱其所居；信任之專，俾各展其所蘊矣。
夫然後君人之實，斯無負也。蓋君道莫重於理物，事既宅，則百揆時敘，帝載有用熙之美；庶績其凝，天工著寅亮之休。君人之責，不於是乎塞耶？君道有在於安民，牧既宅，則本以固，邦以寧，四方成寵綏之治；德惟迪，功惟敘，四海訖聲教之同。君人之道，不於是而盡耶？以至慎罰，又人君之所貴也。既宅乃準焉，則惟察惟法，元命自作，足以副配享之實；有倫有要，天威
translation_en:
…their meaning was that the responsibilities of the three categories of office were unlike those of ordinary ministers: their importance bore directly upon the ruler’s Way. Could one fail to assess men’s virtue when determining their positions? Thus, among those with whom the king jointly administers Heaven’s affairs are the holders of standing appointments. They must possess plans and the ability to act, sufficient to manage complex and demanding affairs; they must neither err nor neglect their duties, so as to establish guiding principles and rectify discipline. Then they have truly been properly placed in charge of those affairs. Among those with whom he jointly nurtures Heaven’s people as his children are the governors. They must lead the people toward sustenance and tranquility, becoming a refuge for the myriad families [?]; they must be capable leaders and rulers, worthy of being called the people’s parents. Then they have truly been properly placed as governors. As for the judicial officers, they jointly uphold Heaven’s laws with the king. They must be discerning and impartial, able to cultivate virtue so that the people rely upon them; through simplicity and leniency, cherishing life, they must ensure that people do not transgress. Then the judicial offices, too, are all properly filled. Thus each man’s fine talents and virtues suit the position he occupies, while the undivided trust placed in each enables him to bring forth all that he possesses.
Only then will the substantive duties of ruling others have been fulfilled. Nothing in the ruler’s Way is more important than ordering affairs. Once the offices responsible for affairs are properly filled, the hundred duties proceed in due order, and the Sovereign’s undertakings flourish splendidly; the many achievements are firmly established, and the work of Heaven displays the excellence of reverent assistance. Is the responsibility of ruling others not thereby discharged? The ruler’s Way also lies in bringing peace to the people. Once the governors are properly placed, the foundation is secured and the state made tranquil, and government that cherishes and pacifies the people is accomplished throughout the land. Virtue is put into practice and achievements are duly ordered, until all within the four seas share the same moral instruction. Is the Way of ruling others not thereby fulfilled? Caution in punishment, moreover, is something the ruler prizes. Once the judicial officers are properly placed, discernment and adherence to law prevail, and the great mandate is secured through one’s own actions, sufficiently fulfilling what is required to share in the sacrificial offerings. There are ordered principles and essentials, and Heaven’s awe-inspiring authority…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
具嚴足以致敬事之誠君道又不於是而盡哉
是則非徒崇高富貴之爲尊而且憂恤擇任之
有道矣有夏人臣教君之敬如此周公舉以爲
成王戒非其忠愛之拳拳能若是耶我儀圖之
夏后之籲俊求盡事天之實耳此其臣之致敬
致告要亦皆以任賢事天爲君人之實猶之商
之丕釐周之敬事皆此意也然羣賢和朝固三
代有道之長而其要在專擇百官有司之長此
周公立政一篇前乎此以常伯常任準人爲言
===
後乎此以三宅三俊三事常事司牧獄愼有司
爲訓鄭重丁寧不一而足蓋深知爲君之實端
在是矣孔子曰爲政在人朱子曰人主以論相
爲職其亦有得於是也夫後之告君者尚其鑒
諸
詩
樂只君子德音是茂
李元陽
同考試官學正方 批南山一題乃美與
punctuated:
具嚴，足以致敬事之誠，君道又不於是而盡哉？是則非徒崇高富貴之爲尊，而且憂恤擇任之有道矣。有夏人臣教君之敬如此，周公舉以爲成王戒，非其忠愛之拳拳，能若是耶？我儀圖之，夏后之籲俊，求盡事天之實耳。此其臣之致敬致告，要亦皆以任賢事天爲君人之實，猶之商之丕釐、周之敬事，皆此意也。然羣賢和朝，固三代有道之長，而其要在專擇百官有司之長。此周公《立政》一篇，前乎此以常伯、常任、準人爲言，後乎此以三宅、三俊、三事、常事、司牧、獄、愼有司爲訓，鄭重丁寧，不一而足，蓋深知爲君之實端在是矣。孔子曰：「爲政在人。」朱子曰：「人主以論相爲職。」其亦有得於是也夫！後之告君者，尚其鑒諸！
詩
樂只君子，德音是茂。
李元陽
同考試官學正方批：南山一題，乃美與
translation_en:
…is fully awe-inspiring, sufficient to express the sincerity of reverent service. Is not the ruler’s Way thereby fully realized? Thus, his dignity consists not merely in exalted station, wealth, and honor: there is also a proper way to show anxious concern and to select men for office. Such was the reverence that the ministers of Xia taught their ruler. The Duke of Zhou cited it as an admonition to King Cheng. Could he have done so without his earnest loyalty and affection? As I consider this [?], the Xia sovereign’s summoning of outstanding men sought only to fulfill the substance of serving Heaven. His ministers’ reverent admonitions likewise took appointing the worthy and serving Heaven as the substance of rulership. The Shang’s great ordering of affairs and the Zhou’s reverent service shared this same meaning.
Yet although the assembled worthy men bringing harmony to court were indeed a strength of the well-governed Three Dynasties, the essential point lay in concentrating on the selection of heads for the various offices and agencies. Thus, in the Duke of Zhou’s Establishing Government, the earlier passage speaks of the standing chiefs, standing officeholders, and officers of justice; the later passage offers instruction concerning the three positions, the three outstanding men, the three kinds of affairs, regular duties, those who govern the people, judicial affairs, and care in appointing responsible officers. His solemn, repeated injunctions were too numerous to enumerate, for he understood deeply that the substance of rulership lay precisely here. Confucius said, “The practice of government depends on men.” Master Zhu said, “The ruler’s duty is to assess chief ministers.” Surely they too grasped this principle! May those who subsequently offer counsel to rulers take this as their guide!
Book of Odes
“Joyful is the noble gentleman; flourishing is his virtuous reputation.”
Li Yuanyang
Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “The topic from ‘Nanshan’ praises those participating in …”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
燕之賓其旨明甚場中作者率以
常語牽合雖多無取也此篇詞氣
舂容豐而不贅善說詩者耳置之
魁選可為得人賀矣
考試官教諭周批文字峻整佳作也
考試官學正季批寫主人尊賓意千
載如見可以為式矣
詩人美與燕之賓著名譽之盛也甚矣名實相
副之難也今與燕之賓而著聲譽之隆謂非斯
===
名稱情者能然哉此亦燕饗通用之樂道達主
人尊賓之意謂夫君子人與以有事而戾止邦
畿以令德而作賓王家昔焉遠處封邦容止不
可即矣今登筵之始而從容氣象宛乎其可親
向焉各居封守威儀不可見矣今即席之初豈
弟威儀溫乎其可即徘徊于尊俎之間嚴而泰
焉使人心乎愛矣而不忘何樂只耶遨遊於獻
酬之頃和而節焉使人中心好之而不已何樂
易耶不寧惟是且其德有可稱脩身樂善而成
punctuated:
燕之賓，其旨明甚。場中作者率以常語牽合，雖多無取也。此篇詞氣舂容，豐而不贅，善說詩者耳。置之魁選，可為得人賀矣。
考試官教諭周批：文字峻整，佳作也。
考試官學正季批：寫主人尊賓意，千載如見，可以為式矣。
詩人美與燕之賓，著名譽之盛也。甚矣，名實相副之難也！今與燕之賓而著聲譽之隆，謂非斯名稱情者能然哉？此亦燕饗通用之樂，道達主人尊賓之意。謂夫君子，人與以有事而戾止邦畿，以令德而作賓王家。昔焉遠處封邦，容止不可即矣；今登筵之始，而從容氣象宛乎其可親。向焉各居封守，威儀不可見矣；今即席之初，豈弟威儀溫乎其可即。徘徊于尊俎之間，嚴而泰焉，使人心乎愛矣而不忘，何樂只耶！遨遊於獻酬之頃，和而節焉，使人中心好之而不已，何樂易耶！不寧惟是，且其德有可稱，脩身樂善而成
translation_en:
…the guests participating in the banquet: its meaning is perfectly clear. Most candidates in the examination hall forced commonplace expressions to fit the topic; numerous though their compositions were, they offered nothing worth selecting. This essay is unhurried and ample in its diction and spirit, rich without being redundant—the work of someone skilled at explaining the Odes. Placing it first among the selected essays gives us cause to congratulate ourselves on having found a worthy man.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The writing is vigorous and well ordered. An excellent composition.”
Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: “It portrays the host’s intention to honor his guests so vividly that, after a thousand years, we seem to see it before us. It may serve as a model.”
The poet praises the guests participating in the banquet and displays the splendor of their reputation. How difficult it is for reputation and reality to correspond! Now these guests at the banquet are shown enjoying an exalted reputation: could this be so unless that reputation matched their true character? This is also music used generally at banquets and sacrificial feasts, conveying the host’s intention to honor his guests. It speaks of those noble men who, being entrusted by others with affairs [?], arrive in the royal domain and, by virtue of their excellent character, become guests of the royal house. Formerly, dwelling far away in their enfeoffed states, they could not be approached to observe their bearing; now, as they first ascend to the banquet, their composed demeanor seems vividly approachable. Previously, each dwelling within his own appointed territory, their dignified deportment could not be seen; now, as they first take their seats, their amiable bearing is warm and welcoming.
