Moving among the wine vessels and sacrificial stands, they are dignified yet at ease, making others love them in their hearts and never forget them. How joyful they are! Mingling as cups are offered and returned, they are harmonious yet restrained, making others cherish them in their hearts without cease. How cheerful and easy they are! Nor is this all: their virtue, moreover, deserves praise; they cultivate themselves, delight in goodness, and bring about…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
積中發外之美善有可名制節謹度而無自用
自專之失由是流而爲聲譽之芳允偉乎甚大
王畿知之侯國知之或内或外皆濯濯厥聲之
孔昭也德音信乎其茂矣豈直不已而已哉播
而爲聲聞之美猶浩乎孔博圻甸聞之要荒聞
之在朝在野一憲憲令名之洋溢也徽音允乎
其盛矣奚但不已而已哉是則非臣之賢無以
得君之懽心非君之明無以知臣之令德有周
燕饗一行而君臣相與相得如此此所以爲明
===
良之會也與大抵君臣之賢否關於氣運之盛
衰盛則治隆於上俗美於下手足腹心相待一
體否則恩禮衰薄將國人視之而已安望其共
成光明俊偉之治哉後世稱盛治者謂泰和在
成周予於此言益信
帝命式于九圍
張𨯤
同考試官學正方批題本明白而場中
作者不纏繞無歸著則渙散無意
punctuated:
積中發外之美，善有可名，制節謹度而無自用自專之失。由是流而爲聲譽之芳，允偉乎甚大！王畿知之，侯國知之，或内或外，皆濯濯厥聲之孔昭也。德音信乎其茂矣，豈直不已而已哉？播而爲聲聞之美，猶浩乎孔博！圻甸聞之，要荒聞之，在朝在野，一憲憲令名之洋溢也。徽音允乎其盛矣，奚但不已而已哉？是則非臣之賢，無以得君之懽心；非君之明，無以知臣之令德。有周燕饗一行，而君臣相與相得如此，此所以爲明良之會也與！大抵君臣之賢否，關於氣運之盛衰。盛則治隆於上，俗美於下，手足腹心，相待一體；否則恩禮衰薄，將國人視之而已，安望其共成光明俊偉之治哉？後世稱盛治者，謂泰和在成周，予於此言益信。

帝命式于九圍
張𨯤

同考試官學正方批：題本明白，而場中作者，不纏繞無歸著，則渙散無意
translation_en:
…the beauty of what accumulates within and manifests itself outwardly. Their goodness merits praise: they regulate their conduct and carefully observe proper measures, without the faults of self-willed or arbitrary action. From this flows the fragrance of their reputation—truly magnificent and great! The royal domain knows it; the feudatory states know it. Within and without, everywhere their reputation shines with brilliant clarity. Their renown for virtue is indeed flourishing: how could one say merely that it does not cease? It spreads as a fine reputation, vast indeed in its reach! The territories surrounding the capital hear of it; the distant and outlying regions hear of it. At court and in the countryside alike, their illustrious good name spreads everywhere. Their excellent reputation is truly abundant: how could one say merely that it does not cease?

Thus, without worthy ministers, the ruler’s pleasure could not be won; without an enlightened ruler, the ministers’ excellent virtue could not be recognized. When the Zhou held a court banquet, ruler and ministers associated in such mutual harmony. This is what made it a meeting of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers! Generally, whether ruler and ministers are worthy or otherwise bears upon the flourishing or decline of the fortunes of the age. When these flourish, government prospers above and customs are fine below; like hands and feet, belly and heart, they depend upon one another as parts of a single body. Otherwise, favor and ritual courtesy dwindle, and they regard one another merely as fellow countrymen. How could one hope that together they would achieve a splendid and outstanding government? Later generations, speaking of flourishing government, have said that supreme harmony prevailed in the Zhou at its height. My confidence in this saying is all the greater.

“The Lord on High commanded him to serve as a model to the Nine Regions.”
Zhang 𨯤 [given-name reading uncertain].

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, School Instructor: The topic is itself clear, yet those writing in the examination hall either become entangled and arrive at no definite point, or are diffuse and lack meaning…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
味令人厭觀既得此卷讀之殊為
快心豁目取之
考試官教諭周批商頌盛德形容之
意此作發之以滂沛而不淫決善
于作頌義者也
考試官學正季批以莊整之辭發脩
敬之德佳作也允稱高薦
詩人頌天眷聖君為法於天下其必有以致之
矣夫天命未易得也聖君所以膺天眷而法天
===
下者謂非一敬致之哉此商人祫祭之詩推本
成湯受命之由蓋謂有商之業雖基於玄王實
成於烈祖烈祖之敬既格乎天心天下之命孰
有外之者哉是故夏失其道天心厭之乆矣昭
假我祖之敬赫然駿命之攸歸政失其平天心
惡之素矣降鑒我祖之德昭然景命之有僕使
之宅中土而聽治焉皇極於此乎建也命之奄
六合以為家焉人紀於是乎脩也作之君作之
師荆梁雍豫無人而不歸於範圍之中賞而慶
punctuated:
味，令人厭觀。既得此卷，讀之殊為快心豁目，取之。
考試官教諭周批：商頌盛德形容之意，此作發之以滂沛而不淫決，善于作頌義者也。
考試官學正季批：以莊整之辭發脩敬之德，佳作也，允稱高薦。
詩人頌天眷聖君，為法於天下，其必有以致之矣。夫天命未易得也，聖君所以膺天眷而法天下者，謂非一敬致之哉？此商人祫祭之詩，推本成湯受命之由，蓋謂有商之業雖基於玄王，實成於烈祖。烈祖之敬既格乎天心，天下之命孰有外之者哉？是故夏失其道，天心厭之乆矣；昭假我祖之敬，赫然駿命之攸歸。政失其平，天心惡之素矣；降鑒我祖之德，昭然景命之有僕。使之宅中土而聽治焉，皇極於此乎建也；命之奄六合以為家焉，人紀於是乎脩也。作之君，作之師，荆梁雍豫，無人而不歸於範圍之中；賞而慶
translation_en:
…flavor, making them tiresome to read. When I obtained this paper, reading it especially delighted my heart and opened my eyes. I selected it.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: This composition develops the intent of the Hymns of Shang to portray flourishing virtue, with an abundant flow that never spills over its bounds. Its author is skilled in composing expositions of the hymns’ meaning.
Examiner Ji, Assistant Instructor, comments: With dignified and orderly language, it brings out the virtue of cultivated reverence. An excellent composition, truly deserving a high recommendation.
The poet praises Heaven’s favor toward the sage ruler, who serves as a model for all under Heaven: surely there must have been something that brought this about. Heaven’s mandate is not easily obtained. Could it be said that anything other than reverence alone enabled the sage ruler to receive Heaven’s favor and serve as a model for all under Heaven? This poem for the Shang joint ancestral sacrifice traces back the reason Cheng Tang received the mandate. Its meaning is that although the enterprise of Shang was founded upon the Mysterious King, it was brought to fulfillment by the Illustrious Ancestor. Once the Illustrious Ancestor’s reverence had reached Heaven’s heart, whose allotted destiny under Heaven could lie outside his sway?
Thus, when Xia lost its Way, Heaven’s heart had long been weary of it. Our ancestor’s reverence reached Heaven in its radiance, and the great mandate turned resplendently toward him. When government lost its equity, Heaven’s heart had long abhorred it. Heaven looked down upon our ancestor’s virtue, and the glorious mandate plainly settled upon him. Heaven caused him to dwell in the central lands and attend to government; thereby the august standard was established. It commanded him to possess all within the six directions as his household; thereby the ordering principles of human relations were cultivated. It made him ruler and made him teacher: in Jing, Liang, Yong, and Yu, no one failed to come within his guiding bounds. He bestowed rewards and honors…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
刑而威冀兗青徐揚何者而不在於甄陶之內
以祖之敬而回威侮之習九圍之大皆欲其成
式矣豈復小國是達而已哉以祖之德而清怠
棄之源萬邦之廣皆欲其取正矣豈止大國是
達而已哉是則湯之王業上承先世長發之祥
下啓後世無窮之祚皆本於一敬之得天也宗
廟以是美盛德而告成功有由矣夫大抵敬者
得天人之本也堯以欽明而膺萬邦之命舜以
溫恭而紹曆數之傳禹祗台文敬止武敬勝得
===
天得人皆是物也所謂克敬惟親惟德是輔書
之言豈欺我哉
春秋
公敗齊師于長勺莊公十年 公會齊侯
盟于柯莊公十有三年
呂鳳池
考試官教諭周 批深得傳旨
考試官學正季 批齊魯構怨釋怨予
奪繫焉此篇融徹傳意馳驟頓挫
punctuated:
刑而威，冀兗青徐揚，何者而不在於甄陶之內？以祖之敬而回威侮之習，九圍之大皆欲其成式矣，豈復小國是達而已哉？以祖之德而清怠棄之源，萬邦之廣皆欲其取正矣，豈止大國是達而已哉？是則湯之王業，上承先世長發之祥，下啓後世無窮之祚，皆本於一敬之得天也。宗廟以是美盛德而告成功，有由矣夫！大抵敬者，得天人之本也。堯以欽明而膺萬邦之命，舜以溫恭而紹曆數之傳，禹祗台，文敬止，武敬勝，得天得人，皆是物也。所謂「克敬惟親，惟德是輔」，書之言豈欺我哉？

春秋
公敗齊師于長勺，莊公十年。公會齊侯盟于柯，莊公十有三年。
呂鳳池
考試官教諭周批：深得傳旨。
考試官學正季批：齊魯構怨、釋怨，予奪繫焉。此篇融徹傳意，馳驟頓挫，
translation_en:
…and awed them through punishment: among Ji, Yan, Qing, Xu, and Yang, which lay outside his molding influence? Through his ancestor’s reverence, he reversed the habit of oppressive arrogance, desiring that all within the vast Nine Regions take it as their model. Could this have amounted merely to reaching the smaller states? Through his ancestor’s virtue, he purged the source of indolence and neglect, desiring that the myriad states throughout their vast extent take it as their standard. Could this have amounted merely to reaching the greater states? Thus Tang’s kingly enterprise carried forward the auspicious promise that had long unfolded through earlier generations and opened the way to blessings without end for later generations. All was rooted in winning Heaven through reverence alone. There was therefore good reason for praising his abundant virtue and proclaiming his completed achievement in the ancestral temple!

In general, reverence is the foundation for winning Heaven and the people. Through his reverence and discernment, Yao received the mandate to rule the myriad states; through his gentleness and respect, Shun continued the succession of Heaven’s allotted reigns. Yu declared, “I am reverent”; King Wen rested in reverence; King Wu’s reverence prevailed. Their winning Heaven and the people all depended upon this same quality. As it is said, “It draws close only to those capable of reverence; it assists only the virtuous.” Could these words of the Book of Documents deceive us?

Spring and Autumn Annals
“The duke defeated the army of Qi at Changshao.” Tenth year of Duke Zhuang.
“The duke met the Marquis of Qi and concluded a covenant at Ke.” Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
Lü Fengchi

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “It thoroughly grasps the purport of the commentary.”

Examiner Ji, School Director, comments: “Qi and Lu’s engendering and resolving enmity are what determine the praise and blame. This essay comprehensively penetrates the meaning of the commentary, advancing at a gallop, pausing and turning…”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而不失嚴整之度末復揭雚之盟
以責魯莊向亡復讎之志尤出人
意表傑作也得子無媿賢科云
望國脩易世之怨可譏釋易世之怨可予此見
聖人惡長亂而善釋怨也觀長勺于柯之書法
可識矣思昔齊桓致脩怨之師魯莊申敵讎之
義長勺之役似所謂敵加于已不得已而應之
宜若無罪也何責耶蓋不師不陣已有明訓襄
也旣亡怨在可釋文告以諭使之不縮而退則
===
善矣夫何行登軾望轍之謀以卒幸一勝之功
用彼竭我盈之計以苟舒一朝之忿耻雖少雪
抑豈知已亂之道不急於尋兵耶故經不書齊
伐而主魯以責之意蓋如此迨夫齊桓欲爲脩
睦之舉魯莊遂締鄰國之交于柯之盟似所謂
不共戴天方再世而忘之宜若無取也何予耶
蓋敵惠敵怨不在後嗣齊桓易世鄰則當善擇
義以從使之釋憾而平則可矣況彼身任安攘
之責而摽劒之仇旣捐與國同推獎之誠而尊
punctuated:
而不失嚴整之度，末復揭雚之盟，以責魯莊向亡復讎之志，尤出人意表，傑作也。得子，無媿賢科云。
望國脩易世之怨可譏，釋易世之怨可予，此見聖人惡長亂而善釋怨也。觀長勺、于柯之書法，可識矣。思昔齊桓致脩怨之師，魯莊申敵讎之義，長勺之役，似所謂敵加于已，不得已而應之，宜若無罪也，何責耶？蓋不師不陣，已有明訓。襄也旣亡，怨在可釋，文告以諭，使之不縮而退則善矣。夫何行登軾望轍之謀，以卒幸一勝之功，用彼竭我盈之計，以苟舒一朝之忿？耻雖少雪，抑豈知已亂之道不急於尋兵耶？故經不書齊伐，而主魯以責之，意蓋如此。迨夫齊桓欲爲脩睦之舉，魯莊遂締鄰國之交，于柯之盟，似所謂不共戴天，方再世而忘之，宜若無取也，何予耶？蓋敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。齊桓易世，鄰則當善，擇義以從，使之釋憾而平則可矣。況彼身任安攘之責，而摽劒之仇旣捐，與國同推獎之誠，而尊
translation_en:
…yet without losing strictness and order. At the end, he further invokes the covenant at Guan [?] to reproach Duke Zhuang of Lu for previously lacking the resolve to avenge his wrong. This is especially unexpected: a masterly composition. With you among its successful candidates, this examination need feel no shame for the worthies it selects.
For a prominent state [?] to pursue a grievance after a change of ruler merits criticism; to relinquish such a grievance merits approval. This shows that the Sage abhors the perpetuation of disorder and commends the relinquishing of grievances. We can recognize this by examining the wording of the entries concerning Changshao and Ke. Consider how Duke Huan of Qi once brought an army to pursue a grievance, while Duke Zhuang of Lu asserted his duty to oppose an enemy. The battle at Changshao seems to exemplify the saying that, when an enemy attacks oneself, one has no choice but to respond. He should seemingly have been blameless. Why, then, is he censured? There was already a clear injunction against raising armies and drawing up battle formations for vengeance. Duke Xiang was already dead, and the grievance could be relinquished. It would have been good to explain matters through a formal proclamation and induce the enemy to withdraw without humiliation [?]. Why, instead, employ the stratagem of mounting the chariot crossbar and examining the wheel tracks, merely to secure one fortunate victory, and use the calculation that their courage was exhausted while ours was full, merely to vent a moment’s anger? Although the disgrace was somewhat effaced, did he understand that the way to end disorder does not lie in hastening to renew hostilities? Thus the Classic does not record Qi’s invasion, but makes Lu the principal actor in order to censure it. This, presumably, was its intention. Later, when Duke Huan of Qi wished to restore harmonious relations, Duke Zhuang of Lu accordingly established friendship with his neighboring state. The covenant at Ke seems a case of forgetting, after only a change of ruler, an enmity so profound that the two should not live beneath the same heaven. It should seemingly have had nothing to commend it. Why, then, is it approved? Because requiting kindness and requiting enmity do not extend to subsequent heirs. With Duke Huan, Qi had passed to a new ruler; relations with a neighbor should therefore be amicable. It was enough to choose and follow what was right, enabling him to relinquish resentment and make peace. Moreover, he personally undertook responsibility for bringing security and repelling outside threats, and had already abandoned his grievance over being threatened with a sword. The allied states shared a sincere desire to support and commend him, and to honor…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
錄
棄險而受制於內春秋之責在貳國扼險而遺
義於外春秋之責在諸侯此虎牢之城不繫鄭
其戍繫之及書楚救也鄭晋之罪無所逃矣且
虎牢鄭地也晋悼復霸從獻子之謀率會戚之
兵以城之將以逼其從巳焉爾曷爲責在鄭耶
聖人以爲制邑之險聞於天下地有所必據城
有所必守而不可棄焉者鄭也不克固守爲晋
所城門戶巳毀非復滎陽之舊封藩籬巳徹非
===
若宛陵之私屬是果世守者乎卒之君臣上下
曾無一息之寧玉帛犧牲徒爲二境之待無所
厎告然後請成誰之責歟經不繫鄭止書城虎
牢若曰鄭人土地本之君親失其所有曾黃人
之不如也其責在鄭如此者夫虎牢旣城矣悼
猶隱憂任魏絳之賢聚初駕之兵以戍之將以
守其復叛焉爾曷爲罪諸侯耶聖人以爲鄭人
從楚固云不義無乃於巳有關亦當在內自省
而不可脅焉者晋也不自省躬伐而復戍非欲
punctuated:
錄

棄險而受制於內，春秋之責在貳國；扼險而遺義於外，春秋之責在諸侯。此虎牢之城不繫鄭，其戍繫之，及書楚救也，鄭晋之罪無所逃矣。且虎牢，鄭地也。晋悼復霸，從獻子之謀，率會戚之兵以城之，將以逼其從巳焉爾，曷爲責在鄭耶？聖人以爲制邑之險聞於天下，地有所必據，城有所必守，而不可棄焉者，鄭也。不克固守，爲晋所城，門戶巳毀，非復滎陽之舊封；藩籬巳徹，非若宛陵之私屬。是果世守者乎？卒之君臣上下，曾無一息之寧，玉帛犧牲徒爲二境之待，無所厎告，然後請成，誰之責歟？經不繫鄭，止書城虎牢，若曰：鄭人土地本之君親，失其所有，曾黃人之不如也。其責在鄭如此者。

夫虎牢旣城矣，悼猶隱憂，任魏絳之賢，聚初駕之兵以戍之，將以守其復叛焉爾，曷爲罪諸侯耶？聖人以爲鄭人從楚固云不義，無乃於巳有關，亦當在內自省，而不可脅焉者，晋也。不自省躬，伐而復戍，非欲
translation_en:
Record

When a state abandons its strategic defenses and submits to control within its own territory, the Spring and Autumn Annals lays blame upon that state for its wavering allegiance; when the feudal lords occupy strategic defenses and disregard righteousness in their external dealings, the Annals lays blame upon them. Thus, in recording the fortification of Hulao, it does not identify the place as belonging to Zheng; in recording its garrisoning, it does, and it also records Chu’s rescue. The culpability of Zheng and Jin therefore cannot escape notice.

Now Hulao was Zheng territory. When Duke Dao of Jin restored his hegemony, he followed Xianzi’s plan and led the troops assembled at Qi to fortify it, intending merely to compel Zheng’s submission. Why, then, does the blame lie with Zheng? The Sage considered the strategic strength of Zhi to be renowned throughout the realm: Zheng had ground that it must occupy and fortifications that it must defend and could not abandon. Yet it failed to hold them firmly, allowing Jin to fortify the place. Its gateway was already destroyed: this was no longer its old domain at Xingyang. Its protective barriers were already removed: this was no longer like its own possession at Wanling. Was this truly the way to preserve an inheritance through the generations? In the end, ruler and ministers, high and low, enjoyed not a moment’s peace. Their jade, silks, and sacrificial animals served merely to make provision for the two neighboring powers [?]. With nowhere to turn for redress, they then sued for peace. Whose responsibility was this? The Classic does not identify the place as belonging to Zheng, but simply records, “Fortified Hulao.” It is as though it says: “The people of Zheng received their lands from their rulers and forebears, yet lost what they possessed; they were not even the equals of the people of Huang.” Such is the blame it places upon Zheng.

Once Hulao had been fortified, Duke Dao still harbored anxieties. He entrusted the task to the worthy Wei Jiang and assembled the troops of his first expedition [?] to garrison it, intending merely to guard against Zheng’s renewed rebellion. Why, then, does the text condemn the feudal lords? The Sage considered that, although Zheng’s adherence to Chu could indeed be called unrighteous, might this not also have something to do with Jin itself? Jin ought also to have examined itself inwardly, and ought not to have resorted to coercion. Instead of examining its own conduct, it attacked and then stationed a garrison; its intention was not to…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
斷荆楚之路以爲鄭蔽仍欲踵前城之志而迫
其求成是果義服者乎已而楚共得聞卽投袂
而起子囊往救遂夾潁而軍事雖假義師則有
名誰之罪歟經繫之鄭又書楚救若曰列國分
地受諸天子肆其凌逼曾荆楚之不若也其罪
諸侯如此者吁責棄險者家天下之心罪扼險
者明王制之意聖人維持世道其所感深矣雖
然鄭之棄華卽夷無足道者悼於三駕之餘推
至誠以待人鄭自此不復叛而楚竟不能爭休
===
兵息民當世有賴嗚呼悼亦賢君也哉
禮記
五者備當上帝其饗
王璠
同考試官訓導張 批備當字作者殊欠
體認此篇發揮眞切筆力蒼然禮
經之冠也錄之
考試官教諭周 批典雅文字適有此
篇
punctuated:
斷荆楚之路，以爲鄭蔽，仍欲踵前城之志而迫其求成，是果義服者乎？已而楚共得聞，卽投袂而起，子囊往救，遂夾潁而軍。事雖假義，師則有名，誰之罪歟？經繫之鄭，又書楚救，若曰：列國分地，受諸天子，肆其凌逼，曾荆楚之不若也。其罪諸侯如此者。吁！責棄險者，家天下之心；罪扼險者，明王制之意。聖人維持世道，其所感深矣！雖然，鄭之棄華卽夷，無足道者。悼於三駕之餘，推至誠以待人，鄭自此不復叛，而楚竟不能爭。休兵息民，當世有賴。嗚呼！悼亦賢君也哉！

禮記
五者備當，上帝其饗。
王璠

同考試官訓導張批：備當字，作者殊欠體認。此篇發揮眞切，筆力蒼然，禮經之冠也，錄之。

考試官教諭周批：典雅文字，適有此篇。
translation_en:
…to cut off the route from Jing-Chu and provide a protective barrier for Zheng, but still wished to pursue the purpose of the earlier fortification and compel Zheng to seek peace. Was this truly securing submission through righteousness? Soon afterward, Duke Gong of Chu heard of this and immediately sprang up, flinging back his sleeves. Zinang went to the rescue, and the armies encamped on opposite sides of the Ying River. Although righteousness was only a pretext for this undertaking, the army had a legitimate cause. Whose fault was this? The Classic identifies the place as belonging to Zheng and also records that Chu came to its rescue. It is as though it says: “The territories allotted to the various states were received from the Son of Heaven. By wantonly bullying and coercing another state, they fell below even Jing-Chu.” Such is its condemnation of the feudal lords.

Ah! In censuring those who abandon defensible terrain, it expresses the concern that treats all under Heaven as one family; in condemning those who seize such terrain to constrain others, it expresses the intention to make clear the royal institutions. Profound indeed was the Sage’s concern in sustaining the moral order of the world! Nevertheless, Zheng’s abandonment of the Chinese states to join the barbarians deserves no praise. After his three campaigns, Duke Dao treated others with the utmost sincerity. From that time onward, Zheng did not rebel again, and Chu ultimately could not contend with him. He halted warfare and gave the people respite, benefiting his age. Ah! Duke Dao, too, was indeed a worthy ruler!

Record of Rites
“When the five things are complete and appropriate, the Lord on High will receive the offering.”
Wang Fan

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: “Writers show a marked lack of understanding of the words ‘complete and appropriate.’ This essay expounds them with authenticity and precision, and its writing has mature strength. It is the finest of the essays on the Classic of Rites. Let it be included.”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “For refined and elegant writing, here is precisely such an essay.”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正季批明淨可錄
物之備者既宜神之尊者必格夫莫尊於天之
帝也於祭物而備且當焉寧不有以來其格哉
記月令者之言如此且禮莫重於祭祭必備乎
物先王於仲秋命宰祝之官供循行之職至此
以為犧牲不備不敢祭也今既於全具於芻豢
有以視之按之而不失於肥瘠於物色有以瞻
之察之而無遺而又於小大長短在所必量是
其於五者無不備焉然備而不當猶不備也今
===
則所視所按者合乎事之程式而無不善所瞻
所察者當於事之倫類而無不宜而與夫所量
者亦中其度是又於備也無不當焉夫然則備
物之敬隆而報本之誠竭殆見皇天上帝雖至
遠也感吾敬之潜孚且將來享於冥冥之中矣
況羣神之近者有不享乎雖至尊也鑒吾誠之
默契且將來格於洋洋之表矣矧羣神之卑者
有不格乎所以致風雨之節在是所以致寒暑
之時在是夫一祭牲之備而來天神之格如此
punctuated:
考試官學正季批：明淨可錄。

物之備者既宜，神之尊者必格。夫莫尊於天之帝也，於祭物而備且當焉，寧不有以來其格哉？記月令者之言如此。且禮莫重於祭，祭必備乎物。先王於仲秋命宰祝之官供循行之職，至此以為犧牲不備，不敢祭也。今既於全具於芻豢，有以視之按之，而不失於肥瘠；於物色，有以瞻之察之，而無遺；而又於小大長短，在所必量。是其於五者無不備焉。然備而不當，猶不備也。今則所視所按者，合乎事之程式而無不善；所瞻所察者，當於事之倫類而無不宜；而與夫所量者，亦中其度。是又於備也無不當焉。夫然則備物之敬隆，而報本之誠竭。殆見皇天上帝雖至遠也，感吾敬之潜孚，且將來享於冥冥之中矣。況羣神之近者，有不享乎？雖至尊也，鑒吾誠之默契，且將來格於洋洋之表矣。矧羣神之卑者，有不格乎？所以致風雨之節在是，所以致寒暑之時在是。夫一祭牲之備，而來天神之格如此
translation_en:
Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: “Clear and lucid; worthy of inclusion.”

When the full complement of offerings is fittingly prepared, the most exalted spirit will surely draw near. Nothing is more exalted than the Lord of Heaven. If the sacrificial offerings are both complete and appropriate, could they fail to bring about his arrival? Such is the meaning of the words of the author of the Monthly Ordinances.

Among rites, none is weightier than sacrifice, and sacrifice requires a full complement of offerings. In mid-autumn, the former kings commanded the officials responsible for slaughter and invocations to perform their duties of inspection. At this point, they held that they dared not sacrifice unless the sacrificial animals were fully prepared. Now, concerning their completeness and their feeding on grass and grain [?], there are means to inspect and examine them, so that their fatness or leanness is properly assessed; concerning their kinds and colors, there are means to observe and scrutinize them, so that nothing is overlooked; and their size and length must also be measured. Thus, in these five respects, nothing is lacking. Yet completeness without appropriateness is tantamount to incompleteness.

Now what is inspected and examined conforms to the prescribed procedures for the undertaking and is good in every respect; what is observed and scrutinized accords with the proper categories for the undertaking and is fitting in every respect; and what is measured likewise meets the required dimensions. Thus, everything that is complete is also appropriate. In this way, reverence expressed through preparing the offerings is exalted, and sincerity in requiting the source of life is fully realized. We may expect to see August Heaven, the Lord on High, though exceedingly distant, moved by the unseen influence of our reverence and coming to partake of the offerings amid the invisible darkness. How much more, then, will the nearer spirits partake of them! Though supremely exalted, he perceives the silent accord of our sincerity and will come and manifest his abundant presence. How much more, then, will the lesser spirits draw near! Herein lies the means of bringing wind and rain in due measure; herein lies the means of bringing cold and heat at their proper times. Thus, the full preparation of sacrificial animals for a single sacrifice brings the heavenly spirits near…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
汝之循行可不慎歟嗟乎仁人之事天也如事
親故先王於郊祭之禮獨隆然豈私其身哉凡
以為民祈福而已其敬天勤民之心何至耶他
章有曰唯聖人為能饗帝言敬之至也以此垂
教後世猶有褻天而不知事者噫
君為正則百姓從政矣
何清
同考試官訓導張批此題有關為政之
體此作寫出上下孚感底意正爾
===
可人錄之不但以其文也
考試官教諭周批辭氣詳雅讀之粲
然
考試官學正季批說得明盡非苟作
者
上能端其所行下必順其所令蓋君正莫不正
也使君有不正欲下之從其政也難矣哉昔孔
子對哀公為政之問及此意謂有國者不患乎
人心之不順而患乎吾政之未脩不患乎吾政
punctuated:
汝之循行，可不慎歟？嗟乎！仁人之事天也如事親，故先王於郊祭之禮獨隆，然豈私其身哉？凡以為民祈福而已。其敬天勤民之心何至耶！他章有曰：「唯聖人為能饗帝。」言敬之至也。以此垂教後世，猶有褻天而不知事者，噫！
君為正，則百姓從政矣。
何清
同考試官訓導張批：此題有關為政之體，此作寫出上下孚感底意，正爾可人。錄之不但以其文也。
考試官教諭周批：辭氣詳雅，讀之粲然。
考試官學正季批：說得明盡，非苟作者。
上能端其所行，下必順其所令。蓋君正，莫不正也。使君有不正，欲下之從其政也，難矣哉！昔孔子對哀公為政之問，及此，意謂有國者不患乎人心之不順，而患乎吾政之未脩；不患乎吾政
translation_en:
…Can you afford to be careless in carrying this out? Ah! The benevolent person serves Heaven as he serves his parents. Thus the former kings accorded particular solemnity to the suburban sacrifice. Yet was this for their own private benefit? It was solely to pray for blessings for the people. How profound was their devotion to revering Heaven and caring diligently for the people! Another chapter says: “Only the sage can offer sacrifice acceptably to the Lord on High.” This speaks of reverence carried to its utmost. Though this teaching was handed down to later generations, there are still those who profane Heaven and do not know how to serve it. Alas!
“When the ruler acts correctly, the common people will follow his government.”
He Qing
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: This topic concerns the essentials of governing. This composition brings out the idea of mutual trust and responsiveness between those above and those below, and is most pleasing. Its inclusion is not solely for its literary merits.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Its language and tone are full and elegant; it shines upon reading.
Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: The explanation is clear and exhaustive. This is no carelessly written composition.
If those above can make their conduct upright, those below will surely obey their commands. For when the ruler is upright, none will fail to be upright. If the ruler is not upright, how difficult it will be to expect those below to follow his government! Long ago, when Confucius answered Duke Ai’s question about governing, he touched upon this point. His meaning was that the ruler of a state should not worry that the people’s hearts are uncompliant, but should worry that his own government has not been put in order; he should not worry that his own government …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之不脩而患乎所爲之不正何則人君一身下
所則也故必敬以脩已使所爲一出於正無大
廷深宫之間也而邪佞不得以惑之道以脩身
俾所行一由於正無大德小德之踰也而儉壬
不容以間之見於刑賞焉刑所當刑賞所當賞
無偏而無黨也形於好惡焉好所當好惡所當
惡無反而無側也夫君之所爲旣無不正則表
率倡導之源以清激勸化成之本以立將見聚
廬而居凡在乎君臨者非一姓也莫不曰吾君
===
正矣吾何以不從自翕然於感化之餘而唯其
所令比閭而處凡歸乎統馭者非一人也罔不
曰吾君正矣吾何以不順自驩然於鼓舞之中
而唯其所施會極歸極順於風之偃草也梗化
者誰與遵道遵路捷於響之應聲也弗率者誰
與吁君正於上而民從之如此斯政之所以爲
政也然則人君烏可以不正耶抑論之君民一
體君以民爲體民以君爲心其所關甚重也柰
何世之爲君者徒恃崇高之位而不知正身以
punctuated: 之不脩，而患乎所爲之不正。何則？人君一身，下所則也。故必敬以脩已，使所爲一出於正，無大廷深宫之間也，而邪佞不得以惑之；道以脩身，俾所行一由於正，無大德小德之踰也，而儉壬不容以間之。見於刑賞焉，刑所當刑，賞所當賞，無偏而無黨也；形於好惡焉，好所當好，惡所當惡，無反而無側也。夫君之所爲旣無不正，則表率倡導之源以清，激勸化成之本以立。將見聚廬而居，凡在乎君臨者，非一姓也，莫不曰：「吾君正矣，吾何以不從？」自翕然於感化之餘，而唯其所令；比閭而處，凡歸乎統馭者，非一人也，罔不曰：「吾君正矣，吾何以不順？」自驩然於鼓舞之中，而唯其所施。會極歸極，順於風之偃草也，梗化者誰與？遵道遵路，捷於響之應聲也，弗率者誰與？吁！君正於上，而民從之如此，斯政之所以爲政也。然則人君烏可以不正耶？抑論之，君民一體，君以民爲體，民以君爲心，其所關甚重也。柰何世之爲君者，徒恃崇高之位，而不知正身以
translation_en: …being left uncultivated, but should worry that his own conduct is not upright. Why is this? The ruler himself is the model for those below. He must therefore cultivate himself through reverence, ensuring that everything he does proceeds from uprightness, without distinction between the great court and the inner palace, so that wicked flatterers cannot delude him. He must cultivate himself through the Way, ensuring that all his conduct follows uprightness, without transgression in either great or small matters of virtue, so that crafty men [?] cannot sow discord. When this is manifested in punishments and rewards, he punishes those who deserve punishment and rewards those who deserve reward, without partiality or factionalism. When it takes form in his likes and dislikes, he likes what deserves to be liked and dislikes what deserves to be disliked, without perversity or bias. Once nothing the ruler does is other than upright, the source of exemplary leadership is purified, and the foundation for encouragement and moral transformation is established. Then we shall see those who dwell in clustered homes—all who live under his rule, comprising many families—say without exception: “Our ruler is upright; how could we fail to follow him?” United spontaneously through his transforming influence, they heed whatever he commands. Those who dwell in adjoining neighborhoods—all who come under his governance, comprising many individuals—will all say: “Our ruler is upright; how could we fail to obey him?” Rejoicing spontaneously in his encouragement, they follow whatever measures he puts into effect. They gather at and return to the supreme standard, as readily as grass bends before the wind: who would resist transformation? They follow the Way and its paths, more swiftly than an echo answers a sound: who would fail to comply? Ah! When the ruler is upright above and the people follow him in this fashion, this is what makes government truly government. How, then, could a ruler fail to be upright? To consider it further, ruler and people form one body: the ruler takes the people as his body, and the people take the ruler as their heart. What depends upon this relationship is of the utmost importance. Why is it that rulers in this world rely solely on their exalted position, yet do not know to rectify themselves in order to…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
帥民嚴刑峻法必使從其所好無惟乎民心之
日離而亂且亡也孔子告哀公以此及其問所
以為正而答之則不出乎三綱其啓之也深矣
哀公卒不能行其言此魯之所以不競歟
第貳場
論
講學為正心之要
張合
同考試官訓導詹批今士子作論下筆
===
輒數百言率皆堆積浮蔓徒以湊
合為能於本題之意全無干涉甚
至好奇喜怪而首尾支離自不知
其何說此時文之弊也是作不惟
意有根據而且層見疊出血脉不
斷於從容委曲之中有峻激雄勁
之態亦何嘗不循時格而穎異之
見自是難掩斯可以為論矣
考試官教諭周批講學以正心此治
punctuated:
帥民，嚴刑峻法，必使從其所好，無惟乎民心之日離而亂且亡也。孔子告哀公以此，及其問所以為正而答之，則不出乎三綱，其啓之也深矣。哀公卒不能行其言，此魯之所以不競歟？

第貳場

論

講學為正心之要

張合

同考試官訓導詹批：今士子作論，下筆輒數百言，率皆堆積浮蔓，徒以湊合為能，於本題之意全無干涉，甚至好奇喜怪，而首尾支離，自不知其何說，此時文之弊也。是作不惟意有根據，而且層見疊出，血脉不斷，於從容委曲之中有峻激雄勁之態。亦何嘗不循時格，而穎異之見自是難掩，斯可以為論矣。

考試官教諭周批：講學以正心，此治
translation_en:
…to lead the people, imposing harsh punishments and severe laws to compel them to follow his own preferences, without considering [?] that the people's hearts grow more estranged each day, until disorder and ruin follow. Confucius instructed Duke Ai on this point; when the duke asked how to become upright, his answer went no further than the Three Bonds. How profound was the guidance he offered! Duke Ai ultimately failed to put his words into practice. Was this why Lu failed to flourish?

Second Session

Discourse

Discussing and Studying Learning Is Essential to Rectifying the Mind

Zhang He

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: Nowadays, when examination candidates compose discourses, they readily write several hundred words. Most merely pile up empty, sprawling verbiage, taking the ability to cobble things together as their sole accomplishment, with no bearing whatever on the meaning of the assigned topic. Some even delight in the strange and bizarre, producing disjointed beginnings and endings without themselves knowing what they are saying. This is the failing of contemporary examination prose. In this composition, however, the ideas are not only well grounded but also unfold in successive layers, with an unbroken thread running through them. Its measured and nuanced exposition also possesses an incisive, vigorous force. It certainly follows contemporary conventions, yet its outstanding insights are naturally impossible to conceal. This may indeed be called a discourse.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Discussing and studying learning in order to rectify the mind—this, in governing…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
道切要之論忠臣愛君莫急於此
子能歷證前代而發明曲盡一字
一句皆含深意非空言者篇末數
語尤見剴切他日見用慎毋忘也
考試官學正季批此作句簡而工意
多而正抑揚開闔不外題旨而清
俊整潔讀自不厭顧不可刻耶
甚矣爲君之難也以天下之大係於一身而身
則有本焉必端本而後可理天下之務然本之
===
端也又有至切之要不可得而緩者苟失其要
而惟末之圖雖勤且勵祗見勞矣大體所在寧
有益乎旣無益於身心必無濟於天下此後世
識治之君毎惓惓以正心爲急而心之由正又
恒以開廣睿聰爲首務也噫朱子斯言其爲宗
社生靈計可謂憂深而慮遠者矣人君忽此而
欲收平治之効於天下未之有也竊嘗觀之行
路矣有大道焉有小徑焉若知平直險夷則必
審所趨避而不陷於顛躓否則混見聞昧取舍
punctuated:
道切要之論，忠臣愛君，莫急於此。子能歷證前代，而發明曲盡，一字一句皆含深意，非空言者。篇末數語，尤見剴切。他日見用，慎毋忘也。
考試官學正季批：此作句簡而工，意多而正，抑揚開闔，不外題旨，而清俊整潔，讀自不厭，顧不可刻耶？
甚矣，爲君之難也！以天下之大，係於一身，而身則有本焉，必端本而後可理天下之務。然本之端也，又有至切之要，不可得而緩者。苟失其要，而惟末之圖，雖勤且勵，祗見勞矣。大體所在，寧有益乎？旣無益於身心，必無濟於天下。此後世識治之君，每惓惓以正心爲急，而心之由正，又恒以開廣睿聰爲首務也。噫！朱子斯言，其爲宗社生靈計，可謂憂深而慮遠者矣。人君忽此，而欲收平治之効於天下，未之有也。竊嘗觀之行路矣：有大道焉，有小徑焉。若知平直險夷，則必審所趨避，而不陷於顛躓；否則混見聞，昧取舍。
translation_en:
…a discourse on the essentials of the Way of governance. For a loyal minister who loves his sovereign, nothing is more urgent than this. You have drawn evidence from successive earlier dynasties and elucidated the matter fully in all its ramifications. Every word and sentence contains profound meaning; these are no empty words. The final few sentences are especially incisive and earnest. When you enter service one day, take care never to forget this.
Examiner Ji, Instructor, comments: This composition is concise and accomplished in its phrasing, rich and sound in its ideas. Its rhetorical rises and falls, expansions and contractions, never stray beyond the topic’s purport. Clear, elegant, orderly, and polished, it never wearies the reader. Surely it deserves to be printed?
How very difficult it is to be a ruler! The vast realm depends upon a single person, and that person has a foundation. Only after setting this foundation upright can he manage the affairs of the realm. Yet in setting the foundation upright, there is a most pressing essential that admits of no delay. If he misses this essential and attends only to peripheral matters, however diligent and vigorous he may be, he will merely exhaust himself. What benefit could this bring to the fundamental concerns of government? Since it brings no benefit to his own person and mind, it can certainly bring no help to the realm. This is why rulers of later ages who understood governance always earnestly regarded rectifying the mind as urgent; and as the means of rectifying their minds, they invariably made broadening their sagely understanding their foremost task. Ah! These words of Master Zhu, spoken out of concern for the dynastic temples, the altars of state, and the living people, may truly be called an expression of profound concern and far-reaching foresight. Never has a ruler neglected this and yet succeeded in bringing peace and good order to the realm.
I have ventured to consider this through the example of travelling along a road. There are broad highways and narrow paths. If one knows which are level and straight, which dangerous and which easy, one will surely judge carefully what to follow and what to avoid, and will not stumble and fall. Otherwise, one’s perceptions will be confused and one will be unable to distinguish what to choose and what to reject…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
一舉足而萬里之悔無及矣是心之邪正其猶
路乎知路之岐其猶學乎學之一言虞夏以前
未聞也至高宗與傅說始言之自是帝王始知
威福不足恃而從事於學矣然學之爲道豈易
言哉若不事詩書者固無足論其少知嚮慕者
則又或惟談苦空或篤好音律或攻書篆以爲
能或騁詞章以競美雖曰工矣心何補哉然就
中取善若漢宣帝以圖籍日陳於前唐太宗銳
意經術宋高宗披覽載籍亦似知務學者矣但
===
人君之學與韋布不同若惟涉獵是務而耀講
學虛名宏綱大法漫然弗究雖曰學矣不如已
焉匪書無益莫知要也要之所在其明理乎理
在天下無所不備有是非焉有善惡焉有邪正
焉其中又有涉於疑似而不容不辨者若徒曰
吾心正矣毋庸學矣則情好偏局而靜之所養
動之所發未必皆由於正猶不知路之險夷而
跬步一差秦越頓異者盍觀夫漢唐叔季之君
乎如崇尚佛老自以爲心之善矣窮極術藝自
punctuated: 一舉足而萬里之悔無及矣。是心之邪正，其猶路乎？知路之岐，其猶學乎？學之一言，虞夏以前未聞也，至高宗與傅說始言之。自是帝王始知威福不足恃，而從事於學矣。然學之爲道，豈易言哉？若不事詩書者，固無足論；其少知嚮慕者，則又或惟談苦空，或篤好音律，或攻書篆以爲能，或騁詞章以競美。雖曰工矣，心何補哉？然就中取善，若漢宣帝以圖籍日陳於前，唐太宗銳意經術，宋高宗披覽載籍，亦似知務學者矣。但人君之學，與韋布不同。若惟涉獵是務，而耀講學虛名，宏綱大法漫然弗究，雖曰學矣，不如已焉。匪書無益，莫知要也。要之所在，其明理乎？理在天下，無所不備。有是非焉，有善惡焉，有邪正焉，其中又有涉於疑似而不容不辨者。若徒曰吾心正矣，毋庸學矣，則情好偏局，而靜之所養、動之所發，未必皆由於正。猶不知路之險夷，而跬步一差，秦越頓異者。盍觀夫漢唐叔季之君乎？如崇尚佛老，自以爲心之善矣；窮極術藝，自
translation_en:
…with a single step, one goes ten thousand li astray, and regret comes too late. Are not the heart’s deviations and rectitude like roads? Is not knowing where roads diverge like learning? Before the ages of Yu and Xia, the term “learning” had not been heard; only with Gaozong and Fu Yue did discussion of it begin. From then on, emperors and kings began to understand that their power to punish and bestow favors could not be relied upon, and they devoted themselves to learning.

Yet is the way of learning easily explained? Those who do not engage with the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents need not even be discussed. Among those who have some inclination toward learning, some speak only of suffering and emptiness; some are deeply fond of musical pitches; some cultivate calligraphy and seal script as demonstrations of ability; and some display their literary compositions in competition for elegance. Skilled though they may be, what benefit does this bring to the heart? Yet if we select the better examples among them, Emperor Xuandi of Han had maps and books set before him daily, Emperor Taizong of Tang applied himself keenly to classical learning, and Emperor Gaozong of Song read through written records. These, too, seem to have understood the need to pursue learning.

But a ruler’s learning differs from that of commoners clad in plain cloth. If he devotes himself only to cursory reading and flaunts an empty reputation for scholarly inquiry, while carelessly neglecting to investigate the great guiding principles and fundamental standards, then, though this may be called learning, he would do better to stop. It is not that books are useless, but that he does not understand what is essential. Does not the essential lie in understanding principle? Principle is present everywhere under Heaven. There are right and wrong, good and evil, deviation and rectitude; among these are also doubtful cases and misleading resemblances that must be distinguished. If one merely says, “My heart is already correct; I have no need to learn,” one’s feelings and preferences will be partial and confined, and neither what one cultivates in stillness nor what one expresses in action will necessarily proceed entirely from rectitude. This is like failing to know whether a road is dangerous or easy: one mistaken half-step, and one’s course suddenly diverges as widely as Qin from Yue.

Why not consider the rulers of the declining years of Han and Tang? In venerating Buddhism and Daoism, they supposed their hearts to be good; in pursuing technical skills and arts to the utmost, they themselves…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以為心之敏矣喜功黷武自以為心之壯矣姑
息寬縱自以為心之仁矣旁搜苛察自以為心
之明矣濫賞私恩自以為心之惠矣殊不知理
在於心自有本然之正今各有所偏而罔覺其
非者由講究弗明而是非疑似之間得以亂之
耳使先知正心之要則必以崇正為急而何累
乎善也必以大體為務而何累乎敏也必以戡
定為威而何累乎壯也必以感化為仁而何累
乎仁也必以周物為智而何累乎明也必以普
===
偏為公而何累乎惠也嗚呼學一不講而心之
所發懸遠如此良可畏哉是以古之賢君明緩
急之序達先後之宜知心之為物雖曰萬理歸
宿之地然隱微之間真妄錯雜苟理不先明則
其所存所發未必皆由於正况近似亂真如前
數者之累而為君心之害愈深如之何而不懼
也於是乎究古今之變察理欲之幾如何為昏
明如何為邪正如何為安危如何為淑慝遠稽
前代何者可以勸懲近鑒祖宗何者可以效法
punctuated:
以為心之敏矣，喜功黷武，自以為心之壯矣；姑息寬縱，自以為心之仁矣；旁搜苛察，自以為心之明矣；濫賞私恩，自以為心之惠矣。殊不知理在於心，自有本然之正。今各有所偏，而罔覺其非者，由講究弗明，而是非疑似之間得以亂之耳。使先知正心之要，則必以崇正為急，而何累乎善也？必以大體為務，而何累乎敏也？必以戡定為威，而何累乎壯也？必以感化為仁，而何累乎仁也？必以周物為智，而何累乎明也？必以普偏為公，而何累乎惠也？
嗚呼！學一不講，而心之所發懸遠如此，良可畏哉！是以古之賢君，明緩急之序，達先後之宜，知心之為物，雖曰萬理歸宿之地，然隱微之間，真妄錯雜。苟理不先明，則其所存所發，未必皆由於正。况近似亂真，如前數者之累，而為君心之害愈深，如之何而不懼也？於是乎究古今之變，察理欲之幾：如何為昏明？如何為邪正？如何為安危？如何為淑慝？遠稽前代，何者可以勸懲？近鑒祖宗，何者可以效法？
translation_en:
…they considered their minds perceptive. Delighting in military achievements and recklessly resorting to arms, they considered their minds strong; indulging others and allowing excessive license, they considered their minds benevolent; searching everywhere and scrutinizing harshly, they considered their minds discerning; bestowing rewards indiscriminately and granting private favors, they considered their minds generous. They failed utterly to understand that principle, residing in the mind, possesses an inherent correctness. That each became biased without recognizing his error was simply because insufficient inquiry had left principle unclear, allowing confusion amid the apparent similarities between right and wrong. Had they first understood the essentials of rectifying the mind, they would surely have made honoring what is correct their urgent priority: how, then, could supposed goodness have encumbered them? They would have attended to the larger concerns: how could supposed perceptiveness have encumbered them? They would have located their majesty in quelling disorder: how could supposed strength have encumbered them? They would have located benevolence in transforming others through moral influence: how could supposed benevolence have encumbered them? They would have located wisdom in caring comprehensively for all things: how could supposed discernment have encumbered them? They would have located impartiality in extending benefits universally [?]: how could supposed generosity have encumbered them?
Alas! Once learning goes unexamined, what issues from the mind can stray so far as this. Truly, it is cause for fear! Thus the worthy rulers of antiquity understood the ordering of urgent and less urgent matters and grasped what should properly come first and afterward. They knew that although the mind is said to be the place where all principles converge, within its hidden recesses truth and falsity intermingle. Unless principle is first made clear, what the mind harbors and expresses will not necessarily proceed entirely from what is correct. How much more so when apparent likenesses confound the true, as with the several impediments just described, doing still deeper harm to the ruler’s mind! How could one fail to be apprehensive? Accordingly, they investigated changes from antiquity to the present and scrutinized the subtle beginnings of principle and desire: what constitutes benightedness or enlightenment? What constitutes deviance or correctness? What constitutes security or peril? What constitutes goodness or wickedness? Looking far back to earlier dynasties, what could provide encouragement or admonition? Looking nearer to their own dynastic ancestors as a mirror, what could serve as a model to follow? …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
講筵啓沃因言而思之方正忠良虛心以訪之
治安易忽曷以慎之儉壬易昵曷以遠之宴安
易懷曷以儆之正邪易混曷以辨之公私易雜
曷以清之思其理而不泛用其心窮其本而不
徒事乎末如此則治理昭明大本以立猶未舉
足而已先知路之險易矣是以當其心之未動
也湛然清明渾然純一及其感發也果在天理
耶必知所以充之在人欲耶必知所以遏之凡
所欲行皆正大光明之體無偏黨反側之私而
===
一心正矣由是推之朝廷則百官承式推之於
國則百姓昭明推之天下則四方風動而莫敢
有不正者矣大學欲正心必先於致知推極其
效至於平天下董子所謂正心以正朝廷而先
之以勉彊學問皆此意耳使學先不講雖天資
敏睿出於尋常而疑似之間見之未必真信之
未必决施於有政可訾多矣雖欲救之其能及
乎與其救之於終孰若審之於始始得其要則
至靜可以制動也至簡可以御繁也至約可以
punctuated: 講筵啓沃，因言而思之；方正忠良，虛心以訪之。治安易忽，曷以慎之？儉壬易昵，曷以遠之？宴安易懷，曷以儆之？正邪易混，曷以辨之？公私易雜，曷以清之？思其理而不泛用其心，窮其本而不徒事乎末。如此則治理昭明，大本以立，猶未舉足而已先知路之險易矣。是以當其心之未動也，湛然清明，渾然純一；及其感發也，果在天理耶？必知所以充之；在人欲耶？必知所以遏之。凡所欲行，皆正大光明之體，無偏黨反側之私，而一心正矣。由是推之朝廷，則百官承式；推之於國，則百姓昭明；推之天下，則四方風動，而莫敢有不正者矣。《大學》欲正心，必先於致知，推極其效，至於平天下。董子所謂正心以正朝廷，而先之以勉彊學問，皆此意耳。使學先不講，雖天資敏睿出於尋常，而疑似之間，見之未必真，信之未必决，施於有政，可訾多矣。雖欲救之，其能及乎？與其救之於終，孰若審之於始？始得其要，則至靜可以制動也，至簡可以御繁也，至約可以
translation_en:
…At the imperial lectures, receive instruction that nourishes the mind and reflect upon what is said; consult upright, loyal, and worthy men with an open mind. Peace and good order readily invite neglect: how can one remain vigilant? Flattering men [?] readily win intimacy: how can one keep them at a distance? Ease and comfort readily attract attachment: how can one guard against them? The upright and the wicked are easily confused: how can one distinguish them? Public and private interests are easily intermixed: how can one keep them clear? Reflect upon the principles involved without applying the mind aimlessly; investigate their roots without merely attending to their branches. In this way the principles of government become clear and the great foundation is established, just as one knows the dangers and ease of a road before taking a step.

Thus, before the mind is stirred, it is limpid and clear, wholly pure and unified. When it responds to things and becomes active, does its impulse truly accord with Heaven’s principle? Then one must know how to develop it fully. Does it arise from human desires? Then one must know how to restrain it. Everything one wishes to carry out embodies uprightness and openness, with none of the selfishness of partiality, factionalism, or deviousness; thus the mind is rectified. Extend this to the court, and the hundred officials follow its example; extend it to the realm, and the people become enlightened; extend it to all under Heaven, and the four quarters are stirred as by the wind, with none daring to remain unrectified.

The Great Learning requires the extension of knowledge before the rectification of the mind, and traces the ultimate effects of this to bringing peace to all under Heaven. Master Dong’s teaching that one should rectify one’s mind in order to rectify the court, first exerting oneself in learning and inquiry, expresses precisely this same intention. If learning has not first been thoroughly pursued, then even if one possesses exceptional natural acuity and wisdom, amid doubtful appearances one’s perceptions may not be true and one’s convictions may not be firm. When put into practice in government, much will be open to criticism. Even if one wishes to remedy this, can it still be done in time? Rather than remedying matters at the end, would it not be better to examine them carefully at the beginning? If one grasps the essentials at the beginning, utmost stillness can govern movement, utmost simplicity can govern complexity, and utmost concision can…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
該博也又何必騁浮華工記誦衒讀書之彌文
而於身心卒無補哉使屑屑必於書焉則堯舜
禹湯文武之時無書可讀又何資也自今觀之
堯惟執中舜惟精一禹惟祗德湯惟建中文不
過敬止武不過建極而已夫精一中敬皆理之
微也正心之要也數聖人能講明之即所謂學
也雖性本生知心不待養而後正然亦何甞緩
於學哉朱子不曰講學以正心而必曰要者可
見學之一言所係甚切欲臻功化之極必須由
===
此進焉猶岐轍不差而萬里可馴至矣辟之行
路不亦信乎夫欲正君心固本於講學矣但人
主一心攻者甚衆安能保其終無間乎故古之
聖君尤於是乎致謹也左右前後罔非正人深
宫禁密凛然弗懈所以涵養君德而維持聖學
者無所不用其極夫然後本固性成治行化洽
無負乎天下望也嗚呼為君之難詎不信夫知
其難而及時講學亦無難者是又在於立志之
堅如說命所謂念終始典于學雖二帝三王亦
punctuated: 該博也，又何必騁浮華、工記誦、衒讀書之彌文，而於身心卒無補哉？使屑屑必於書焉，則堯舜禹湯文武之時，無書可讀，又何資也？自今觀之，堯惟執中，舜惟精一，禹惟祗德，湯惟建中，文不過敬止，武不過建極而已。夫精一中敬，皆理之微也，正心之要也。數聖人能講明之，即所謂學也。雖性本生知，心不待養而後正，然亦何甞緩於學哉？朱子不曰「講學以正心」，而必曰「要」者，可見學之一言所係甚切。欲臻功化之極，必須由此進焉，猶岐轍不差，而萬里可馴至矣。辟之行路，不亦信乎？夫欲正君心，固本於講學矣。但人主一心，攻者甚衆，安能保其終無間乎？故古之聖君尤於是乎致謹也。左右前後，罔非正人；深宫禁密，凛然弗懈。所以涵養君德而維持聖學者，無所不用其極。夫然後本固性成，治行化洽，無負乎天下望也。嗚呼！為君之難，詎不信夫？知其難而及時講學，亦無難者。是又在於立志之堅，如《說命》所謂「念終始典于學」，雖二帝三王亦
translation_en:
…encompass the vast and varied. Why, then, indulge in superficial embellishment, become adept at memorization and recitation, and flaunt elaborate displays of book learning, yet ultimately gain nothing for one’s person and mind? If learning necessarily meant fussing over books, then in the days of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, when there were no books to read, what resources could they have drawn upon? Viewed from the present, Yao simply held fast to the mean; Shun was discerning and single-minded; Yu revered virtue; Tang established the mean; King Wen did no more than abide in reverence, and King Wu no more than establish the supreme standard. Discernment, single-mindedness, the mean, and reverence are all subtle aspects of principle and essentials for rectifying the mind. These sages’ ability to investigate and clarify them is precisely what is meant by learning. Although they were by nature born with knowledge, and their minds did not need cultivation before becoming correct, when did they ever slacken in learning? Master Zhu did not merely say, “Investigate learning in order to rectify the mind,” but insisted on the word “essential.” This shows how much hinges upon that single word, “learning.” To attain the utmost achievement in government and moral transformation, one must advance by this route, just as, if one does not take the wrong track at a fork, one may gradually reach a destination ten thousand li away. Is not the analogy with travelling a road convincing?

The wish to rectify the ruler’s mind is indeed rooted in the investigation of learning. Yet the ruler has but one mind, and so many things assail it: how can one guarantee that no breach will ever occur? Thus the sage rulers of antiquity were especially vigilant in this respect. Those to their left and right, before and behind them, were all upright men; deep within the secluded palace, they remained solemnly attentive and never relaxed. They spared no effort in nurturing the ruler’s virtue and sustaining his sagely learning. Only then could the foundation be secure and the moral nature fully formed, good government take effect and moral transformation spread everywhere, fulfilling the expectations of all under Heaven. Alas! Is it not truly difficult to be a ruler? Yet if one recognizes that difficulty and undertakes the investigation of learning in good time, there is nothing difficult about it. This, in turn, depends upon firmness of resolve. As the Charge to Yue says, “Keep learning constantly in mind, from beginning to end.” Even the Two Emperors and Three Kings…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易及耳夫何難哉使漢唐宋號稱英敏之君能
知此義何至君德不純治功小就卒貽後世無
窮之惜哉玩一時之安貽千載之戒可慨也巳
詩曰殷鑒不遠其是之謂乎又曰學有緝熈于
光明惟守成賢君能之噫朱子斯言豈但為當
時告實為萬世為君者告也
表
擬宋製觀文鑒古圖輔臣賀表慶曆四年
張合
===
同考試官訓導詹批標著事序使之明
白謂之表此作不惟鋪敘詳明且
四六流麗而典雅不浮非記誦陳
言者
考試官教諭周批詞不深僻而含蓄
忠義未審當時有此作否
考試官學正季批得體製而精緻可
嘉
慶曆四年二月丙辰
punctuated:
易及耳，夫何難哉？使漢唐宋號稱英敏之君能知此義，何至君德不純，治功小就，卒貽後世無窮之惜哉？玩一時之安，貽千載之戒，可慨也巳！詩曰：「殷鑒不遠。」其是之謂乎？又曰：「學有緝熈于光明。」惟守成賢君能之。噫！朱子斯言，豈但為當時告，實為萬世為君者告也。

表
擬宋製觀文鑒古圖輔臣賀表，慶曆四年。
張合

同考試官訓導詹批：標著事序，使之明白，謂之表。此作不惟鋪敘詳明，且四六流麗而典雅不浮，非記誦陳言者。

考試官教諭周批：詞不深僻，而含蓄忠義，未審當時有此作否。

考試官學正季批：得體製而精緻，可嘉。

慶曆四年二月丙辰。
translation_en:
…could readily be equaled. What difficulty would there be? Had the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song renowned for their brilliance and acuity understood this principle, how could their sovereign virtue have remained impure and their achievements in government so limited, ultimately leaving later generations with endless regret? To indulge in a moment’s ease and leave a warning for a thousand years—how lamentable! The Book of Odes says, “Yin’s warning mirror is not far away.” Is this not what it means? It also says, “Through learning, continue onward into brightness.” Only a worthy ruler who preserves the inherited achievement can accomplish this. Ah! These words of Master Zhu were surely addressed not merely to his own time, but to rulers throughout all ages.

Memorial
A model congratulatory memorial by assisting ministers on the Song court’s production of Illustrations for Viewing Patterns and Taking Antiquity as a Mirror (Guanwen jiangu tu), set in the fourth year of Qingli [1044].
By Zhang He 張合.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: A composition that sets forth the sequence of events and makes it clear is called a memorial. This piece not only develops its account fully and lucidly; its four- and six-character parallel phrases are also flowing and elegant, refined without being frivolous. It is no mere recitation of memorized, conventional expressions.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Its language is neither abstruse nor obscure, yet it holds loyalty and righteousness within it. I do not know whether such a composition existed at the time.

Comment by Examiner Ji, School Instructor: It conforms to the proper form and is finely wrought. Commendable.

On the bingchen day of the second month of the fourth year of Qingli [1044]…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
上命圖製前代帝王美惡之迹可為鑒戒者號
曰觀文鑒古圖
御迎陽門出示臣等者伏以
以人為監帝王致治之良規取善為師令
主保邦之要道欲光前而啓後因考古以
儀今朝野揚休臣鄰稱慶臣某等誠懽誠
忭稽首頓首上言竊惟
心莫要於審幾治莫先於擇術是以明堂
素墉悉登聖哲之容太液新亭盡寫唐虞
===
之跡開元寳千秋之鑑憲宗繪三合之屏
無非明聖撝謙急欲隨時體道治安愈慎
常思觸事警心逮至欲縱情迷遂畫洛神
之賦神搖心蕩遽張列女之圖妖華遍染
於重闈粉黛旁施於四壁豈知涉川攸利
在視乎前舟而行道無危須觀乎往轍孰
愚孰智遺後人褒貶之公可戒可師關世
道興衰之運
昌期偉觀曠古奇逢兹蓋伏遇
punctuated:
上命圖製前代帝王美惡之迹可為鑒戒者，號曰《觀文鑒古圖》，御迎陽門，出示臣等者。伏以：以人為監，帝王致治之良規；取善為師，令主保邦之要道。欲光前而啓後，因考古以儀今。朝野揚休，臣鄰稱慶。臣某等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言。
竊惟：心莫要於審幾，治莫先於擇術。是以明堂素墉，悉登聖哲之容；太液新亭，盡寫唐虞之跡。開元寳千秋之鑑，憲宗繪三合之屏。無非明聖撝謙，急欲隨時體道；治安愈慎，常思觸事警心。逮至欲縱情迷，遂畫洛神之賦；神搖心蕩，遽張列女之圖。妖華遍染於重闈，粉黛旁施於四壁。豈知涉川攸利，在視乎前舟；而行道無危，須觀乎往轍。孰愚孰智，遺後人褒貶之公；可戒可師，關世道興衰之運。
昌期偉觀，曠古奇逢。兹蓋伏遇
translation_en:
…His Majesty ordered that those deeds of former emperors and kings, good and bad, which could serve as examples and warnings be depicted in illustrations, entitled Illustrations for Viewing Culture and Taking Antiquity as a Mirror (Guanwen jiangu tu). He appeared at Yingyang Gate and displayed them to us, his servants. We humbly submit:
Taking other people as a mirror is an excellent rule by which emperors and kings bring about good government; taking goodness as one’s teacher is an essential way for worthy rulers to preserve their realm. To bring glory to their predecessors and open the way for their successors, they examine antiquity as a model for the present. Court and countryside acclaim this splendid deed, and ministers offer congratulations. We, your servants, So-and-so and the others, in heartfelt joy and delight, bow our heads to the ground and submit this memorial.
We reflect that nothing is more essential to the mind than discerning the first stirrings of events, and nothing takes precedence in government over choosing the right methods. Thus, upon the plain walls of the Hall of Enlightenment were displayed the likenesses of sages and worthies; in the new pavilion at Taiye were fully portrayed the deeds of Tang and Yu. The ruler of the Kaiyuan era treasured the Mirror for a Thousand Autumns, and Xianzong had the Screen of the Three Unions painted [?]. These were all instances of enlightened, sage rulers exercising humility, earnestly wishing to embody the Way as circumstances required. Ever more cautious amid peace and good order, they constantly sought to keep their minds vigilant through everything they encountered. But when desires ran unchecked and feelings became deluded, they had the Rhapsody on the Goddess of the Luo illustrated; when their spirits wavered and their hearts were unsettled, they hastily displayed Pictures of Exemplary Women. Seductive beauty spread throughout the inner palace, and images of women adorned with powder and eyebrow pigment covered its walls. How could they understand that success in crossing a river depends upon watching the boat ahead, and that travelling a road without danger requires observing the tracks of those who went before? Who was foolish and who was wise is left to the impartial praise and blame of later generations; what offers a warning and what provides a model bears upon the rise and decline of order in the world.
This magnificent spectacle in a flourishing age is a rare encounter unparalleled in antiquity. This is because we have humbly had the good fortune to serve…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
〇〇〇〇
握紀御天應期啓運以鎮靜人心爲本以阜
安海宇爲先
誠意感乎甘雨已徵於黙禱仁慈周恤燒羊
寧忍於宵饑兢業以斡化機憂勤以靖王
略比隆三代治兼教養之施叅賛兩儀身
任綱常之責正邪弗殽於偏聽予奪一循
乎至公刑以不殺爲威財以不畜爲富崇
儒重道恢弘
===
列聖之丕基偃武脩文度越百王之至治
聖人之德何以加焉太平之功可謂盛矣猶謂
帝王事跡雖備載於簡編然美惡儀形須
顯憑於采繪始因儒臣之請旁搜秘閣之
藏遠從軒轅之時邇接貞觀之季記分十
二煥
雲漢之昭回事列百餘燦丹青之藻麗治道
有純有雜朝綱或是或非創業最難每起
於憂勤之積守成不易常生於安靖之驕
punctuated: 〇〇〇〇，握紀御天，應期啓運，以鎮靜人心爲本，以阜安海宇爲先。誠意感乎甘雨，已徵於黙禱；仁慈周恤，燒羊寧忍於宵饑？兢業以斡化機，憂勤以靖王略。比隆三代，治兼教養之施；叅賛兩儀，身任綱常之責。正邪弗殽於偏聽，予奪一循乎至公。刑以不殺爲威，財以不畜爲富。崇儒重道，恢弘列聖之丕基；偃武脩文，度越百王之至治。聖人之德，何以加焉？太平之功，可謂盛矣！猶謂帝王事跡，雖備載於簡編，然美惡儀形，須顯憑於采繪。始因儒臣之請，旁搜秘閣之藏，遠從軒轅之時，邇接貞觀之季。記分十二，煥雲漢之昭回；事列百餘，燦丹青之藻麗。治道有純有雜，朝綱或是或非。創業最難，每起於憂勤之積；守成不易，常生於安靖之驕。
translation_en:
…〇〇〇〇 [?], who grasps the governing order and rules in accordance with Heaven, responding to the appointed time and inaugurating a new era of fortune, takes calming the people’s hearts as his foundation and enriching and securing the realm as his first priority. His sincerity moves Heaven to send timely rain, as his silent prayers have already demonstrated. His benevolence extends care to all: could he bear to have a sheep roasted to satisfy his hunger at night? With reverent diligence he directs the workings of transformation; with anxious devotion he brings peace to the royal domains. Rivaling the Three Dynasties in greatness, his government both educates and nourishes the people. Assisting Heaven and Earth, he personally shoulders responsibility for the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. He does not confuse the upright and the depraved by listening to one side alone; his bestowals and deprivations follow perfect impartiality throughout. In punishment, he makes refraining from killing the source of his awe; in finance, he makes refraining from hoarding the source of his wealth. Honoring Confucian scholars and esteeming the Way, he enlarges the great foundation laid by the sage emperors before him. Laying aside arms and cultivating civil virtues, he surpasses the finest government of all former kings. What could be added to the virtue of such a sage? His achievement of great peace may indeed be called magnificent!
Yet he considers that, although the deeds of emperors and kings are fully recorded in books, their exemplary forms, good and bad, must be made visibly manifest through painted images. Accordingly, at the request of his scholarly officials, a wide search was made through the holdings of the imperial library, reaching back to the time of Xuanyuan and extending down to the closing years of the Zhenguan era. The accounts are divided into twelve sections, radiant with the revolving brilliance of the River of Heaven; more than a hundred episodes are arranged, resplendent in the rich beauty of painted colors. Ways of governing are sometimes pure and sometimes mixed; the ordering of the court is sometimes right and sometimes wrong. Founding a dynasty is supremely difficult and commonly proceeds from accumulated anxious effort. Preserving its achievements is no easy matter, the difficulty often arising from the arrogance bred by peace and tranquility.…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
好惡同情自是難逃輿論昏明異域何嘗
不本諸心身雖往而名猶存貌雖疑而事
則實片言之善亦當垂範千年一念之差
遂至貽譏萬世左瞻右盼揖古人於想像
之間前規後箴悟心事於丰神之表蓋將
覩狂爲而興嘆觀賢主而若親懲勸森嚴
正邪炳若是誠
一代之令典信爲億載之徽章臣等才慙鼎
軸職玷班行世際唐虞敢廢詩書之舊學
===
君同堯舜尚期稷契之愚忠伏願
拊迹論心永作邦家之鑒
因人進德無更山水之圖直超近代之規模
允復隆平之景象臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖踴躍歡忭之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
punctuated:
好惡同情，自是難逃輿論；昏明異域，何嘗不本諸心？身雖往而名猶存，貌雖疑而事則實。片言之善，亦當垂範千年；一念之差，遂至貽譏萬世。左瞻右盼，揖古人於想像之間；前規後箴，悟心事於丰神之表。蓋將覩狂爲而興嘆，觀賢主而若親。懲勸森嚴，正邪炳若。是誠一代之令典，信爲億載之徽章。
臣等才慙鼎軸，職玷班行。世際唐虞，敢廢詩書之舊學？君同堯舜，尚期稷契之愚忠。伏願拊迹論心，永作邦家之鑒；因人進德，無更山水之圖。直超近代之規模，允復隆平之景象。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、踴躍歡忭之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
translation_en:
…People share the same feelings of approval and aversion, so public judgment is naturally hard to escape. Though benighted and enlightened rule belong to different realms, when have they not been rooted in the heart? Though the person has passed away, his name survives; though his likeness may be uncertain, his deeds are real. The goodness of a single utterance deserves to serve as an example for a thousand years; the error of a single thought may incur reproach for ten thousand generations. Looking left and right, we salute the ancients in our imagination; admonished and instructed at every turn, we apprehend their inner concerns through their outward bearing. Beholding reckless deeds, we sigh; viewing worthy rulers, we feel as though we were in their presence. The warnings and encouragements are stern and imposing; right and wrong stand clearly revealed. This is truly an excellent institution of the dynasty, indeed a glorious emblem for countless ages.
We, your servants, possess talents unworthy of the highest ministerial responsibilities and hold office to the discredit of the official ranks. Living in an age like that of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, how could we abandon our longstanding study of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents? With a sovereign equal to Yao and Shun, we still aspire, in our humble loyalty, to emulate Ji and Xie. We humbly wish that Your Majesty will examine these deeds and assess the intentions behind them, forever making them a mirror for the state; that through these figures you will advance in virtue, without replacing their images with pictures of mountains and waters. May you far surpass the patterns of recent ages and truly restore the prospect of flourishing peace. We, your servants, looking up to Heaven and reverently beholding Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain our boundless joy and exultation. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第叄場
策
第一問
張合
同考試官訓導詹批帝王爲治之道聖
人傳心之要我
聖祖深體力行之功燕翼貽謀之訓悉明習而
揄揚之末寓諷諫有裨
聖政子豈賈董之儔歟
===
大廷之對拭目於子矣
考試官敎諭周批
聖祖脩身制治之道實自洪範大學中來此篇
鋪張有體而文亦閎深不卜可知
爲佳士矣
考試官學正季批我
聖祖學問心思之奧立法貽謀之詳此策叙述
無遺豈亦有志於用世者乎
對觀百王傳道之大要則知
punctuated:
第叄場
策
第一問
張合

同考試官訓導詹批：「帝王爲治之道，聖人傳心之要，我聖祖深體力行之功，燕翼貽謀之訓，悉明習而揄揚之。末寓諷諫，有裨聖政。子豈賈董之儔歟？大廷之對，拭目於子矣！」

考試官敎諭周批：「聖祖脩身制治之道，實自洪範、大學中來。此篇鋪張有體，而文亦閎深，不卜可知爲佳士矣。」

考試官學正季批：「我聖祖學問心思之奧，立法貽謀之詳，此策叙述無遺，豈亦有志於用世者乎？」

對：觀百王傳道之大要，則知
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Zhang He

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: “The way by which emperors and kings govern, the essentials of the sages’ transmission of the mind, our sagely founding ancestor’s achievements in profoundly comprehending and vigorously practicing these principles, and his instructions for securing his descendants’ welfare and bequeathing plans to them—you understand all these thoroughly and expound them with praise. At the end you embed indirect remonstrance, beneficial to the sagely government. Might you be a peer of Jia Yi and Dong Zhongshu? I shall eagerly await your response at the Palace Examination!”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “Our sagely founding ancestor’s way of cultivating himself and establishing good government truly derived from the Great Plan and the Great Learning. This essay develops its subject with proper structure, and its writing is also expansive and profound. Without resorting to divination, one can know that you are a worthy scholar.”

Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: “The profundity of our sagely founding ancestor’s learning and thought, and the thoroughness with which he established laws and bequeathed plans to posterity—this policy essay recounts them without omission. Might you too aspire to put your abilities to use in public service?”

Response: By examining the great essentials of how the kings of successive ages transmitted the Way, one comes to understand…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖學之原觀
一代致治之弘規則知
聖心之用夫學之要原於理治之規本於法者
也是則言之所立雖不能以盡同而理之
所該則不能以獨異規之所制雖不能以
盡一而法之所統則不能以或偏知乎是
可以論斯道矣仰惟我
太祖高皇帝以
天縱之資加
===
日新之學當夫戎馬倥偬而講藝之罔休迨
夫
崇高已極而論道之不怠
思古聖之心則皇皇焉如有求而弗得
圖古聖之治則汲汲焉如有望而未見以帝
王為治之要道莫粹於洪範也則
親御宸翰而詳疏其旨以百聖傳心之要典莫
粹於大學也則揭之
殿廡而時復睇觀是何若是其勤勤也愚嘗
punctuated: 聖學之原，觀一代致治之弘規，則知聖心之用。夫學之要原於理，治之規本於法者也。是則言之所立，雖不能以盡同，而理之所該，則不能以獨異；規之所制，雖不能以盡一，而法之所統，則不能以或偏。知乎是，可以論斯道矣。仰惟我太祖高皇帝，以天縱之資，加日新之學。當夫戎馬倥偬，而講藝之罔休；迨夫崇高已極，而論道之不怠。思古聖之心，則皇皇焉如有求而弗得；圖古聖之治，則汲汲焉如有望而未見。以帝王為治之要道，莫粹於《洪範》也，則親御宸翰而詳疏其旨；以百聖傳心之要典，莫粹於《大學》也，則揭之殿廡而時復睇觀。是何若是其勤勤也？愚嘗
translation_en:
…the source of sagely learning; by observing the grand principles through which a dynasty achieves good government, one understands the workings of the sagely mind. The essentials of learning originate in principle, and the rules of government are rooted in laws. Thus, although the propositions advanced in words cannot all be identical, the principles they encompass cannot be uniquely different; although the regulations established cannot all be uniform, what the laws govern cannot be partial in any respect. Understanding this, one may discuss this Way.
I reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao combined Heaven-endowed gifts with learning renewed each day. Amid the tumult of military campaigns, he never ceased discussing the classical arts; after attaining the loftiest position, he remained tireless in discussing the Way. In pondering the minds of the ancient sages, he was restless, as though seeking something he had not yet obtained; in planning to realize their government, he was eager, as though looking for something he had not yet seen. Believing that no essential teaching on government for emperors and kings was more refined than the Great Plan (Hongfan), he personally took up the imperial brush and expounded its meaning in detail. Believing that no essential canon transmitting the understanding of all the sages was more refined than the Great Learning (Daxue), he had it displayed in the palace halls and galleries and repeatedly examined it. Why was he so unremittingly diligent? I, in my humble ignorance, once…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
仰窺
聖心之所在矣請以洪範言之初一曰五行次
二曰敬用五事次三曰農用八政次四曰
協用五紀次五曰建用皇極次六曰乂用
三德次七曰明用稽疑次八曰念用庶徵
次九曰嚮用五福威用六極而天人之理
備矣故宋儒蔡沈曰人君治天下之法是
孰有加於此以大學言之一曰格物二曰
致知三曰誠意四曰正心五曰脩身六曰
===
齊家七曰治國八曰平天下而先後之序
悉矣故宋儒朱熹有曰大學如行程謂造
道者用力之途次也我
聖祖知其然潜心體乎此而有以會其要領篤
志察乎此而有以收其實效觀乎遺
東宮
親王有
訓
諭臣民有
punctuated:
仰窺聖心之所在矣。請以《洪範》言之：初一曰五行，次二曰敬用五事，次三曰農用八政，次四曰協用五紀，次五曰建用皇極，次六曰乂用三德，次七曰明用稽疑，次八曰念用庶徵，次九曰嚮用五福、威用六極，而天人之理備矣。故宋儒蔡沈曰：「人君治天下之法。」是孰有加於此？以《大學》言之：一曰格物，二曰致知，三曰誠意，四曰正心，五曰脩身，六曰齊家，七曰治國，八曰平天下，而先後之序悉矣。故宋儒朱熹有曰：「大學如行程。」謂造道者用力之途次也。
我聖祖知其然，潜心體乎此，而有以會其要領；篤志察乎此，而有以收其實效。觀乎遺東宮、親王有訓，諭臣民有
translation_en:
…reverently discerned where the sagely mind is directed. Let me speak first of the Great Plan (Hongfan): first, the Five Phases; second, the reverent use of the Five Activities; third, the diligent use of the Eight Affairs of Government; fourth, the harmonious use of the Five Regulators of Time; fifth, the establishment of the Imperial Standard; sixth, government through the Three Virtues; seventh, the discerning use of means for resolving doubts; eighth, attentive consideration of the Various Signs; ninth, encouraging through the Five Blessings and instilling awe through the Six Extremities. Thus the principles of Heaven and humanity are fully encompassed. Hence the Song scholar Cai Shen said, “The method by which the ruler governs all under Heaven.” What could surpass this? Speaking of the Great Learning (Daxue): first, investigating things; second, extending knowledge; third, making the intentions sincere; fourth, rectifying the mind; fifth, cultivating oneself; sixth, regulating the family; seventh, governing the state; eighth, bringing peace to all under Heaven. Thus the sequence of what comes first and what follows is fully set out. Hence the Song scholar Zhu Xi said, “The Great Learning is like the stages of a journey.” He meant the successive stages at which those advancing toward the Way must exert themselves.
Our sagely founder understood this. He devoted his mind to embodying these teachings and thereby grasped their essentials; he steadfastly examined them and thereby secured their practical results. Consider how, for transmission to the heir apparent and the imperial princes, there were Instructions; for admonishing officials and commoners, there were…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
誥教民有
令齊民有
律而
大誥一序四民之業極其詳悉而於攸好德
考終命之義特致意焉其所以敘彞倫立
皇極而保萬民者皆本於天道而驗於人
事謂非有得於洪範之奧者乎觀乎因節
用愛人而取孔子之言以明白易知而賛
典謨之旨語善惡則有稂莠害苗之諭語
===
毀譽則辨賢不肖之真尊孟子仁義之說
而黜漢武帝之神仙稱李沆災異之奏而
抑宋真宗之侈大
諭侍臣則曰人民凋弊生息未遂也
諭郡縣則曰天下初定百姓困窮也亢旱為
災則脩己以答
天甘露獻賀則因瑞而致戒毁鏤金之牀損食
肉之獸謂聲色為伐性之斧謂技巧為覆
車之轍
punctuated: 誥，教民有令，齊民有律，而《大誥》一序，四民之業極其詳悉，而於攸好德、考終命之義特致意焉。其所以敘彞倫、立皇極而保萬民者，皆本於天道而驗於人事，謂非有得於《洪範》之奧者乎？觀乎因節用愛人而取孔子之言，以明白易知而賛典謨之旨。語善惡，則有稂莠害苗之諭；語毀譽，則辨賢不肖之真。尊孟子仁義之說，而黜漢武帝之神仙；稱李沆災異之奏，而抑宋真宗之侈大。諭侍臣則曰：「人民凋弊，生息未遂也。」諭郡縣則曰：「天下初定，百姓困窮也。」亢旱為災，則脩己以答天；甘露獻賀，則因瑞而致戒。毁鏤金之牀，損食肉之獸，謂聲色為伐性之斧，謂技巧為覆車之轍。
translation_en: …proclamations; he issued orders to instruct the people and statutes to regulate them. In a single preface to the Grand Pronouncement (Da Gao), he treated the occupations of the four classes of people in exhaustive detail, giving particular attention to the meaning of “loving virtue” and “fulfilling one’s allotted lifespan.” The means by which he ordered the enduring human relationships, established the sovereign’s supreme standard, and protected the myriad people were all rooted in the Way of Heaven and verified in human affairs. Can one say that he had not grasped the profound meaning of the Great Plan (Hong Fan)? Consider how, in advocating frugality in expenditure and care for the people, he drew upon Confucius’s words, and how he praised the purport of the Canons and Counsels for their clarity and ease of understanding. When discussing good and evil, he offered the admonition that weeds harm the grain seedlings; when discussing blame and praise, he distinguished the true worth of the worthy and the unworthy. He honored Mencius’s teachings on benevolence and righteousness and rejected Emperor Wu of Han’s pursuit of immortals. He praised Li Hang’s memorial on calamities and anomalies and censured Emperor Zhenzong of Song’s extravagance and grandiosity. In instructing his attendant officials, he said: “The people are impoverished and exhausted; they have not yet been able to recover and prosper.” In instructing the prefectures and counties, he said: “All under Heaven has only just been pacified, and the common people are in distress and poverty.” When prolonged drought brought disaster, he cultivated himself in response to Heaven; when congratulations were presented on the appearance of sweet dew, he took the auspicious sign as an occasion to issue warnings. He destroyed a bed ornamented with carved gold and reduced the number of meat-eating beasts he kept. He called music and sensual pleasures an axe that hews away at one’s moral nature, and ingenious craftsmanship the wheel ruts of an overturned carriage.…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
無優伶近狎之失無酣歌夜飲之歡
正宫無自縱之權妃嬪無寵恣之幸教
太子則欲其熟聞善言不邇詖行擇臺省都
督府之官以兼
東宫賛輔之職其所以明道術辨人才審治
體察民情崇敬畏戒逸欲嚴
内治定
國本皆由於身心而達於天下謂非有得於
大學之實者乎蓋嘗聞之文中子曰不學
===
書無以議制又嘗聞之西山真氏曰爲人
君而不知大學無以清出治之原我
聖祖並用之以收創業之明效而一時輔業之
臣相與都俞咨度以
制定不刊之典爲垂範無窮之謀誠以
聖學之源固深
聖心之用則妙上有以接三聖之道統下有以
開萬世之太平所以比隆於唐虞三代者
端在於是而所以示法於
punctuated: 無優伶近狎之失，無酣歌夜飲之歡。正宫無自縱之權，妃嬪無寵恣之幸。教太子，則欲其熟聞善言，不邇詖行；擇臺省都督府之官，以兼東宫賛輔之職。其所以明道術、辨人才、審治體、察民情、崇敬畏、戒逸欲、嚴内治、定國本，皆由於身心而達於天下，謂非有得於《大學》之實者乎？蓋嘗聞之文中子曰：「不學《書》，無以議制。」又嘗聞之西山真氏曰：「爲人君而不知《大學》，無以清出治之原。」我聖祖並用之，以收創業之明效，而一時輔業之臣，相與都俞咨度，以制定不刊之典，爲垂範無窮之謀。誠以聖學之源固深，聖心之用則妙，上有以接三聖之道統，下有以開萬世之太平。所以比隆於唐虞三代者，端在於是，而所以示法於
translation_en:
…He committed no fault of undue familiarity with entertainers and took no pleasure in drunken singing and nocturnal drinking. The empress had no power to indulge herself unchecked, and the consorts enjoyed no favor that allowed them to act without restraint. In educating the crown prince, he wished him to hear good words constantly and keep away from wayward conduct. He selected officials of the central administrative and censorial agencies and the Chief Military Commission to serve concurrently as advisers and assistants to the crown prince. His means of elucidating the Way and its arts, discerning talent, examining the essentials of government, understanding the people’s circumstances, cultivating reverence and awe, guarding against ease and desire, strictly regulating the inner palace, and securing the foundation of the state all proceeded from his own person and mind and extended to all under Heaven. Could one say that he had not grasped the substance of the Great Learning?

I have heard that Wenzhongzi said, “Without studying the Book of Documents, one cannot discuss institutions.” I have also heard Master Zhen of Xishan say, “If a ruler does not understand the Great Learning, he cannot purify the source from which good government issues.” Our sagely founding ancestor applied both, thereby achieving conspicuous results in founding the dynasty. The ministers who assisted his enterprise at that time joined in exchanges of assent, consultation, and deliberation to establish enduring statutes and devise plans that would provide a model forever. This was truly because the wellspring of his sagely learning was deep and the workings of his sagely mind were subtle. Looking back, he could carry forward the transmission of the Way from the Three Sages; looking ahead, he could inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations. It was precisely this that enabled him to equal the glory of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties, and it was this by which he provided a model for…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖子
神孫者亦無二道矣雖然人主之心斂之足以
妙衆理放之足以舉八埏但他岐之貳外
誘之私後宮盛色之溺讒邪利口之移養
之者無幾而攻之者甚衆夫以無幾之養
奪於甚衆之攻内之所操者無主故外之
作則者無法而欲其政之不紊者難矣是
以高宗之得傅說則望以格心之事成王
之詔羣臣亦期以示德之方卒之成中興
===
之功而光文武之業者良有以也後世願
治之君宜莫如漢之文帝唐之太宗矣蓋
文帝靳百金之費而已一臺之作示敦朴
之先而簡帷帳之文太宗言及稼穡之艱
難則務遵節儉言及閭閻之疾苦則議息
征徭是故刑措之化貞觀之治三代以下
之所無也然能脩清淨之道而不能不狃
於晁錯之刑名能詢鬼神之理而不能不
惑於新垣平之詭詐能燭譽樹之姦而不
punctuated:
聖子神孫者，亦無二道矣。雖然，人主之心，斂之足以妙衆理，放之足以舉八埏。但他岐之貳、外誘之私、後宮盛色之溺、讒邪利口之移，養之者無幾，而攻之者甚衆。夫以無幾之養，奪於甚衆之攻，内之所操者無主，故外之作則者無法，而欲其政之不紊者難矣。是以高宗之得傅說，則望以格心之事；成王之詔羣臣，亦期以示德之方。卒之成中興之功，而光文武之業者，良有以也。
後世願治之君，宜莫如漢之文帝、唐之太宗矣。蓋文帝靳百金之費，而已一臺之作，示敦朴之先，而簡帷帳之文；太宗言及稼穡之艱難，則務遵節儉，言及閭閻之疾苦，則議息征徭。是故刑措之化、貞觀之治，三代以下之所無也。然能脩清淨之道，而不能不狃於晁錯之刑名；能詢鬼神之理，而不能不惑於新垣平之詭詐；能燭譽樹之姦，而不
translation_en:
…there was likewise no other Way by which to provide a model for his sagely sons and divine grandsons. Nevertheless, when the ruler’s mind is gathered inward, it can comprehend the subtleties of all principles; when extended outward, it can encompass the eight bounds of the earth. Yet divided allegiance to divergent paths, selfish desires prompted by external temptations, infatuation with the beauties of the inner palace, and the sway of slanderous, wicked men with glib tongues provide countless assaults upon it, while the things that nourish it are few. When this scant nourishment is overwhelmed by so many assaults, what one holds inwardly has no master, and thus one’s outward conduct provides no proper model. It is then difficult to keep government from falling into disorder. Thus, when Gaozong obtained the services of Fu Yue, he looked to him to rectify his mind; when King Cheng issued instructions to his assembled ministers, he likewise expected them to show him the way of virtue. There was good reason why they ultimately achieved a restoration and brought lustre to the legacy of Kings Wen and Wu.
Among later rulers who aspired to good government, surely none surpassed Emperor Wen of Han and Taizong of Tang. Emperor Wen begrudged the expenditure of a hundred measures of gold and therefore halted the construction of a terrace; he took the lead in demonstrating simplicity and reduced the ornamentation of his curtains and hangings. Whenever Taizong spoke of the hardships of sowing and reaping, he strove to practise frugality; whenever he spoke of the sufferings of ordinary households, he discussed ending levies and corvée service. Thus, the transforming influence under which punishments were laid aside, and the good government of the Zhenguan reign, were unmatched since the Three Dynasties. Yet although Emperor Wen could cultivate the way of purity and tranquillity, he could not avoid becoming habituated to Chao Cuo’s doctrines of punishments and administrative accountability; although he could inquire into the principles governing ghosts and spirits, he could not avoid being deceived by Xinyuan Ping’s impostures. Although Taizong could discern the duplicity of praising a tree, he could not…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
能不牽於狐媚之愛能抑萬紀之規利而
不能謹於十漸之不終何者天性之仁雖
厚學問之力雖博而正心之實均未切耳
此我
祖訓持守之二言又爲百聖傳心之大要也敢
用爲
今日法
祖正心之獻謹對
第二問
===
同考試官學正方批此策正欲觀士子
事君使民之心志而此篇援古證
今出入帝王之途轍豈布衣而有
天下之慮者乎行將見用執此以
往可也得士如此良慶良慶
考試官教諭周批條答之餘而忠愛
拳拳是可與論世道者
考試官學正季批才氣橫逸識見超
banxin: 鄉試錄 六十一 李元陽
punctuated:
能不牽於狐媚之愛，能抑萬紀之規利，而不能謹於十漸之不終。何者？天性之仁雖厚，學問之力雖博，而正心之實均未切耳。此我祖訓持守之二言，又爲百聖傳心之大要也。敢用爲今日法祖正心之獻。謹對。
第二問
同考試官學正方批：此策正欲觀士子事君使民之心志，而此篇援古證今，出入帝王之途轍，豈布衣而有天下之慮者乎？行將見用，執此以往可也。得士如此，良慶良慶！
考試官教諭周批：條答之餘，而忠愛拳拳，是可與論世道者。
考試官學正季批：才氣橫逸，識見超
translation_en:
…could not help being swayed by affection for someone of foxlike charm; he could restrain Wanji’s pursuit of profit, yet could not guard against the failure to persevere illustrated by the “ten gradual failings.” Why was this? Although their innate benevolence was abundant and their learning extensive, neither had truly applied himself to rectifying the mind. Thus the two words in our ancestral instructions, “maintain” and “preserve,” are also the essential teaching transmitted from mind to mind by the hundred sages. I venture to offer this as a contribution toward following the ancestors and rectifying the mind today. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: This policy question was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ intentions concerning service to the ruler and employment of the people. This essay draws on antiquity to substantiate its arguments about the present and ranges through the paths followed by emperors and kings. Is its author not a commoner who nevertheless takes thought for all under Heaven? He will soon be appointed to service; he may proceed holding firmly to these principles. To obtain a scholar like this is truly cause for rejoicing, truly cause for rejoicing!
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Beyond answering point by point, he displays earnest loyalty and affection. Here is someone with whom one can discuss the moral and political condition of the age.
Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: His talent and spirit range freely; his insight surpasses…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
較場中之士少有及之者佳士也
參之前二塲允稱高薦
天下一氣也而伸縮由於心天下一體也
而動定由於心心也者君是也氣也者臣
是也體也者民是也心以使氣氣以使體
自然之勢也其心正則其氣順其體安此
亦自然之理也心蘊於中正耶邪耶人鮮
得而知也惟其發於言也則其邪正始可
得而見矣傳曰其心明乎正理則其言平
===
正通達此不易之定論也君之運天下也
亦然君正則其臣順而天下之民安且和
矣然人君高拱於穆清之上心之正與邪
焉天下未易測也聽其言也則其撫我虐
我也昭於人目盈於人耳矣孰謂詔令非
所以動天下之大幾也耶請因明問而復
之仰惟我
聖天子屬以倫序入繼
大統奉天即位改元一詔正往昔奸邪之誤
punctuated:
較場中之士，少有及之者，佳士也。參之前二塲，允稱高薦。
天下一氣也，而伸縮由於心；天下一體也，而動定由於心。心也者，君是也；氣也者，臣是也；體也者，民是也。心以使氣，氣以使體，自然之勢也。其心正，則其氣順，其體安，此亦自然之理也。心蘊於中，正耶邪耶，人鮮得而知也。惟其發於言也，則其邪正始可得而見矣。傳曰：「其心明乎正理，則其言平正通達。」此不易之定論也。君之運天下也亦然。君正，則其臣順，而天下之民安且和矣。然人君高拱於穆清之上，心之正與邪焉，天下未易測也。聽其言也，則其撫我、虐我也，昭於人目，盈於人耳矣。孰謂詔令非所以動天下之大幾也耶？請因明問而復之。仰惟我聖天子，屬以倫序入繼大統，奉天即位，改元一詔，正往昔奸邪之誤
translation_en:
…Compared with the other candidates in the examination hall, few can match him: he is an excellent scholar. Considered alongside his work in the preceding two sessions, he truly merits recommendation at a high rank.
All under Heaven is a single vital force, whose expansion and contraction proceed from the heart; all under Heaven is a single body, whose movement and repose proceed from the heart. The heart is the ruler; the vital force is his ministers; the body is the people. The heart directs the vital force, and the vital force directs the body: this is the natural disposition of things. When the heart is upright, the vital force flows harmoniously and the body is at ease. This, too, is a natural principle. The heart lies concealed within: whether it is upright or deviant, few can know. Only when it finds expression in speech can its deviation or uprightness begin to be seen. The commentary says: “When the heart clearly understands correct principle, its words are balanced, upright, coherent, and clear.” This is an unalterable judgment.
The ruler’s governance of all under Heaven is likewise. When the ruler is upright, his ministers are compliant, and the people throughout the realm are secure and harmonious. Yet the ruler sits with hands folded high above in the solemn purity of his court; whether his heart is upright or deviant is not readily fathomed by the world. Once people hear his words, however, whether he cherishes us or oppresses us becomes plain to their eyes and fills their ears. Who could say that edicts and commands are not the crucial means by which all under Heaven is moved? Allow me to reply in accordance with your illuminating question.
I reverently reflect that our sagely Son of Heaven, by his place in the order of imperial kinship, entered into succession to the imperial throne. In obedience to Heaven, he ascended the throne and changed the reign title. With a single edict, he corrected the way in which the treacherous and wicked of former days had misled …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
主申
祖宗舊章以告民其於諫止
遊巡之臣而被廢者則復其生者之官而加
之顯恤其沒者之後而加之贈此非成湯
顯忠遂良之德意也乎其於應濟征伐之
類而被擾者則蠲其往者之逋而不之追
寬其來者之稅而免之半此非武王散財
發粟之遺意也乎民年八十九十者賜予
有差使民知曰
===
朝廷之待老如此我何以不孝且敬乎官年
賜休乞休者存問有禮使民知曰
朝廷之優賢如此我何以不脩爾德乎將由
是而興起於孝將由是而勸勉於德而三
代之俗可跂而待也五帝之化可望而及
也邦其永昌不在于茲乎民生得其所則
元氣固矣傳曰民惟邦本本固邦寧此聖
王之訓也恐奉行者之未至則使風憲官
糾察之孰敢有廢閣者乎慮蒞事者之或
punctuated: 主，申祖宗舊章以告民。其於諫止遊巡之臣而被廢者，則復其生者之官而加之顯，恤其沒者之後而加之贈。此非成湯顯忠遂良之德意也乎？其於應濟征伐之類而被擾者，則蠲其往者之逋而不之追，寬其來者之稅而免之半。此非武王散財發粟之遺意也乎？民年八十九十者，賜予有差，使民知曰：「朝廷之待老如此，我何以不孝且敬乎？」官年賜休乞休者，存問有禮，使民知曰：「朝廷之優賢如此，我何以不脩爾德乎？」將由是而興起於孝，將由是而勸勉於德，而三代之俗可跂而待也，五帝之化可望而及也。邦其永昌，不在于茲乎？民生得其所，則元氣固矣。傳曰：「民惟邦本，本固邦寧。」此聖王之訓也。恐奉行者之未至，則使風憲官糾察之，孰敢有廢閣者乎？慮蒞事者之或
translation_en: …the ruler, and reaffirmed the established statutes of the imperial ancestors, proclaiming them to the people. As for ministers dismissed for remonstrating against imperial tours, he restored those still living to office and bestowed further distinction upon them; he provided for the descendants of those who had died and granted the deceased posthumous honors. Is this not the benevolent intent of Cheng Tang, who honored the loyal and advanced the worthy? As for those subjected to exactions for supplying military campaigns and similar undertakings, he canceled their past arrears, forgoing collection, and lightened their future taxes by remitting half. Is this not the surviving spirit of King Wu’s distribution of wealth and opening of the grain stores? To commoners aged eighty or ninety he granted gifts in varying amounts, so that the people would understand and say: “Since the court treats the elderly in this way, how could I fail to be filial and respectful?” To officials granted retirement on account of age [?], or who had requested retirement, he extended solicitous inquiries with due ceremony, so that the people would understand and say: “Since the court favors the worthy in this way, how could I fail to cultivate your virtue [?]?” Thus they will be stirred to filial devotion and encouraged in virtue. The customs of the Three Dynasties may then be eagerly awaited, and the transforming influence of the Five Emperors may be hoped for and attained. Does not the enduring prosperity of the state depend upon this? When the people’s livelihoods are secure, the state’s vital force is firmly established. The transmitted text says: “The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace.” This is the teaching of the sage kings. Fearing that those charged with implementing these measures might fall short, he ordered the censorial officials to investigate them. Who would dare leave the measures unimplemented? Concerned lest those attending to official affairs might…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
怠則使分道官考驗之孰敢有不振舉者
乎即是而之焉主之以誠心加之以持久
二帝三王之治可復見也雖典謨之相得
而相告者即此心也商之誓則淺於前日
君民之心矣周之末則詛且慝而怨焉於
是刑之革之矣革且不從而上下之心背
馳矣秦漢而下日趨於非不足論矣是固
時使之然亦教化不明之過也君有作臣
有守則世有教化矣有教化自不患乎世
===
無善治也是故教化者治之本也君臣者
教化之本也故曰爲政在人取人以身孔
子之治天下如斯而已矣昔者漢高曰聞
王者莫高於周文覇者莫高於齊桓皆得
賢人而成名賢士大夫有肯從我游者吾
能尊顯之夫是詔也乃諳練閱歷之言不
有是心漢幾何而能成乎天下之士始欣
欣然有詩書禮樂之願而漢之命脉生矣
漢武曰朕即位以來所爲狂悖使天下愁
punctuated:
怠，則使分道官考驗之，孰敢有不振舉者乎？即是而之焉，主之以誠心，加之以持久，二帝三王之治可復見也。雖典謨之相得而相告者，即此心也。商之誓則淺於前日君民之心矣；周之末則詛且慝而怨焉，於是刑之、革之矣。革且不從，而上下之心背馳矣。秦漢而下，日趨於非，不足論矣。是固時使之然，亦教化不明之過也。君有作，臣有守，則世有教化矣；有教化，自不患乎世無善治也。是故教化者，治之本也；君臣者，教化之本也。故曰：「爲政在人，取人以身。」孔子之治天下，如斯而已矣。
昔者漢高曰：「聞王者莫高於周文，覇者莫高於齊桓，皆得賢人而成名。賢士大夫有肯從我游者，吾能尊顯之。」夫是詔也，乃諳練閱歷之言。不有是心，漢幾何而能成乎？天下之士始欣欣然有詩書禮樂之願，而漢之命脉生矣。漢武曰：「朕即位以來，所爲狂悖，使天下愁
translation_en:
…become negligent, have the officials assigned to the several circuits examine their performance. Who would dare fail to carry out these measures vigorously? Proceed along this course, grounding it in sincerity and sustaining it with perseverance, and the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings may be seen again. Even the mutual understanding and counsel recorded in the Canons and Counsels sprang from this same intention.
