In the Oaths of Shang, however, the bond between ruler and people had grown shallower than in earlier days. By the end of Zhou, there were curses, wickedness, and resentment; consequently, punishments and corrective measures were imposed. Yet even with correction, people would not obey, and the intentions of those above and below diverged. From Qin and Han onward, things moved daily further toward error and scarcely merit discussion. This was certainly a result of the times, but it was also the fault of failing to make moral instruction clear. When the ruler initiates and his ministers uphold his work, moral instruction prevails in the world. With moral instruction, there is naturally no need to fear that the world will lack good government. Thus moral instruction is the foundation of government, and ruler and ministers are the foundation of moral instruction. Hence the saying: “The conduct of government depends on men; obtaining men depends on one’s own person.” This, and nothing more, was Confucius’s way of governing the world.
Formerly, Emperor Gao of Han said: “I have heard that among true kings none surpassed King Wen of Zhou, and among hegemons none surpassed Duke Huan of Qi. Both won their renown by obtaining worthy men. If there are worthy scholars and gentlemen willing to associate with me, I can honor them and raise them to distinction.” This edict spoke from seasoned experience. Without such an intention, how could the Han have succeeded? Only then did the scholars of the realm joyfully begin to aspire to the Poetry, the Documents, rites, and music, and the lifeblood of the Han began to flow. Emperor Wu of Han said: “Since I ascended the throne, my actions have been reckless and perverse, causing all under Heaven distress…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
苦不可追悔今事有傷害百姓糜費天下
者悉罷之夫是詔也乃悔悟深切之言不
有是言漢幾於不可知也天下之民始帖
帖然無背叛反復之想而漢之肌膚固矣
夫往者鑒式於今者也來者取法於今者
也商書曰事不師古匪說攸聞使傅說而
愚人焉則亦已矣如曰天賚中興之賢佐
則其言固可信矣周書亦曰慎厥麗乃勸
厥民使成湯而庸君焉則亦已矣如曰天
錫一代之聖主則其言固可信矣愚也樂
===
育
明時躬逢
聖主尚當以緝熈
聖敬終始典于學為
獻則德可久業可大而愚芹曝之誠舍此無
敢言者也庶可免隨何遇漢文而不能興
文之誚雖然上有明君則下有良臣臣之
能為臣又在其君致之也兹惟時哉謹對
punctuated:
苦，不可追悔。今事有傷害百姓、糜費天下者，悉罷之。」夫是詔也，乃悔悟深切之言。不有是言，漢幾於不可知也。天下之民始帖帖然，無背叛反復之想，而漢之肌膚固矣。
夫往者，鑒式於今者也；來者，取法於今者也。《商書》曰：「事不師古，匪說攸聞。」使傅說而愚人焉，則亦已矣；如曰天賚中興之賢佐，則其言固可信矣。《周書》亦曰：「慎厥麗，乃勸厥民。」使成湯而庸君焉，則亦已矣；如曰天錫一代之聖主，則其言固可信矣。
愚也樂育明時，躬逢聖主，尚當以緝熈聖敬、終始典于學為獻，則德可久，業可大。而愚芹曝之誠，舍此無敢言者也。庶可免隨何遇漢文而不能興文之誚。雖然，上有明君，則下有良臣；臣之能為臣，又在其君致之也。兹惟時哉！謹對。
translation_en:
…suffering; regret cannot undo it. Henceforth, abolish all undertakings that harm the common people or squander the resources of the realm.” This edict expressed profound remorse and awakening. Without these words, the fate of the Han would have been nearly beyond knowing. Only then did the people of the realm begin to settle peacefully, without thoughts of rebellion or renewed disaffection, and the flesh and skin of the Han became secure.
The past provides a mirror and model for the present; the future will take its example from the present. The Documents of Shang says: “To conduct affairs without taking antiquity as one’s teacher is something I, Yue, have never heard of.” If Fu Yue had been a fool, we might leave it at that. But if he was a worthy assistant bestowed by Heaven to bring about a restoration, then his words surely deserve belief. The Documents of Zhou also says: “Be careful whom you associate with; thereby encourage your people.” If Cheng Tang had been a mediocre ruler, we might leave it at that. But if he was a sage sovereign bestowed by Heaven upon his age, then his words surely deserve belief.
In my ignorance, I have enjoyed nurturing instruction in this enlightened age and have personally encountered a sage sovereign. I should therefore offer this counsel: continually brighten your sagely reverence, and from beginning to end take learning as your constant guide. Then your virtue can endure and your achievements can become great. Such is my humble sincerity in offering celery and the warmth of the sun; beyond this I dare offer no other words. Perhaps I may thus escape the reproach that Sui He encountered Emperor Wen of Han yet could not promote civil culture [?]. Nevertheless, when there is an enlightened ruler above, there are worthy ministers below; whether ministers can fulfill their duties also depends on their ruler bringing this about. Now indeed is the time! Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第三問
趙汝濂
同考試官訓導鄭批前輩業儒者兼律
令習之故學爲有用是篇考究詳
明斷制精當推之於政而可行本
之於經而有據非平日諳練世故
决不至此子其有志於致
君堯舜者乎
考試官教諭周批策貴警拔彬蔚如
===
前輩對策何甞拘拘對偶而文自
可觀此作其庶幾矣
考試官學正季批全篇雖不爲劘刻
斬絶之言而其鋒自不可犯亦可
謂筆底秋霜者
刑以弼教聖人不得已用之也然有法焉
有情焉法固在所當執情亦不可不原雖
有畫一之法每有不一之情情原故誤之
分法歸輕重之等如是或决遣之或收贖
punctuated:
第三問
趙汝濂

同考試官訓導鄭批：「前輩業儒者兼律令習之，故學爲有用。是篇考究詳明，斷制精當，推之於政而可行，本之於經而有據。非平日諳練世故，决不至此。子其有志於致君堯舜者乎？」

考試官教諭周批：「策貴警拔彬蔚。如前輩對策，何甞拘拘對偶，而文自可觀？此作其庶幾矣。」

考試官學正季批：「全篇雖不爲劘刻斬絶之言，而其鋒自不可犯，亦可謂筆底秋霜者。」

刑以弼教，聖人不得已用之也。然有法焉，有情焉。法固在所當執，情亦不可不原。雖有畫一之法，每有不一之情。情原故誤之分，法歸輕重之等。如是，或决遣之，或收贖
translation_en:
Third Question
Zhao Rulian

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: “Earlier generations of Confucian scholars studied the statutes and ordinances as well, so their learning had practical use. This essay’s investigations are thorough and clear, and its judgments precise and apt. Its proposals can be put into practice in government and find support in the Classics. Without habitual familiarity with worldly affairs, one could never attain this level. Might you aspire to bring your ruler to the stature of Yao and Shun?”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “A policy essay is valued for its striking insight, distinction, refinement, and richness. When did the policy responses of earlier generations ever fuss over parallel phrasing? Yet their writing was naturally worthy of admiration. This composition comes close to that standard.”

Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: “Although nowhere in this essay does the author resort to cutting or categorical pronouncements, its edge cannot be challenged. One might indeed say that autumn frost issues from beneath his brush.”

Punishment supports moral instruction; the sages employ it only when they have no alternative. Yet there is the law, and there are the circumstances of the case. The law must certainly be upheld, but the circumstances must also be investigated. Although the law is uniform, the circumstances are often different. In examining the circumstances, distinguish deliberate wrongdoing from inadvertent error; in applying the law, assign the appropriate degree of severity or leniency. Proceeding thus, one may either pronounce sentence and carry it out, or accept payment in redemption of punishment…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之而先王天討之公欽恤之仁兩全而無
害矣嗚呼天地之大德曰生矣然春生秋
殺旣潤之以風雨復鼓之以雷霆何甞專
於生也聖人效法於是乎制刑焉然刑期
無刑辟以止辟而生意亦未甞不存乎其
間也夫刑有五而干犯在所弗宥法之正
也其見之虞典有曰金作贖刑者蔡氏以
爲刑莫輕於鞭扑蓋官府學校之所用耳
於是許贖所以養其愧耻之心也若吕刑
===
贖法蓋五刑之中疑其可赦者不遽赦之
姑取其鍰以示罰耳繼曰閱實其罪則無
可疑者惡能逃乎自是贖罰之途旣開遷
就之謀紛起漢宣帝因討西羌兵食告乏
張敞議令諸州非殺人及盜者皆入穀贖
罪以若所爲免轉輸之勞實邊徼之備亦
何不可而蕭望之以爲如此則富者得生
貧者獨死恐開利路以傷治化是固老臣
經世之慮而事體輕重之間權之熟矣宋
punctuated: 之，而先王天討之公、欽恤之仁兩全而無害矣。嗚呼！天地之大德曰生矣，然春生秋殺，旣潤之以風雨，復鼓之以雷霆，何甞專於生也？聖人效法於是乎制刑焉，然刑期無刑，辟以止辟，而生意亦未甞不存乎其間也。夫刑有五，而干犯在所弗宥，法之正也。其見之虞典有曰「金作贖刑」者，蔡氏以爲刑莫輕於鞭扑，蓋官府學校之所用耳，於是許贖，所以養其愧耻之心也。若吕刑贖法，蓋五刑之中疑其可赦者，不遽赦之，姑取其鍰以示罰耳。繼曰：「閱實其罪。」則無可疑者惡能逃乎？自是贖罰之途旣開，遷就之謀紛起。漢宣帝因討西羌，兵食告乏，張敞議令諸州非殺人及盜者皆入穀贖罪。以若所爲，免轉輸之勞，實邊徼之備，亦何不可？而蕭望之以爲如此則富者得生，貧者獨死，恐開利路以傷治化。是固老臣經世之慮，而事體輕重之間權之熟矣。宋
translation_en:
…them, thereby preserving without detriment both the impartiality with which the former kings carried out Heaven’s punishments and their benevolent concern for those facing punishment. Ah! The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life-giving. Yet spring brings growth and autumn brings death; after nourishing things with wind and rain, they stir them with thunder. Have they ever concerned themselves solely with giving life? The sages followed this example in establishing punishments. Yet punishment aims at bringing about the absence of punishment, and penalties serve to put an end to offenses: the life-giving intent has never been absent from them.

There are five punishments, and that those who commit offenses should not be pardoned is the proper rule of law. As for the statement in the Canon of Yu, “Let metal serve to redeem punishment,” Master Cai explains that no punishments are lighter than whipping and beating, which were used in government offices and schools. Allowing redemption in such cases served to nurture the offenders’ sense of shame. As for the rules of redemption in the Punishments of Lü, where an offense subject to one of the five punishments was doubtful and might warrant pardon, the offender was not immediately pardoned; instead, a fine in units of huan was collected to signify punishment. The text continues, “Examine and establish the facts of the offense.” How, then, could those whose guilt admitted of no doubt escape?

Once this avenue of redeeming punishment had opened, schemes for accommodating offenders arose in profusion. During Emperor Xuan of Han’s campaign against the Western Qiang, provisions for the troops ran short. Zhang Chang proposed that throughout the provinces all offenders other than murderers and thieves be allowed to redeem their offenses by delivering grain. What objection could there be to such a measure, which spared the labor of transporting supplies and replenished the frontier’s reserves? Xiao Wangzhi, however, argued that this would allow the rich to live while the poor alone died, and feared that opening an avenue for material gain would damage good government and moral transformation. This was indeed a veteran minister’s concern for governing the realm, reflecting a mature weighing of the relative importance of the matters at issue. In the Song…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
仁宗以先王用法簡約後世刑用滋章令
天下或有冒刑犯禁過誤可憫者以穀麥
錢帛贖焉此詔一下或以爲寬慈之仁稀
濶之典可以常行而識者以爲富人皆得
贖罪貧者曷能自免豈朝廷用法之意哉
是固大臣體國之忠而舉措得失之辨籌
之審矣夫張敞建議不及賊盜殺人仁宗
詔令止言犯禁過誤而當時臣屬尚以爲
非則贖罰一節果無益於世敎明矣我
===
太祖高皇帝裁定律令實上稽天理中順時宜
下合人心立萬世之準繩爲百王之憲度
者至於贖法雖沿唐舊而就中斟酌事情
權衡輕重實脗合堯舜慎獄好生之意自
制律以來所未有者伏睹
聖祖諭刑部有曰自今十惡非常赦所原者則
云重刑其餘雜犯許聽收贖至
太宗文皇帝又令死罪情重者依律處治情輕
及公罪皆得收贖仰惟
punctuated:
仁宗以先王用法簡約，後世刑用滋章，令天下或有冒刑犯禁、過誤可憫者，以穀麥錢帛贖焉。此詔一下，或以爲寬慈之仁、稀濶之典，可以常行；而識者以爲富人皆得贖罪，貧者曷能自免？豈朝廷用法之意哉？是固大臣體國之忠，而舉措得失之辨，籌之審矣。夫張敞建議不及賊盜殺人，仁宗詔令止言犯禁過誤，而當時臣屬尚以爲非，則贖罰一節果無益於世敎明矣。
我太祖高皇帝裁定律令，實上稽天理，中順時宜，下合人心，立萬世之準繩，爲百王之憲度者。至於贖法，雖沿唐舊，而就中斟酌事情，權衡輕重，實脗合堯舜慎獄好生之意，自制律以來所未有者。伏睹聖祖諭刑部有曰：「自今十惡非常赦所原者，則云重刑；其餘雜犯，許聽收贖。」至太宗文皇帝，又令死罪情重者依律處治，情輕及公罪皆得收贖。仰惟
translation_en:
…Emperor Renzong considered that the former kings had applied the law simply and sparingly, whereas in later ages penal provisions had grown increasingly elaborate. He ordered that throughout the realm, those who incurred punishment by violating prohibitions, or whose inadvertent offenses merited compassion, should be allowed to redeem their penalties with grain, wheat, money, or silk. Once this edict was issued, some regarded it as an act of generous benevolence and an exceptionally lenient provision that could be applied permanently. Discerning men, however, held that if the wealthy could all redeem their offenses, how could the poor secure their own release? Could this be the court’s intention in applying the law? This was indeed the loyalty of great ministers who took the interests of the state to heart; they had carefully weighed the merits and faults of such measures. Zhang Chang’s proposal did not extend to robbery, theft, or homicide, and Renzong’s edict spoke only of violations of prohibitions and inadvertent offenses. Yet even then their ministers considered these measures wrong. It is thus clear that the redemption of penalties indeed offers no benefit to the moral instruction of society.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao established the statutes and ordinances by consulting Heaven’s principles above, accommodating the needs of the times in between, and conforming to the people’s hearts below. He established a standard for all ages and a model for all sovereigns. As for the provisions governing redemption, although he followed Tang precedents, he carefully considered the circumstances of cases and weighed their relative gravity. This truly accorded with Yao and Shun’s concern for caution in judicial proceedings and their love of life, to a degree unprecedented since statutes were first enacted. I have reverently read the sacred founder’s instruction to the Ministry of Justice: “Henceforth, offenses among the Ten Abominations that are not pardoned under ordinary amnesties shall be deemed subject to severe punishment; for other miscellaneous offenses, redemption payments may be accepted.” In the reign of Emperor Taizong Wen, it was further ordered that capital offenses involving grave circumstances should be dealt with according to the statutes, while those involving less serious circumstances, as well as offenses committed in an official capacity, could all be redeemed by payment. Reverently considering…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
祖宗立法之意止以贖罪待情輕者而重罪未
嘗寬貸奈何在外所司罔思體悉但知儲
蓄不審罪情積財多者爲良吏減罪衆者
爲陰德嗚呼
朝廷何少此毫芒錢穀而翻致干犯愈衆法
柅不行哉先王之制刑與
祖宗之律令果如是乎否也愚聞之書曰天討
有罪又曰天齊于民蓋用刑之權出於天
人君與有司特奉行之耳旣知天法又可
===
任情以高下於其間乎夫有罪不刑雖堯
舜不能以化天下以漢高帝約法三章猶
曰殺人者死若不論情之輕重雖賊盜殺
人以至於罪惡滔天者一槩移情就法以
利贖之則刑不出於天而秖爲姦邪市恩
之具罪不據乎律而翻爲豪强解脫之資
決遣皆貧窮而富饒獲免配没皆寒苦而
雄黠得安古之狃于姦宄敗常亂俗三細
不宥者後世皆夤緣請託而曲從輕典矣
punctuated:
祖宗立法之意，止以贖罪待情輕者，而重罪未嘗寬貸。奈何在外所司罔思體悉，但知儲蓄，不審罪情，積財多者爲良吏，減罪衆者爲陰德。嗚呼！朝廷何少此毫芒錢穀，而翻致干犯愈衆，法柅不行哉？先王之制刑與祖宗之律令，果如是乎？否也。
愚聞之，《書》曰：「天討有罪。」又曰：「天齊于民。」蓋用刑之權出於天，人君與有司特奉行之耳。旣知天法，又可任情以高下於其間乎？夫有罪不刑，雖堯舜不能以化天下。以漢高帝約法三章，猶曰：「殺人者死。」若不論情之輕重，雖賊盜殺人，以至於罪惡滔天者，一槩移情就法，以利贖之，則刑不出於天，而秖爲姦邪市恩之具；罪不據乎律，而翻爲豪强解脫之資。決遣皆貧窮，而富饒獲免；配没皆寒苦，而雄黠得安。古之狃于姦宄、敗常亂俗、三細不宥者，後世皆夤緣請託，而曲從輕典矣。
translation_en:
…the intention of the imperial ancestors in establishing the law was to allow redemption of punishment only for those whose offenses involved mitigating circumstances; serious offenses were never treated leniently. Why, then, do the responsible authorities outside the capital give no thought to understanding this intention, but concern themselves only with accumulating revenue, without examining the circumstances of offenses? Those who amass the most wealth are regarded as good officials, and reducing punishments for many is considered an act of hidden virtue. Alas! How could the court be so short of this trifling amount of money and grain that it should instead cause violations to multiply and the law’s restraints to become ineffective? Were the punishments instituted by the former kings and the statutes and ordinances of the imperial ancestors really like this? They were not.
I have heard these words from the Book of Documents: “Heaven punishes the guilty.” It also says: “Heaven brings order to the people.” The authority to impose punishments comes from Heaven; the ruler and the responsible officials merely carry it out. Once they recognize this as Heaven’s law, can they arbitrarily increase or reduce punishments within it? If the guilty go unpunished, even Yao and Shun could not transform the realm through moral influence. Even Emperor Gao of Han, when he reduced the laws to three articles, still declared: “Those who kill shall die.” If, without considering whether the circumstances are mitigating or grave, officials uniformly distort the circumstances to fit the law and permit redemption through payment—even for robbers and murderers, and those whose wickedness reaches to Heaven—then punishment no longer proceeds from Heaven, but becomes merely a means for the wicked to purchase favor. The treatment of offenses no longer rests on the statutes, but instead becomes a resource through which the powerful obtain release. Those sentenced and dispatched for punishment are all poor, while the wealthy escape; those subjected to penal assignment or confiscation are all destitute, while the powerful and cunning remain secure. Those who in antiquity persisted in wrongdoing, subverted established norms, and corrupted customs, and whose offenses were not pardoned even when committed three times and minor [?], all obtain preferential treatment in later ages through connections and intercession, with the law improperly bent toward lighter penalties.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
良可慨夫况又所贖之金不資軍國之用
或充貪墨之囊考之周禮貨罰入於司兵
蓋以為治兵之工直也今則皆如是否乎
噫法以止姦刑以繩慝使有罪者皆得以
利免則人皆曰吾金多矣何畏乎官司吾
謀巧矣何憂乎斧鉞汲汲焉惟利之務盈
元姦鉅蠹何憚而不為惡乎此所以犯者
接踵人心弗平而甚失先王明刑弼教之
意也昔人謂何以孝弟為財多而光榮蓋
===
亦有感於是矣然贖法亦律之不廢者若
不失先王制刑之意上體
祖宗欽恤之仁必如何而可也盍考諸書乎舜
典曰宥過無大刑故無小呂刑曰上刑適
輕下服下刑適重上服使法輕而情可惡
矣必寘於罪以為豪橫之戒有力不必論
也法重而情可憫矣或令收贖以開自新
之路正典自不廢也如此則咸知有意干
彞者莫能逃利刃無心觸法者亦得以改
punctuated:
良可慨夫！况又所贖之金不資軍國之用，或充貪墨之囊。考之《周禮》，貨罰入於司兵，蓋以為治兵之工直也。今則皆如是，否乎？噫！法以止姦，刑以繩慝，使有罪者皆得以利免，則人皆曰：「吾金多矣，何畏乎官司？吾謀巧矣，何憂乎斧鉞？」汲汲焉惟利之務，盈元姦鉅蠹，何憚而不為惡乎？此所以犯者接踵，人心弗平，而甚失先王明刑弼教之意也。昔人謂：「何以孝弟為？財多而光榮。」蓋亦有感於是矣。
然贖法亦律之不廢者，若不失先王制刑之意，上體祖宗欽恤之仁，必如何而可也？盍考諸書乎？《舜典》曰：「宥過無大，刑故無小。」《呂刑》曰：「上刑適輕，下服；下刑適重，上服。」使法輕而情可惡矣，必寘於罪，以為豪橫之戒，有力不必論也。法重而情可憫矣，或令收贖，以開自新之路，正典自不廢也。如此，則咸知有意干彞者莫能逃利刃，無心觸法者亦得以改
translation_en:
How truly lamentable! Moreover, the money paid in redemption of punishment does not support military and state expenditure, but may instead fill the purses of corrupt officials. According to the Rites of Zhou, monetary penalties were paid to the Director of Weapons, presumably to cover the wages of those making weapons. Is this still invariably the case today? Alas! Laws serve to stop wrongdoing, and punishments to restrain wickedness. If all the guilty can secure exemption through money, everyone will say: “I have plenty of gold; why should I fear the authorities? My schemes are clever; why should I worry about the executioner’s axe?” Eagerly pursuing profit alone, these great villains and monstrous parasites [?]—what scruple would keep them from doing evil? This is why offenders follow one another in succession, people feel injustice, and the former kings’ intention of making punishments clear to support moral instruction is so gravely betrayed. Someone in former times said: “What use are filial piety and brotherly deference? Wealth brings glory and honor.” This, too, was surely prompted by such circumstances.
Yet redemption of punishment is also a provision that the legal code retains. What must be done to preserve the former kings’ intention in establishing punishments and to embody the imperial ancestors’ benevolence in treating penal matters with reverence and compassion? Why not examine the documents? The Canon of Shun says: “Pardon inadvertent offenses, however great; punish deliberate offenses, however small.” The Punishments of Lü says: “When an offense carrying a heavier punishment warrants mitigation, apply the lighter penalty; when an offense carrying a lighter punishment warrants aggravation, apply the heavier penalty.” If the statutory penalty is light but the circumstances are abhorrent, the offender must be punished as a warning to the powerful and overbearing; his means need not enter into consideration. If the statutory penalty is heavy but the circumstances merit compassion, redemption may be permitted to open a path to self-reform; the established code will thereby remain intact. In this way, all will know that those who deliberately violate the enduring norms cannot escape the keen blade, while those who unintentionally transgress the law may also be allowed to turn over …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
絃貧富同刑强弱胥懼人情悉體大法固
存必如此而後謂之明刑必如此而不失
祖宗御世防姦之意抑究而言之又在乎所司
之公明剛正也惟公則輕重適平而自不
偏於私惟明則隱微洞照而自不流於枉
剛則不徇時而徇理之中正則不惟情而
惟法之執否則剖斷未真操持未定縱出
有罪虐入無辜傷天地之和玩經常之典
關係國家誠非細故此書所以簡重司政
===
典獄而惓惓於非佞惟良之訓也嗚呼人
君用人可不慎與愚生章句迂疎罔知刑
律敢掇拾平日所聞以為明問復諒執事
亦原其未學而不深罪之也
第四問
呂鳳池
考試官教諭周批歷數古人之學如
對面談而商確焉者且歸宿于責
志深得聖賢心事豈亦用心于內
punctuated:
絃，貧富同刑，强弱胥懼，人情悉體，大法固存。必如此而後謂之明刑，必如此而不失祖宗御世防姦之意。抑究而言之，又在乎所司之公明剛正也。惟公則輕重適平，而自不偏於私；惟明則隱微洞照，而自不流於枉；剛則不徇時而徇理之中，正則不惟情而惟法之執。否則剖斷未真，操持未定，縱出有罪，虐入無辜，傷天地之和，玩經常之典，關係國家，誠非細故。此《書》所以簡重司政典獄，而惓惓於非佞惟良之訓也。嗚呼！人君用人，可不慎與？愚生章句迂疎，罔知刑律，敢掇拾平日所聞，以為明問復，諒執事亦原其未學，而不深罪之也。
第四問
呂鳳池
考試官教諭周批：歷數古人之學，如對面談而商確焉者，且歸宿于責志，深得聖賢心事，豈亦用心于內
translation_en:
…mend their ways. Poor and rich would face the same punishments, and strong and weak alike would stand in fear. Human circumstances would be fully considered, while the great laws remained intact. Only thus could punishments be called discerning; only thus could the intent of the imperial ancestors in governing the realm and preventing wrongdoing be preserved. Yet, pursued to its root, this also depends on the impartiality, discernment, firmness, and uprightness of the responsible officials. Impartiality ensures that severity and leniency are properly balanced, without bias toward private interests; discernment illuminates what is hidden and subtle, preventing injustice. Firmness means following the proper balance of principle rather than bending to the times; uprightness means holding fast to the law rather than being guided by personal feeling. Otherwise, judgments will lack accuracy and resolve will be uncertain: the guilty will be indulgently released and the innocent cruelly convicted, injuring the harmony of Heaven and Earth and treating enduring statutes lightly. This concerns the state and is certainly no small matter. That is why the Book of Documents lays such weight on selecting those who administer government and oversee prisons, and earnestly repeats the injunction to choose the virtuous rather than the glib. Alas! Can a ruler fail to exercise care in employing men? I, an ignorant student, am pedantic and ill-informed, occupied with textual explication and knowing nothing of penal law. I venture to gather what I have heard in ordinary study as a reply to your illuminating question, trusting that you will excuse my lack of learning and not condemn me too severely.
Fourth Question
Lü Fengchi
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: He recounts the learning of the ancients one by one, as though discussing and weighing it with them face to face. Moreover, he ultimately returns to demanding resolve of oneself [?], profoundly grasping the intentions of the sages and worthies. Might he too have applied himself inwardly …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而有得者乎
考試官學正季批開闔抑揚若王良
之御見馬而不見路真擅塲手也
置之高選良有光于主司
性之囿於氣也其賦同學之變乎氣也其
功大氣者人所賴以生者也而不能無清
濁厚薄之殊性者人所禀以為人之理也
則固無古今聖愚之異惟其性之同也是
以人皆可以為堯舜惟其氣之殊也是以
===
必資於學焉學也者反其同而變其異之
道也此聖人善憂天下後世而為之立此
法也粵稽古堯舜孟子所謂性之也其為
聖之道故不待於學亦未嘗廢學也觀其
曰欽明文思曰允恭克讓此眾人所可見
之德容也然其中心恆如不少間斷雖出
於自然即此便是學之道也自禹湯文武
之為君臯陶伊傅周召之為臣則皆孜孜
以學為言矣曰綠圖曰務成曰甘盤之數
punctuated:
而有得者乎？
考試官學正季批：開闔抑揚，若王良之御，見馬而不見路，真擅塲手也。置之高選，良有光于主司。
性之囿於氣也，其賦同；學之變乎氣也，其功大。氣者，人所賴以生者也，而不能無清濁厚薄之殊；性者，人所禀以為人之理也，則固無古今聖愚之異。惟其性之同也，是以人皆可以為堯舜；惟其氣之殊也，是以必資於學焉。學也者，反其同而變其異之道也。此聖人善憂天下後世而為之立此法也。粵稽古，堯舜，孟子所謂性之也。其為聖之道，故不待於學，亦未嘗廢學也。觀其曰欽明文思，曰允恭克讓，此眾人所可見之德容也。然其中心恆如不少間斷，雖出於自然，即此便是學之道也。自禹湯文武之為君，臯陶伊傅周召之為臣，則皆孜孜以學為言矣。曰綠圖，曰務成，曰甘盤之數
translation_en:
…and thereby attained understanding?
Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: “In its opening and closing, restraint and emphasis, this essay is like Wang Liang’s charioteering: one sees the horses but not the road. Truly, this is the work of a master of the examination field. To rank it among the highest selections indeed brings credit to the presiding examiners.”
Although human nature is circumscribed by vital substance (qi), its endowment is the same in everyone; learning’s achievement in transforming that vital substance is great. Vital substance is what people depend upon for life, yet it inevitably differs in clarity and turbidity, thickness and thinness. Human nature is the principle people receive that makes them human; in this there is fundamentally no difference between ancient and modern people, sages and fools. Precisely because their nature is the same, everyone can become a Yao or a Shun; precisely because their vital substance differs, they must rely upon learning. Learning is the way to return to what is common and transform what differs. The sages, in their provident concern for the world and later generations, therefore established this method for them.
Looking back into antiquity, Yao and Shun were those whom Mengzi described as possessing virtue by nature. Their way of becoming sages thus did not depend upon learning, yet they never abandoned learning either. Consider the descriptions “reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful” and “truly respectful and capable of yielding”: these were manifestations of virtue visible to everyone. Yet within their hearts this constancy suffered not the slightest interruption. Although it arose spontaneously, this itself was the way of learning. From Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as rulers to Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao as ministers, all spoke tirelessly of learning. Those several figures named Lütu [?], Wucheng, and Gan Pan…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
君子者皆相資以學之人也周衰道廢異
端並興幸而天心篤愛乎斯人神物黙相
乎吾道時則有若孔子之聖者出雖不得
堯舜之位以澤當時然已得堯舜之傳以
澤後世而吾道吾學有主矣春風沂水所
樂者堯舜之氣象秋月尼山所談者堯舜
之文章師友雍雍道義侃侃立正學之高
壇拓正學之大道揭正學之弘名歸乎此
者曰吾黨之徒也背乎此者曰異端之徒
===
也以此立法猶有異言者有如李斯田子
方之徒皆借名吾道自成一家牢不可破
而吾孔氏之說不能不為之亂也使天下
貿貿焉卒無所之而吾道隱矣迨夫天運
轉乎上而五星則聚于奎人事恊于下而
諸儒則出乎世濂水之源一開月岩之光
遂揭太極一圖天理明而人事顯矣二程
繼之相與闡明此學清風一嘘率土四應
則吾道之氣復完於天地間矣朱子起焉
punctuated:
君子者，皆相資以學之人也。周衰道廢，異端並興。幸而天心篤愛乎斯人，神物黙相乎吾道，時則有若孔子之聖者出。雖不得堯舜之位以澤當時，然已得堯舜之傳以澤後世，而吾道吾學有主矣。春風沂水，所樂者堯舜之氣象；秋月尼山，所談者堯舜之文章。師友雍雍，道義侃侃，立正學之高壇，拓正學之大道，揭正學之弘名。歸乎此者，曰吾黨之徒也；背乎此者，曰異端之徒也。以此立法，猶有異言者，有如李斯、田子方之徒，皆借名吾道，自成一家，牢不可破，而吾孔氏之說不能不為之亂也。使天下貿貿焉，卒無所之，而吾道隱矣。
迨夫天運轉乎上，而五星則聚于奎；人事恊于下，而諸儒則出乎世。濂水之源一開，月岩之光遂揭。太極一圖，天理明而人事顯矣。二程繼之，相與闡明此學，清風一嘘，率土四應，則吾道之氣復完於天地間矣。朱子起焉。
translation_en:
…these gentlemen were all men who aided one another in learning. As the Zhou declined and the Way fell into disuse, heterodox teachings arose together. Fortunately, Heaven profoundly cherished these people, and spiritual powers silently assisted our Way. At that time a sage such as Confucius appeared. Although he did not attain the position of Yao and Shun so as to benefit his own age, he had received their transmission so as to benefit later generations: our Way and our learning now had a master. In the spring breeze beside the Yi River, what they delighted in was the spirit of Yao and Shun; beneath the autumn moon at Mount Ni, what they discussed was the cultural achievement of Yao and Shun. Teachers and friends were harmonious, their discussion of the Way and righteousness assured and forthright. They erected the lofty platform of orthodox learning, opened its great road, and raised its illustrious name. Those who adhered to it were called followers of our fellowship; those who turned their backs on it were called followers of heterodoxy. Even with this established as the standard, dissenting voices remained. Men such as Li Si and Tian Zifang borrowed the name of our Way to establish their own schools, so firmly entrenched that they could not be broken; inevitably, the teachings of our Master Kong were thrown into confusion by them. They left the world bewildered, ultimately with nowhere to turn, and our Way became obscured.
Then Heaven’s cycles turned above, and the five planets gathered in the constellation Kui; human affairs came into harmony below, and the Confucian scholars appeared in the world. Once the source of the Lian River was opened, the radiance of Yueyan shone forth. Through the single Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Heaven’s principle was made clear and human affairs were illuminated. The two Cheng brothers followed, together elucidating this learning. With one breath of their pure breeze, all the land responded from every direction, and the vital force of our Way was once again restored to wholeness between Heaven and Earth. Master Zhu arose…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以天授頴敏之資天挺豪傑之才聰明始
開即能沙畫八卦端坐黙視此謂非天有
意於吾道而篤生乎斯人不可也位不滿
德潜脩于家得以俯而讀仰而思大究乎
聖言問者師辨者友深明乎正學嘗膺玉
山尹之聘也感其建學延師為之設座開
講首以孔子古之學者為己今之學者為
人為從游者言之以見聖人教人為學非
是使人綴緝言語造化文辭但為科名爵
===
祿之計而已須是格物致知誠意正心脩
身而推之以至於齊家治國平天下方是
正當學問復因程珙之問而為之詳說孔
子言仁孟子兼言仁義使之於身上用力
不可於冊上漫談至於氣質之清濁工夫
之淺深無不並舉而兼教之雖以副邑大
夫建學教人之良意實以廣吾道脩己治
人之正傳也同時有象山陸子靜者少服
父兄師友之訓克勵聖賢道義之心因郡
punctuated:
以天授頴敏之資、天挺豪傑之才，聰明始開，即能沙畫八卦，端坐黙視。此謂非天有意於吾道而篤生乎斯人，不可也。位不滿德，潜脩于家，得以俯而讀、仰而思，大究乎聖言；問者師，辨者友，深明乎正學。嘗膺玉山尹之聘也，感其建學延師，為之設座開講，首以孔子「古之學者為己，今之學者為人」為從游者言之，以見聖人教人為學，非是使人綴緝言語、造化文辭，但為科名爵祿之計而已。須是格物致知、誠意正心、脩身，而推之以至於齊家、治國、平天下，方是正當學問。復因程珙之問，而為之詳說孔子言仁、孟子兼言仁義，使之於身上用力，不可於冊上漫談。至於氣質之清濁、工夫之淺深，無不並舉而兼教之。雖以副邑大夫建學教人之良意，實以廣吾道脩己治人之正傳也。

同時有象山陸子靜者，少服父兄師友之訓，克勵聖賢道義之心，因郡
translation_en:
…endowed by Heaven with keen intelligence and the talents of an outstanding man. As soon as his understanding began to awaken, he could draw the Eight Trigrams in the sand and sit upright contemplating them in silence. It would be impossible to say that Heaven had not deliberately brought forth this man in its concern for our Way. His official position did not measure up to his virtue. Cultivating himself in retirement at home, he could bend his head to read and raise it to reflect, thoroughly investigating the words of the sages. He treated those whom he questioned as teachers and those with whom he debated as friends, attaining a profound understanding of orthodox learning.

Once, accepting an invitation from the magistrate of Yushan, he was moved by the magistrate’s establishment of a school and recruitment of teachers, and took his seat to lecture there. He began by explaining to his followers Confucius’s saying, “Those who learned in antiquity did so for themselves; those who learn today do so for others.” This showed that when the sage taught people to learn, he did not intend merely to have them piece together expressions and fashion literary compositions [?] as a means of securing examination distinction, official rank, and emoluments. They must investigate things and extend knowledge, make their intentions sincere and rectify their minds, cultivate themselves, and extend this to ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven. Only this constituted proper learning.

In response to a question from Cheng Gong, he further explained in detail why Confucius spoke of benevolence and Mencius spoke of both benevolence and righteousness. He directed him to exert himself in his own person, rather than engage in idle discussion confined to books. As for the purity or turbidity of one’s psychophysical endowment and the shallowness or depth of one’s efforts at cultivation, he addressed and taught all of these together. Although this fulfilled the county magistrate’s good intention in establishing a school and teaching people, it truly served to extend the orthodox transmission of our Way: cultivating oneself and governing others.

At the same time there was Lu Zijing, known as Xiangshan. From his youth he followed the instruction of his father, elder brothers, teachers, and friends, diligently nurturing a mind devoted to the Way and righteousness of the sages and worthies. At the invitation of the prefect…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
侯之請開白鹿之堂集郡邑羣賢於講筵
揭論語一章之大義其曰君子喻於義謂
君子之志義則所習者必在於義斯曉然
於義也其曰小人喻於利謂小人之志利
則所習者必在於利斯曉然於利也至於
謂科舉取士久矣名儒鉅公皆由於此士
由此而出亦可謂正也但於未得之則不
可以得失爲計既得之則不可以祿位爲
念但當悉心於國事盡力於民隱能以職
===
業爲心便是君子之喻於義若以祿位爲
心便是小人之喻於利斯言亦救世之良
劑也朱陸之學昔人辨之詳矣玆其所謂
喻於義者非爲己之學歟喻於利者非爲
人之學歟何所異哉春秋講義吕東萊之
作也首言學欲切而思欲近春秋夫子筆
也而以深切自命傳經者亦謂撥亂世反
之正莫近於春秋君子將用力於切近之
地置是經其何從降隱迄哀所褒者既往
punctuated:
侯之請，開白鹿之堂，集郡邑羣賢於講筵，揭《論語》一章之大義。其曰「君子喻於義」，謂君子之志義，則所習者必在於義，斯曉然於義也。其曰「小人喻於利」，謂小人之志利，則所習者必在於利，斯曉然於利也。至於謂：「科舉取士久矣，名儒鉅公皆由於此，士由此而出，亦可謂正也。但於未得之，則不可以得失爲計；既得之，則不可以祿位爲念。但當悉心於國事，盡力於民隱。能以職業爲心，便是君子之喻於義；若以祿位爲心，便是小人之喻於利。」斯言亦救世之良劑也。朱陸之學，昔人辨之詳矣。玆其所謂喻於義者，非爲己之學歟？喻於利者，非爲人之學歟？何所異哉？
《春秋講義》，吕東萊之作也。首言學欲切而思欲近。《春秋》，夫子筆也，而以深切自命。傳經者亦謂：「撥亂世，反之正，莫近於《春秋》。」君子將用力於切近之地，置是經，其何從？降隱迄哀，所褒者既往
translation_en:
… at the prefect’s invitation, he opened the hall at White Deer Grotto and assembled the worthies of the prefecture and its counties for a lecture, expounding the central meaning of a passage in the Analects. Its statement, “The gentleman understands righteousness,” means that the gentleman sets his purpose on righteousness, so what he practices must concern righteousness; thus he understands it clearly. Its statement, “The petty man understands profit,” means that the petty man sets his purpose on profit, so what he practices must concern profit; thus he understands it clearly. He went on to say: “The selection of men through the civil-service examinations has long been established. Celebrated scholars and eminent officials have all come through this route. For scholars to enter service by this means may indeed be called proper. But before attaining success, they must not calculate gains and losses; once successful, they must not dwell on salary and rank. They should simply devote their whole minds to affairs of state and exert themselves fully to relieve the people’s hidden sufferings. To make one’s official duties one’s concern is precisely the gentleman’s understanding of righteousness; to make salary and rank one’s concern is precisely the petty man’s understanding of profit.” These words, too, are an excellent remedy for saving the age. Earlier scholars have distinguished the teachings of Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan in detail. Yet is what is here called understanding righteousness not learning for one’s own moral cultivation? Is understanding profit not learning for the sake of others’ approval? What difference is there between them here?
Lectures on the Spring and Autumn Annals is a work by Lü Donglai. It begins by saying that learning should be closely engaged and reflection should concern what is near at hand. The Spring and Autumn Annals was written by the Master, and its declared purpose was profound and immediate relevance. Those who transmitted the classic likewise said: “For bringing order to a disordered age and restoring it to what is right, nothing is more pertinent than the Spring and Autumn Annals.” If the gentleman wishes to devote his efforts to matters of immediate concern, where can he turn if he sets this classic aside? From Duke Yin down to Duke Ai, what it praises belongs to the past …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之功也所貶者既往之罪也終日歴數古
人而我無與焉豈所謂切近者哉乾卦講
義黄勉齋之作也首詳元亨利貞四德之
切於人而以孟子人之有是四端於我而
自謂不能者自賊者也謂其君不能者賊
其君者也數言繼之且曰五帝三王載籍
之傳以仁義禮智對立而並言者自孟子
始蓋人受天地之中無非此性雜之以氣
質撓之以習俗不能親師取友以致其學
===
問之功雖有此性亦未免於晦而不明窒
而不通矣吕黄之學源流傳之正矣兹其
所謂切者即四端根於心也所謂近者即
四端備於己也奚有於二哉講於東湖書
院者則道之不行也我知之矣智愚賢不
肖之過不及而指其道爲仁敬孝慈信之
在於人者中而已矣過與不及人失之也
講於竹林精舍者教人之方則曰居敬曰
窮理曰力行讀書之法則先大學次論孟
punctuated:
之功也，所貶者既往之罪也。終日歴數古人，而我無與焉，豈所謂切近者哉？《乾卦講義》，黄勉齋之作也。首詳元亨利貞四德之切於人，而以孟子「人之有是四端於我而自謂不能者，自賊者也；謂其君不能者，賊其君者也」數言繼之。且曰：「五帝三王載籍之傳，以仁義禮智對立而並言者，自孟子始。蓋人受天地之中，無非此性。雜之以氣質，撓之以習俗，不能親師取友以致其學問之功，雖有此性，亦未免於晦而不明、窒而不通矣。」吕黄之學，源流傳之正矣。兹其所謂切者，即四端根於心也；所謂近者，即四端備於己也。奚有於二哉？
講於東湖書院者，則「道之不行也，我知之矣」，智愚賢不肖之過不及，而指其道爲仁敬孝慈信之在於人者，中而已矣。過與不及，人失之也。講於竹林精舍者，教人之方則曰居敬，曰窮理，曰力行；讀書之法則先《大學》，次《論》《孟》。
translation_en:
…achievements; what it censures are past offenses. To spend the entire day recounting the ancients, while I myself have no part in it—can this be what is meant by being personally pertinent and close at hand? Lectures on the Qian Hexagram is the work of Huang Mianzhai. It begins by explaining in detail how the four virtues of origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy bear directly upon human beings, and follows this with these words of Mencius: “People possess these four beginnings within themselves. Those who nevertheless say they are incapable injure themselves; those who say their ruler is incapable injure their ruler.” It further says: “In the written traditions handed down from the Five Emperors and Three Kings, it was Mencius who first set benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom alongside one another and discussed them together. What human beings receive as the balanced endowment of Heaven and Earth is entirely this nature. If it is mixed with their material disposition and disturbed by customary habits, and they cannot draw close to teachers and choose friends through whom to bring their learning to fruition, then, although they possess this nature, it will inevitably remain obscured rather than clear, obstructed rather than freely expressed.” The learning of Lü and Huang derives from an orthodox line of transmission. Here, what they call “personally pertinent” is precisely the four beginnings rooted in the heart; what they call “close at hand” is precisely the four beginnings fully present within oneself. How could there be two different teachings?
The lectures at Donghu Academy take up the statement, “I know why the Way is not practiced,” discussing how the wise and foolish, the worthy and unworthy, go too far or fall short. They identify this Way as the benevolence, reverence, filial piety, parental kindness, and trustworthiness present in human beings: it is simply the Mean. Excess and deficiency arise when people depart from it. The lectures at Zhulin Retreat set out the methods of teaching as maintaining reverence, investigating principle, and earnestly putting it into practice. As for the method of reading, they place the Great Learning first, followed by the Analects and Mencius…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而終之以中庸勉人以立志則拳拳以去
私慾信道篤爲要言示人以歸宿則切切
以希堯舜學禹湯爲地位陳北溪之講於
嚴陵也其設條目則有曰道學體統曰師
友淵源曰用工節目曰讀書次序蔡久軒
之講於和靖書院也其名義蓋以和靖甫
生爲程門高第其學深有得於大易敬義
之旨以爲終身受用之地此立學之體也
程子謂和靖之學他日必有用於世爲先
===
生之學者亦將以有用於世此行學之用
也體立用行吾道之學備矣以此而用於
世則可以堯舜其君民也以此而用於家
則可以堯舜其倫族也以此而爲人則順
以此而爲己則祥信矣哉聖賢之學不我
欺也然豈強人所不能哉出於人性之固
有求於人力之能爲彼僞學之徒自壞乃
性耳夫豈其性則然哉聞諸李延平曰道
可以治心猶食之充飽衣之禦寒也學也
punctuated: 而終之以《中庸》。勉人以立志，則拳拳以去私慾、信道篤爲要言；示人以歸宿，則切切以希堯舜、學禹湯爲地位。陳北溪之講於嚴陵也，其設條目則有曰道學體統，曰師友淵源，曰用工節目，曰讀書次序。蔡久軒之講於和靖書院也，其名義蓋以和靖甫生爲程門高第，其學深有得於《大易》敬義之旨，以爲終身受用之地，此立學之體也。程子謂和靖之學，他日必有用於世。爲先生之學者，亦將以有用於世，此行學之用也。體立用行，吾道之學備矣。以此而用於世，則可以堯舜其君民也；以此而用於家，則可以堯舜其倫族也；以此而爲人則順，以此而爲己則祥。信矣哉！聖賢之學不我欺也。然豈強人所不能哉？出於人性之固有，求於人力之能爲，彼僞學之徒自壞乃性耳，夫豈其性則然哉？聞諸李延平曰：「道可以治心，猶食之充飽、衣之禦寒也。學也
translation_en: …and conclude with the Doctrine of the Mean. In urging people to establish their resolve, he earnestly made eliminating selfish desires and believing firmly in the Way his essential counsel; in showing people their ultimate destination, he insistently set aspiring to Yao and Shun and learning from Yu and Tang as the level to attain. When Chen Beixi lectured at Yanling, the headings he established included the overall structure of learning the Way, the lineage of teachers and friends, the stages of practical effort, and the sequence for reading books. When Cai Jiuxuan lectured at Hejing Academy, the significance of its name rested on Master Hejing [?] having been an outstanding disciple of Cheng. His learning had profoundly grasped the purport of reverence and righteousness in the great Book of Changes, which he made a foundation to draw upon throughout his life. This is the substance upon which learning is established. Master Cheng said that Hejing’s learning would surely prove useful to the world in days to come. Those who pursue this master’s learning will likewise seek to be useful to the world: this is the practical application of learning. With its substance established and its application put into practice, the learning of our Way is complete. Applied to the world, it can make one’s ruler and people like Yao and Shun; applied to the family, it can make one’s kin and clan like Yao and Shun. Practised for others, it brings harmony; practised for oneself, it brings well-being. How true it is! The learning of the sages and worthies does not deceive us. Yet how could it compel people to do what lies beyond their abilities? It proceeds from what is inherent in human nature and seeks what human effort can accomplish. Those adherents of false learning merely corrupt their own nature. How could their nature itself be like that? I have heard these words of Li Yanping: “The Way can order the mind, just as food satisfies hunger and clothing wards off cold. As for learning…”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
者耕耨蠶績之功也求其人而證之可乎
伊周孔孟同一學也而伊周遇時故事功
成之於當時孔孟雖不偶於時而其事功
垂之於萬世傳曰脩身人也遇不遇天也
君子知脩吾學而已遇之則當為伊周不
遇則當為孔孟是固在我之立志務學如
何
第五問
王璠
===
同考試官訓導張批先有濟世之志而
發之於文庶不泥於古不流於俗
使無定見則惟空言是逞雖華何
益此作參考往迹而昌以正論固
有體而欲達諸用者
考試官教諭周批儒生不達世務者
皆目曰腐此作關係政體曲盡事
情根據舊聞深悉民隱迂腐者能
為是言乎
punctuated:
者，耕耨蠶績之功也。求其人而證之，可乎？伊周孔孟，同一學也。而伊周遇時，故事功成之於當時；孔孟雖不偶於時，而其事功垂之於萬世。傳曰：「脩身，人也；遇不遇，天也。」君子知脩吾學而已。遇之，則當為伊周；不遇，則當為孔孟。是固在我之立志務學如何。
第五問
王璠
同考試官訓導張批：先有濟世之志，而發之於文，庶不泥於古，不流於俗。使無定見，則惟空言是逞，雖華何益？此作參考往迹，而昌以正論，固有體而欲達諸用者。
考試官教諭周批：儒生不達世務者，皆目曰腐。此作關係政體，曲盡事情，根據舊聞，深悉民隱。迂腐者能為是言乎？
translation_en:
…is the work of plowing and hoeing, raising silkworms and spinning thread. May we seek out men who exemplify this and verify it through them? Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius shared the same learning. Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou encountered favorable times, and thus their achievements were accomplished in their own age. Although Confucius and Mencius did not find favorable circumstances in their time, their achievements have endured for ten thousand generations. The transmitted text says: “Cultivating oneself rests with man; encountering or failing to encounter opportunity rests with Heaven.” The gentleman knows only to cultivate his learning. Given opportunity, he should become like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; without it, he should become like Confucius and Mencius. This indeed depends on how we set our resolve and devote ourselves to learning.
Fifth Question
Wang Fan
Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: One must first possess the resolve to aid the world and then express it in writing; only then may one avoid being confined by antiquity or swept along by prevailing fashions. Without settled judgments, one merely parades empty words. However ornate they may be, what benefit do they bring? This composition examines past events and develops them through sound argument. It assuredly possesses substance and seeks to bring it into practical use.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: Confucian scholars who do not understand worldly affairs are all branded pedants. This composition addresses the workings of government, thoroughly explores the circumstances of affairs, draws upon accounts of the past, and shows a deep understanding of the people's hidden sufferings. Could an impractical pedant speak like this?

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正季　批叙事不遺工詞有
理頓挫起伏而嚴整不亂孰意風
簷寸晷有此作也
民困不可不憫也欲施一念之仁須盡萬
全之慮若徒知益下而無經理周防之術
雖頻蠲屢貸而閭閻之困固自若也如是
則上之所施下之所望不亦兩負也哉嗚
呼仁覆斯民如三代帝王亦云至矣而未
見有所蠲貸者蓋取民雖用田賦而又隨
===
時隨地爲之權衡民皆遵從輸納自不至
於逋負尚何用蠲貸爲哉自是以後賦稅
之額始定額外之征又繁不得不視時之
豐歉民之貧富而時布蠲放之恩亦其勢
然也故逋貸之蠲起於漢武帝逋負之寬
起於吳嘉禾以晉惠帝有戶調絹綿之除
以唐宣宗有度支鹽鐵之免減上供饋運
者始於大中九年也免官司債負和買役
錢者昉於紹興三十二載也是皆有仁民
punctuated:
考試官學正季　批：叙事不遺，工詞有理，頓挫起伏而嚴整不亂，孰意風簷寸晷有此作也？

民困不可不憫也。欲施一念之仁，須盡萬全之慮。若徒知益下，而無經理周防之術，雖頻蠲屢貸，而閭閻之困固自若也。如是，則上之所施、下之所望，不亦兩負也哉？嗚呼！仁覆斯民，如三代帝王，亦云至矣，而未見有所蠲貸者。蓋取民雖用田賦，而又隨時隨地爲之權衡，民皆遵從輸納，自不至於逋負，尚何用蠲貸爲哉？自是以後，賦稅之額始定，額外之征又繁，不得不視時之豐歉、民之貧富，而時布蠲放之恩，亦其勢然也。故逋貸之蠲，起於漢武帝；逋負之寬，起於吳嘉禾；以晉惠帝有戶調絹綿之除，以唐宣宗有度支鹽鐵之免。減上供饋運者，始於大中九年也；免官司債負、和買、役錢者，昉於紹興三十二載也。是皆有仁民
translation_en:
Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: “The narration omits nothing; the polished wording is well reasoned. Its pauses and turns, rises and falls, remain disciplined and orderly. Who would have expected such a composition under the wind-swept eaves, in so brief a span of time?”

The people’s distress cannot but arouse compassion. To put a single benevolent intention into practice requires utterly thorough deliberation. If one knows only how to benefit those below, but lacks the means to administer affairs and guard comprehensively against difficulties, then even frequent remissions and repeated relief will leave the distress of ordinary households unchanged. In that case, will not both what those above bestow and what those below hope for come to nothing? Alas! The benevolence with which the kings and emperors of the Three Dynasties sheltered their people may be called consummate, yet we find no instances of their granting remissions or relief. Although they collected revenue from the people through land taxes, they also adjusted their demands to the circumstances of each time and place. The people all complied and made their payments, naturally avoiding arrears. What need, then, was there for remissions or relief?

Thereafter, tax quotas began to be fixed, while exactions beyond those quotas multiplied. It became necessary to consider whether harvests were abundant or poor and whether the people were wealthy or impoverished, and periodically to bestow the grace of tax remission. Circumstances themselves made this inevitable. Thus, cancellation of overdue loans began under Emperor Wu of Han; relief from arrears began in the Jiahe reign period of Wu. Under Emperor Hui of Jin there was the abolition of household levies in silk cloth and silk floss, and under Emperor Xuanzong of Tang there were remissions relating to revenue administration and the salt and iron monopolies [?]. Reductions in supplies offered to the court and their transport began in the ninth year of Dazhong. Exemptions from debts owed to government offices, compulsory government purchases, and service payments began in the thirty-second year of Shaoxing. These were all instances of having a heart benevolent toward the people …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之心者矣然其間又有不盡免而權宜於
其中者考之宋哲宗時令諸路屢年負欠
以十分爲率每年帶納一分似爲便民矣
而蘇東坡訪問濠壽父老有豐年不如凶
年之云者蓋以天災流行民雖乏食縮衣
節口猶可聊生若豐年舉催積欠符檄日
至其門鞭笞日加其身則人皆求死而不
可得反不若凶歲之易過也夫恩典雖厚
奉宣匪人民何由而受惠哉宋自紹興以
===
來邊隅多警役繁賦重極力寬之民病猶
未甦也而朱元晦上封事有遷延一分以
待蠲放之議者蓋宋初舊法凡催理官物
數及九分者諸司即行住催版曹亦置不
問州縣得其贏餘以相補助貧民亦得遷
延以待蠲除恩自朝廷惠及閭里較之虛
文無實所謂黃紙放白紙取者不亦相去
遠哉愚竊聞之天下財賦一歲所入止足
一歲之用況又水旱無常虧縮未足若憫
punctuated:
之心者矣。然其間又有不盡免而權宜於其中者。考之宋哲宗時，令諸路屢年負欠，以十分爲率，每年帶納一分，似爲便民矣。而蘇東坡訪問濠壽父老，有豐年不如凶年之云者，蓋以天災流行，民雖乏食，縮衣節口，猶可聊生；若豐年舉催積欠，符檄日至其門，鞭笞日加其身，則人皆求死而不可得，反不若凶歲之易過也。夫恩典雖厚，奉宣匪人，民何由而受惠哉？宋自紹興以來，邊隅多警，役繁賦重，極力寬之，民病猶未甦也。而朱元晦上封事，有遷延一分以待蠲放之議者，蓋宋初舊法，凡催理官物，數及九分者，諸司即行住催，版曹亦置不問，州縣得其贏餘以相補助，貧民亦得遷延以待蠲除。恩自朝廷，惠及閭里，較之虛文無實，所謂黃紙放、白紙取者，不亦相去遠哉？

愚竊聞之，天下財賦，一歲所入，止足一歲之用。況又水旱無常，虧縮未足。若憫
translation_en:
…had hearts that cared for the people. Yet among these measures were some that did not remit everything, but adopted expedients. Examining the reign of Emperor Zhezong of the Song, we find that the circuits were ordered to divide arrears accumulated over successive years into ten portions and collect one portion each year alongside current dues. This would seem to have benefited the people. Yet when Su Dongpo questioned the elders of Haozhou and Shouzhou, some said that a good harvest year was worse than a bad one. This was because, when natural disasters spread, although the people lacked food, they could still eke out a living by stinting on clothing and meals. But in a good harvest year, all accumulated arrears were pressed for payment: official demands arrived at their doors daily, and daily they suffered flogging. Everyone then sought death but could not obtain it; a bad year was actually easier to endure. However generous an act of grace might be, if those charged with carrying it out were unfit, how could the people receive its benefits?

From the Shaoxing reign period onward, the Song faced frequent alarms along its frontiers, numerous labor obligations, and heavy taxation. Even the utmost efforts at relief failed to alleviate the people's distress. In a sealed memorial, Zhu Yuanhui proposed allowing payment of one portion to be deferred pending remission. Under an old rule from the early Song, whenever collection of dues owed to the government reached nine-tenths, the various offices immediately ceased pressing for payment, and the Ministry of Revenue likewise let the matter rest without inquiry. Prefectures and counties could use their surpluses to make up one another's shortfalls, while poor people could defer payment and await remission. Grace thus came from the court, and its benefits reached the villages. Was this not far removed from empty formalities with no substance—the practice described as “remitting on yellow paper and collecting on white paper”?

I have humbly heard that the empire's annual revenue in money and goods suffices only for that year's expenditure. Moreover, floods and droughts occur unpredictably, diminishing receipts and leaving them insufficient. If, taking pity…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
民彫悴舉數年逋負而一旦免之固歡欣
鼓舞於田野矣然大而軍國邊境之需次
而官胥廩祿之費當取辦於何所哉倉庾
儲峙在在空虛如之何其可也是以宋高
宗因湖秀水災欲除下戶積欠慮恐侵損
歲支輒於內庫撥補乃曰內庫所積正備
水旱本是民財却為民用何所顧惜夫湖
秀一隅侵損未多補給尚易也若舉天下
而出內帑給之勢亦難乎其為繼愚恐高
===
宗亦末如之何也由是觀之則蠲貸之令
豈可輕舉而無周悉萬全之慮哉昔人謂
赦者小人之幸愚初未敢以為然今夷考
往迹始知非虛語也盍觀之唐乎玄宗蠲
免七年以前逋負當時稱為異數而識者
猶有未然蓋寬貸之舉止為貧民若果貧
民欠負盡數免之以蘇疲困有何不可但
膏脂已竭於貧窮而恩典翻歸於豪猾中
間雖究已收未收之等然亦誰肯自陳其
punctuated:
民彫悴，舉數年逋負而一旦免之，固歡欣鼓舞於田野矣。然大而軍國邊境之需，次而官胥廩祿之費，當取辦於何所哉？倉庾儲峙，在在空虛，如之何其可也？是以宋高宗因湖秀水災，欲除下戶積欠，慮恐侵損歲支，輒於內庫撥補，乃曰：「內庫所積，正備水旱，本是民財，却為民用，何所顧惜？」夫湖秀一隅，侵損未多，補給尚易也。若舉天下而出內帑給之，勢亦難乎其為繼，愚恐高宗亦末如之何也。由是觀之，則蠲貸之令，豈可輕舉而無周悉萬全之慮哉？
昔人謂：「赦者，小人之幸。」愚初未敢以為然，今夷考往迹，始知非虛語也。盍觀之唐乎？玄宗蠲免七年以前逋負，當時稱為異數，而識者猶有未然。蓋寬貸之舉，止為貧民。若果貧民欠負，盡數免之，以蘇疲困，有何不可？但膏脂已竭於貧窮，而恩典翻歸於豪猾。中間雖究已收未收之等，然亦誰肯自陳其
translation_en:
…the people's impoverished condition, and cancel several years of arrears at a single stroke, there would certainly be rejoicing throughout the countryside. Yet where would the funds come from for the greater demands of the military, the state, and the frontiers, and, next in importance, the costs of grain allowances and salaries for officials and clerks? With granary reserves everywhere depleted, how could this be practicable? Thus, when floods struck Hu and Xiu, Emperor Gaozong of the Song wished to cancel the accumulated arrears of lower-status households. Fearing a shortfall in funds for annual expenditure, he allocated funds from the inner treasury to make it good, saying: “The reserves in the inner treasury are precisely for floods and droughts. They were originally the people's wealth and are now being used for the people. Why begrudge them?” Hu and Xiu constituted only one small area: the shortfall was modest and still easy to replenish. But if funds from the imperial treasury were disbursed to cover the whole realm, this would be difficult to sustain. I fear that even Gaozong could have done nothing about it. Viewed in this light, how could orders granting remission and relief be issued lightly, without thorough consideration and a fully adequate plan?
An earlier saying holds: “Amnesty is the good fortune of petty men.” At first I did not presume to accept this as true; only now, after examining past events dispassionately, do I recognize that these are no empty words. Why not consider the Tang? Emperor Xuanzong remitted arrears dating from before the seventh year [?]. At the time this was acclaimed as an extraordinary act of grace, yet discerning men still had reservations. Measures granting leniency and relief are intended solely for the poor. If the arrears really were owed by poor people, what objection could there be to cancelling them in full to relieve their exhaustion and hardship? Yet the poor had already been drained of their substance, while the benefit of imperial grace went instead to powerful and unscrupulous men. Although inquiries distinguished amounts already collected from those not yet collected, who among those involved would willingly disclose his own…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
弊哉官司欲證其實未免拘集小民里胥
追呼文移煩複農事因之妨廢貪污緣以
爲姦况又懼包攬之强而俛首認納畏械
繫之苦而依令重陪害及雞豚利歸豺虎
小人之幸良不誣也使當時君臣果知此
弊勿免日前逋負止於次歲量除明開何
等徵霈定與減免分數庶窮鄉僻壤盡知
應免應納之數而貪吏豪猾亦難肆重徵
侵剋之姦矣昔宋臣趙善防議稱貧民下
===
戶每歲二稅但有重納未甞拖欠朝廷蠲
放利歸攬戶鄉胥而小民未甞霑恩乞明
詔自今郊霈惟減次年賦稅其日前殘零
務依數納足則貧民實被寬恩官賦亦易
催理此誠切要之策而當時未盡舉行良
可惜也嗚呼自昔有天下者欲施不忍之
政而必竭盡心思典法之立非徒然者使
行法得人則蠲減新徵固可也寬貸積逋
亦可也否則德意徒存奉宣未至不但視
punctuated:
弊哉？官司欲證其實，未免拘集小民，里胥追呼，文移煩複，農事因之妨廢，貪污緣以爲姦。况又懼包攬之强而俛首認納，畏械繫之苦而依令重陪，害及雞豚，利歸豺虎。小人之幸，良不誣也。使當時君臣果知此弊，勿免日前逋負，止於次歲量除，明開何等徵霈，定與減免分數，庶窮鄉僻壤盡知應免應納之數，而貪吏豪猾亦難肆重徵侵剋之姦矣。昔宋臣趙善防議稱：「貧民下戶，每歲二稅，但有重納，未甞拖欠。朝廷蠲放，利歸攬戶鄉胥，而小民未甞霑恩。乞明詔自今郊霈，惟減次年賦稅，其日前殘零，務依數納足，則貧民實被寬恩，官賦亦易催理。」此誠切要之策，而當時未盡舉行，良可惜也。

嗚呼！自昔有天下者，欲施不忍之政，而必竭盡心思，典法之立非徒然者。使行法得人，則蠲減新徵固可也，寬貸積逋亦可也。否則德意徒存，奉宣未至，不但視
translation_en:
…their abuses? When the authorities seek to ascertain the facts, they inevitably detain and assemble the common people. Village clerks pursue and summon them, and official correspondence becomes burdensome and repetitive. Farm work is consequently disrupted and neglected, while corrupt officials exploit the opportunity for fraud. Moreover, fearing the power of those who undertake tax payments on others’ behalf, the people bow their heads and accept liability; dreading the suffering of shackles and confinement, they obey orders and pay a second time. The harm reaches even their chickens and pigs, while the profits go to jackals and tigers. That this is good fortune for petty men is indeed no empty claim.

Had the ruler and his ministers at that time truly understood these abuses, they would have remitted no past arrears, but instead made measured reductions in the following year’s taxes. They would have clearly specified the categories of assessment [?] and fixed the proportions to be reduced or remitted. Then even people in remote villages and outlying districts would have known exactly how much was exempt and how much remained payable, and corrupt officials and powerful rogues would have found it difficult to perpetrate duplicate collections and embezzlement unchecked.

Zhao Shanfang [?], a minister of the Song, once argued: “Poor people and households in the lowest category pay the two annual taxes twice over, if anything; they have never fallen into arrears. When the court grants remissions, the benefits go to households that undertake others’ tax payments and to village clerks, while the common people receive no grace. I request an explicit edict that henceforth, when acts of grace are proclaimed on the occasion of the suburban sacrifices, only the following year’s taxes be reduced, while all outstanding balances from earlier years must be paid in full according to the amounts due. Then the poor will actually receive this generous relief, and official tax revenues will also be easier to collect and administer.” This was indeed a policy addressing the essential problem. That it was not fully implemented at the time is truly regrettable.

Alas! From ancient times, those who ruled the realm and wished to practice government compassionate toward suffering had to devote all their thought to it; the establishment of statutes and regulations was no idle undertaking. If suitable men administer the laws, reducing or remitting new assessments is certainly permissible, as is granting relief on accumulated arrears. Otherwise, benevolent intentions merely remain intentions, without being properly carried into effect, and not only are they regarded as…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
為紙上之文而反重為閭閻之擾甚至罔
民之愚侵國之用徒知飽煖乎巳不思失
信於民此淳熈州縣之吏不能仰體至懷
而屢詔以督責之也然則赦之布也豈但
豪猾小人之幸亦貪墨之幸耳嗚呼心何
忍哉是以漢時欲安斯民必擇守令而傳
曰文武之政布在方策其人存則其政舉
此雖儒生常談而人君治世之規恐不出
此執事以為何如惟貸其狂而教之幸也
punctuated: 為紙上之文，而反重為閭閻之擾，甚至罔民之愚，侵國之用，徒知飽煖乎巳，不思失信於民。此淳熈州縣之吏不能仰體至懷，而屢詔以督責之也。然則赦之布也，豈但豪猾小人之幸，亦貪墨之幸耳。嗚呼！心何忍哉！是以漢時欲安斯民，必擇守令。而傳曰：「文武之政，布在方策。其人存，則其政舉。」此雖儒生常談，而人君治世之規，恐不出此。執事以為何如？惟貸其狂而教之，幸也。
translation_en:
…as mere words on paper, but instead become an additional disturbance to the common people. Officials even exploit the people's ignorance and misappropriate state funds, thinking only of keeping themselves well fed and warm, without considering how they betray the people's trust. This is why, during the Chunxi reign period, prefectural and county officials, unable reverently to embody the sovereign's deepest concern, were repeatedly admonished and held to account by imperial edicts. If so, when an amnesty is proclaimed, how could it benefit only powerful and crafty scoundrels? It also benefits corrupt officials. Alas! How can they have the heart to act so?

Thus, in Han times, those who wished to bring peace to the people invariably selected prefects and county magistrates with care. The transmitted text says: “The government of Kings Wen and Wu is set forth on wooden tablets and bamboo slips. When the right men are present, their government is put into effect.” Although this is a commonplace among Confucian scholars, the principles by which a ruler governs the world probably do not extend beyond it. What is your judgment, honored Examiner? I would count myself fortunate if you would pardon my presumption and instruct me.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄後序
夫科舉必有錄錄必有序錄
之式載官使以昭事載名氏
以昭賢載文章以昭用序之
式申勸戒以昭義列撫臣藩
臬以昭類列守臣以昭備總
之皆爲貴士設也是之謂制
===
制之行合天下而同也夫合
天下而同於貴士士宜乎軼
前脩而上之矣而顧或不逮
意者勢使然乎是故科舉之
制益飭而有志之士或鬱而
不暢或興而不奮者有矣今
天子以聖神入嗣大歷服躬脩德
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄後序

夫科舉必有錄，錄必有序。錄之式，載官使以昭事，載名氏以昭賢，載文章以昭用。序之式，申勸戒以昭義，列撫臣、藩臬以昭類，列守臣以昭備。總之，皆爲貴士設也，是之謂制。制之行，合天下而同也。夫合天下而同於貴士，士宜乎軼前脩而上之矣，而顧或不逮，意者勢使然乎？是故科舉之制益飭，而有志之士或鬱而不暢，或興而不奮者有矣。今天子以聖神入嗣大歷服，躬脩德
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

Civil-service examinations must have records, and records must have prefaces. The prescribed form of the record lists the officials charged with its duties to make their service known, records the candidates’ names to make their worth known, and includes their writings to make their capabilities known. The prescribed form of the preface sets forth encouragements and admonitions to clarify moral principles, lists the grand coordinators, provincial administration commissioners, and provincial surveillance commissioners to indicate their respective categories, and lists the prefects to show the full complement. In sum, all these provisions are established to honor scholars. This is what is meant by the established regulations. Their implementation is uniform throughout the realm. Since the entire realm is united in honoring scholars, scholars ought to surpass their worthy predecessors and rise above them. Yet some instead fall short. Might circumstances have made this so? Thus, even as the regulations governing the examinations become more rigorous, some scholars of aspiration remain stifled and unable to express themselves, or are stirred but fail to exert themselves. Now the Son of Heaven, in his sagely and divine wisdom, has succeeded to the great dynastic mandate and personally cultivates virtue…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
教體貌儒臣表忠節登俊良
作士氣以培
國家之元氣於永久凡含生之
類莫不振動忭蹈訖于無外
則夫有司飭制以貴士者皆
聖神精微之所運用已是蓋古聖
賢遑遑終老而不獲見者而
===
况雲貴之遠乎傳曰周之士
也貴此其時矣請與諸士驗
諸今之場屋如監察御史羅
玉之風裁藩臬之慎肅羣司
百執事之恪共道洽而通氣
和而豐祺然韙然罔不心快
目爽於諸士之進曰今科其
punctuated: 教，體貌儒臣，表忠節，登俊良，作士氣，以培國家之元氣於永久。凡含生之類，莫不振動忭蹈，訖于無外。則夫有司飭制以貴士者，皆聖神精微之所運用已。是蓋古聖賢遑遑終老而不獲見者，而况雲貴之遠乎！傳曰：「周之士也貴。」此其時矣！請與諸士驗諸今之場屋：如監察御史羅玉之風裁，藩臬之慎肅，羣司百執事之恪共，道洽而通，氣和而豐，祺然韙然，罔不心快目爽於諸士之進，曰：「今科其
translation_en:
…instruction, treats Confucian officials with ceremonial respect, honors loyalty and integrity, promotes the talented and worthy, and rouses the spirit of scholars, thereby nurturing the vital energy of the state for all time. All living beings are stirred and dance with joy, with none beyond its reach. Thus, when the responsible officials uphold the regulations to honor scholars, all this is the working of His Majesty’s sagely and divine discernment in its finest subtleties. This is surely what the sages and worthies of antiquity strove anxiously throughout their lives without ever witnessing—how much more so in places as distant as Yunnan and Guizhou! The tradition says, “The scholars of Zhou were honored.” Now is indeed such a time!

Let me examine this together with the scholars in the present examination precincts: the bearing and judgment of Investigating Censor Luo Yu, the care and gravity of the provincial administration and surveillance authorities, and the scrupulous respect of the various offices and all their functionaries. The Way pervades and flows freely; the vital energies are harmonious and abundant. All is auspicious and fitting. At the scholars’ advancement, there is no one whose heart is not gladdened and whose eyes are not refreshed, saying: “This examination—what…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
何時今士其何遇也際千載
難逢之會殆必有千載間出
之士起應之乎如是而諸士
猶踵故常以自居惡在其爲
士也夫士之貴于世者非人
也天也天畀之以聰明靈哲
將使之以是而導人也君人
===
者奉若天道故取而官之使
盡其分有也苟昧於分有以
學則曲以志則溺以才則局
以行則肆以名則忽即不忽
則加之好矣是故曲則失正
溺則失義局則失用肆則失
己忽而好則失實如是則於
punctuated:
何時？今士其何遇也？際千載難逢之會，殆必有千載間出之士起應之乎？如是而諸士猶踵故常以自居，惡在其爲士也？夫士之貴于世者，非人也，天也。天畀之以聰明靈哲，將使之以是而導人也。
君人者奉若天道，故取而官之，使盡其分有也。苟昧於分有，以學則曲，以志則溺，以才則局，以行則肆，以名則忽，即不忽則加之好矣。是故曲則失正，溺則失義，局則失用，肆則失己，忽而好則失實。如是則於
translation_en:
…what a time is this? What an opportunity the scholars of today have encountered! At this juncture, such as one scarcely encounters in a thousand years, surely scholars who appear but once in a thousand years will rise to meet it? If, under such circumstances, these scholars still follow accustomed ways and rest content, wherein lies their claim to be scholars? What makes scholars esteemed in the world comes not from men, but from Heaven. Heaven endows them with intelligence, discernment, spiritual insight, and wisdom so that they may use these to guide others.
The ruler of men reverently follows the Way of Heaven. He therefore selects them and appoints them to office, enabling them to fulfill their allotted endowments. If they fail to understand these endowments, their learning becomes distorted, their aspirations become submerged, their abilities become confined, their conduct becomes unrestrained, and their attitude toward reputation becomes careless—or, if not careless, excessively attached to it [?]. Thus, distortion forfeits correctness; submersion forfeits righteousness; confinement forfeits usefulness; lack of restraint forfeits mastery of oneself; and carelessness or attachment in matters of reputation forfeits substance [?]. If this is so, then with respect to…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
分所當貴者篾矣士自賤之
誰其貴之而世焉賴之世無
賴於士而天下之事有不僨
乎西漢趙宋之末其士可考
也諸生誦法孔孟學不可謂
不正期在効用志不可謂不
立抱負竒氣才不可謂不達
===
蒙養童習行不可謂不脩疾
無聞而耻干譽名不可謂不
實所可委之外者惟曰時不
勝道也位不勝用也今遭值
盛時位有待而無可委矣其甚可
畏也哉且雲貴之士校天下
嘗寡至于今則文鳴四方志
punctuated: 分所當貴者篾矣。士自賤之，誰其貴之？而世焉賴之？世無賴於士，而天下之事有不僨乎？西漢、趙宋之末，其士可考也。諸生誦法孔孟，學不可謂不正；期在効用，志不可謂不立；抱負竒氣，才不可謂不達；蒙養童習，行不可謂不脩；疾無聞而耻干譽，名不可謂不實。所可委之外者，惟曰時不勝道也，位不勝用也。今遭值盛時，位有待而無可委矣，其甚可畏也哉！且雲貴之士，校天下嘗寡，至于今則文鳴四方，志
translation_en:
…what ought to be esteemed in one’s allotted duties is treated with contempt. If scholars debase themselves, who will esteem them? And how can the world rely upon them? If the world cannot rely upon scholars, can the affairs of the realm escape ruin? The scholars of the closing years of the Western Han and the Zhao Song offer evidence for examination.

You students recite and take as your models Confucius and Mencius: your learning cannot be called incorrect. You aspire to render useful service: your resolve cannot be called unformed. You possess exceptional spirit: your talents cannot be called undeveloped. Nurtured and trained from childhood, your conduct cannot be called uncultivated. You deplore remaining unknown yet are ashamed to solicit praise: your reputation cannot be called unfounded. The only external circumstances upon which you might lay responsibility are that the times cannot accommodate the Way, or that your position does not permit the exercise of your abilities. Now, however, you have encountered a flourishing age; official positions await you, and there is nothing upon which to shift responsibility. How greatly this should inspire apprehension!

Moreover, scholars from Yunnan and Guizhou were formerly few compared with those of the realm as a whole. By now, their literary accomplishments are renowned throughout the land, and their aspirations …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
角天下賢埒諸藩巳信乎我
國家覆露之恩乆則無間也然
亦文焉是徵耳要之因才考
行舉學明志而又求以佐其
名雖天下士容敢謂其分之
畢盡乎似於此又不容以多
讓爲也忠校文事事諸士策
===
名于賢科而負時深望故曰
可畏甚而不可以故常自居
也
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學教
諭周忠謹序
punctuated:
角天下，賢埒諸藩，巳信乎我國家覆露之恩乆則無間也。然亦文焉是徵耳。要之，因才考行，舉學明志，而又求以佐其名，雖天下士，容敢謂其分之畢盡乎？似於此又不容以多讓爲也。忠校文事，事諸士策名于賢科，而負時深望，故曰可畏甚，而不可以故常自居也。
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學教諭周忠謹序。
translation_en:
…vie with all under Heaven, their worth matching that of scholars in the other provinces. Truly, the sheltering and nurturing grace of our dynasty, extended over time, has left no region outside its embrace. Yet it is only their writing that has been examined. Ultimately, one must assess conduct in light of talent, bring forth learning to make aspirations clear, and further seek the substance to sustain one’s reputation. Would even the scholars of the entire realm dare claim that they had fully discharged their responsibilities? Here, it seems, one cannot leave too much to others [?]. I, Zhong, have assessed the examination writings [?]. You scholars have had your names inscribed among those successful in this worthy examination and bear the great expectations of the age. Thus I say that this is deeply to be feared, and that you must not rest content with customary standards.
Preface respectfully written by Zhou Zhong, Instructor of the Confucian School of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試録序
仰惟
聖天子御極紀元之初載實天下
開科取士之期
飛龍在天萬物利覩於是雲藩
得遵行故事合雲貴兩省之
士試焉先是巡按雲南監察
===
御史羅玉謀于前巡撫雲南
右副都御史何孟春暨今巡
撫右副都御史王啓集藩臬
議禮聘學職司試事戒脩百
具以協禮典維時鎮守雲南
總兵官黔國公沐紹勛貴州
鎮守太監楊廣巡撫右副都
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試録序

仰惟聖天子御極紀元之初載，實天下開科取士之期。飛龍在天，萬物利覩。於是雲藩得遵行故事，合雲貴兩省之士試焉。先是，巡按雲南監察御史羅玉謀于前巡撫雲南右副都御史何孟春暨今巡撫右副都御史王啓，集藩臬議禮聘學職司試事，戒脩百具，以協禮典。維時，鎮守雲南總兵官黔國公沐紹勛、貴州鎮守太監楊廣、巡撫右副都
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

We reverently reflect that the first year of our sagely Son of Heaven’s accession and inauguration of his reign era was indeed the appointed time throughout the realm to hold examinations and select scholars. “The flying dragon is in Heaven”: all beings benefit from beholding him. Thus the Yunnan provincial administration was able to follow established precedent and assemble scholars from the two provinces of Yunnan and Guizhou for examination.

Previously, Luo Yu, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Yunnan, consulted with He Mengchun, formerly Grand Coordinator of Yunnan and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Wang Qi, the current Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. They convened the provincial administration and surveillance officials to deliberate on ceremoniously inviting educational officials to oversee the examination, and directed that all necessary arrangements be made in accordance with the ritual statutes. At this time, Mu Shaoxun, Duke of Qianguo and Regional Commander stationed in Yunnan; Yang Guang, Grand Defender in Guizhou and Grand Eunuch; and the Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
御史湯沐鎮守署都督僉事
陳珣巡按貴州監察御史陳
克宅咸祗若
德意崇獎士類時戸科右給事中
吳廉監察御史李美刑部郎
中王袍各以公至與議焉期
既屆御史羅玉實主監臨之
===
任考試則學正王鑾教諭周忠
同考試則學正方田訓導張
嵩詹文慶鄭要提調則雲南
右布政使黃衷參政劉鶴年
監試則雲南按察使陳良珊
僉事潘棠外則左布政使方
璘參政鄧相晁必登參議羅
punctuated: 御史湯沐、鎮守署都督僉事陳珣、巡按貴州監察御史陳克宅，咸祗若德意，崇獎士類。時戸科右給事中吳廉、監察御史李美、刑部郎中王袍，各以公至，與議焉。期既屆，御史羅玉實主監臨之任。考試則學正王鑾、教諭周忠；同考試則學正方田、訓導張嵩、詹文慶、鄭要；提調則雲南右布政使黃衷、參政劉鶴年；監試則雲南按察使陳良珊、僉事潘棠；外則左布政使方璘、參政鄧相、晁必登、參議羅
translation_en: … Censor-in-Chief Tang Mu, Regional Commander and Acting Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Chen Xun, and Chen Kezhai, Investigating Censor on巡按 duty in Guizhou, all reverently complied with the imperial intentions and encouraged and honored the scholars. At this time, Wu Lian, Right Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue; Li Mei, Investigating Censor; and Wang Pao, Director in the Ministry of Justice, each arrived on official business and participated in the deliberations. When the appointed time came, Censor Luo Yu assumed responsibility as Supervising Official. The Examiners were Wang Luan, a Subprefectural School Instructor, and Zhou Zhong, a County School Instructor. The Associate Examiners were Fang Tian, a Subprefectural School Instructor, and Zhang Song, Zhan Wenqing, and Zheng Yao, Assistant Instructors. The Proctors were Huang Zhong, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, and Liu Henian, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner. Those overseeing the examination were Chen Liangshan, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan, and Pan Tang, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. Other participating officials were Fang Lin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Deng Xiang and Chao Bideng, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners; and Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner Luo …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
方陶心副使王忠陳璋詹源
姜龍僉事周愚陳卿翁素各
賛翊之自餘印卷以下諸執
事罔不遴具而貴州左布政
使宗璽參政鄭錫文傅習參
議江玠按察使李麟副使劉
瓚僉事王瑞之沈圻亦續食
===
多士迆邐而來廼集提學副
使鄭元僉事夏邦謨所選士
鎖院三試之雲南都指揮胡
章張松方仲外率其屬防範
惟謹御史羅玉且誓于眾曰
以人事
君臣之職也所不盡心于
punctuated: 方、陶心，副使王忠、陳璋、詹源、姜龍，僉事周愚、陳卿、翁素，各賛翊之。自餘印卷以下諸執事，罔不遴具。而貴州左布政使宗璽、參政鄭錫文、傅習、參議江玠、按察使李麟、副使劉瓚、僉事王瑞之、沈圻，亦續食。多士迆邐而來，廼集提學副使鄭元、僉事夏邦謨所選士，鎖院三試之。雲南都指揮胡章、張松、方仲，外率其屬，防範惟謹。御史羅玉且誓于眾曰：「以人事君，臣之職也。所不盡心于
translation_en:
…Fang [completing the name Luo Fang on the preceding page] and Tao Xin; Vice Commissioners Wang Zhong, Chen Zhang, Zhan Yuan, and Jiang Long; and Assistant Commissioners Zhou Yu, Chen Qing, and Weng Su each assisted in the undertaking. All the other functionaries, from those responsible for printing the examination papers downward, were carefully selected and duly appointed. In Guizhou, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zong Xi, Administration Vice Commissioners Zheng Xiwen and Fu Xi, Administration Assistant Commissioner Jiang Jie, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Li Lin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Liu Zan, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Wang Ruizhi and Shen Qi likewise supplied provisions along the way [?].

The many candidates arrived in succession. Those selected by Education Intendant Zheng Yuan, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Xia Bangmo, a Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, were then assembled, and the examination compound was locked for their three examination sessions. Outside, Yunnan Regional Military Commissioners Hu Zhang, Zhang Song, and Fang Zhong led their subordinates in maintaining strict security.

Censor Luo Yu also swore an oath before the assembled officials, saying: “To serve the ruler by finding worthy men is a minister’s duty. Should we fail to devote ourselves wholeheartedly to …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
國事違公徇私拔庸黜賢者神
則臨之殄厥祿誓已退各事
事鑾等精一校讎靡有夙暮
額得士五十五人其不能悉
取者或有矣旣乃刻其文之
純者爲錄以
獻鑾當序諸首惟雲貴古泰黔之
===
地而西南之紀也然其風厚
其氣和山水之會萃陰陽之
融結固必有異物出焉往時
如良馬犀象金貝文石或産
于絕域利用中土然皆禹貢
所棄雖勤遠貴異之世猶未
之取迺今則纖無遺矣孰知
punctuated: 國事，違公徇私，拔庸黜賢者，神則臨之，殄厥祿。」誓已，退各事事。鑾等精一校讎，靡有夙暮，額得士五十五人。其不能悉取者，或有矣。旣乃刻其文之純者爲錄，以獻。鑾當序諸首。惟雲貴，古泰黔之地，而西南之紀也。然其風厚，其氣和，山水之會萃，陰陽之融結，固必有異物出焉。往時如良馬、犀象、金貝、文石，或産于絕域，利用中土，然皆《禹貢》所棄，雖勤遠貴異之世，猶未之取。迺今則纖無遺矣。孰知
translation_en:
…state affairs, violate public duty to serve private interests, and promote the mediocre while rejecting the worthy—the spirits shall watch over them and extinguish their emoluments.” When the oath was concluded, they withdrew, each to perform his duties. Luan and his colleagues examined the papers with single-minded concentration, regardless of morning or evening, selecting the prescribed quota of fifty-five men. There may have been worthy men whom they could not admit. They then had the finest essays carved into printing blocks to produce a record for presentation to the throne. It fell to Luan to write the preface at its beginning.

Yunnan and Guizhou occupy the ancient lands of Tai and Qian [?] and form the bounds of the southwest. Their customs are generous and their vital energies harmonious. Where mountains and waters converge, and yin and yang blend, extraordinary things must surely emerge. In former times, fine horses, rhinoceroses, elephants, gold, cowries, and patterned stones sometimes came from remote regions and served useful purposes in the central lands. Yet these were all excluded from the Tribute of Yu. Even in ages that cultivated distant regions and prized rarities, they had not yet been procured. Now, however, not the slightest thing is left out. Who knows…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
瑰瑋俶儻卓犖不羣之士固
彬彬然先後繼出其間皆能
和其聲以鳴
國家之盛邪蓋山川之正氣不
鍾于物而鍾于人太平之景
象不寶異物而寶賢人矧惟
我
國家仁覆海隅聲教四訖外夷
子弟亦知嚮義求入大學肆
今餘百五十年學校之設殆
徧天下而雲貴遐土尤切霑
濡至于增學校廣解額實與
夫鼓舞作興之機
皇上稽古右文柄用儒碩羣姦宿
punctuated:
瑰瑋俶儻、卓犖不羣之士，固彬彬然先後繼出其間，皆能和其聲以鳴國家之盛邪？蓋山川之正氣，不鍾于物而鍾于人；太平之景象，不寶異物而寶賢人。矧惟我國家，仁覆海隅，聲教四訖，外夷子弟亦知嚮義，求入大學。肆今餘百五十年，學校之設殆徧天下，而雲貴遐土尤切霑濡。至于增學校、廣解額，實與夫鼓舞作興之機。
皇上稽古右文，柄用儒碩，羣姦宿
translation_en:
… men of extraordinary gifts and unfettered spirit, outstanding and beyond the common run, have indeed emerged here in cultivated succession, all able to join their voices in proclaiming the flourishing of the dynasty? For the upright vital force of mountains and rivers gathers not in objects but in people; an age of peace finds its treasures not in exotic things but in worthy men. Moreover, our dynasty’s benevolence extends to the remotest shores, and its civilizing influence reaches in all four directions. Even the sons of foreign peoples know to turn toward righteousness and seek admission to the Imperial University. Now, after more than a hundred and fifty years, schools have been established almost everywhere under Heaven, and the distant lands of Yunnan and Guizhou have received particularly abundant benefits. Increasing the schools and enlarging the quota of provincial graduates have indeed provided the means to encourage and invigorate learning.
His Majesty examines antiquity, honors literary culture, and entrusts authority to eminent Confucian scholars; the many malefactors and long-standing …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
弊一切掃除而嘉靖一
詔拳拳以却貢獻禁守臣爲言夷
裔老幼携扶往聽想見
德化之成士以逢掖遊庠序者
苟非暴棄之徒皆欲抱忠貞
以求自効蓋
祖宗豐芑之遺
===
列聖菁莪之化於是爲至宜其人
才之盛物產之嗇而士之投
牒而進者加多於昔也是豈
山川之靈淑能獨使之然哉
夫今茲之選諸士既有以自
見矣由是益加砥礪不爲空
言期於實用上以贊
punctuated: 弊一切掃除，而嘉靖一詔，拳拳以却貢獻、禁守臣爲言。夷裔老幼携扶往聽，想見德化之成。士以逢掖遊庠序者，苟非暴棄之徒，皆欲抱忠貞以求自効。蓋祖宗豐芑之遺、列聖菁莪之化，於是爲至。宜其人才之盛，物產之嗇，而士之投牒而進者加多於昔也。是豈山川之靈淑能獨使之然哉？夫今茲之選，諸士既有以自見矣。由是益加砥礪，不爲空言，期於實用，上以贊
translation_en:
…abuses were all swept away. In the inaugural decree of the Jiajing reign, earnest emphasis was placed on refusing tribute offerings and restraining territorial officials. Among the non-Han peoples, old and young supported one another as they went to hear it: one can envision the success of this moral transformation. Scholars who attend the schools wearing the ample robes of learning, unless they have utterly abandoned themselves, all wish to embrace loyalty and integrity and seek to render service. Indeed, the founding ancestors’ legacy of nurturing future generations, evoked by “Luxuriant Millet,” and the successive sage emperors’ cultivation of scholars, evoked by “Flourishing Southernwood,” have here reached their fullest expression. It is fitting that talent should flourish, and that, although local produce is scant, more scholars than formerly should submit their papers and come forward. Could the auspicious influences of the mountains and rivers alone have brought this about?

Now, through this selection, you scholars have already had an opportunity to demonstrate your abilities. Henceforth, sharpen and temper yourselves still further; do not indulge in empty words, but aim at practical usefulness, so that you may, above, assist…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
休明之治而下求所以異於齊
民我之所應而有司之所求
舉於責無訾焉則亦幾矣脫
或行不掩言名浮于實甘於
卑下而不耻僞爲矯飾以欺
人則科目何賴於賢而吾儒
光大之功用固如是乎哉諸
===
士其慎厥始圖惟厥終無貽
終身之悔可矣
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學
正季鑾謹序
punctuated:
休明之治，而下求所以異於齊民。我之所應，而有司之所求，舉於責無訾焉，則亦幾矣。脫或行不掩言，名浮于實，甘於卑下而不耻，僞爲矯飾以欺人，則科目何賴於賢，而吾儒光大之功用固如是乎哉？諸士其慎厥始，圖惟厥終，無貽終身之悔可矣。
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正季鑾謹序。
translation_en:
…enlightened government, and, below, seek the means of distinguishing yourselves from the common people. If, in meeting what is incumbent upon us and what the responsible officials seek, we fulfill all our duties without reproach, then we will have come close to the ideal. If, however, conduct fails to match words, reputation exceeds substance, and you willingly sink into baseness without shame, putting on a false appearance to deceive others, then what benefit can the examination system derive from such worthies? Can this truly be the way we Confucian scholars exercise our power to extend and illuminate the Way? You scholars should take care at the beginning and give thought to the end, so that you leave yourselves no cause for lifelong regret.
Preface respectfully composed by Ji Luan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
國治而后天下平
夫子喟然嘆曰吾與點也
學問之道無他求其放心而已矣
易
比吉原筮元永貞无咎
進以正可以正邦也
是以明於天之道而察於民之故是興神
===
物以前民用
易之爲書也不可遠爲道也屢遷
書
敬敷五敎在寬
恭默思道夢帝賚予良弼
文王不敢盤于遊田以庶邦惟正之供
宅乃事宅乃牧宅乃準兹惟后矣
詩
于以采蘩于沼于沚于以用之公侯之事
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
國治而后天下平。
夫子喟然嘆曰：「吾與點也。」
學問之道無他，求其放心而已矣。

易
比，吉。原筮，元永貞，无咎。
進以正，可以正邦也。
是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。
易之爲書也，不可遠；爲道也，屢遷。

書
敬敷五敎，在寬。
恭默思道，夢帝賚予良弼。
文王不敢盤于遊田，以庶邦惟正之供。
宅乃事，宅乃牧，宅乃準，兹惟后矣。

詩
于以采蘩？于沼于沚。于以用之？公侯之事。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
Only after the state is well governed is all under Heaven brought to peace.
The Master sighed deeply and said, “I am with Dian.”
The way of learning is nothing other than seeking to recover one’s strayed heart.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
Holding Together brings good fortune. Examine the matter through divination: with fundamental goodness, constancy, and steadfast correctness, there will be no blame.
By advancing with correctness, one can set the state right.
Thus, understanding the Way of Heaven and discerning the circumstances of the people, they instituted numinous objects to guide the people in their use of them.
The Changes is a book from which one must not remain distant; as a Way, it continually changes.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
Reverently disseminate the five teachings, exercising forbearance.
Reverently and silently I pondered the Way, and dreamed that the Lord on High bestowed upon me a worthy helper.
King Wen did not dare indulge in excursions and hunting; he concerned himself with the proper tribute supplied by the many states.
Set in their places those who administer your affairs, those who govern your people, and those who administer your justice: this is what it means to be a ruler.

Book of Odes (Shijing)
Where do we gather white southernwood? By the pools and on the islets. For what do we use it? For the sacrificial services of dukes and lords.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
樂只君子德音是茂
既燕于宗福祿攸降公尸燕飲福祿來崇
帝命式于九圍
春秋
公會齊侯于防〔隱公九年〕
公敗齊師于長勺〔莊公十年〕公會齊侯
盟于柯〔莊公十有三年〕
晉人宋人衛人曹人同盟于清丘〔宣公十
有二年〕
遂城虎牢〔襄公二年〕戍鄭虎牢楚公子
貞帥師救鄭〔襄公十年〕
禮記
五者備當上帝其饗
雜帶君朱綠大夫玄華士緇辟二寸再繚
四寸
禮樂之說管乎人情矣
君爲正則百姓從政矣
第貳場
punctuated:
樂只君子，德音是茂。
既燕于宗，福祿攸降；公尸燕飲，福祿來崇。
帝命式于九圍。

春秋
公會齊侯于防〔隱公九年〕。
公敗齊師于長勺〔莊公十年〕。公會齊侯，盟于柯〔莊公十有三年〕。
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人同盟于清丘〔宣公十有二年〕。
遂城虎牢〔襄公二年〕。戍鄭虎牢。楚公子貞帥師救鄭〔襄公十年〕。

禮記
五者備當，上帝其饗。
雜帶：君朱綠，大夫玄華，士緇；辟二寸，再繚四寸。
禮樂之說，管乎人情矣。
君爲正，則百姓從政矣。

第貳場
translation_en:
Joyful is the noble gentleman; his virtuous reputation flourishes.
When the feast is held in the ancestral temple, blessings and emoluments descend. The ancestral impersonator feasts and drinks; blessings and emoluments come in abundance.
The Lord on High commanded him to serve as a model for the nine regions.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke met the Marquis of Qi at Fang. 〔Ninth year of Duke Yin〕
The duke defeated the army of Qi at Changshao. 〔Tenth year of Duke Zhuang〕 The duke met the Marquis of Qi and concluded a covenant at Ke. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang〕
Men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao jointly concluded a covenant at Qingqiu. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan〕
They thereupon fortified Hulao. 〔Second year of Duke Xiang〕 A garrison was stationed at Hulao in Zheng. Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to rescue Zheng. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang〕

Record of Rites
When all five are complete and fitting, the Lord on High will accept the offering.
For belts with variegated edging: the ruler uses vermilion and green; grandees use black with ornamentation; servicemen use black. The width is two cun, doubled to make four cun [?].
The teachings concerning rites and music encompass human feelings.
When the ruler is upright, the common people follow his governance.

Second Session

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
論
講學爲正心之要
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢勸農桑禁采黃金珠玉詔〔景帝後三〕
〔年〕
擬唐以楊綰爲國子祭酒誥〔大曆五年〕
擬宋製觀文鑒古圖輔臣賀表〔慶曆四年〕
判語〔五條〕
損壞倉庫財物
===
守掌在官財物
乘驛馬齎私物
私受公侯財物
官吏聽許財物
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問帝王爲治之要道莫粹於洪範百聖傳
心之要典莫粹於大學善乎儒先有曰
不學書無以議制又曰爲人君而不知
punctuated:
論
講學爲正心之要。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢勸農桑、禁采黃金珠玉詔〔景帝後三年〕。
擬唐以楊綰爲國子祭酒誥〔大曆五年〕。
擬宋製觀文鑒古圖，輔臣賀表〔慶曆四年〕。
