損壞倉庫財物。
守掌在官財物。
乘驛馬齎私物。
私受公侯財物。
官吏聽許財物。

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：帝王爲治之要道，莫粹於《洪範》；百聖傳心之要典，莫粹於《大學》。善乎儒先有曰：「不學《書》，無以議制。」又曰：「爲人君而不知
translation_en:
Discourse
The investigation and discussion of learning are essential to rectifying the mind.

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han ruler encouraging agriculture and sericulture and prohibiting the extraction of gold, pearls, and jade. 〔Third year of Emperor Jing’s latter reign period〕
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Yang Wan as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education. 〔Fifth year of Dali〕
Compose a congratulatory memorial from the chief ministers of the Song on the production of the Illustrations for Viewing Cultural Achievements and Taking Antiquity as a Mirror (Guanwen jiangu tu). 〔Fourth year of Qingli〕

Legal judgments 〔Five items〕
Damaging goods in granaries and storehouses.
Custody and management of government property.
Carrying private goods while riding relay horses.
Privately accepting property from dukes and marquises.
Officials and clerks agreeing to accept property.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔Five questions〕
Question: Of the essential principles by which emperors and kings govern, none is more refined than the Great Plan (Hongfan); of the essential canonical texts transmitting the inner teaching of the hundred sages, none is more refined than the Great Learning (Daxue). Apt indeed are the words of an earlier Confucian scholar: “Without studying the Book of Documents, one has no basis for discussing institutions.” He also said: “To be a ruler of men and yet not understand …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
大學無以清出治之原是故唐虞三代
治隆俗美而非後世所及者蓋有堯舜
禹之中湯之敬文之純武之極大本立
而大用著夫豈徒哉洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝
天聰明之至
妙聖神之機當
大業甫定之餘即
===
聖學緝熈之日於尚書洪範則
親御翰墨詳疏其旨於大學衍義則揭於
殿廡時復睇觀蓋得二書之純以立其本也
審矣其間
聖製之所述
聖政之所施與凡當時侍臣之所論議無非經
世之用千載而下可仰而窺也其脗合
於洪範大學與比隆於唐虞三代者多
矣諸生涵濡
punctuated: 大學，無以清出治之原。是故唐虞三代治隆俗美，而非後世所及者，蓋有堯舜禹之中、湯之敬、文之純、武之極，大本立而大用著，夫豈徒哉！洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，天聰明之至，妙聖神之機，當大業甫定之餘，即聖學緝熈之日。於尚書洪範，則親御翰墨，詳疏其旨；於大學衍義，則揭於殿廡，時復睇觀。蓋得二書之純以立其本也，審矣。其間聖製之所述、聖政之所施，與凡當時侍臣之所論議，無非經世之用，千載而下，可仰而窺也。其脗合於洪範、大學，與比隆於唐虞三代者多矣。諸生涵濡
translation_en:
…the Great Learning, he has no means of purifying the source from which governance proceeds. Thus, under Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, government flourished and customs were admirable to a degree unattainable in later ages. This was because there were the centrality of Yao, Shun, and Yu, the reverence of Tang, the purity of King Wen, and the supreme standard of King Wu. The great foundation was established and its great efficacy became manifest. Could this have been without cause?

We reverently consider how our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao possessed the utmost heaven-endowed intelligence [?] and wondrous powers of sagely insight. As soon as his great undertaking had been secured, he devoted himself to continuing and illuminating sagely learning. Concerning the “Great Plan” in the Book of Documents, he personally took up brush and ink and expounded its meaning in detail. As for the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi), he had it displayed in the palace halls and galleries and repeatedly examined it. Surely he grasped the pure essence of these two works and thereby established his foundation.

What his sagely writings set forth, what his sagely government put into practice, and everything discussed by the attendant officials of that time all served the ordering of the world. Even a thousand years later, one may look up to these achievements and discern them. Many accorded closely with the “Great Plan” and the Great Learning and rivaled the flourishing rule of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. You students have been steeped in…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖化蓋已有年其敬陳之毋忽
問詔令者帝王以心動天下之大幾也幾
動於善則天下應之以善矣堯舜聖者
也其幾動於治天下也一出言即可爲
世法令觀其典謨所載都俞吁咈之間
君臣氣通内外機應天下即形之矣湯
雖聖者自時則有誓矣誓也者終不若
典謨相信之深也周之末則詛矣民不
惟不信且有作慝作怨之刑而上下之
===
心離矣秦尚奚足言哉自漢之興詔多
可紀有聞之而士生色者有聞之而民
伸眉者惟士與民天下元氣元氣理則
百體從令矣仰惟我
皇上即位一詔上以昭天道下以悉人情其錄
忠褒節與詩書所載者何所同其愛民
惜財與帝王所行者何所合敬老乃示
民以知孝也優賢乃示民以崇德也皆
慎固邦本之大端培養元氣之首務令
punctuated:
聖化，蓋已有年，其敬陳之，毋忽。
問：詔令者，帝王以心動天下之大幾也。幾動於善，則天下應之以善矣。堯舜，聖者也，其幾動於治天下也，一出言即可爲世法令。觀其典謨所載，都俞吁咈之間，君臣氣通，内外機應，天下即形之矣。湯雖聖者，自時則有誓矣。誓也者，終不若典謨相信之深也。周之末則詛矣，民不惟不信，且有作慝作怨之刑，而上下之心離矣。秦尚奚足言哉！自漢之興，詔多可紀，有聞之而士生色者，有聞之而民伸眉者。惟士與民，天下元氣；元氣理，則百體從令矣。仰惟我皇上即位一詔，上以昭天道，下以悉人情。其錄忠褒節，與詩書所載者何所同？其愛民惜財，與帝王所行者何所合？敬老乃示民以知孝也，優賢乃示民以崇德也，皆慎固邦本之大端、培養元氣之首務。令
translation_en:
…the sage influence for what must already be many years. Respectfully set forth your views on this; do not be careless.
Question: Edicts and commands are the great pivotal means by which emperors and kings move all under Heaven through their own hearts. When the impulse tends toward goodness, all under Heaven respond with goodness. Yao and Shun were sages: when their impulse moved toward governing all under Heaven, a single utterance could become a rule and command for the world. Consider what is recorded in their Canons and Counsels: amid expressions of approval, assent, caution, and dissent, ruler and ministers were in sympathetic accord, and impulses within and without responded to one another; this then took visible form throughout the realm [?]. Although Tang was a sage, from his time there were already Oaths. Oaths, after all, could not match the depth of mutual trust found in the Canons and Counsels. By the end of the Zhou there were curses. Not only did the people lack trust; there were also punishments for doing evil and stirring resentment, and the hearts of those above and below became estranged. What need is there even to speak of the Qin!
From the rise of the Han, many edicts deserve to be recorded. Some brought a glow to scholars’ faces when they heard them; others smoothed the brows of the common people. Scholars and common people are the vital energy of all under Heaven. When that vital energy is properly regulated, all the body’s members obey its commands.
We reverently consider the edict issued by Our Emperor upon his accession: above, it made manifest the Way of Heaven; below, it fully comprehended human feelings. In recognizing loyalty and honoring integrity, what does it share with what is recorded in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents? In cherishing the people and conserving wealth, how does it accord with the practices of emperors and kings? Respecting the aged teaches the people to understand filial piety; favoring the worthy teaches them to esteem virtue. These are all principal means of carefully securing the foundations of the state and foremost tasks in nourishing its vital energy. Let…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
並舉而互言焉宜天下之感動如此其
速也矧察其廢閣也有方考其振舉也
有法即是而之焉三代之治可復也諸
生仰聽之餘不知尚將何以爲
獻請明著于篇毋使隨何之誚嘖嘖
問昔人謂讀書萬卷不讀律致君堯舜終
無術則刑律一節固學者之所當講者
我
朝法律因時以定制緣情以制刑誠萬世所
===
當遵守者也竊以平日所疑者與諸生
議之夫五刑在古所不宥也而舜典許
其贖金至穆王五刑之疑罰鍰有等然
則贖罰固可訓乎抑或别有論也延及
於漢因討西羌兵食不繼建爲入穀贖
罪之法謀國可謂忠矣何以有開利路
傷治化之譏又至於宋因人情冒利犯
禁别爲贖法使人重穀帛免刑罰憫下
可謂切矣何以有貧者不能自免之議
punctuated:
並舉而互言焉，宜天下之感動如此其速也。矧察其廢閣也有方，考其振舉也有法，即是而之焉，三代之治可復也。諸生仰聽之餘，不知尚將何以爲獻？請明著于篇，毋使隨何之誚嘖嘖。
問：昔人謂「讀書萬卷不讀律，致君堯舜終無術」，則刑律一節，固學者之所當講者。我朝法律，因時以定制，緣情以制刑，誠萬世所當遵守者也。竊以平日所疑者與諸生議之。夫五刑，在古所不宥也，而舜典許其贖金；至穆王，五刑之疑，罰鍰有等。然則贖罰固可訓乎？抑或别有論也？延及於漢，因討西羌，兵食不繼，建爲入穀贖罪之法，謀國可謂忠矣，何以有開利路、傷治化之譏？又至於宋，因人情冒利犯禁，别爲贖法，使人重穀帛、免刑罰，憫下可謂切矣，何以有貧者不能自免之議？
translation_en:
…all are put into effect together and articulated in conjunction. It is fitting that the realm should have been moved so swiftly. Moreover, there are proper means for investigating their neglect and suspension, and established methods for examining their revival and implementation. By proceeding along this course, the good government of the Three Dynasties can be restored. Having reverently heard these pronouncements, what further proposals will you candidates offer? Set them out clearly in your essays, so that Sui He’s reproach does not resound incessantly.
Question: A man of former times said, “If you read ten thousand volumes but do not study the statutes, you will ultimately lack the means to make your ruler a Yao or Shun.” Thus, penal statutes are certainly a subject scholars ought to study. Our dynasty’s laws establish institutions according to the needs of the times and prescribe punishments according to the circumstances. They are indeed provisions to be observed for ten thousand generations. I would venture to discuss with you candidates certain matters that have long puzzled me. In antiquity, offenses subject to the Five Punishments were not pardoned, yet the Canon of Shun permitted their redemption by payments of metal. Under King Mu, doubtful cases involving the Five Punishments were subject to graded fines assessed in huan, a unit of weight for metal. Should redemption payments and fines, then, indeed serve as a model? Or is there another interpretation? Later, under the Han, when campaigns against the Western Qiang left the army inadequately supplied with grain, a system was established allowing people to redeem their offenses by contributing grain. Such planning for the state may certainly be called loyal; why, then, was it criticized for opening a path to profit and undermining good government and moral transformation? Again, under the Song, because people pursued profit recklessly and violated prohibitions, a separate system of redemption was established, enabling people to attach value to grain and silk and escape punishment [?]. Such compassion for the people may certainly be called earnest; why, then, was it objected that the poor could not secure their own exemption? …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
夫刑以繩姦在盛世亦所不免而准贖
一法又非後人之所裁定毫芒輕重之
間世教勸懲所係諸生蓋必有超然之
見矣願一言之
問學之一言其來尚矣至孔門辨之始無
遺義而後世謂之學者尚多可疑焉其
借名於孔門以售己說者類亦多矣至
宋有五星聚奎之祥而諸儒應徵而出
發古人未言之妙啓後學難知之微使
===
無志於斯學者則亦已矣如有志於斯
焉舍是宜無所與論也試舉一二與商
之玉山有講義白鹿洞亦有講義其所
講之義同歟異歟春秋有講義乾卦亦
有講義其所講之義一歟二歟講於東
湖書院者可得指而陳耶講於竹林精
舍者可得舉而言耶嚴陵一講其條目
凡幾和靖一講其名義何居是皆正學
之階梯入聖之門路諸生不欲爲吾道
punctuated:
夫刑以繩姦，在盛世亦所不免，而准贖一法，又非後人之所裁定。毫芒輕重之間，世教勸懲所係，諸生蓋必有超然之見矣，願一言之。
問：學之一言，其來尚矣。至孔門辨之，始無遺義，而後世謂之學者，尚多可疑焉。其借名於孔門以售己說者，類亦多矣。至宋，有五星聚奎之祥，而諸儒應徵而出，發古人未言之妙，啓後學難知之微。使無志於斯學者，則亦已矣；如有志於斯焉，舍是宜無所與論也。試舉一二與商之：玉山有講義，白鹿洞亦有講義，其所講之義同歟異歟？春秋有講義，乾卦亦有講義，其所講之義一歟二歟？講於東湖書院者，可得指而陳耶？講於竹林精舍者，可得舉而言耶？嚴陵一講，其條目凡幾？和靖一講，其名義何居？是皆正學之階梯、入聖之門路。諸生不欲爲吾道
translation_en:
Punishments serve to restrain wrongdoing and cannot be dispensed with even in an age of flourishing government. Yet the provision permitting redemption of punishment was not devised by later generations either. The finest distinctions in severity bear upon the moral teaching of the age and the encouragement of good and deterrence of evil. You candidates surely have insights that rise above the ordinary; please set them forth.
Question: The term “learning” has a long history. Only when it was elucidated in the school of Confucius was its meaning fully expressed. Yet much of what later generations called learning remains open to doubt. There have also been many who borrowed the name of Confucius’s school to peddle their own doctrines. In the Song, the auspicious gathering of the five planets in the Kui constellation occurred, and Confucian scholars emerged in response to this portent. They brought to light subtleties that the ancients had not expressed and disclosed refinements difficult for later students to grasp. For those without aspirations to this learning, the matter may rest there. But for those who aspire to it, there should be no basis for discussion apart from these teachings. Let us raise one or two examples for consideration. There are Lecture Expositions from Yushan, and also Lecture Expositions from Bailudong. Are the principles expounded in them the same or different? There are Lecture Expositions on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and also on the Qian hexagram. Are the principles they expound one or two? Can you identify and explain what was taught at Donghu Academy? Can you cite and discuss what was taught at the Zhulin Study Retreat? How many items were there in the lecture at Yanling? What is the significance of the name of Hejing’s lecture? These are all steps toward orthodox learning and pathways into sagehood. If you candidates do not wish to pursue the learning of our Way …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之學吾固不得而强聒也如耻爲世俗
之學焉舍是則無所與共圖者盍悉之
以觀脩身用世之具
問蠲貸之令三代之時不聞然則何從而
始也豈後世之寬仁反過於古與自是
有蠲逋貸者有寬逋賦者有除戶調絹
綿者有蠲度支鹽鐵者有減上供饋運
者有免官司債負和買役錢者條目雖
殊而寬貸之仁一也然儒臣建議又多
===
不同夫積欠負欠每年帶納一分似爲
便民矣何以有豐年不如凶年之論民
窮賦重盡數蠲除而困尚未甦也何以
有催理九分遷延一分以待蠲放之說
嗚呼蠲貸之典本欲厚民而歲計未免
侵損本欲博愛而小民未必霑恩果何
如而使德澤旁通困窮受惠也其詳言
之以觀經制之策
punctuated:
之學，吾固不得而强聒也。如耻爲世俗之學焉，舍是則無所與共圖者。盍悉之，以觀脩身用世之具？

問：蠲貸之令，三代之時不聞，然則何從而始也？豈後世之寬仁反過於古與？自是有蠲逋貸者，有寬逋賦者，有除戶調絹綿者，有蠲度支鹽鐵者，有減上供饋運者，有免官司債負、和買、役錢者。條目雖殊，而寬貸之仁一也。然儒臣建議，又多不同。夫積欠、負欠，每年帶納一分，似爲便民矣，何以有豐年不如凶年之論？民窮賦重，盡數蠲除，而困尚未甦也，何以有催理九分、遷延一分以待蠲放之說？嗚呼！蠲貸之典，本欲厚民，而歲計未免侵損；本欲博愛，而小民未必霑恩。果何如而使德澤旁通、困窮受惠也？其詳言之，以觀經制之策。
translation_en:
…such learning, I certainly cannot insist upon wearying you with my words. If you are ashamed to pursue worldly learning, however, then apart from this there is nothing we can plan together. Why not explain it fully, so that we may assess your resources for cultivating yourselves and serving the world?

Question: Orders granting remission and relief were unheard of during the Three Dynasties. When, then, did they originate? Could the generosity and benevolence of later ages actually have surpassed those of antiquity? Since their introduction, there have been remissions of overdue loans, relief from tax arrears, exemptions from household levies of silk cloth and silk floss, remissions of fiscal levies on salt and iron [?], reductions in supplies sent to the court and the transport of provisions, and exemptions from debts owed to government offices, compulsory government purchases, and payments in lieu of labor service. Although the provisions differ, the benevolence expressed in granting relief is the same. Yet proposals submitted by Confucian officials have also differed considerably.

Collecting one tenth of accumulated arrears and outstanding obligations each year alongside current payments would seem convenient for the people. Why, then, has it been argued that a plentiful year is worse than a famine year? When the people are impoverished and taxes burdensome, even complete remission has failed to relieve their distress. Why, then, is there talk of pressing for collection of nine tenths while delaying payment of the remaining tenth in anticipation of remission?

Alas! The established practice of remission and relief was intended to benefit the people, yet annual state finances inevitably suffer losses. It was intended to extend care widely, yet ordinary people do not necessarily receive its favors. What, then, would ensure that imperial beneficence reaches everywhere and that those in poverty and distress receive its benefits? Explain this in detail, so that we may assess your proposals for fiscal administration.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
國治而后天下平
張合
同考試官訓導詹批大學一題人皆能
習之皆能道之下筆處便欠切當
是篇發明經意畧無汎漫之語而
氣格復整豈深於造道者邪
考試官教諭周批講聖經本色語自
是難造此作妙矣
===
考試官學正季批無一句可疵錄之
既有以新一邦之民斯有以新一世之民甚矣
化行自近始也新民之功由一邦而推之於一
世焉其序固如是哉聖經覆言大學之條目至
此蓋謂國於天下雖有遠近之殊而化之所被
初無彼此之間是故提封井井而根本乎諸夏
天子之國政令於是乎出京邑翼翼而表正乎
四方天子之邦聲教於是乎行烝民之生習俗
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
國治而后天下平
張合

同考試官訓導詹批：大學一題，人皆能習之，皆能道之，下筆處便欠切當。是篇發明經意，畧無汎漫之語，而氣格復整，豈深於造道者邪？

考試官教諭周批：講聖經本色語，自是難造，此作妙矣。

考試官學正季批：無一句可疵，錄之。

既有以新一邦之民，斯有以新一世之民。甚矣，化行自近始也！新民之功，由一邦而推之於一世焉，其序固如是哉！聖經覆言大學之條目，至此蓋謂：國於天下，雖有遠近之殊，而化之所被，初無彼此之間。是故提封井井，而根本乎諸夏，天子之國，政令於是乎出；京邑翼翼，而表正乎四方，天子之邦，聲教於是乎行。烝民之生，習俗
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When the state is well governed, all under Heaven is at peace.”
Zhang He

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: Everyone can study a topic from the Great Learning and discuss it, yet when they put brush to paper, they readily fall short of precision and aptness. This essay elucidates the classic’s meaning without the slightest vague or rambling expression; its vigor and style are also well ordered. Might its author be someone deeply advanced in attaining the Way?

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Expounding the sages’ classic in language true to its character is certainly difficult to accomplish. This composition is excellent.

Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: Not a single sentence can be faulted. Include it in the record.

Once there are the means to renew the people of one state, there are thereby the means to renew the people of an entire age. How profoundly true it is that transforming influence begins with those nearby! The work of renewing the people extends from one state to an entire age: surely this is its proper sequence! At this point, where the sages’ classic reiterates the successive articles of the Great Learning, its meaning is presumably this: although the state and all under Heaven differ in their nearness and remoteness, the reach of transforming influence makes no distinction between here and there. Thus, with its territorial boundaries in orderly array, it forms the foundation of the states of Xia: this is the Son of Heaven’s realm, from which governmental commands issue. With its capital majestic and well ordered, it sets a correct example for the four quarters: this is the Son of Heaven’s state, from which moral instruction spreads. As for the lives of the common people, their accustomed practices…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
所移未易一也然自新之德出于身而加于民
凡有所觀感者舊染之汚以革翕然遵道遵義
之風羣黎之聚氣品所拘未易化也然自明之
德發乎邇而見乎遠凡知所興起者敦睦之俗
自成居然不識不知之域國其有不治耶夫大
道之行有可化之機至仁之推無不準之理由
是薄海之內體國之外天下固大矣皆歸于允
脩之極天之所覆地之所載四海固廣矣舉囿
于昭明之天凡民有行意以之誠心以之正而
===
矯僞之惑不作蕩蕩乎民恊于中之盛也有生
之衆身知所脩家知所齊而親長之愛以流熈
熈乎萬國咸寧之休也天下有不平邪是則舍
近而謀遠其爲力也難篤近而舉遠其責效也
易自新之功既至新民之化自成蓋有不期然
而然者矣大學君子可不知所務哉蓋嘗論之
治天下有本身之謂也治天下有則家之謂也
大學言明德新民之序極其體用之全蓋不徒
爲入德之門雖堯舜之治亦不過此而後之君
punctuated: 所移，未易一也。然自新之德出于身而加于民，凡有所觀感者，舊染之汚以革，翕然遵道遵義之風。羣黎之聚，氣品所拘，未易化也。然自明之德發乎邇而見乎遠，凡知所興起者，敦睦之俗自成，居然不識不知之域。國其有不治耶？夫大道之行，有可化之機；至仁之推，無不準之理。由是薄海之內，體國之外，天下固大矣，皆歸于允脩之極；天之所覆，地之所載，四海固廣矣，舉囿于昭明之天。凡民有行，意以之誠，心以之正，而矯僞之惑不作，蕩蕩乎民恊于中之盛也！有生之衆，身知所脩，家知所齊，而親長之愛以流，熈熈乎萬國咸寧之休也！天下有不平邪？是則舍近而謀遠，其爲力也難；篤近而舉遠，其責效也易。自新之功既至，新民之化自成，蓋有不期然而然者矣。大學君子可不知所務哉？蓋嘗論之：治天下有本，身之謂也；治天下有則，家之謂也。大學言明德新民之序，極其體用之全，蓋不徒爲入德之門，雖堯舜之治亦不過此，而後之君
translation_en:
…are shaped by customs and cannot readily be made uniform. Yet when the virtue of renewing oneself proceeds from one’s own person and extends to the people, all who witness it and are moved by it cast off the defilement of their former habits, joining together in a spirit of following the Way and righteousness. The multitudes of common people, constrained by their differing endowments of vital force, cannot readily be transformed. Yet when the virtue of illuminating oneself begins nearby and becomes manifest afar, all who know to rouse themselves naturally develop customs of generosity and concord. They dwell, at ease, in a realm where goodness is practiced without conscious knowledge or understanding. How could the state fail to be well governed?

When the great Way prevails, there is an opportunity for transformation; when utmost benevolence is extended, its principle is applicable everywhere. Thus, throughout the lands bounded by the seas and beyond the capital [?], vast though all under Heaven may be, everyone returns to the highest standard of true cultivation. Throughout all that Heaven covers and Earth sustains, broad though the Four Seas may be, everyone is embraced beneath a radiant heaven. In all the people’s conduct, their intentions thereby become sincere and their minds thereby become rectified, so that the delusions of pretence and falsehood do not arise. How expansive is this flourishing condition, in which the people accord with the mean! All living people know to cultivate themselves and regulate their families, and love for parents and elders spreads abroad. How joyful is the blessed condition in which the myriad states all enjoy peace! How could all under Heaven fail to be at peace?

Thus, to abandon what is near and plan for what is distant makes the undertaking difficult; to attend earnestly to what is near and thereby extend one’s efforts afar makes results easy to obtain. Once the work of renewing oneself has reached its culmination, the transformation that renews the people comes about of itself. There are indeed effects that arise without being deliberately sought. Can the gentleman devoted to the Great Learning fail to know where to direct his efforts?

I have considered this: governing all under Heaven has a root—one’s own person; governing all under Heaven has a model—one’s family. The Great Learning explains the sequence of illuminating virtue and renewing the people, encompassing the completeness of both substance and function. It is more than merely the gateway to entering into virtue: even the governance of Yao and Shun went no further than this. Yet the gentlemen of later ages…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
子卒致慨乎至治之澤何哉大學之道不明而
正心之功未講耳善乎董子之言曰正心以正
朝廷正朝廷以正百官正百官以正萬民森然
孔氏家法也聖君賢相苟欲共成正大光明之
業者尚鑒兹哉
夫子喟然嘆曰吾與點也
趙汝濂
同考試官訓導鄭批場中作此題者率
爲暮春以下數句纏繞於聖人許
===
點之意全形容不出此作於清明
峻潔之中有雍容頓挫之態亦異
乎諸士之撰矣
考試官教諭周批寫出曾點自得及
聖人嘆許氣象宛然在目
考試官學正季批胸次不凡立論自
别
聖人於賢者形於嘆而許之深所以重其志也
蓋聖人不輕以譽人也於曾點而嘆許之深者
punctuated:
子卒致慨乎至治之澤，何哉？大學之道不明，而正心之功未講耳。善乎董子之言曰：「正心以正朝廷，正朝廷以正百官，正百官以正萬民。」森然孔氏家法也。聖君賢相苟欲共成正大光明之業者，尚鑒兹哉！
夫子喟然嘆曰：「吾與點也。」
趙汝濂
同考試官訓導鄭批：場中作此題者，率爲暮春以下數句纏繞，於聖人許點之意，全形容不出。此作於清明峻潔之中，有雍容頓挫之態，亦異乎諸士之撰矣。
考試官教諭周批：寫出曾點自得及聖人嘆許氣象，宛然在目。
考試官學正季批：胸次不凡，立論自别。
聖人於賢者，形於嘆而許之深，所以重其志也。蓋聖人不輕以譽人也，於曾點而嘆許之深者，
translation_en:
…why, then, have later gentlemen come to lament the loss of the blessings of perfect government? It is simply because the Way of the Great Learning has not been understood, and the work of rectifying the mind has not been examined. Excellent are Master Dong’s words: “Rectify the mind to rectify the court; rectify the court to rectify the hundred officials; rectify the hundred officials to rectify the myriad people.” Here stands, in imposing order, the teaching handed down in the school of Confucius. If sage rulers and worthy chief councillors wish together to accomplish an upright and radiant undertaking, let them take this as their guide!
The Master sighed deeply and said: “I am with Dian.”
Zhao Rulian
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: Those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic were generally entangled in the several sentences beginning with “late spring,” and entirely failed to convey the sage’s intention in approving of Dian. This composition combines clarity, loftiness, and purity with an unhurried bearing and well-modulated turns. It is indeed different from the compositions of the other candidates.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: The depiction of Zeng Dian’s inner contentment and of the sage’s sigh of approval brings their bearing vividly before the eyes.
Comment by Examiner Ji, School Instructor: His cast of mind is uncommon, and his argument stands apart.
When the sage expressed himself in a sigh and gave a worthy man his profound approval, it was because he esteemed that man’s aspirations. For the sage did not lightly bestow praise upon others. As for his sigh and profound approval of Zeng Dian …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
其亦有所感哉昔吾夫子當門人言志之餘正
曾點敷陳之際真樂氣象感觸乎與物同體之
天順適襟懷契合乎隨寓而安之妙於是天機
黙應而感嘆隨之心有所樂而口之宣揚自有
不能已者矣妙理潜孚而嘆息繼之中有所悅
而言之吐露盖有不容遏者矣其意以為人孰
無志也而或失於外馳志非不壯也而每忽於
内重惟爾曾點充然自得崛起於儔伍之中脫
然無累傑出乎風塵之表涵養既熟而動靜從
===
容依稀乎欲盡理還之境較之汲汲於功名之
會者自不侔矣寧容已於嘆賞乎識見既精而
志嚮卓越彷佛乎安土樂天之趣比之規規於
事為之末者有間矣寧容已於稱許乎數言之
間具見心事真實可以激頹風者在是吾不許
點而誰許哉一時之對足知操履真純可以敦
士行者在是吾不與點而誰與哉是則非諸子
不能見曾點之高非曾點不能發聖人之嘆孔
門師弟子雍容交與之氣象於是乎見矣雖然
punctuated: 其亦有所感哉！昔吾夫子當門人言志之餘，正曾點敷陳之際，真樂氣象感觸乎與物同體之天，順適襟懷契合乎隨寓而安之妙。於是天機黙應，而感嘆隨之；心有所樂，而口之宣揚，自有不能已者矣。妙理潜孚，而嘆息繼之；中有所悅，而言之吐露，盖有不容遏者矣。其意以為：人孰無志也，而或失於外馳；志非不壯也，而每忽於内重。惟爾曾點，充然自得，崛起於儔伍之中；脫然無累，傑出乎風塵之表。涵養既熟，而動靜從容，依稀乎欲盡理還之境，較之汲汲於功名之會者，自不侔矣，寧容已於嘆賞乎？識見既精，而志嚮卓越，彷佛乎安土樂天之趣，比之規規於事為之末者，有間矣，寧容已於稱許乎？數言之間，具見心事真實，可以激頹風者在是，吾不許點而誰許哉？一時之對，足知操履真純，可以敦士行者在是，吾不與點而誰與哉？是則非諸子不能見曾點之高，非曾點不能發聖人之嘆。孔門師弟子雍容交與之氣象，於是乎見矣。雖然，
translation_en:
…must he not also have been moved by something? Formerly, when the other disciples had finished speaking of their aspirations and Zeng Dian was setting forth his own, his air of genuine joy stirred in our Master that heavenly nature which forms one body with all things; his ease of heart accorded with the wondrous capacity to be at peace wherever one finds oneself. Thus the spontaneous workings of Heaven responded silently within the Master, and an admiring sigh followed. His heart found joy, and he could not help giving voice to it. Subtle principle found an unspoken correspondence within him, and a sigh ensued. Pleased inwardly, he could not restrain the expression of his delight.

His meaning was this: Who lacks aspirations? Yet some go astray in pursuing things outside themselves. Their aspirations are not without grandeur, yet they often neglect the weightier concerns within. You alone, Zeng Dian, abundantly content within yourself, rise above your companions; free and unencumbered, you stand beyond the dust and turmoil of the world. Your self-cultivation has ripened, and you are composed in both activity and stillness, approaching the state in which desires are exhausted and principle returns. You are quite unlike those who anxiously seek opportunities for achievement and fame. How could I refrain from sighing in admiration? Your understanding is refined and your aspirations lofty, approaching the spirit of resting content in one’s circumstances and rejoicing in Heaven. You are far removed from those narrowly occupied with the minor details of practical affairs. How could I refrain from praising you? In a few words, the sincerity of your innermost concerns is fully revealed. Here is what can rouse a declining moral climate. If I do not approve of Dian, whom should I approve of? Your reply on this occasion suffices to show the sincerity and purity of your conduct. Here is what can strengthen the conduct of scholars. If I do not endorse Dian, whom should I endorse?

Thus, without the other disciples, Zeng Dian’s loftiness could not have been revealed; without Zeng Dian, the sage’s sigh could not have been elicited. Here we see the gracious ease with which master and disciples in the school of Confucius responded to and appreciated one another. Even so, …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
曾點之志固高矣使人皆潔身遠引獨善廢倫
則天下之事孰與共理哉但世至春秋急於功
利或失身喪節而不能自振者多欲累之也果
心境虚豁而不爲勢利紛華所制則其建立必
有大過人者此可見事業之偉實原於人品之
高惟有壁立之風度斯有孤高之氣節固相須
而難掩者噫曾點豈易及哉
學問之道無他求其放心而已矣
李元陽
===
同考試官學正方批此題場中作者多
以學問二字混講枯澁可厭且於
本章說仁義處略不相關此作專
主周易學聚問辨立意發揮殆盡
其起結又能照管仁義深得孟子
立言微旨子可謂究心理學有素
矣
考試官教諭周批遍觀諸作全非孟
子本意獨此篇體認真切筆力雄
punctuated:
曾點之志固高矣，使人皆潔身遠引，獨善廢倫，則天下之事孰與共理哉？但世至春秋，急於功利，或失身喪節而不能自振者多，欲累之也。果心境虚豁，而不爲勢利紛華所制，則其建立必有大過人者。此可見事業之偉，實原於人品之高。惟有壁立之風度，斯有孤高之氣節，固相須而難掩者。噫！曾點豈易及哉！

學問之道無他，求其放心而已矣。
李元陽

同考試官學正方批：此題場中作者，多以學問二字混講，枯澁可厭，且於本章說仁義處略不相關。此作專主《周易》學聚問辨，立意發揮殆盡。其起結又能照管仁義，深得孟子立言微旨。子可謂究心理學有素矣。

考試官教諭周批：遍觀諸作，全非孟子本意。獨此篇體認真切，筆力雄
translation_en:
…Zeng Dian’s aspirations were indeed lofty. Yet if everyone kept himself pure and withdrew far from public life, cultivating his own goodness while abandoning human relationships, with whom could one govern the affairs of the realm? But by the Spring and Autumn period, people were intent on achievement and profit. Many compromised themselves and forfeited their integrity, unable to recover, because desire encumbered them. If one’s mind is truly open and untrammeled, unconstrained by power, profit, worldly bustle, or splendor, one’s accomplishments will surely far surpass those of others. This shows that greatness of achievement truly originates in loftiness of character. Only with a bearing as sheer and unyielding as a cliff can one possess lofty, independent integrity. These qualities necessarily sustain each other and cannot readily be concealed. Ah! How could Zeng Dian be easy to equal!

“The way of learning and inquiry is nothing other than seeking one’s strayed mind.”
Li Yuanyang

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, School Instructor: Among those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic, most treated the two words ‘learning’ and ‘inquiry’ indiscriminately together. Their writing was dry, labored, and tiresome; moreover, it bore virtually no relation to the discussion of benevolence and righteousness in this chapter. This composition focuses specifically on the teaching in the Book of Changes that learning accumulates knowledge and inquiry discriminates among things, developing its conception almost exhaustively. Its opening and conclusion also attend to benevolence and righteousness, profoundly grasping the subtle intention behind Mencius’s words. You may indeed be said to have long devoted yourself to investigating the Learning of Principle.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: Having examined all the compositions, I find that they entirely miss Mencius’s original meaning. This piece alone shows a genuine and penetrating understanding, and its writing is powerful…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
健非平日養心靜而充之以學者
不能至此
考試官學正季批洗滌舊聞可以式
矣
大賢論為學之要收心之外無餘事也甚矣人
心易放也為學之要亦惟存此而已豈復有他
道哉昔孟子論仁為人心而嘆人失之不求及
此謂夫人不可以不學學莫貴於知要是故天
下事物之理有所當然者焉載諸古訓而可知
===
有所以然者焉布在方册而可考學不容已也
必須學以聚之或索之文字之間或資諸師友
之論何為所當然而體驗之不遺何為所以然
而講求之匪懈學不可謂不博矣理之所當然
者學雖有知猶或涉於疑似理之所以然者學
雖有得猶或滯於彷佛問不容已也必須問以
辨之或博考乎羣書或延訪乎衆論决其疑於
師匪直資諸人而已辨其義於友非但訪於衆
而已問不可謂不審矣夫學問之事固非一端
punctuated:
健，非平日養心靜而充之以學者不能至此。
考試官學正季批：洗滌舊聞，可以式矣。
大賢論為學之要，收心之外無餘事也。甚矣，人心易放也！為學之要，亦惟存此而已，豈復有他道哉？昔孟子論仁為人心，而嘆人失之不求。及此，謂夫人不可以不學，學莫貴於知要。是故天下事物之理，有所當然者焉，載諸古訓而可知；有所以然者焉，布在方册而可考。學不容已也，必須學以聚之。或索之文字之間，或資諸師友之論，何為所當然而體驗之不遺，何為所以然而講求之匪懈，學不可謂不博矣。理之所當然者，學雖有知，猶或涉於疑似；理之所以然者，學雖有得，猶或滯於彷佛。問不容已也，必須問以辨之。或博考乎羣書，或延訪乎衆論，决其疑於師，匪直資諸人而已；辨其義於友，非但訪於衆而已。問不可謂不審矣。夫學問之事，固非一端。
translation_en:
…vigorous. Only someone who habitually nurtures his mind in stillness and enriches it through learning could attain this.
Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: “This clears away received notions and may serve as a model.”
The great worthy discusses the essentials of learning: beyond gathering in the mind, there is nothing further to do. How readily the human mind wanders! The essential task of learning is simply to preserve this mind. Could there be any other way? Earlier, Mengzi explained that benevolence is the human mind and lamented that people lose it without seeking it. Here he says that people cannot dispense with learning, and that in learning nothing is more valuable than knowing what is essential. Thus, the principles governing the affairs and things of the world have aspects concerning what ought to be so, recorded in ancient teachings and available to be known; they also have aspects concerning why it is so, set out in books and available to be investigated. Learning cannot cease: one must learn in order to accumulate understanding. Whether seeking it in written texts or drawing upon discussions with teachers and friends, one must experience and examine what ought to be so without omission, and investigate why it is so without slackening. Such learning can certainly be called broad.
As for what ought to be so in principle, although through learning one knows something of it, one may still fall into uncertainty and apparent likenesses. As for why it is so in principle, although through learning one gains some understanding, one may still remain confined to vague impressions. Inquiry cannot cease: one must inquire in order to distinguish clearly. Whether consulting many books extensively or seeking out a wide range of views, one resolves doubts with a teacher, rather than merely drawing upon others; one distinguishes the meaning with friends, rather than merely consulting the multitude. Such inquiry can certainly be called discerning. Indeed, the work of learning and inquiry has more than one aspect…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
推原其要惟求諸心耳蓋心也者人之神明所
以具衆理者此其體所以應萬事者此其用易
放也或出或入無一定之時易失也于彼于斯
無常止之處必斂之於翼翼之天使既出者而
復入鎮靜自如無時不存可也約之於惺惺之
地使在彼者常在此一真自若無處不然可也
學問之道如此而已豈復有他求哉夫如是則
學問有益於己而心存心存則仁存矣仁存則
内而心之有制外而事之得宜義亦在其中矣
===
學者欲求仁義之理可不先於此心之致力與
抑孟子生丁是時權謀功利之徒縱橫游說之
輩藉此相高可謂月異而歲不同矣一旦憫人
心之陷溺慨道學之不明而揭此以示人有功
於吾道顧不偉哉先儒謂其功不在禹下益信
其然矣
易
進以正可以正邦也
趙汝濂
punctuated:
推原其要，惟求諸心耳。蓋心也者，人之神明，所以具衆理者，此其體；所以應萬事者，此其用。易放也，或出或入，無一定之時；易失也，于彼于斯，無常止之處。必斂之於翼翼之天，使既出者而復入，鎮靜自如，無時不存，可也；約之於惺惺之地，使在彼者常在此，一真自若，無處不然，可也。學問之道，如此而已，豈復有他求哉？夫如是，則學問有益於己而心存。心存則仁存矣；仁存，則内而心之有制，外而事之得宜，義亦在其中矣。學者欲求仁義之理，可不先於此心之致力與？抑孟子生丁是時，權謀功利之徒、縱橫游說之輩，藉此相高，可謂月異而歲不同矣。一旦憫人心之陷溺，慨道學之不明，而揭此以示人，有功於吾道，顧不偉哉？先儒謂其功不在禹下，益信其然矣。

易
進以正，可以正邦也。
趙汝濂
translation_en:
…Tracing these matters back to their essentials, one need only seek within the heart-mind. The heart-mind is the spiritual intelligence of the human being: its substance consists in encompassing the many principles; its function consists in responding to the myriad affairs. It readily wanders, going out or coming in at no fixed time; it is readily lost, now there, now here, with no constant resting place. One must gather it into a heaven of reverent watchfulness [?], bringing back within what has gone out, so that it remains tranquil and composed, present at all times. One must hold it within a realm of alert awareness, keeping always here what was there, so that its undivided genuineness remains unchanged wherever it may be. This alone is the way of learning and inquiry. What else could one seek? In this way, learning and inquiry benefit oneself, and the heart-mind is preserved. When the heart-mind is preserved, benevolence is preserved. When benevolence is preserved, the heart-mind is regulated within and affairs are handled fittingly without; righteousness is also contained therein. Can students who seek the principles of benevolence and righteousness fail first to devote their efforts to this heart-mind? Now, Mencius lived in a time when practitioners of political stratagems and the pursuit of achievement and profit, together with itinerant persuaders promoting rival alliances, used these arts to outdo one another. Their devices could indeed be said to change from month to month and year to year. Moved by pity for the submergence of people’s hearts and by distress that learning concerning the Way was obscure, he set forth this teaching to instruct others. Was his contribution to our Way not great indeed? Earlier Confucian scholars said that his achievement was no less than that of Yu. All the more do we believe this to be true.

Book of Changes
“By advancing with correctness, one can set the state right.”
Zhao Rulian

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導鄭批講正邦處嚴整條
暢一結尤見忠愛得士如此進之
可自慶矣
考試官教諭周批因卦變而推治道
誰不知之但有根據而善發揮如
此者少
考試官學正季批得彖傳微意
即卦變晉正之善見治道表正之本彖傳釋利
貞之意也蓋治化之行繋於身也本既端矣而
===
施之於政焉有不正者哉彖傳之意蓋如此今
夫漸之所以利貞者何所取哉嘗觀諸卦變矣
九居於二昭於渙也今進處於三則變於艮而
得陽位之正矣九居於四著於旅也今進位於
五則變於巽而得陽體之正矣由下僚而晉具
瞻之地何有乎僭躐之嫌從潛邸而履帝位之
尊允恊乎歸依之願夫如是則爲世道一新之
會朝廷更化之機邦國豈有不正乎吾知上下
同心以正理而應庶務君臣合德以正法而肅
punctuated:
同考試官訓導鄭批：講正邦處，嚴整條暢；一結尤見忠愛。得士如此，進之可自慶矣。
考試官教諭周批：因卦變而推治道，誰不知之？但有根據而善發揮如此者少。
考試官學正季批：得彖傳微意。
即卦變晉正之善，見治道表正之本，彖傳釋利貞之意也。蓋治化之行繋於身也，本既端矣，而施之於政，焉有不正者哉？彖傳之意蓋如此。今夫漸之所以利貞者，何所取哉？嘗觀諸卦變矣。九居於二，昭於渙也；今進處於三，則變於艮而得陽位之正矣。九居於四，著於旅也；今進位於五，則變於巽而得陽體之正矣。由下僚而晉具瞻之地，何有乎僭躐之嫌？從潛邸而履帝位之尊，允恊乎歸依之願。夫如是，則爲世道一新之會、朝廷更化之機，邦國豈有不正乎？吾知上下同心，以正理而應庶務；君臣合德，以正法而肅
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zheng, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “The discussion of setting the state right is rigorous, orderly, and lucid; the conclusion especially reveals loyalty and loving concern. Having obtained a scholar such as this, one may congratulate oneself on advancing him.”
Examiner Zhou, an Instructor, comments: “Who does not know how to infer the way of government from transformations of the hexagrams? Yet few ground their argument securely and develop it as skillfully as this.”
Examiner Ji, a School Instructor, comments: “This captures the subtle meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments.”
To discern, through the excellence of advancing into a correct position in a hexagram’s transformation, that setting an upright example is the foundation of the way of government: this is the intent of the Commentary on the Judgments in explaining ‘it is beneficial to remain correct.’ For the implementation of government and moral transformation depends upon one’s own person. Once this foundation is upright, how could its application to government fail to be correct? Such, indeed, is the intent of the Commentary on the Judgments.
Now, on what grounds does the hexagram Jian (Gradual Progress) signify that ‘it is beneficial to remain correct’? I have examined this through the transformations of the hexagrams. A nine occupying the second position is clearly seen in Huan (Dispersion). When it now advances to occupy the third position, the trigram changes to Gen (Keeping Still), and it attains the correctness of a yang position. A nine occupying the fourth position is manifest in Lü (The Traveler). When it now advances to the fifth position, the trigram changes to Xun (The Gentle), and it attains the correctness appropriate to its yang character.
When one advances from a subordinate office to a position toward which all eyes turn, what grounds are there for suspicion of usurpation or irregular advancement? When one proceeds from the princely residence occupied before accession to the exalted imperial throne, this truly accords with the people’s wish to give their allegiance. Under such circumstances, there is an occasion for renewing the ways of the world and an opportunity for reforming government at court. How could the state fail to be set right? I know that those above and below will be of one mind, attending to the manifold affairs of government through correct principles; ruler and ministers will unite in virtue, employing correct laws to bring order to …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
斯民操乾剛之正於崇高之上而左右臣屬咸
以堯舜之道輔之凡紀綱法度之施悉皆光明
正大之宏規也秉陽德之正於宸極之嚴而奔
走百辟咸以仁義之道佐之凡詔令政刑之舉
絕無偏黨反側之夙弊也自一心以推之於萬
幾罔非王道之懿而可以挽回風化矣凡囿於
覆冒者孰有不正乎自朝廷以達之於邦域莫
非天德之純而可以斡旋世道矣凡得於觀感
者烏有不正乎是則先有正己之本而後有正
===
人之用使進若可議則人皆弗信弗從矣雖一
家尚難況欲正其邦耶此筮而得漸者不可不
利於貞也抑進得其正而效可以正邦是固然
矣使玩安忽治而或以匪人間之亦安能保其
終無敝哉是以古昔盛時志同道合都俞吁咈
之間莫非警戒相成之道猶恐憸邪乘隙以撓
正而隄防疎遠無所不至嗚呼是豈得已哉蓋
天下之勢治日常少而天下之人邪佞易親此
保治之策自不容於不謹也
punctuated:
斯民。操乾剛之正於崇高之上，而左右臣屬咸以堯舜之道輔之，凡紀綱法度之施，悉皆光明正大之宏規也。秉陽德之正於宸極之嚴，而奔走百辟咸以仁義之道佐之，凡詔令政刑之舉，絕無偏黨反側之夙弊也。自一心以推之於萬幾，罔非王道之懿，而可以挽回風化矣，凡囿於覆冒者，孰有不正乎？自朝廷以達之於邦域，莫非天德之純，而可以斡旋世道矣，凡得於觀感者，烏有不正乎？是則先有正己之本，而後有正人之用。使進若可議，則人皆弗信弗從矣，雖一家尚難，況欲正其邦耶？此筮而得漸者，不可不利於貞也。
抑進得其正而效可以正邦，是固然矣。使玩安忽治，而或以匪人間之，亦安能保其終無敝哉？是以古昔盛時，志同道合，都俞吁咈之間，莫非警戒相成之道。猶恐憸邪乘隙以撓正，而隄防疎遠，無所不至。嗚呼！是豈得已哉？蓋天下之勢，治日常少，而天下之人，邪佞易親，此保治之策，自不容於不謹也。
translation_en:
…these people. Exercising the rectitude of Qian’s firmness from his exalted position, the ruler receives assistance from all his attendant ministers in accordance with the Way of Yao and Shun. Every application of governing principles, laws, and institutions follows grand designs that are enlightened, upright, and just. Upholding the rectitude of yang virtue in the majesty of the imperial throne, he receives assistance from all the officials who hasten to serve him in accordance with the Way of benevolence and righteousness. His edicts, administrative measures, and punishments are entirely free of the longstanding abuses of partiality, factionalism, and duplicity. Extended from his single mind to the myriad affairs of government, all is the excellence of the kingly Way, capable of restoring moral influence and transforming customs. Among all who live beneath his sheltering protection, who would fail to become upright? Extended from the court throughout the realm, all is the purity of Heaven’s virtue, capable of turning the course of the age. Among all who are moved by observing his example, who would fail to become upright? Thus the foundation of rectifying oneself comes first, followed by its application in rectifying others. If his advancement were open to question, people would neither trust nor follow him. Even rectifying a single household would be difficult; how much more so rectifying his state! This is why, for one who obtains the hexagram Gradual Progress (Jian) through divination, benefit must depend upon steadfast correctness.
Yet that advancement in accordance with rectitude can have the effect of rectifying the state is certainly true. If, however, he grows complacent in peace and neglects governance, and unworthy men are allowed to intrude, how can he ensure that no deterioration occurs in the end? Thus, in the flourishing ages of antiquity, rulers and ministers shared the same aspirations and followed the same Way. Their exchanges of assent and dissent were all means of warning and admonishing one another and helping one another achieve good government. Still they feared that crafty and wicked men might seize an opening to undermine rectitude, and so they took every possible measure to guard against and keep such men at a distance. Alas! Could they have done otherwise? For in the course of the world’s affairs, days of good order are always few, while among the world’s people, the wicked and sycophantic readily gain intimacy. In measures to preserve good order, one therefore cannot afford to be anything but vigilant.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易之爲書也不可遠爲道也屢遷
封祖裔
同考試官訓導鄭批場中講屢遷處多
牽引下文變動周流四句填實則
此句似無味矣是作融會全節而
句格亦新蓋邃於易者
考試官教諭周批易有至妙不可違
得士如此吾敢違而不取乎
考試官學正季批說理之文難乎明
===
暢此可謂易人之所難也
大傳論易切於人由其有變通之妙也蓋易道
有資於人大矣苟少違焉則所具之理何由而
自行於人哉大傳之意蓋如此今夫易之爲書
本爲卜筮而設若可遠也然卦爻森列括盡天
下之理切於民生而不可須臾離焉變象具陳
曲盡古今之事利於日用而不可頃刻違焉不
存於心終爲韋編之陳迹而吾操縱之權無其
本矣豈若他書專爲一事而作者猶可違乎不
punctuated:
易之爲書也不可遠，爲道也屢遷。
封祖裔
同考試官訓導鄭批：「場中講屢遷處，多牽引下文變動周流四句填實，則此句似無味矣。是作融會全節，而句格亦新，蓋邃於易者。」
考試官教諭周批：「易有至妙，不可違。得士如此，吾敢違而不取乎？」
考試官學正季批：「說理之文難乎明暢，此可謂易人之所難也。」
大傳論易切於人，由其有變通之妙也。蓋易道有資於人大矣，苟少違焉，則所具之理何由而自行於人哉？大傳之意蓋如此。今夫易之爲書，本爲卜筮而設，若可遠也。然卦爻森列，括盡天下之理，切於民生，而不可須臾離焉；變象具陳，曲盡古今之事，利於日用，而不可頃刻違焉。不存於心，終爲韋編之陳迹，而吾操縱之權無其本矣。豈若他書專爲一事而作者，猶可違乎？不
translation_en:
“As a book, the Changes cannot be kept at a distance; as a Way, it constantly shifts.”
Feng Zuyi
Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor, comments: “When discussing ‘constantly shifts,’ many candidates in this examination draw upon the four subsequent clauses beginning ‘changing and moving, circulating everywhere’ to supply concrete substance. This leaves the present clause seemingly without flavor. This composition comprehends and integrates the entire section, and its sentence patterns are also fresh. Its author is surely deeply versed in the Changes.”
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The Changes contains the utmost subtlety and cannot be departed from. Having found a scholar like this, would I dare turn away and fail to select him?”
Examiner Ji, Instructor, comments: “In writing that expounds principles, clarity and fluency are difficult to achieve. This may be said to make easy what others find difficult.”
The Great Commentary explains that the Changes is intimately relevant to human beings because it possesses the subtle efficacy of transformation and adaptation. Indeed, the Way of the Changes offers immense assistance to people. If they depart from it even slightly, how could the principles it contains put themselves into practice among them? Such, broadly, is the meaning of the Great Commentary. Now, as a book, the Changes was originally devised for divination with tortoise shells and milfoil stalks, so it might seem something that could be kept at a distance. Yet its hexagrams and lines stand in ordered array, encompassing all the principles under Heaven. They bear directly upon people’s lives and cannot be left behind even for a moment. Its transformations and images are fully displayed, comprehensively embracing the affairs of past and present. They benefit everyday practice and cannot be departed from even for an instant. If it is not kept in the heart, it ultimately becomes merely an old relic in leather-bound pages, and our capacity to judge when to hold firm and when to let go loses its foundation. How could it be like other books written exclusively for a single matter, which one might still set aside? If it does not…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
接於目卒為簡策之虚文而吾張弛之方無其
要矣豈若諸書偏於一節而言者猶可忘乎夫
易之不可離者如是其切由道之載於書者莫
測其機如詩理性情書之局於一者也易則變
化無端而未甞少有凝滯如禮謹節文書之偏
於一者也易則通變無方而未甞少有拘泥雖
曰不過卦爻而已耳其中精微之道在此在彼
而動盪之無常可以守經也可以行權也從之
則安外之則危顧可得而遠哉雖曰不過變象
===
而已耳其間玄妙之理或往或来而流行之匪
定可以行已也可以應物也循之則吉悖之則
凶又可得而離哉是則人有百為必玩易而後
善易有萬變須待人而後行聖人言此無非欲
人體易而開物成務之心始慰矣嗚呼六經皆
聖人垂世之典也曷獨於易而不可遠哉蓋易
之為教雖曰廣大悉備總而言之不過曰時而
已時在造化亦不能違而況於人乎人徒知讀
易而不知隨時之義雖常存心目而卒歸於無
punctuated: 接於目，卒為簡策之虚文，而吾張弛之方無其要矣，豈若諸書偏於一節而言者猶可忘乎？夫易之不可離者，如是其切，由道之載於書者莫測其機。如詩理性情，書之局於一者也；易則變化無端，而未甞少有凝滯。如禮謹節文，書之偏於一者也；易則通變無方，而未甞少有拘泥。雖曰不過卦爻而已耳，其中精微之道，在此在彼，而動盪之無常，可以守經也，可以行權也。從之則安，外之則危，顧可得而遠哉？雖曰不過變象而已耳，其間玄妙之理，或往或来，而流行之匪定，可以行已也，可以應物也。循之則吉，悖之則凶，又可得而離哉？是則人有百為，必玩易而後善；易有萬變，須待人而後行。聖人言此，無非欲人體易，而開物成務之心始慰矣。嗚呼！六經皆聖人垂世之典也，曷獨於易而不可遠哉？蓋易之為教，雖曰廣大悉備，總而言之，不過曰時而已。時在造化亦不能違，而況於人乎？人徒知讀易，而不知隨時之義，雖常存心目，而卒歸於無
translation_en:
…unless it is brought before the eyes, it ultimately becomes empty writing on bamboo slips, and my methods of tightening and relaxing lack their essential guide. Could it be like other books, whose teachings concern only a particular matter and which may still be forgotten? That the Changes cannot be left behind is thus a matter of immediate importance, because the workings of the Way recorded in this book are unfathomable. For example, the Odes regulate human nature and feelings: this is a book confined to one aspect. The Changes, however, transforms without limit and never shows the slightest stagnation. Likewise, the Rites enjoin care in ritual observances and forms: this is a book devoted to one aspect. The Changes, however, adapts to transformation without fixed methods and never shows the slightest rigidity. Although one might say that it consists only of hexagrams and lines, the subtle Way within it is here and there, moving without constancy. Through it one may uphold enduring principles; through it one may exercise discretionary judgment. Following it brings security; setting it aside brings peril. How, then, could one keep it at a distance? Although one might say that it consists only of transformations and images, the profound principles within it go and come, circulating without fixed location. Through them one may govern one's conduct [?]; through them one may respond to things. Following them brings good fortune; opposing them brings misfortune. How, then, could one depart from them?

Thus, among people's hundred undertakings, only by pondering the Changes can they act well; and the Changes, with its myriad transformations, must await people before it can be put into practice. In saying this, the sage wanted only that people should embody the Changes; only then would his desire to disclose the nature of things and bring undertakings to completion be satisfied. Ah! The Six Classics are all canonical works handed down to the world by the sages. Why, then, is it the Changes alone that must not be kept at a distance? Although the teaching of the Changes is vast and complete, in sum it amounts to nothing more than timeliness. Even the processes of creation and transformation cannot run counter to the time—how much less can human beings! If people know only how to read the Changes, without understanding the meaning of adapting to the time, then, though they constantly keep it in mind and before their eyes, it ultimately proves of no…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
補也噫使人皆知此義則易具六十四卦亦足
矣而曷用煩辭爲哉於此見聖人憂世之心果
不得已也
書
恭默思道夢帝賚予良弼
張合
同考試官訓導詹批高宗中興事業都
在恭默思道上此篇極其形容渾
雄偉麗無不有之錄以爲學書者
法
考試官教諭周批發明傳意略無費
辭佳作也
考試官學正季批意圓詞贍程式之
文也
極圖治之誠感輔治之兆賢王自敘之辭也夫
天人相與之際微矣賢王圖治甚誠而得賢甚
異感應之理有如是哉昔高宗因羣臣之諫故
作書喻在己之意若曰表正四方固予之責不
punctuated:
補也。噫！使人皆知此義，則易具六十四卦亦足矣，而曷用煩辭爲哉？於此見聖人憂世之心，果不得已也。
書
恭默思道，夢帝賚予良弼。
張合
同考試官訓導詹批：高宗中興事業，都在恭默思道上。此篇極其形容，渾雄偉麗，無不有之，錄以爲學書者法。
考試官教諭周批：發明傳意，略無費辭，佳作也。
考試官學正季批：意圓詞贍，程式之文也。
極圖治之誠，感輔治之兆，賢王自敘之辭也。夫天人相與之際微矣，賢王圖治甚誠，而得賢甚異，感應之理有如是哉！昔高宗因羣臣之諫，故作書喻在己之意，若曰：表正四方，固予之責；不…
translation_en:
…of no benefit. Ah! If everyone understood this principle, the Changes with its sixty-four hexagrams would suffice; what need would there be for elaborate explanations? Here we see that the sage’s concern for the world truly left him no alternative.

Book of Documents

“Reverently and silently I pondered the Way; in a dream, the Supreme Lord bestowed upon me an excellent assistant.”

Zhang He

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, an Assistant Instructor: “Gaozong’s achievement in restoring the dynasty rested entirely upon reverently and silently pondering the Way. This essay describes this to the fullest: rounded strength, grandeur, and beauty are all present. It is recorded as a model for those studying the Documents.”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, an Instructor: “It elucidates and conveys the meaning without a single wasted expression. An excellent work.”

Comment by Examiner Ji, an Instructor: “Its ideas are fully developed and its language abundant. This is an essay worthy to serve as a model.”

Utmost sincerity in seeking good government elicited an auspicious sign of assistance in governing: these are the words in which a worthy king recounts his own experience. How subtle is the meeting of Heaven and humankind! The worthy king sought good government with profound sincerity, and his acquisition of a worthy minister was most extraordinary. Such indeed is the principle of stimulus and response! In former times, Gaozong, responding to the remonstrances of his assembled ministers, composed a written statement to explain his intentions, saying in effect: “To set an upright example for the four quarters is certainly my responsibility; not…”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
肖先德允予之懼顧敢易言乎由是斂此身於
整齊嚴肅之中凝神淵默而沉思之不已囿此
身於齊莊恭敬之內戒謹隱微而致念之不忘
如何而可以飭百官如何而可以統萬民凡爲
治道之圖者反覆思惟如有不及而孜孜法祖
之心亦甚切焉如何而可以正宮闈如何而可
以馭四夷凡爲化理之計者往來念慮若有不
逮而拳拳憲天之念亦甚急焉夫惟望治之心
有甚於饑渴故得賢之兆有感於夢寐予當蘧
===
蘧然氣定之時精神感召儼然上帝以良弼而
授我焉栩栩然神遊之表意氣招來宛乎上帝
以賢佐而賚予焉想像之真戀慕恒切雖未見
焉將欲物色以求之也庶輔弼有資而圖治法
祖之心可少慰乎思賢之極景慕何深雖未接
焉將欲弓旌以招之也庶贊襄有賴而思治憲
天之念可少紓乎夫惟賢王求治之心誠故上
天錫賢之事異如此宜自叙之以爲羣臣告也
與雖然君臣相遇自古爲難也商造中微賢人
punctuated:
肖先德，允予之懼，顧敢易言乎？由是斂此身於整齊嚴肅之中，凝神淵默而沉思之不已；囿此身於齊莊恭敬之內，戒謹隱微而致念之不忘。如何而可以飭百官？如何而可以統萬民？凡爲治道之圖者，反覆思惟，如有不及，而孜孜法祖之心亦甚切焉。如何而可以正宮闈？如何而可以馭四夷？凡爲化理之計者，往來念慮，若有不逮，而拳拳憲天之念亦甚急焉。夫惟望治之心有甚於饑渴，故得賢之兆有感於夢寐。予當蘧蘧然氣定之時，精神感召，儼然上帝以良弼而授我焉；栩栩然神遊之表，意氣招來，宛乎上帝以賢佐而賚予焉。想像之真，戀慕恒切，雖未見焉，將欲物色以求之也。庶輔弼有資，而圖治法祖之心可少慰乎？思賢之極，景慕何深，雖未接焉，將欲弓旌以招之也。庶贊襄有賴，而思治憲天之念可少紓乎？」
夫惟賢王求治之心誠，故上天錫賢之事異如此，宜自叙之以爲羣臣告也與！雖然，君臣相遇，自古爲難也。商造中微，賢人
translation_en:
“…to fall short of my forebears’ virtue is truly what I fear. How could I dare speak lightly? Thus I disciplined myself through orderliness and solemnity, concentrating my spirit in profound silence and pondering without cease. I confined myself within gravity and reverence, remaining watchful even over what was hidden and subtle, and never forgetting to attend to it. How might I bring the hundred officials into proper order? How might I govern the myriad people? I repeatedly considered every plan for good government, as though my efforts were still insufficient; my diligent resolve to emulate my ancestors was indeed most earnest. How might I set the palace quarters in order? How might I govern the peoples of the four quarters? I turned over every plan for moral transformation and orderly rule, as though I still fell short; my devoted resolve to model myself on Heaven was indeed most urgent.
“Precisely because my longing for good government exceeded hunger and thirst, a portent of obtaining a worthy man came to me in a dream. When I was at ease and my vital energies were settled, my spirit called forth a response: vividly, the Lord on High bestowed an excellent minister upon me. As my spirit wandered freely beyond myself, my thoughts and energies summoned a response: distinctly, the Lord on High granted me a worthy assistant. So lifelike was the image that my longing remained ever keen. Though I have not yet seen him, I intend to seek him by his appearance. Might I then have someone to assist and guide me, bringing some comfort to my resolve to achieve good government and emulate my ancestors? My yearning for a worthy man has reached its utmost; how profound is my admiration! Though I have not yet met him, I intend to summon him with bow and banner. Might I then have someone upon whom to rely for assistance, bringing some relief to my concern for good government and my resolve to model myself on Heaven?”
It was precisely because the worthy king’s desire for good government was sincere that Heaven’s bestowal of a worthy man was so extraordinary. Surely it was fitting for him to recount it himself and make it known to his assembled ministers! Nevertheless, encounters between ruler and minister have been difficult to bring about since antiquity. When the fortunes of the Shang declined midway through the dynasty, the worthy man…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
在下傅巖之築所謂若將終身焉者高宗帝賚
之辭其事若跡亦異矣豈賢人之生固自不偶
邪卒之舟楫霖雨麴糵鹽梅之喻致乎中興之
功則夫帝賚之事夫豈偶然之故哉噫湯以伊
尹而開基高宗以傅說而再造後先一轍抑所
謂上下交而德業成者歟
宅乃事宅乃牧宅乃準茲惟后矣
龔瑀
同考試官訓導詹批說周公述夏臣告
===
君之言以戒其君意首尾明盡而
辭莊氣裕有亹亹之風即子之言
他日所用將無疑於子矣
考試官教諭周批書義要如此作
考試官學正季批明贍可誦是好文
字
克安大臣之位斯盡大君之實蓋大臣之位未
易得其安也今既有以安之人君之實有不盡
乎夏臣敘之以告其君其知恤也何如哉且其
punctuated:
在下，傅巖之築，所謂若將終身焉者。高宗帝賚之辭，其事若跡亦異矣。豈賢人之生固自不偶邪？卒之舟楫、霖雨、麴糵、鹽梅之喻，致乎中興之功，則夫帝賚之事，夫豈偶然之故哉？噫！湯以伊尹而開基，高宗以傅說而再造，後先一轍，抑所謂上下交而德業成者歟？
宅乃事，宅乃牧，宅乃準，茲惟后矣。
龔瑀
同考試官訓導詹批：說周公述夏臣告君之言以戒其君意，首尾明盡，而辭莊氣裕，有亹亹之風。即子之言，他日所用，將無疑於子矣。
考試官教諭周批：書義要如此作。
考試官學正季批：明贍可誦，是好文字。
克安大臣之位，斯盡大君之實。蓋大臣之位未易得其安也，今既有以安之，人君之實有不盡乎？夏臣敘之以告其君，其知恤也何如哉！且其
translation_en:
…in humble circumstances, building at Fuyan, seemingly destined, as the saying goes, to spend his entire life there. Gaozong’s statement that the Supreme Lord had bestowed him as a gift, and the circumstances and manifestations of that event, were indeed extraordinary. Could it be that a worthy man is born necessarily to go unrecognized? In the end, the metaphors of boats and oars, timely rain, yeast and ferment, and salt and plums culminated in the achievement of dynastic restoration. How, then, could this gift from the Supreme Lord have been mere chance? Ah! Tang laid the foundations with Yi Yin, and Gaozong restored the dynasty with Fu Yue. Earlier and later, they followed the same course. Is this not what is meant by those above and below joining together so that virtue and achievement are brought to fruition?
“Settle in their posts your ministers of affairs, your governors, and your officers of justice: this is what it means to be a sovereign.”
Gong Yu
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: The explanation of how the Duke of Zhou recounted the words with which a Xia minister admonished his ruler, in order to warn his own ruler, is clear and exhaustive from beginning to end. The language is dignified, the manner composed, and the exposition has an unflagging momentum. Judging by your words, there will be no doubt about you when the time comes to employ you.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: An essay on the meaning of the Book of Documents should be written like this.
Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: Clear, ample, and worthy of recitation: this is fine writing.
Only by successfully securing the great ministers in their posts can one fully realize the substance of being a great ruler. For it is no easy matter to secure the great ministers in their posts. Once there is a means to secure them, can the substance of rulership remain unfulfilled? The Xia minister set this forth to admonish his ruler: how well he understood what should concern a ruler! Moreover, his…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
意以爲三宅之官職任旣非羣臣之比關係實
爲君道之重可不度德以定其位乎是故王之
所與共治天事者有常任焉必其有猷有爲足
以剸繁而治劇不愆不忘足以立綱而正紀信
乎其宅乃事矣所與共子天民者有牧夫焉必
其引養引恬爲萬姓之歸墍克長克君稱斯民
之父母信乎其宅乃牧矣以至準人則與王共
守天法者也務使惟明惟允克種德而民乃依
以簡以寬惟好生而人不犯準亦無不宅焉是
===
則才德之美固各稱其所居信任之專俾各展
其所蘊矣夫然後君人之實斯無負也蓋君道
莫重於理物事旣宅則百揆時叙帝載有用熈
之美庶績其凝天工著寅亮之休君人之責不
於是乎塞耶君道有在於安民牧旣宅則本以
固邦以寧四方成寵綏之治德惟迪功惟叙四
海訖聲教之同君人之道不於是而盡耶以至
愼罰又人君之所貴也旣宅乃準焉則惟察惟
法元命自作足以副配享之實有倫有要天威
punctuated:
意以爲，三宅之官，職任旣非羣臣之比，關係實爲君道之重，可不度德以定其位乎？是故王之所與共治天事者，有常任焉，必其有猷有爲，足以剸繁而治劇；不愆不忘，足以立綱而正紀，信乎其宅乃事矣。所與共子天民者，有牧夫焉，必其引養引恬，爲萬姓之歸墍；克長克君，稱斯民之父母，信乎其宅乃牧矣。以至準人，則與王共守天法者也，務使惟明惟允，克種德而民乃依；以簡以寬，惟好生而人不犯，準亦無不宅焉。是則才德之美，固各稱其所居；信任之專，俾各展其所蘊矣。夫然後君人之實，斯無負也。

蓋君道莫重於理物。事旣宅，則百揆時叙，帝載有用熈之美；庶績其凝，天工著寅亮之休，君人之責不於是乎塞耶？君道有在於安民。牧旣宅，則本以固，邦以寧，四方成寵綏之治；德惟迪，功惟叙，四海訖聲教之同，君人之道不於是而盡耶？以至愼罰，又人君之所貴也。旣宅乃準焉，則惟察惟法，元命自作，足以副配享之實；有倫有要，天威
translation_en:
…the meaning is that the duties of the officials holding the three kinds of appointment are unlike those of ordinary ministers, and their responsibilities are of the greatest consequence for the ruler’s Way. Can one fail to assess their virtue in determining their positions? Thus, among those with whom the king jointly administers Heaven’s affairs are the holders of regular offices. They must possess plans and the ability to act, sufficient to handle complexities and manage difficult affairs; they must neither err nor forget, and so be capable of establishing the guiding principles and setting the governing order right. Then truly the offices for affairs are properly filled. Among those with whom he jointly cherishes Heaven’s people as his children are the governors. They must bring the people nourishment and tranquillity, becoming a refuge and resting place for the myriad families; they must be capable of leading and ruling, worthy of being called the people’s fathers and mothers. Then truly the governorships are properly filled. As for the judicial officers, they jointly uphold Heaven’s laws with the king. Care must be taken that they are discerning and fair, able to cultivate virtue so that the people rely on them; that they act with simplicity and leniency, cherishing life so that people do not transgress. Thus the judicial posts, too, are all properly filled. In this way, each man’s excellence in ability and virtue accords with the position he occupies, while the undivided trust placed in him allows him fully to exercise his capacities. Only then will the substantive duties of ruling others be fulfilled.

For nothing in the ruler’s Way is weightier than ordering affairs. Once the administrative offices are properly filled, the hundred duties are duly ordered, and the sovereign’s undertakings attain the excellence of flourishing achievement; the many accomplishments are consolidated, and Heaven’s work displays the glory of reverent assistance. Is the ruler’s responsibility not thereby discharged? The ruler’s Way also consists in bringing peace to the people. Once the governorships are properly filled, the foundation is secure and the state tranquil, and throughout the four quarters government brings favour and peace; virtue is put into practice and achievements duly ordered, while all within the four seas share in the same civilizing instruction. Is the ruler’s Way not thereby fully realized? Furthermore, caution in punishment is also something the ruler prizes. Once the judicial posts are properly filled, there is discernment and adherence to law, and the great Mandate is secured through one’s own actions—enough to fulfil in substance the duty of worthily sharing in the sacrificial offerings to Heaven. There are proper principles and essential standards, and Heaven’s awe-inspiring majesty…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
具嚴足以致敬事之誠君道又不於是而盡哉
是則非徒崇高富貴之爲尊而且憂恤擇任之
有道矣有夏人臣教君之敬如此周公舉以爲
成王戒非其忠愛之拳拳能若是耶我儀圖之
夏后之籲俊求盡事天之實耳此其臣之致敬
致告要亦皆以任賢事天爲君人之實猶之商
之丕釐周之敬事皆此意也然羣賢和朝固三
代有道之長而其要在專擇百官有司之長此
周公立政一篇前乎此以常伯常任準人爲言
後乎此以三宅三俊三事常事司牧獄愼有司
爲訓鄭重丁寧不一而足蓋深知爲君之實端
在是矣孔子曰爲政在人朱子曰人主以論相
爲職其亦有得於是也夫後之告君者尚其鑒
諸
詩
樂只君子德音是茂
李元陽
同考試官學正方 批南山一題乃美與
punctuated:
具嚴，足以致敬事之誠，君道又不於是而盡哉？是則非徒崇高富貴之爲尊，而且憂恤擇任之有道矣。有夏人臣教君之敬如此，周公舉以爲成王戒，非其忠愛之拳拳，能若是耶？我儀圖之，夏后之籲俊，求盡事天之實耳。此其臣之致敬致告，要亦皆以任賢事天爲君人之實，猶之商之丕釐、周之敬事，皆此意也。然羣賢和朝，固三代有道之長，而其要在專擇百官有司之長。此周公《立政》一篇，前乎此以常伯、常任、準人爲言，後乎此以三宅、三俊、三事、常事、司牧、獄、愼有司爲訓，鄭重丁寧，不一而足，蓋深知爲君之實端在是矣。孔子曰：「爲政在人。」朱子曰：「人主以論相爲職。」其亦有得於是也夫！後之告君者，尚其鑒諸！
詩
樂只君子，德音是茂。
李元陽
同考試官學正方 批：南山一題，乃美與
translation_en:
…is fully awe-inspiring, sufficient to bring to fulfillment the sincerity of reverent service. Is not the Way of the ruler thereby fully realized as well? Thus, his exalted position rests not merely on eminence, wealth, and honor: he also follows the proper way in caring for the people and selecting those to entrust with office. Such was the reverence with which the ministers of Xia instructed their ruler. The Duke of Zhou cited this as an admonition to King Cheng. Could he have done so without his deeply earnest loyalty and affection? As I consider it, the Xia sovereign’s summons to outstanding men sought simply to fulfill the substance of serving Heaven. His ministers’ reverent admonitions likewise essentially took employing the worthy and serving Heaven as the substance of rulership. The Shang injunction to “greatly regulate” and the Zhou injunction to “serve reverently” both convey this same meaning.
Yet although a court harmonized by worthy men was indeed a distinctive strength of the well-governed Three Dynasties, the essential point lay in concentrating on the selection of the heads of the various offices and their officials. Thus, in the Duke of Zhou’s chapter “Establishing Government,” the preceding passage speaks of the chief ministers, those entrusted with responsibilities, and officers of justice; the following passages offer instruction concerning the three positions and their outstanding occupants, the three great responsibilities, regular duties, those who govern and shepherd the people, judicial affairs, and care in appointing officials. These solemn, repeated admonitions are too numerous to enumerate fully. He understood profoundly that the substance of rulership lay precisely here. Confucius said, “The practice of government depends on men.” Master Zhu said, “The ruler’s duty is to assess chief ministers.” Surely they too grasped this principle! May those who subsequently advise rulers take it as their lesson!
Book of Odes
“Joyful is the noble man; his virtuous reputation flourishes.”
Li Yuanyang
Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, an instructor: “The topic from ‘Nanshan’ praises those who take part in…”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
燕之賓其旨明甚場中作者率以
常語牽合雖多無取也此篇詞氣
舂容豐而不贅善說詩者耳置之
魁選可爲得人賀矣
考試官教諭周批文字峻整佳作也
考試官學正季批寫主人尊賓意千
載如見可以爲式矣
詩人美與燕之賓著名譽之盛也甚矣名實相
副之難也今與燕之賓而著聲譽之隆謂非斯
===
名稱情者能然哉此亦燕饗通用之樂道達主
人尊賓之意謂夫君子人與以有事而戾止邦
畿以令德而作賓王家昔焉遠處封邦容止不
可即矣今登筵之始而從容氣象宛乎其可親
向焉各居封守威儀不可見矣今即席之初豈
弟威儀温乎其可即徘徊于尊俎之間嚴而泰
焉使人心乎愛矣而不忘何樂只耶遨遊於獻
酬之頃和而節焉使人中心好之而不已何樂
易耶不寧惟是且其德有可稱脩身樂善而成
punctuated:
燕之賓，其旨明甚。場中作者率以常語牽合，雖多無取也。此篇詞氣舂容，豐而不贅，善說詩者耳。置之魁選，可爲得人賀矣。
考試官教諭周批：文字峻整，佳作也。
考試官學正季批：寫主人尊賓意，千載如見，可以爲式矣。
詩人美與燕之賓，著名譽之盛也。甚矣，名實相副之難也！今與燕之賓而著聲譽之隆，謂非斯名稱情者能然哉？此亦燕饗通用之樂，道達主人尊賓之意。謂夫君子人，與以有事而戾止邦畿，以令德而作賓王家。昔焉遠處封邦，容止不可即矣；今登筵之始，而從容氣象宛乎其可親。向焉各居封守，威儀不可見矣；今即席之初，豈弟威儀温乎其可即。徘徊于尊俎之間，嚴而泰焉，使人心乎愛矣而不忘，何樂只耶！遨遊於獻酬之頃，和而節焉，使人中心好之而不已，何樂易耶！不寧惟是，且其德有可稱，脩身樂善而成
translation_en:
…the guests participating in the banquet: its meaning is perfectly clear. Writers in the examination hall mostly forced commonplace expressions to fit the subject; numerous though their compositions were, they offered nothing worth selecting. This essay’s language and cadence are spacious and unhurried, ample without being verbose: here is someone skilled at explaining the Odes. Placing it first among the selections gives us cause to rejoice at having found a worthy man.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: The writing is vigorous and well ordered—a fine composition.
Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: It depicts the host’s intention to honor his guests so vividly that, a thousand years later, we seem to see it before us. It may serve as a model.
The poet praises the guests participating in the banquet, making manifest the greatness of their renown. How difficult it is for reputation and reality to correspond! Now the guests at the banquet are shown to enjoy lofty reputations: could this be so unless their reputations accorded with their true qualities? This, too, is music used generally at banquets, expressing the host’s intention to honor his guests. It speaks of these gentlemen, who come to participate in ceremonial affairs [?] and arrive in the royal domain, becoming guests of the royal house by virtue of their excellent character. Formerly, dwelling far away in their enfeoffed states, they could not be approached to observe their bearing; now, as they first ascend to the banquet, their composed demeanor seems so approachable and familiar. Previously, each residing within his own territorial charge, their dignified deportment could not be seen; now, as they first take their seats, their gracious deportment is warm and inviting. Moving among the wine vessels and sacrificial stands, they are dignified yet at ease, inspiring heartfelt affection that cannot be forgotten. How joyous they are! Mingling as cups are offered and returned, they are harmonious yet restrained, inspiring unceasing affection in people’s hearts. How cheerful and at ease they are! Nor is this all: their virtue also merits praise; they cultivate themselves and delight in goodness, thereby achieving…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
積中發外之美善有可名制節謹度而無自用
自專之失由是流而爲聲譽之芳允偉乎甚大
王畿知之侯國知之或内或外皆濯濯厥聲之
孔昭也德音信乎其茂矣豈直不已而已哉播
而爲聲聞之美猶浩乎孔博圻甸聞之要荒聞
之在朝在野一憲憲令名之洋溢也徽音允乎
其盛矣奚但不已而已哉是則非臣之賢無以
得君之懽心非君之明無以知臣之令德有周
燕饗一行而君臣相與相得如此此所以爲明
===
良之會也與大抵君臣之賢否關於氣運之盛
衰盛則治隆於上俗美於下手足腹心相待一
體否則恩禮衰薄將國人視之而已安望其共
成光明俊偉之治哉後世稱盛治者謂泰和在
成周予於此言益信
帝命式于九圍
張𨯤
同考試官學正方批題本明白而場中
作者不纏繞無歸著則渙散無意
punctuated:
積中發外之美，善有可名，制節謹度而無自用自專之失。由是流而爲聲譽之芳，允偉乎甚大。王畿知之，侯國知之，或内或外，皆濯濯厥聲之孔昭也。德音信乎其茂矣，豈直不已而已哉！播而爲聲聞之美，猶浩乎孔博。圻甸聞之，要荒聞之，在朝在野，一憲憲令名之洋溢也。徽音允乎其盛矣，奚但不已而已哉！是則非臣之賢，無以得君之懽心；非君之明，無以知臣之令德。有周燕饗一行，而君臣相與相得如此，此所以爲明良之會也與！大抵君臣之賢否，關於氣運之盛衰。盛則治隆於上，俗美於下，手足腹心，相待一體；否則恩禮衰薄，將國人視之而已，安望其共成光明俊偉之治哉！後世稱盛治者，謂泰和在成周，予於此言益信。

帝命式于九圍
張𨯤

同考試官學正方批：題本明白，而場中作者，不纏繞無歸著，則渙散無意
translation_en:
…the beauty of virtue accumulated within and manifested outwardly. Their goodness deserves praise: they regulate their conduct and carefully observe proper limits, without the faults of following only their own judgment or acting arbitrarily. From this flows their fragrant reputation, truly magnificent and far-reaching. The royal domain knows it; the feudal states know it. Within and beyond, their reputation shines with exceptional brilliance. The renown of their virtue is indeed flourishing—how could it merely endure without ceasing? Spreading abroad as a fine reputation, it is vast and extensive. The lands surrounding the capital hear of it; the distant frontier regions hear of it. At court and among the people, their illustrious good name overflows everywhere. Their admirable renown is truly abundant—how could it merely endure without ceasing?

Thus, without the ministers’ worthiness, they could not win their ruler’s glad affection; without the ruler’s discernment, he could not recognize his ministers’ excellent virtue. When a banquet was held under the Zhou, ruler and ministers associated in such mutual accord: this is what made it a meeting of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers! Generally, the worthiness or unworthiness of ruler and ministers is bound up with the flourishing or decline of the fortunes of the age. When these flourish, government prospers above and customs are good below; ruler and ministers depend upon one another as hands and feet, belly and heart, belonging to a single body. Otherwise, favor and courtesy dwindle, and they regard one another merely as ordinary countrymen. How could one then expect them jointly to achieve enlightened and outstanding government? Those in later ages who praised flourishing government said that supreme harmony prevailed in the perfected Zhou order. My belief in this statement is strengthened by this passage.

“By the Lord on High’s command, he set a model for the nine regions.”
Zhang 𨯤 [given-name reading uncertain].

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, an Instructor: “The topic is clear enough in itself, yet the candidates writing in the examination hall either become entangled and reach no definite conclusion, or become diffuse and lack meaning…”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
味令人厭觀既得此卷讀之殊爲
快心豁目取之
考試官教諭周批商頌盛德形容之
意此作發之以滂沛而不淫泆善
于作頌義者也
考試官學正季批以莊整之辭發脩
敬之德佳作也允稱高薦
詩人頌天眷聖君爲法於天下其必有以致之
矣夫天命未易得也聖君所以膺天眷而法天
===
下者謂非一敬致之哉此商人祫祭之詩推本
成湯受命之由蓋謂有商之業雖基於玄王實
成於烈祖烈祖之敬既格乎天心天下之命孰
有外之者哉是故夏失其道天心厭之久矣昭
假我祖之敬赫然駿命之攸歸政失其平天心
惡之素矣降鑒我祖之德昭然景命之有僕使
之宅中土而聽治焉皇極於此乎建也命之奄
六合以爲家焉人紀於是乎脩也作之君作之
師荆梁雍豫無人而不歸於範圍之中賞而慶
punctuated:
味，令人厭觀。既得此卷，讀之殊爲快心豁目，取之。
考試官教諭周批：商頌盛德形容之意，此作發之以滂沛而不淫泆，善于作頌義者也。
考試官學正季批：以莊整之辭，發脩敬之德，佳作也，允稱高薦。
詩人頌天眷聖君，爲法於天下，其必有以致之矣。夫天命未易得也，聖君所以膺天眷而法天下者，謂非一敬致之哉？此商人祫祭之詩，推本成湯受命之由，蓋謂有商之業，雖基於玄王，實成於烈祖。烈祖之敬既格乎天心，天下之命孰有外之者哉？是故夏失其道，天心厭之久矣；昭假我祖之敬，赫然駿命之攸歸。政失其平，天心惡之素矣；降鑒我祖之德，昭然景命之有僕。使之宅中土而聽治焉，皇極於此乎建也；命之奄六合以爲家焉，人紀於是乎脩也。作之君，作之師，荆梁雍豫無人而不歸於範圍之中；賞而慶
translation_en:
…meaning, making them tiresome to read. Once I obtained this script, reading it greatly delighted my heart and opened my eyes. I selected it.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: This composition develops the intent of the Hymns of Shang to depict flourishing virtue, with abundant force but without excess. Its author is skilled in composing expositions of the hymns.
Examiner Ji, Education Official, comments: With dignified and orderly language, it brings out the virtue of cultivating reverence. An excellent composition, fully deserving recommendation at a high rank.
The poet praises Heaven’s favor toward the sage ruler, who serves as a model for all under Heaven: surely something must have brought this about. Heaven’s mandate is not easily obtained. Can we say that anything other than reverence alone enabled the sage ruler to receive Heaven’s favor and serve as a model for all under Heaven? This poem for the Shang collective ancestral sacrifice traces the origins of Cheng Tang’s reception of the mandate. Its meaning is that although the enterprise of Shang was founded upon the Dark King, it was truly brought to completion by the Illustrious Ancestor. Once the Illustrious Ancestor’s reverence had reached Heaven’s heart, what part of the destiny of all under Heaven could remain outside his sway?
Thus, when Xia lost the Way, Heaven’s heart had long been weary of it. Our ancestor’s reverence rose brightly to Heaven, and to him the great mandate gloriously turned. When government lost its fairness, Heaven’s heart had long detested it. Heaven looked down upon our ancestor’s virtue, and the great mandate plainly attached itself to him. Heaven caused him to dwell in the central lands and attend to government: here the August Ultimate—the supreme standard of rule—was established. Heaven commanded him to possess the six directions as his household: thus the ordering principles of human relations were cultivated. It made him their ruler and their teacher; in Jing, Liang, Yong, and Yu, no one failed to come within the compass of his rule. He rewarded and bestowed blessings …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
刑而威冀兗青徐揚何者而不在於甄陶之內
以祖之敬而回威侮之習九圍之大皆欲其成
式矣豈復小國是達而已哉以祖之德而清怠
棄之源萬邦之廣皆欲其取正矣豈止大國是
達而已哉是則湯之王業上承先世長發之祥
下啓後世無窮之祚皆本於一敬之得天也宗
廟以是美盛德而告成功有由矣夫大抵敬者
得天人之本也堯以欽明而膺萬邦之命舜以
溫恭而紹曆數之傳禹祗台文敬止武敬勝得
===
天得人皆是物也所謂克敬惟親惟德是輔書
之言豈欺我哉
春秋
公敗齊師于長勺莊公十年公會齊侯
盟于柯莊公十有三年
呂鳳池
考試官教諭周批深得傳旨
考試官學正季批齊魯搆怨釋怨予
奪繫焉此篇融徹傳意馳驟頓挫
punctuated:
刑而威，冀兗青徐揚何者而不在於甄陶之內？以祖之敬而回威侮之習，九圍之大皆欲其成式矣，豈復小國是達而已哉？以祖之德而清怠棄之源，萬邦之廣皆欲其取正矣，豈止大國是達而已哉？是則湯之王業，上承先世長發之祥，下啓後世無窮之祚，皆本於一敬之得天也。宗廟以是美盛德而告成功，有由矣夫！大抵敬者，得天人之本也。堯以欽明而膺萬邦之命，舜以溫恭而紹曆數之傳，禹祗台，文敬止，武敬勝，得天得人皆是物也。所謂「克敬惟親，惟德是輔」，《書》之言豈欺我哉？
春秋
公敗齊師于長勺，莊公十年。公會齊侯盟于柯，莊公十有三年。
呂鳳池
考試官教諭周批：深得傳旨。
考試官學正季批：齊魯搆怨、釋怨，予奪繫焉。此篇融徹傳意，馳驟頓挫
translation_en:
…and imposed punishments to inspire awe: among Ji, Yan, Qing, Xu, and Yang, what place lay outside his shaping influence? Through the ancestor’s reverence, he transformed habits of intimidation and contempt, desiring that all within the vast nine regions follow his model. How could this have meant merely reaching the small states? Through the ancestor’s virtue, he cleared away the source of negligence and abandonment, desiring that all the myriad states take him as their standard. How could this have meant merely reaching the great states? Thus Tang’s royal enterprise carried forward the auspicious promise of enduring prosperity from earlier generations and opened the way to blessings without end for later generations. All was rooted in winning Heaven through reverence alone. There was therefore good reason for praising his abundant virtue and proclaiming his accomplished work in the ancestral temple!
Reverence is, in general, the foundation for winning Heaven and the people. Through reverent discernment, Yao received the mandate to rule the myriad states; through warmth and respect, Shun inherited the succession ordained by Heaven. Yu said, “I am reverent”; King Wen “rested in reverence”; King Wu held that “reverence overcomes.” What won Heaven and the people was in every case this same quality. As it is said, “It draws close only to those capable of reverence; it assists only the virtuous.” Could these words of the Book of Documents deceive us?
Spring and Autumn Annals
“The duke defeated the army of Qi at Changshao.” Tenth year of Duke Zhuang.
“The duke met the Marquis of Qi and concluded a covenant at Ke.” Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
Lü Fengchi.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “Profoundly grasps the purport of the commentary.”
Comment by Examiner Ji, School Instructor: “Approval and disapproval turn upon Qi and Lu’s fostering and resolving their enmity. This essay thoroughly comprehends the meaning of the commentary; its prose surges forward, pauses, and turns…”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而不失嚴整之度末復揭蔑之盟
以責魯莊向亡復讎之志尤出人
意表傑作也得子無媿賢科云
望國脩易世之怨可譏釋易世之怨可予此見
聖人惡長亂而善釋怨也觀長勺于柯之書法
可識矣思昔齊桓致脩怨之師魯莊申敵讎之
義長勺之役似所謂敵加于已不得已而應之
宜若無罪也何責耶蓋不師不陣已有明訓襄
也旣亡怨在可釋文告以諭使之不縮而退則
===
善矣夫何行登軾望轍之謀以卒幸一勝之功
用彼竭我盈之計以苟舒一朝之忿耻雖少雪
抑豈知已亂之道不急於尋兵耶故經不書齊
伐而主魯以責之意蓋如此迨夫齊桓欲爲脩
睦之舉魯莊遂締鄰國之交于柯之盟似所謂
不共戴天方再世而忘之宜若無取也何予耶
蓋敵惠敵怨不在後嗣齊桓易世鄰則當善擇
義以從使之釋憾而平則可矣况彼身任安攘
之責而摽劒之仇旣捐與國同推獎之誠而尊
punctuated:
而不失嚴整之度，末復揭蔑之盟，以責魯莊向亡復讎之志，尤出人意表，傑作也！得子，無媿賢科云。
望國，脩易世之怨可譏，釋易世之怨可予，此見聖人惡長亂而善釋怨也。觀長勺、于柯之書法，可識矣。思昔齊桓致脩怨之師，魯莊申敵讎之義，長勺之役，似所謂敵加于已，不得已而應之，宜若無罪也，何責耶？蓋不師不陣，已有明訓。襄也旣亡，怨在可釋，文告以諭，使之不縮而退，則善矣。夫何行登軾望轍之謀，以卒幸一勝之功；用彼竭我盈之計，以苟舒一朝之忿？耻雖少雪，抑豈知已亂之道不急於尋兵耶？故經不書齊伐，而主魯以責之，意蓋如此。迨夫齊桓欲爲脩睦之舉，魯莊遂締鄰國之交，于柯之盟，似所謂不共戴天，方再世而忘之，宜若無取也，何予耶？蓋敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。齊桓易世，鄰則當善，擇義以從，使之釋憾而平，則可矣。况彼身任安攘之責，而摽劒之仇旣捐，與國同推獎之誠，而尊
translation_en:
…yet without losing its rigor and order. At the end, he again invokes the covenant at Mie to reproach Duke Zhuang of Lu for having previously lacked the resolve to avenge his father [?]. This is especially unexpected: a masterpiece! With a candidate like you, this distinguished examination need feel no shame.
Regarding the state [?]: to pursue a grievance after a change of generation merits censure; to relinquish such a grievance merits approval. This shows that the Sage abhorred the prolongation of disorder and commended the relinquishing of grievances. This can be understood by examining the wording of the entries concerning Changshao and Ke. Consider how Duke Huan of Qi once brought an army to pursue an old grievance, while Duke Zhuang of Lu asserted the duty to oppose an enemy. The battle at Changshao seems to exemplify the saying that when an enemy attacks oneself, one has no choice but to respond. Apparently there should have been no fault: why, then, the reproach? There was already a clear teaching that vengeance should not be pursued by mobilizing armies and drawing up battle formations. Duke Xiang was dead, and the grievance could be relinquished. It would have been well to issue a proclamation explaining this and induce the enemy to withdraw without humiliation [?]. Why, instead, employ the stratagem of mounting the chariot’s crossbar and inspecting the wheel tracks, merely to obtain one fortunate victory; or use the calculation that ‘their courage is exhausted while ours is full,’ merely to vent a moment’s anger? Although the disgrace was somewhat effaced, did he not understand that the way to end disorder does not give priority to renewed warfare? Thus the Classic does not record an invasion by Qi, but makes Lu the principal actor in order to censure it. Such, presumably, was its intent.
When Duke Huan of Qi wished to restore amity, Duke Zhuang of Lu accordingly established friendly relations with the neighboring state. The covenant at Ke seems to concern an enemy with whom one ‘cannot share the same sky’; yet scarcely a generation later, the enmity was forgotten. Apparently there should have been nothing to commend: why, then, the approval? For reciprocating kindness and requiting enmity do not devolve upon descendants. With Duke Huan, Qi had undergone a change of generation, and relations with a neighboring state ought to be amicable. It was proper to choose and follow what was right, bringing about the relinquishment of resentment and the restoration of peace. Moreover, he personally assumed responsibility for bringing peace within and repelling threats from without, and had already abandoned his resentment over the brandished sword. Together with the allied states, [Lu] sincerely supported and commended him, and honored…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
周之義以重心雖有在抑不思盡孝之道實切
於安邦耶故經於平怨而書爵以予之意蓋如
此噫怨不可構也魯故可責也怨可釋也魯故
可與也聖人權輕重而立法此所以爲經世之
典歟傳者或舉齊襄之事以爲莊公深罪君子
曰柯之盟魯不得而干也齊桓倡伯尊王安夏
使莊如不赴是讎周耳然則莊公賢已乎曰當
無知之亂莊公不能聲大義於讎人之國顧及
大夫之盟以謀其所不當立復讎之志于蕱荒
===
矣莊公之罪安得而委之哉
遂城虎牢〔襄公二年〕戍鄭虎牢楚公子
貞帥師救鄭〔襄公十年〕
沈森
考試官教諭周 批二傳書法甚大作
者多戾本旨而文亦欠整此以森
然法度之言發春秋謹嚴之意讀
之令人敬服錄以爲習麟經者式
考試官學正季 批此傳要如此作可
punctuated:
周之義以重，心雖有在，抑不思盡孝之道實切於安邦耶？故經於平怨而書爵以予之，意蓋如此。噫！怨不可構也，魯故可責也；怨可釋也，魯故可與也。聖人權輕重而立法，此所以爲經世之典歟？傳者或舉齊襄之事，以爲莊公深罪。君子曰：「柯之盟，魯不得而干也。齊桓倡伯尊王安夏，使莊如不赴，是讎周耳。」然則莊公賢已乎？曰：「當無知之亂，莊公不能聲大義於讎人之國，顧及大夫之盟，以謀其所不當立，復讎之志于蕱荒矣。莊公之罪安得而委之哉？」
遂城虎牢〔襄公二年〕。戍鄭虎牢，楚公子貞帥師救鄭〔襄公十年〕。
沈森。
考試官教諭周批：「二傳書法甚大，作者多戾本旨，而文亦欠整。此以森然法度之言，發春秋謹嚴之意，讀之令人敬服，錄以爲習麟經者式。」
考試官學正季批：「此傳要如此作，可
translation_en:
…the duty of honoring Zhou carried great weight. Although his heart had its purpose, did he not consider that fulfilling filial duty was closely bound up with securing the state? Thus, when the Classic records the settling of the feud, it uses his noble title to signify approval. Such, presumably, was its intention. Alas! Enmity must not be provoked: hence Lu deserves blame. Enmity may be relinquished: hence Lu deserves approval. The Sage weighed the relative importance of things and established standards. Is this not what makes the work a canon for governing the world?
Some commentators cite the affair of Duke Xiang of Qi to charge Duke Zhuang with grave wrongdoing. The gentleman says: “Lu could not properly oppose the covenant at Ke. Duke Huan of Qi took the lead as hegemon, honoring the king and bringing peace to the Xia states. Had Duke Zhuang failed to attend, this would have amounted to treating Zhou as an enemy.” Does this mean, then, that Duke Zhuang was worthy? The reply is: “During Wuzhi’s rebellion, Duke Zhuang failed to proclaim the great moral obligation in the state of his enemy. Instead, he entered into a covenant with its grandees to scheme for the installation of someone who ought not to have been installed. His resolve to avenge the wrong had fallen into neglect [?]. How, then, can Duke Zhuang’s guilt be set aside?”
“They thereupon fortified Hulao.” 〔Second year of Duke Xiang.〕 “They garrisoned Hulao in Zheng. Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to relieve Zheng.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Shen Sen.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, an Instructor: “The principles of wording in these two passages are of great significance. Writers frequently depart from their original purport, and their prose also lacks order. This composition uses language of imposing discipline to bring out the meticulous rigor of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Reading it inspires respect and admiration. It is included as a model for those studying the Classic of the Unicorn.”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
錄
棄險而受制於內春秋之責在貳國扼險而遺
義於外春秋之責在諸侯此虎牢之城不繫鄭
其戍繫之及書楚救也鄭晉之罪無所逃矣且
虎牢鄭地也晉悼復霸從獻子之謀率會戚之
兵以城之將以逼其從已焉爾曷為責在鄭耶
聖人以為制邑之險聞於天下地有所必據城
有所必守而不可棄焉者鄭也不克固守為晉
所城門戶已毀非復滎陽之舊封藩籬已徹非
===
若宛陵之私屬是果世守者乎卒之君臣上下
曾無一息之寧玉帛犧牲徒為二境之待無所
底告然後請成誰之責歟經不繫鄭止書城虎
牢若曰鄭人土地本之君親失其所有曽黃人
之不如也其責在鄭如此者夫虎牢既城矣悼
猶隱憂任魏絳之賢聚初駕之兵以戍之將以
守其復叛焉爾曷為罪諸侯耶聖人以為鄭人
從楚固云不義無乃於已有關亦當在內自省
而不可脅焉者晉也不自省躬伐而復戍非欲
punctuated:
錄。
棄險而受制於內，春秋之責在貳國；扼險而遺義於外，春秋之責在諸侯。此虎牢之城不繫鄭，其戍繫之，及書楚救也，鄭晉之罪無所逃矣。且虎牢，鄭地也。晉悼復霸，從獻子之謀，率會戚之兵以城之，將以逼其從已焉爾，曷為責在鄭耶？聖人以為制邑之險聞於天下，地有所必據，城有所必守，而不可棄焉者，鄭也。不克固守，為晉所城，門戶已毀，非復滎陽之舊封；藩籬已徹，非若宛陵之私屬。是果世守者乎？卒之君臣上下，曾無一息之寧；玉帛犧牲，徒為二境之待，無所底告，然後請成。誰之責歟？經不繫鄭，止書城虎牢，若曰：鄭人土地，本之君親，失其所有，曽黃人之不如也。其責在鄭如此者。
夫虎牢既城矣，悼猶隱憂，任魏絳之賢，聚初駕之兵以戍之，將以守其復叛焉爾，曷為罪諸侯耶？聖人以為鄭人從楚，固云不義，無乃於已有關，亦當在內自省，而不可脅焉者，晉也。不自省躬，伐而復戍，非欲
translation_en:
…included.
When a state abandons its strategic defenses and submits to control within its own territory, the Spring and Autumn Annals places responsibility on the state that wavers between two allegiances. When rulers seize strategic defenses abroad and disregard righteousness, the Annals places responsibility on those rulers. Thus, when recording the fortification of Hulao, it does not identify the place as belonging to Zheng; when recording its garrisoning, it does. Together with its record of Chu coming to Zheng’s aid, these entries leave neither Zheng nor Jin any escape from blame.
Now Hulao was territory belonging to Zheng. Duke Dao of Jin, restoring his hegemony, followed Xianzi’s plan and led the troops assembled at Qi to fortify it, intending simply to compel Zheng to follow him. Why, then, does responsibility rest with Zheng? The Sage considered that the strategic strength of the town of Zhi was renowned throughout the realm. Zheng had ground that it must occupy and a city that it must defend and could not abandon. Yet it failed to hold firm, and Jin fortified the place.
