Its gateway was already destroyed: this was no longer its former domain at Xingyang. Its protective fence had already been dismantled: this was unlike its exclusive possession of Wanling. Was this truly how one guarded an inherited domain? In the end, ruler and ministers, high and low, enjoyed not a moment’s peace. Their jade, silks, and sacrificial animals served merely to meet the demands of the two neighboring powers. With nowhere to turn, they then sued for peace. Whose responsibility was this? The Classic does not identify the place as belonging to Zheng, but writes only, “Fortified Hulao,” as if to say: “The people of Zheng received their lands from their rulers and forebears, yet lost what they possessed. They were not even the equals of the people of Huang.” Such is its assignment of responsibility to Zheng.
Once Hulao had been fortified, Duke Dao still harbored anxiety. Employing the worthy Wei Jiang, he assembled the troops of the ‘first mobilization’ [?] to garrison it, intending simply to guard against Zheng’s renewed rebellion. Why, then, blame the regional rulers? The Sage considered that, although Zheng’s adherence to Chu could certainly be called unrighteous, might Jin itself not bear some responsibility? Jin, too, ought to examine itself inwardly rather than coerce Zheng. Without examining its own conduct, it attacked and then stationed a garrison there. Its intention was not to…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
斷荆楚之路以為鄭蔽仍欲踵前城之志而迫
其求成是果義服者乎已而楚共得聞即投袂
而起子囊往救遂夾潁而軍事雖假義師則有
名誰之罪歟經繫之鄭又書楚救若曰列國分
地受諸天子肆其凌逼曽荆楚之不若也其罪
諸侯如此者吁責棄險者家天下之心罪扼險
者明王制之意聖人維持世道其所感深矣雖
然鄭之棄華即夷無足道者悼於三駕之餘推
至誠以待人鄭自此不復叛而楚竟不能爭休
===
兵息民當世有賴嗚呼悼亦賢君也哉
禮記
五者備當上帝其饗
王璠
同考試官訓導張批備當字作者殊欠
體認此篇發揮真切筆力蒼然禮
經之冠也錄之
考試官教諭周批典雅文字適有此
篇
punctuated:
斷荆楚之路，以為鄭蔽，仍欲踵前城之志而迫其求成，是果義服者乎？已而楚共得聞，即投袂而起，子囊往救，遂夾潁而軍。事雖假義，師則有名，誰之罪歟？經繫之鄭，又書楚救，若曰：「列國分地，受諸天子，肆其凌逼，曽荆楚之不若也。」其罪諸侯如此者。吁！責棄險者，家天下之心；罪扼險者，明王制之意。聖人維持世道，其所感深矣！雖然，鄭之棄華即夷，無足道者。悼於三駕之餘，推至誠以待人，鄭自此不復叛，而楚竟不能爭。休兵息民，當世有賴。嗚呼！悼亦賢君也哉！

禮記
五者備當，上帝其饗。
王璠

同考試官訓導張批：「備當字，作者殊欠體認。此篇發揮真切，筆力蒼然，禮經之冠也，錄之。」

考試官教諭周批：「典雅文字，適有此篇。」
translation_en:
…to cut off the route to Jing-Chu and provide Zheng with a defensive screen; he still wished to pursue the intention behind the earlier fortification and force Zheng to seek peace. Was this truly submission won through righteousness? Soon afterward, when Duke Gong of Chu heard of it, he immediately shook his sleeves and rose. Zinang went to the rescue, and the armies encamped on opposite banks of the Ying River. Although this undertaking merely borrowed the guise of righteousness, the army nevertheless had a legitimate cause. Whose fault was this? The Classic identifies the place as belonging to Zheng and also records that Chu came to its rescue, as though saying: “The several states received their allotted territories from the Son of Heaven. To subject them to unrestrained intimidation is to fall below even Jing-Chu.” Such is its condemnation of the feudal lords. Ah! In reproaching those who abandon strategic defenses, it expresses the wish to make all under Heaven one family; in condemning those who seize strategic defenses, it expresses the intention to uphold the royal institutions. Profound indeed is the Sage’s concern in sustaining the moral order of the world!

Nevertheless, Zheng’s abandonment of the Chinese states to join the barbarians merits no praise. After his three campaigns, Duke Dao treated others with utmost sincerity. From then on, Zheng no longer rebelled, and Chu ultimately could no longer contend with him. He rested the troops and gave the people respite, benefiting his age. Ah! Duke Dao was indeed a worthy ruler!

Book of Rites
“When the five are complete and appropriate, the Sovereign on High will surely accept the offering.”
Wang Fan

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: “Writers have been notably deficient in grasping the words ‘complete and appropriate.’ This essay expounds them with precision and fidelity, and its writing has a mature vigor. It is the finest of the essays on the Book of Rites. Include it in the record.”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “For writing of classical elegance, here is precisely such an essay.”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正季批明淨可錄
物之備者既宜神之尊者必格夫莫尊於天之
帝也於祭物而備且當焉寧不有以來其格哉
記月令者之言如此且禮莫重於祭祭必備乎
物先王於仲秋命宰祝之官供循行之職至此
以為犧牲不備不敢祭也今既於全具於芻豢
有以視之按之而不失於肥瘠於物色有以瞻
之察之而無遺而又於小大長短在所必量是
其於五者無不備焉然備而不當猶不備也今
===
則所視所按者合乎事之程式而無不善所瞻
所察者當於事之倫類而無不宜而與夫所量
者亦中其度是又於備也無不當焉夫然則備
物之敬隆而報本之誠竭殆見皇天上帝雖至
遠也感吾敬之潛孚且將來享於冥冥之中矣
況羣神之近者有不享乎雖至尊也鑒吾誠之
默契且將來格於洋洋之表矣矧羣神之卑者
有不格乎所以致風雨之節在是所以致寒暑
之時在是夫一祭牲之備而來天神之格如此
punctuated:
考試官學正季批：明淨可錄。

物之備者既宜，神之尊者必格。夫莫尊於天之帝也，於祭物而備且當焉，寧不有以來其格哉？記月令者之言如此。且禮莫重於祭，祭必備乎物。先王於仲秋命宰祝之官供循行之職，至此以為犧牲不備，不敢祭也。今既於全具、於芻豢有以視之、按之，而不失於肥瘠；於物色有以瞻之、察之而無遺；而又於小大長短，在所必量，是其於五者無不備焉。然備而不當，猶不備也。今則所視所按者合乎事之程式而無不善，所瞻所察者當於事之倫類而無不宜，而與夫所量者亦中其度，是又於備也無不當焉。夫然則備物之敬隆，而報本之誠竭。殆見皇天上帝雖至遠也，感吾敬之潛孚，且將來享於冥冥之中矣，況羣神之近者有不享乎？雖至尊也，鑒吾誠之默契，且將來格於洋洋之表矣，矧羣神之卑者有不格乎？所以致風雨之節在是，所以致寒暑之時在是。夫一祭牲之備，而來天神之格如此，
translation_en:
Examiner Ji, Instructor, comments: “Clear and lucid; worthy of inclusion.”

When the offerings are complete and fitting, the most exalted spirit will surely come. Nothing is more exalted than the Sovereign of Heaven. If the sacrificial offerings are both complete and appropriate, could they fail to bring about his coming? Such is the meaning of the words of the recorder of the Monthly Ordinances.

Among rites, none is more weighty than sacrifice, and sacrifice requires complete offerings. In the middle month of autumn, the former kings commanded the officers responsible for slaughter and invocation to perform their duties of inspection. At this point, they held that if the sacrificial animals were not fully prepared, they dared not sacrifice. Now the animals’ completeness of form and their feeding on grass or grain have been examined and checked, so that their fatness or leanness is properly assessed; their appearance and color have been observed and scrutinized, with nothing overlooked; and their size and length must also be measured. Thus none of the five requirements is left unfulfilled. Yet completeness without appropriateness is as good as incompleteness.

Now what is examined and checked conforms to the prescribed procedures, and is good in every respect; what is observed and scrutinized accords with the proper categories, and is fitting in every respect; and what is measured likewise meets its prescribed dimensions. Thus everything that is complete is also appropriate. In this way, reverence expressed through preparing the offerings reaches its height, and sincerity in requiting the source of life is fully exerted. We may then expect that, although August Heaven, the Sovereign on High, is supremely distant, he will respond to the unseen influence of our reverence and come to partake of the offerings amid the invisible realm. How much more, then, could the nearer spirits fail to partake? Although he is supremely exalted, he will discern the silent accord of our sincerity and come, manifesting his abundant presence. How much more, then, could the lesser spirits fail to come? Herein lies the means of bringing wind and rain in due measure; herein lies the means of bringing cold and heat in their proper seasons. If the full preparation of the animals for a single sacrifice can thus bring the heavenly spirits to attend …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
汝之循行可不慎歟嗟乎仁人之事天也如事
親故先王於郊祭之禮獨隆然豈私其身哉凡
以為民祈福而已其敬天勤民之心何至耶他
章有曰唯聖人為能饗帝言敬之至也以此垂
教後世猶有褻天而不知事者噫
君為正則百姓從政矣
何清
同考試官訓導張批此題有關為政之
體此作寫出上下孚感底意正爾
===
可人錄之不但以其文也
考試官教諭周批辭氣詳雅讀之粲
然
考試官學正季批說得明盡非苟作
者
上能端其所行下必順其所令盖君正莫不正
也使君有不正欲下之從其政也難矣哉昔孔
子對哀公為政之問及此意謂有國者不患乎
人心之不順而患乎吾政之未脩不患乎吾政
punctuated:
汝之循行，可不慎歟？嗟乎！仁人之事天也如事親，故先王於郊祭之禮獨隆，然豈私其身哉？凡以為民祈福而已。其敬天勤民之心何至耶！他章有曰：「唯聖人為能饗帝。」言敬之至也。以此垂教後世，猶有褻天而不知事者，噫！

君為正，則百姓從政矣。
何清

同考試官訓導張批：此題有關為政之體，此作寫出上下孚感底意，正爾可人。錄之，不但以其文也。

考試官教諭周批：辭氣詳雅，讀之粲然。

考試官學正季批：說得明盡，非苟作者。

上能端其所行，下必順其所令。盖君正，莫不正也。使君有不正，欲下之從其政也，難矣哉！昔孔子對哀公為政之問，及此，意謂有國者不患乎人心之不順，而患乎吾政之未脩；不患乎吾政
translation_en:
…Can you fail to be cautious in carrying this out? Ah! A humane person serves Heaven as he serves his parents. Thus the former kings accorded exceptional solemnity to the rites of the suburban sacrifice. Yet was this for their own private benefit? It was entirely to pray for blessings for the people. How profound was their devotion to revering Heaven and caring diligently for the people! Another chapter says: “Only a sage can make offerings acceptable to the Lord on High.” This speaks of reverence at its utmost. Although this teaching was handed down to later generations, there are still those who profane Heaven and do not know how to serve it. Alas!

“If the ruler acts correctly, the common people will follow his government.”
He Qing

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: This topic concerns the essentials of governing. This composition brings out the idea of mutual trust and responsiveness between those above and those below, and is most pleasing. It is selected for more than its literary merit alone.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Its language and tone are thorough and elegant; it shines upon reading.

Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: The explanation is clear and exhaustive. This is no carelessly composed work.

If the one above can rectify his conduct, those below will surely obey his commands. For when the ruler is correct, none will fail to be correct. If the ruler himself is not correct, how difficult it will be to wish those below to follow his government! In former times, when Confucius answered Duke Ai’s question about governing, he touched upon this point. His meaning was that one who rules a state should worry not that people’s hearts are disobedient, but that his own government has not been put in order; he should worry not that his own government…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之不脩而患乎所爲之不正何則人君一身下
所則也故必敬以脩己使所爲一出於正無大
廷深宮之間也而邪佞不得以惑之道以脩身
俾所行一由於正無大德小德之踰也而憸壬
不容以間之見於刑賞焉刑所當刑賞所當賞
無偏而無黨也形於好惡焉好所當好惡所當
惡無反而無側也夫君之所爲旣無不正則表
率倡導之源以清激勸化成之本以立將見聚
廬而居凡在乎君臨者非一姓也莫不曰吾君
===
正矣吾何以不從自翕然於感化之餘而唯其
所令比閭而處凡歸乎統馭者非一人也罔不
曰吾君正矣吾何以不順自驩然於鼓舞之中
而唯其所施會極歸極順於風之偃草也梗化
者誰與遵道遵路捷於響之應聲也弗率者誰
與吁君正於上而民從之如此斯政之所以爲
政也然則人君烏可以不正耶抑論之君民一
體君以民爲體民以君爲心其所關甚重也柰
何世之爲君者徒恃崇高之位而不知正身以
punctuated: 之不脩，而患乎所爲之不正。何則？人君一身，下所則也。故必敬以脩己，使所爲一出於正，無大廷深宮之間也，而邪佞不得以惑之；道以脩身，俾所行一由於正，無大德小德之踰也，而憸壬不容以間之。見於刑賞焉，刑所當刑，賞所當賞，無偏而無黨也；形於好惡焉，好所當好，惡所當惡，無反而無側也。夫君之所爲旣無不正，則表率倡導之源以清，激勸化成之本以立。將見聚廬而居，凡在乎君臨者，非一姓也，莫不曰：「吾君正矣，吾何以不從？」自翕然於感化之餘，而唯其所令；比閭而處，凡歸乎統馭者，非一人也，罔不曰：「吾君正矣，吾何以不順？」自驩然於鼓舞之中，而唯其所施。會極歸極，順於風之偃草也，梗化者誰與？遵道遵路，捷於響之應聲也，弗率者誰與？吁！君正於上，而民從之如此，斯政之所以爲政也。然則人君烏可以不正耶？抑論之，君民一體，君以民爲體，民以君爲心，其所關甚重也。柰何世之爲君者，徒恃崇高之位，而不知正身以
translation_en:
…that his government is not well ordered, but should worry that his own conduct is not upright. Why is this? The ruler’s own person is the model for those below. He must therefore cultivate himself through reverence, ensuring that everything he does proceeds from uprightness, with no distinction between the great court and the secluded palace, so that the wicked and flattering cannot mislead him. He must cultivate himself through the Way, ensuring that all his conduct accords with uprightness, with no transgression in either great or small virtues, so that treacherous men cannot interfere. When this manifests itself in punishments and rewards, he punishes those who ought to be punished and rewards those who ought to be rewarded, without partiality or faction. When it takes shape in his likes and dislikes, he likes what ought to be liked and dislikes what ought to be disliked, without perversity or bias. Once nothing the ruler does is other than upright, the source of exemplary leadership is purified, and the foundation for encouragement and moral transformation is established.
Then one will see that those who dwell in clustered homes—all who come under his rule, comprising many families—will all say: “Our ruler is upright; how could we fail to follow him?” Having been moved and transformed, they will naturally unite in obeying his commands. Those who live in neighboring villages—all who fall under his governance, comprising many people—will all say: “Our ruler is upright; how could we fail to obey him?” Amid this encouragement and inspiration, they will naturally rejoice in complying with his measures. Gathering at and turning toward the supreme standard, they will submit as readily as grass bends before the wind: who will resist transformation? Following the Way and pursuing its path, they will respond as swiftly as an echo answers a sound: who will fail to follow?
Ah! When the ruler is upright above and the people follow him in this way, this is what makes government truly government. How, then, could a ruler fail to be upright? To consider it further, ruler and people form one body: the ruler takes the people as his body, and the people take the ruler as their heart. What rests upon this relationship is exceedingly weighty. How is it that the rulers of this world merely rely upon their exalted position, yet do not know to make themselves upright so as to…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
帥民嚴刑峻法必使從其所好無恤乎民心之
日離而亂且亡也孔子告哀公以此及其問所
以爲正而答之則不出乎三綱其啓之也深矣
哀公卒不能行其言此魯之所以不競歟
第貳場
論
講學爲正心之要
張合
同考試官訓導詹批今士子作論下筆
===
輒數百言率皆堆積浮蔓徒以凑
合爲能於本題之意全無干涉甚
至好奇喜怪而首尾支離自不知
其何説此時文之弊也是作不惟
意有根據而且層見疊出血脉不
斷於從容委曲之中有峻激雄勁
之態亦何嘗不循時格而穎異之
見自是難掩斯可以爲論矣
考試官教諭周批講學以正心此治
punctuated:
帥民，嚴刑峻法，必使從其所好，無恤乎民心之日離，而亂且亡也。孔子告哀公以此，及其問所以爲正而答之，則不出乎三綱，其啓之也深矣。哀公卒不能行其言，此魯之所以不競歟？
第貳場
論
講學爲正心之要
張合
同考試官訓導詹批：今士子作論，下筆輒數百言，率皆堆積浮蔓，徒以凑合爲能，於本題之意全無干涉，甚至好奇喜怪，而首尾支離，自不知其何説，此時文之弊也。是作不惟意有根據，而且層見疊出，血脉不斷，於從容委曲之中，有峻激雄勁之態。亦何嘗不循時格，而穎異之見自是難掩，斯可以爲論矣。
考試官教諭周批：講學以正心，此治
translation_en:
…to lead the people, but instead employs harsh punishments and severe laws, insisting that they conform to his own preferences, heedless that the people's hearts grow daily more estranged and that disorder and ruin will follow. Confucius instructed Duke Ai on this point; when the duke asked how to achieve rectitude, his answer remained within the Three Bonds. How profound was the guidance he offered! Yet Duke Ai ultimately could not put his words into practice. Was this why Lu failed to become strong?
Second Session
Discourse
“Expounding Learning Is Essential to Rectifying the Mind”
Zhang He
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: Nowadays, when examination candidates compose discourses, they readily write several hundred words. Most merely pile up empty, rambling phrases, treating the ability to cobble them together as an accomplishment, with no connection whatever to the meaning of the assigned topic. Some even delight in the bizarre and strange, leaving beginning and end disconnected, themselves unaware of what they are saying. This is the failing of contemporary examination prose. In this composition, however, the ideas are not only well grounded but unfold in successive layers, with an unbroken thread running through them. Within its measured and nuanced exposition there is an incisive, vigorous force. Nor does it fail to follow the prevailing form; yet its exceptional insights are naturally impossible to conceal. This may indeed be called a discourse.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Expounding learning in order to rectify the mind: this, for governing…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
道切要之論忠臣愛君莫急於此
子能歷證前代而發明曲盡一字
一句皆含深意非空言者篇末數
語尤見剴切他日見用慎毋忘也
考試官學正季批此作句簡而工意
多而正抑揚開闔不外題旨而清
俊整潔讀自不厭顧不可刻耶
甚矣爲君之難也以天下之大係於一身而身
則有本焉必端本而後可理天下之務然本之
===
端也又有至切之要不可得而緩者苟失其要
而惟末之圖雖勤且勵祗見勞矣大體所在寧
有益乎既無益於身心必無濟於天下此後世
識治之君毎惓惓以正心爲急而心之由正又
恒以開廣睿聰爲首務也噫朱子斯言其爲宗
社生靈計可謂憂深而慮遠者矣人君忽此而
欲收平治之効於天下未之有也竊嘗觀之行
路矣有大道焉有小徑焉若知平直險夷則必
審所趨避而不陷於顛躓否則混見聞昧取舍
punctuated:
道切要之論，忠臣愛君莫急於此。子能歷證前代，而發明曲盡，一字一句皆含深意，非空言者。篇末數語尤見剴切，他日見用，慎毋忘也。
考試官學正季批：此作句簡而工，意多而正，抑揚開闔不外題旨，而清俊整潔，讀自不厭，顧不可刻耶？
甚矣，爲君之難也！以天下之大係於一身，而身則有本焉，必端本而後可理天下之務。然本之端也，又有至切之要，不可得而緩者。苟失其要，而惟末之圖，雖勤且勵，祗見勞矣。大體所在，寧有益乎？既無益於身心，必無濟於天下。此後世識治之君毎惓惓以正心爲急，而心之由正，又恒以開廣睿聰爲首務也。噫！朱子斯言，其爲宗社生靈計，可謂憂深而慮遠者矣。人君忽此而欲收平治之効於天下，未之有也。竊嘗觀之行路矣：有大道焉，有小徑焉。若知平直險夷，則必審所趨避，而不陷於顛躓；否則混見聞，昧取舍。
translation_en:
…an argument addressing the essentials of the Way of government. For a loyal minister who loves his ruler, nothing is more urgent than this. You have drawn evidence from successive earlier dynasties and elucidated the matter fully in all its ramifications. Every word and sentence contains profound meaning; these are no empty words. The final few sentences are especially pertinent and forthright. When you are employed in office in days to come, take care never to forget them.
Examiner Ji, an Instructor, comments: This composition has concise yet accomplished sentences and abundant yet sound ideas. Its shifts of emphasis and its developments and conclusions remain within the purport of the topic. Clear, elegant, orderly, and polished, it never wearies the reader. Surely it deserves to be printed?
How very difficult it is to be a ruler! The vast realm depends upon a single person, and that person has a root. Only after setting this root upright can he manage the affairs of the realm. Yet in setting the root upright, there is a most pressing essential that permits no delay. If he misses that essential and attends only to the branches, however diligent and strenuous his efforts, he will achieve nothing but toil. What benefit can this bring to what matters as a whole? Since it brings no benefit to his person and mind, it certainly cannot help the realm. Thus, rulers of later ages who understood government continually and earnestly treated rectifying the mind as urgent; and as the means of rectifying it, they invariably made broadening their sagely understanding their first task. Ah! In these words, Master Zhu, taking thought for the dynastic temples, the altars of state, and the living people, may indeed be said to have shown profound concern and far-reaching foresight. There has never been a ruler who disregarded this yet succeeded in bringing peace and good government to the realm.
I have ventured to consider this through the example of traveling along a road. There are broad highways and narrow paths. If one knows which are level and straight, which dangerous and which safe, one will surely discern carefully which to follow and which to avoid, and will not stumble and fall. Otherwise, one becomes confused in what one sees and hears, and fails to discern what to choose and what to reject…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
一舉足而萬里之悔無及矣是心之邪正其猶
路乎知路之岐其猶學乎學之一言虞夏以前
未聞也至高宗與傅說始言之自是帝王始知
威福不足恃而從事於學矣然學之爲道豈易
言哉若不事詩書者固無足論其少知嚮慕者
則又或惟談苦空或篤好音律或攻書篆以爲
能或騁詞章以競美雖曰工矣心何補哉然就
中取善若漢宣帝以圖籍日陳於前唐太宗鋭
意經術宋高宗披覽載籍亦似知務學者矣但
===
人君之學與韋布不同若惟涉獵是務而耀講
學虛名宏綱大法漫然弗究雖曰學矣不如已
焉匪書無益莫知要也要之所在其明理乎理
在天下無所不備有是非焉有善惡焉有邪正
焉其中又有涉於疑似而不容不辨者若徒曰
吾心正矣毋庸學矣則情好偏局而靜之所養
動之所發未必皆由於正猶不知路之險夷而
跬步一差秦越頓異者盍觀夫漢唐叔季之君
乎如崇尚佛老自以爲心之善矣窮極術藝自
punctuated: 一舉足而萬里之悔無及矣。是心之邪正，其猶路乎？知路之岐，其猶學乎？學之一言，虞夏以前未聞也，至高宗與傅說始言之。自是帝王始知威福不足恃，而從事於學矣。然學之爲道，豈易言哉？若不事詩書者，固無足論；其少知嚮慕者，則又或惟談苦空，或篤好音律，或攻書篆以爲能，或騁詞章以競美。雖曰工矣，心何補哉？然就中取善，若漢宣帝以圖籍日陳於前，唐太宗鋭意經術，宋高宗披覽載籍，亦似知務學者矣。但人君之學，與韋布不同。若惟涉獵是務，而耀講學虛名，宏綱大法漫然弗究，雖曰學矣，不如已焉。匪書無益，莫知要也。要之所在，其明理乎？理在天下，無所不備：有是非焉，有善惡焉，有邪正焉，其中又有涉於疑似而不容不辨者。若徒曰：「吾心正矣，毋庸學矣。」則情好偏局，而靜之所養、動之所發，未必皆由於正。猶不知路之險夷，而跬步一差，秦越頓異者。盍觀夫漢唐叔季之君乎？如崇尚佛老，自以爲心之善矣；窮極術藝，自
translation_en:
…with a single step, one may go ten thousand li astray, beyond remedy or regret. Is the heart’s deviation or rectitude not like a road? And is knowing the road’s forks not like learning? Before the ages of Yu and Xia, the very term “learning” had not been heard; only with Gaozong of Shang and Fu Yue did it begin to be spoken of. From then on, emperors and kings began to understand that their power to punish and bestow favor could not be relied upon, and devoted themselves to learning.

Yet is the way of learning easy to discuss? Those who do not occupy themselves with the Odes and the Documents are, of course, scarcely worth discussing. But among those who have some inclination toward learning, some speak only of suffering and emptiness; some are passionately fond of musical pitches; some cultivate calligraphy and seal script as accomplishments; and some display their literary compositions in competition for elegance. Skilled though they may be called, what benefit does this bring to the heart? Still, if we select the better examples among them, Emperor Xuandi of Han had maps and books laid before him daily, Emperor Taizong of Tang eagerly pursued classical learning, and Emperor Gaozong of Song read through historical writings. These, too, seem to have understood the need to apply themselves to learning.

But a ruler’s learning differs from that of an ordinary scholar in plain clothing. If he devotes himself solely to cursory reading and flaunts the empty reputation of pursuing learning, while carelessly neglecting to investigate its great guiding principles and fundamental standards, then, though this may be called learning, he would be better off stopping. It is not that books are useless, but that he does not know what is essential. Does the essential point not lie in understanding principle? Principle is present everywhere under Heaven: there are right and wrong, good and evil, deviation and rectitude. Among these are also matters of ambiguity and apparent resemblance that must be distinguished.

If one merely says, “My heart is already correct; there is no need to learn,” one’s feelings and preferences will be partial and confined. What one nurtures in stillness and expresses in action will not necessarily all proceed from rectitude. It is like being ignorant of a road’s dangers and ease: an error of even half a step suddenly separates one’s course as widely as Qin from Yue. Why not consider the rulers of the declining and final ages of Han and Tang? They exalted Buddhism and Daoism, believing this showed the goodness of their hearts; they pursued technical arts to the utmost, themselves …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以為心之敏矣喜功黷武自以為心之壯矣姑
息寬縱自以為心之仁矣旁搜苛察自以為心
之明矣濫賞私恩自以為心之惠矣殊不知理
在於心自有本然之正今各有所偏而罔覺其
非者由講究弗明而是非疑似之間得以亂之
耳使先知正心之要則必以崇正為急而何累
乎善也必以大體為務而何累乎敏也必以戡
定為威而何累乎壯也必以感化為恩而何累
乎仁也必以周物為智而何累乎明也必以普
===
偏為公而何累乎惠也嗚呼學一不講而心之
所發懸遠如此良可畏哉是以古之賢君明緩
急之序達先後之宜知心之為物雖曰萬理歸
宿之地然隱微之間真妄錯雜苟理不先明則
其所存所發未必皆由於正況近似亂真如前
數者之累而為君心之害愈深如之何而不懼
也於是乎究古今之變察理欲之幾如何為昏
明如何為邪正如何為安危如何為淑慝遠稽
前代何者可以勸懲近鑒祖宗何者可以效法
punctuated:
以為心之敏矣，喜功黷武，自以為心之壯矣；姑息寬縱，自以為心之仁矣；旁搜苛察，自以為心之明矣；濫賞私恩，自以為心之惠矣。殊不知理在於心，自有本然之正。今各有所偏而罔覺其非者，由講究弗明，而是非疑似之間得以亂之耳。使先知正心之要，則必以崇正為急，而何累乎善也？必以大體為務，而何累乎敏也？必以戡定為威，而何累乎壯也？必以感化為恩，而何累乎仁也？必以周物為智，而何累乎明也？必以普偏為公，而何累乎惠也？
嗚呼！學一不講，而心之所發懸遠如此，良可畏哉！是以古之賢君，明緩急之序，達先後之宜，知心之為物，雖曰萬理歸宿之地，然隱微之間，真妄錯雜。苟理不先明，則其所存所發未必皆由於正。況近似亂真，如前數者之累，而為君心之害愈深，如之何而不懼也？於是乎究古今之變，察理欲之幾：如何為昏明，如何為邪正，如何為安危，如何為淑慝；遠稽前代，何者可以勸懲；近鑒祖宗，何者可以效法。
translation_en:
…considered their minds quick-witted. Delighting in achievement and recklessly resorting to arms, they considered their minds strong; indulging and tolerating others, they considered their minds benevolent; searching everywhere and scrutinizing harshly, they considered their minds discerning; bestowing rewards indiscriminately and granting private favors, they considered their minds generous. Little did they understand that principle within the mind has its own inherent correctness. That each now inclined toward some partiality without recognizing his error arose simply from a failure to attain clarity through study and inquiry, allowing confusion amid right and wrong and their deceptive semblances. Had they first understood the essentials of rectifying the mind, they would surely have made honoring what is correct their priority: how, then, could supposed goodness have encumbered them? They would have attended to the larger concerns: how could supposed quickness have encumbered them? They would have found their authority in restoring order: how could supposed strength have encumbered them? They would have expressed their grace through moral transformation: how could supposed benevolence have encumbered them? They would have found wisdom in caring comprehensively for all things: how could supposed discernment have encumbered them? They would have understood impartiality as extending universally to all [?]: how could supposed generosity have encumbered them?
Alas! Once learning goes unexamined, what issues from the mind can stray this far. This is truly alarming! Thus the worthy rulers of antiquity understood the ranking of less urgent and urgent matters and grasped what should properly come first and afterward. They knew that although the mind may be called the place where all principles find their home, truth and delusion mingle in its hidden recesses. Unless principle is first made clear, what the mind harbors and expresses will not necessarily all proceed from correctness. Moreover, when semblances confound the true—as with the encumbrances just enumerated—the harm to the ruler’s mind grows still deeper. How could one fail to be afraid? Accordingly, they investigated changes past and present and scrutinized the subtle beginnings of principle and desire: what constitutes darkness or clarity, perversity or correctness, security or danger, goodness or wickedness. Looking far back to earlier dynasties, they examined what might serve as encouragement or warning; taking their own dynastic ancestors as nearer mirrors, they examined what might be emulated…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
講筵啓沃因言而思之方正忠良虛心以訪之
治安易忽曷以慎之儉壬易昵曷以遠之宴安
易懷曷以儆之正邪易混曷以辨之公私易雜
曷以清之思其理而不泛用其心窮其本而不
徒事乎末如此則治理昭明大本以立猶未舉
足而已先知路之險易矣是以當其心之未動
也湛然清明渾然純一及其感發也果在天理
耶必知所以充之在人欲耶必知所以遏之凡
所欲行皆正大光明之體無偏黨反側之私而
===
一心正矣由是推之朝廷則百官承式推之於
國則百姓昭明推之天下則四方風動而莫敢
有不正者矣大學欲正心必先於致知推極其
效至於平天下董子所謂正心以正朝廷而先
之以勉彊學問皆此意耳使學先不講雖天資
敏睿出於尋常而疑似之間見之未必真信之
未必决施於有政可訾多矣雖欲救之其能及
乎與其救之於終孰若審之於始始得其要則
至靜可以制動也至簡可以御繁也至約可以
punctuated:
講筵啓沃，因言而思之；方正忠良，虛心以訪之。治安易忽，曷以慎之？儉壬易昵，曷以遠之？宴安易懷，曷以儆之？正邪易混，曷以辨之？公私易雜，曷以清之？思其理而不泛用其心，窮其本而不徒事乎末。如此則治理昭明，大本以立，猶未舉足而已先知路之險易矣。是以當其心之未動也，湛然清明，渾然純一；及其感發也，果在天理耶？必知所以充之；在人欲耶？必知所以遏之。凡所欲行，皆正大光明之體，無偏黨反側之私，而一心正矣。由是推之朝廷，則百官承式；推之於國，則百姓昭明；推之天下，則四方風動，而莫敢有不正者矣。
《大學》欲正心，必先於致知，推極其效，至於平天下。董子所謂正心以正朝廷，而先之以勉彊學問，皆此意耳。使學先不講，雖天資敏睿出於尋常，而疑似之間，見之未必真，信之未必决，施於有政，可訾多矣。雖欲救之，其能及乎？與其救之於終，孰若審之於始？始得其要，則至靜可以制動也，至簡可以御繁也，至約可以
translation_en:
…At the imperial lectures, receive instruction that nourishes the mind and reflect upon what is said; consult upright, loyal, and worthy men with an open mind. Peace and good order readily invite neglect: how can one remain vigilant? Sycophants [?] readily become intimates: how can one keep them at a distance? Ease and comfort readily win attachment: how can one guard against them? The upright and the wicked are easily confused: how can one distinguish them? Public and private interests are easily mingled: how can one separate them clearly? Reflect upon principle without employing the mind aimlessly; investigate the root without merely attending to the branches. In this way, the principles of government become clear and the great foundation is established. It is like knowing beforehand whether a road is dangerous or easy, even before taking a step. Thus, before the mind is stirred, it is limpid and clear, wholly pure and undivided. When it responds to things and becomes active, does its impulse truly accord with heavenly principle? Then one must know how to extend it fully. Does it arise from human desires? Then one must know how to restrain it. Everything one wishes to carry out embodies uprightness and openness, without the selfishness of partiality, faction, or deviousness, and the mind is thereby rectified. Extend this to the court, and the officials all follow its example; extend it to the state, and the people become enlightened; extend it throughout all under Heaven, and the four quarters respond as to a wind, with none daring to remain unrectified.
The Great Learning holds that, to rectify the mind, one must first extend knowledge; pursued to its fullest effect, this leads to bringing peace to all under Heaven. Master Dong’s teaching that one should rectify the mind in order to rectify the court, and should precede this with diligent effort in learning, conveys precisely this meaning. If learning is not first examined thoroughly, then even someone endowed with intelligence and insight beyond the ordinary may fail to perceive truly or believe decisively when confronted with doubtful distinctions. When this is put into practice in government, much will be open to criticism. Even if one wishes to remedy it, can one still do so in time? Rather than remedying matters at the end, how much better to scrutinize them at the beginning! If one grasps the essentials at the outset, utmost stillness can control movement, utmost simplicity can govern complexity, and utmost concision can…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
該博也又何必騁浮華工記誦衒讀書之彌文
而於身心卒無補哉使屑屑必於書焉則堯舜
禹湯文武之時無書可讀又何資也自今觀之
堯惟執中舜惟精一禹惟祗德湯惟建中文不
過敬止武不過建極而已夫精一中敬皆理之
微也正心之要也數聖人能講明之即所謂學
也雖性本生知心不待養而後正然亦何甞緩
於學哉朱子不曰講學以正心而必曰要者可
見學之一言所係甚切欲臻功化之極必須由
===
此進焉猶岐轍不差而萬里可馴至矣辟之行
路不亦信乎夫欲正君心固本於講學矣但人
主一心攻者甚眾安能保其終無間乎故古之
聖君尤於是乎致謹也左右前後罔非正人深
宫禁密凛然弗懈所以涵養君德而維持聖學
者無所不用其極夫然後本固性成治行化洽
無負乎天下望也嗚呼為君之難詎不信夫知
其難而及時講學亦無難者是又在於立志之
堅如說命所謂念終始典于學雖二帝三王亦
punctuated:
該博也。又何必騁浮華、工記誦，衒讀書之彌文，而於身心卒無補哉？使屑屑必於書焉，則堯舜禹湯文武之時，無書可讀，又何資也？自今觀之，堯惟執中，舜惟精一，禹惟祗德，湯惟建中，文不過敬止，武不過建極而已。夫精一中敬，皆理之微也，正心之要也。數聖人能講明之，即所謂學也。雖性本生知，心不待養而後正，然亦何甞緩於學哉？朱子不曰「講學以正心」，而必曰「要」者，可見學之一言所係甚切。欲臻功化之極，必須由此進焉，猶岐轍不差，而萬里可馴至矣。辟之行路，不亦信乎？
夫欲正君心，固本於講學矣。但人主一心，攻者甚眾，安能保其終無間乎？故古之聖君尤於是乎致謹也。左右前後，罔非正人；深宫禁密，凛然弗懈。所以涵養君德而維持聖學者，無所不用其極。夫然後本固性成，治行化洽，無負乎天下望也。嗚呼！為君之難，詎不信夫？知其難而及時講學，亦無難者。是又在於立志之堅，如《說命》所謂「念終始典于學」，雖二帝三王亦
translation_en:
…encompass the extensive. Why, then, indulge in superficial brilliance, cultivate skill in memorization and recitation, and flaunt the elaborate ornament of book learning, when in the end it contributes nothing to one’s person and mind? If one insists on attending to books in every petty detail, then in the days of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, when there were no books to read, what could they have drawn upon? Viewed from the present, Yao simply held fast to the Mean; Shun practiced refinement and singleness of purpose; Yu revered virtue; Tang established the Mean; Wen did no more than abide in reverence, and Wu no more than establish the supreme standard. Refinement, singleness of purpose, the Mean, and reverence are all subtle aspects of principle and essentials for rectifying the mind. These sages’ ability to investigate and elucidate them is precisely what is meant by learning. Although their nature endowed them with innate knowledge, and their minds did not have to await cultivation before becoming correct, when did they ever relax their efforts in learning? Master Zhu did not merely say, “Investigate learning in order to rectify the mind,” but insisted on the word “essential.” This shows how much hinges upon that single word, learning. To attain the utmost in achievement and moral transformation, one must advance by this path, just as, if one does not take the wrong track at a fork, one may gradually reach a destination ten thousand li away. Is not the comparison with traveling a road indeed apt?
The desire to rectify the ruler’s mind certainly has its foundation in the investigation of learning. Yet so many influences assail the ruler’s single mind: how can one ensure that no breach will ever arise? Thus the sage rulers of antiquity exercised particular vigilance in this matter. Those to their left and right, before and behind them, were all upright men; even in the secluded depths of the palace, they remained vigilant and never relaxed. They employed to the utmost every means of nurturing the ruler’s virtue and sustaining sagely learning. Only then would the foundation become firm and the moral nature fully developed, good government prevail and transforming influence spread everywhere, so that the expectations of all under Heaven would not be disappointed. Alas! Is it not indeed true that being a ruler is difficult? Yet if one recognizes its difficulty and undertakes the investigation of learning in good time, there need be no difficulty. This, in turn, depends upon firmness of resolve, as expressed in the Charge to Yue: “Keep learning constantly in mind, from beginning to end.” Even the Two Emperors and Three Kings…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易及耳夫何難哉使漢唐宋號稱英敏之君能
知此義何至君德不純治功小就卒貽後世無
窮之惜哉玩一時之安貽千載之戒可慨也已
詩曰殷鑒不遠其是之謂乎又曰學有緝熈于
光明惟守成賢君能之噫朱子斯言豈但爲當
時告實爲萬世爲君者告也
表
擬宋製觀文鑒古圖輔臣賀表慶曆四年
張合
===
同考試官訓導詹批標著事序使之明
白謂之表此作不惟鋪叙詳明且
四六流麗而典雅不浮非記誦陳
言者
考試官教諭周批詞不深僻而含蓄
忠義未審當時有此作否
考試官學正季批得體製而精緻可
嘉
慶曆四年二月丙辰
punctuated:
易及耳，夫何難哉？使漢唐宋號稱英敏之君能知此義，何至君德不純，治功小就，卒貽後世無窮之惜哉？玩一時之安，貽千載之戒，可慨也已！詩曰：「殷鑒不遠。」其是之謂乎？又曰：「學有緝熈于光明，惟守成賢君能之。」噫！朱子斯言，豈但爲當時告？實爲萬世爲君者告也。

表
擬宋製觀文鑒古圖輔臣賀表，慶曆四年。
張合

同考試官訓導詹批：標著事序，使之明白，謂之表。此作不惟鋪叙詳明，且四六流麗而典雅不浮，非記誦陳言者。

考試官教諭周批：詞不深僻，而含蓄忠義，未審當時有此作否。

考試官學正季批：得體製而精緻，可嘉。

慶曆四年二月丙辰，
translation_en:
… can readily be equaled. What difficulty could there be? Had those rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song who were acclaimed as brilliant and perceptive understood this principle, how could their rulerly virtue have remained impure and their achievements in government so modest, ultimately leaving endless regret to later generations? To indulge in the ease of a moment and leave a warning for a thousand years—how lamentable! The Book of Odes says, “Yin’s warning mirror is not far away.” Does this not describe precisely that? It also says, “Learning continues ever onward toward brightness; only a worthy ruler who preserves an inherited achievement can accomplish this.” Ah! Were these words of Master Zhu addressed merely to his own age? In truth, they were addressed to rulers for all ages.

Memorial
A congratulatory memorial in the voice of the assisting ministers of the Song, on the production of Illustrations for Viewing Patterns and Taking Antiquity as a Mirror (Guanwen jiangu tu), in the fourth year of Qingli [1044].
By Zhang He.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: “To set out the sequence of events distinctly and make it clear is what is meant by a memorial. This composition not only unfolds its account fully and clearly; its four- and six-character parallel phrases are also fluent and graceful, refined without being superficial. This is no mere recitation of memorized conventional phrases.”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The language is neither abstruse nor obscure, yet it holds within it loyalty and righteousness. I wonder whether there was such a composition at the time.”

Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: “It observes the proper form and is finely crafted: commendable.”

On the bingchen day of the second month of the fourth year of Qingli [1044] …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
上命圖製前代帝王美惡之迹可爲鑒戒者號
曰觀文鑒古圖
御迎陽門出示臣等者伏以
以人爲監帝王致治之良規取善爲師令
主保邦之要道欲光前而啓後因考古以
儀今朝野揚休臣鄰稱慶臣某等誠懽誠
忭稽首頓首上言竊惟
心莫要於審幾治莫先於擇術是以明堂
素墉悉登聖哲之容太液新亭盡寫唐虞
===
之跡開元寶千秋之鑑憲宗繪三合之屏
無非明聖撝謙急欲隨時體道治安愈愼
常思觸事警心逮至欲縱情迷遂畫洛神
之賦神搖心蕩遽張列女之圖妖華遍染
於重闈粉黛旁施於四壁豈知涉川攸利
在視乎前舟而行道無危須觀乎往轍孰
愚孰智遺後人褒貶之公可戒可師關世
道興衰之運
昌期偉觀曠古竒逢玆蓋伏遇
punctuated:
上命圖製前代帝王美惡之迹可爲鑒戒者，號曰《觀文鑒古圖》，御迎陽門，出示臣等者。
伏以：以人爲監，帝王致治之良規；取善爲師，令主保邦之要道。欲光前而啓後，因考古以儀今。朝野揚休，臣鄰稱慶。臣某等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言：竊惟心莫要於審幾，治莫先於擇術。是以明堂素墉，悉登聖哲之容；太液新亭，盡寫唐虞之跡。開元寶千秋之鑑，憲宗繪三合之屏。無非明聖撝謙，急欲隨時體道；治安愈愼，常思觸事警心。逮至欲縱情迷，遂畫洛神之賦；神搖心蕩，遽張列女之圖。妖華遍染於重闈，粉黛旁施於四壁。豈知涉川攸利，在視乎前舟；而行道無危，須觀乎往轍。孰愚孰智，遺後人褒貶之公；可戒可師，關世道興衰之運。昌期偉觀，曠古竒逢。玆蓋伏遇
translation_en:
…His Majesty ordered illustrations of the good and evil deeds of emperors and kings of former ages that could serve as mirrors and warnings, entitled Illustrations for Contemplating Culture and Taking Antiquity as a Mirror (Guanwen jiangu tu). He appeared at Yingyang Gate and displayed them to us, his servants.
We humbly submit: Taking people as a mirror is an excellent rule by which emperors and kings achieve good government; taking goodness as one’s teacher is the essential way by which worthy rulers preserve their realms. To glorify predecessors and enlighten successors, one therefore examines antiquity to set a standard for the present. Court and countryside proclaim this blessing; ministers and attendants voice their congratulations. We, your servants So-and-so and others, in heartfelt joy and delight, bow our heads to the ground and kowtow, submitting these words: We reflect that nothing is more essential to the mind than discerning the first stirrings of events, and nothing takes precedence in government over choosing the proper methods. Thus the plain walls of the Hall of Light bore the likenesses of sages and worthies, and the new pavilion at Taiye depicted the deeds of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. The emperor of the Kaiyuan era treasured the Mirror for a Thousand Autumns; Xianzong had the Screen of the Three Harmonies painted [?]. In every case, these enlightened sages exercised humility, eagerly seeking to embody the Way as circumstances required. Amid peace and good government they became still more circumspect, constantly seeking reminders in every occurrence to keep their minds alert. But when desires ran unchecked and feelings became deluded, rulers had the Rhapsody on the Goddess of the Luo River illustrated; when their spirits were unsettled and their hearts led astray, they hastily displayed pictures of exemplary women. Seductive beauty spread throughout the inner palace, and powdered and painted faces adorned its walls on every side. How could they understand that success in crossing a river depends on watching the boat ahead, and that travelling a road without danger requires observing the tracks of those who went before? Who was foolish and who was wise is left to the impartial praise and blame of posterity; what offers a warning and what provides a model bears upon the rise and decline of the age. This magnificent sight in a flourishing era is an extraordinary encounter unparalleled in antiquity. This is because we have humbly had the good fortune to encounter…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
〇〇〇〇
握紀御天應期啓運以鎮靜人心爲本以阜
安海宇爲先
誠意感孚甘雨巳徵於黙禱仁慈周恤燒羊
寧忍於宵饑兢業以斡化機憂勤以靖王
略比隆三代治兼教養之施叅賛兩儀身
任綱常之責正邪弗殽於偏聽予奪一循
乎至公刑以不殺爲威財以不畜爲富崇
儒重道恢弘
===
===
列聖之丕基偃武脩文度越百王之至治
聖人之德何以加焉太平之功可謂盛矣猶謂
帝王事跡雖備載於簡編然美惡儀形須
顯憑於采繪始因儒臣之請旁搜秘閣之
藏遠從軒轅之時邇接貞觀之季記分十
二煥
雲漢之昭回事列百餘燦丹青之藻麗治道
有純有雜朝綱或是或非創業最難每起
於憂勤之積守成不易常生於安靖之驕
punctuated: 〇〇〇〇，握紀御天，應期啓運，以鎮靜人心爲本，以阜安海宇爲先。誠意感孚，甘雨巳徵於黙禱；仁慈周恤，燒羊寧忍於宵饑？兢業以斡化機，憂勤以靖王略。比隆三代，治兼教養之施；叅賛兩儀，身任綱常之責。正邪弗殽於偏聽，予奪一循乎至公。刑以不殺爲威，財以不畜爲富。崇儒重道，恢弘列聖之丕基；偃武脩文，度越百王之至治。聖人之德何以加焉？太平之功可謂盛矣！猶謂帝王事跡雖備載於簡編，然美惡儀形須顯憑於采繪。始因儒臣之請，旁搜秘閣之藏，遠從軒轅之時，邇接貞觀之季。記分十二，煥雲漢之昭回；事列百餘，燦丹青之藻麗。治道有純有雜，朝綱或是或非。創業最難，每起於憂勤之積；守成不易，常生於安靖之驕。
translation_en:
… 〇〇〇〇, who grasps the guiding principles and rules in accordance with Heaven, responding to the appointed time and inaugurating a new destiny, takes calming the people's hearts as his foundation and enriching and securing the realm as his foremost concern. His sincerity moves Heaven to respond: timely rain has already attested to his silent prayers. His benevolence extends solicitously to all: though hungry at night, how could he bear to have a sheep roasted? Through vigilance and reverence he directs the workings of transformation; through anxious diligence he pacifies the royal domains. Rivaling the flourishing Three Dynasties, his government both educates and sustains the people; assisting Heaven and Earth, he personally shoulders responsibility for the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. He does not confuse the upright and the wicked by listening to only one side; his grants and withdrawals follow perfect impartiality throughout. His punishments command awe without killing; his finances achieve wealth without hoarding. Honoring Confucian learning and esteeming the Way, he enlarges the great foundation of the successive sage emperors; laying down arms and cultivating civil governance, he surpasses the finest rule of the hundred kings. What could be added to the virtue of this sage? His achievements in bringing great peace may indeed be called magnificent!

Yet he holds that, although the deeds of emperors and kings are fully recorded in books, their admirable and reprehensible conduct must be made visibly evident through colored illustrations. Thus, acting on the request of his Confucian officials, he searched widely through the holdings of the imperial library, reaching back to the time of Xuanyuan and extending down to the closing years of the Zhenguan era. The accounts are divided into twelve sections, radiant as the Milky Way in its luminous circuit; the events number more than a hundred, resplendent in the ornate beauty of painted colors. Ways of governing were sometimes pure and sometimes mixed; the guiding principles of court government were sometimes right and sometimes wrong. Founding a dynasty is supremely difficult, and commonly arises from accumulated anxious toil; preserving its achievements is no easy matter, its difficulties often arising from the arrogance bred by peace and stability.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
好惡同情自是難逃輿論昏明異域何嘗
不本諸心身雖往而名猶存貌雖疑而事
則實片言之善亦當垂範千年一念之差
遂至貽譏萬世左瞻右盻揖古人於想像
之間前規後箴悟心事於丰神之表蓋將
覩狂爲而興嘆觀賢主而若親懲勸森嚴
正邪炳若是誠
一代之令典信爲億載之徽章臣等才慙鼎
軸職玷班行世際唐虞敢廢詩書之舊學
===
君同堯舜尚期稷契之愚忠伏願
捄迹論心永作邦家之鑒
因人進德無更山水之圖直超近代之規模
允復隆平之景象臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖踴躍歡抃之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
punctuated:
好惡同情，自是難逃輿論；昏明異域，何嘗不本諸心？身雖往而名猶存，貌雖疑而事則實。片言之善，亦當垂範千年；一念之差，遂至貽譏萬世。左瞻右盻，揖古人於想像之間；前規後箴，悟心事於丰神之表。蓋將覩狂爲而興嘆，觀賢主而若親。懲勸森嚴，正邪炳若。是誠一代之令典，信爲億載之徽章。
臣等才慙鼎軸，職玷班行。世際唐虞，敢廢詩書之舊學？君同堯舜，尚期稷契之愚忠。伏願捄迹論心，永作邦家之鑒；因人進德，無更山水之圖。直超近代之規模，允復隆平之景象。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、踴躍歡抃之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
translation_en:
People share the same feelings of approval and disapproval; thus public judgment is naturally inescapable. Benightedness and enlightenment lie far apart, yet when have they not both originated in the heart? Though the person has departed, his name survives; though his likeness may be uncertain, his deeds are real. Even a single good utterance ought to serve as a model for a thousand years; an error in a single thought may bring reproach for ten thousand generations. Looking left and right, we salute the ancients in our imagination; admonished on every side, we discern their inward concerns through their outward bearing. Beholding reckless conduct, we will sigh; contemplating worthy rulers, we will feel as though in their presence. Stern are the warnings and encouragements; clear is the distinction between right and wrong. This is truly an excellent canon for this dynasty, assuredly a splendid testament for countless ages.
We, your servants, possess talents unworthy of the highest ministerial responsibilities and hold our places in the official ranks undeservedly. Living in an age like that of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, how dare we abandon our longstanding study of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents? Serving a sovereign the equal of Yao and Shun, we still aspire to the simple loyalty of Ji and Xie. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will examine their deeds [?] and assess their intentions, forever taking them as a mirror for the realm; that through these figures you will advance in virtue, without replacing their images with pictures of mountains and waters. May you directly surpass the patterns of recent ages and truly restore the spectacle of flourishing peace. Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, we, your servants, cannot contain our utmost joy, leaping and clapping our hands. We respectfully submit this memorial to convey our congratulations to Your Majesty.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第叄場
策
第一問
張合
同考試官訓導詹批帝王爲治之道聖
人傳心之要我
聖祖深體力行之功燕翼貽謀之訓悉明習而
揄揚之末寓諷諫有裨
聖政子豈賈董之儔歟
===
大廷之對拭目於子矣
考試官教諭周批
聖祖脩身制治之道實自洪範大學中來此篇
鋪張有體而文亦閎深不卜可知
爲佳士矣
考試官學正季批我
聖祖學問心思之奧立法貽謀之詳此策叙述
無遺豈亦有志於用世者乎
對觀百王傳道之大要則知
punctuated:
第叄場
策
第一問
張合

同考試官訓導詹批：帝王爲治之道，聖人傳心之要，我聖祖深體力行之功，燕翼貽謀之訓，悉明習而揄揚之。末寓諷諫，有裨聖政。子豈賈董之儔歟？大廷之對，拭目於子矣。

考試官教諭周批：聖祖脩身制治之道，實自《洪範》《大學》中來。此篇鋪張有體，而文亦閎深，不卜可知爲佳士矣。

考試官學正季批：我聖祖學問心思之奧，立法貽謀之詳，此策叙述無遺。豈亦有志於用世者乎？

對：觀百王傳道之大要，則知
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Zhang He

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Assistant Instructor: The way emperors and kings govern, the essentials of the sages’ transmission of the mind, our sagely progenitor’s achievements in deeply comprehending and vigorously practicing these principles, and his instructions for protecting his descendants and bequeathing plans to them—you have thoroughly understood and mastered all these, and have expounded and extolled them. The conclusion contains indirect remonstrance that can benefit the sage emperor’s government. Are you perhaps a peer of Jia Yi and Dong Zhongshu? I eagerly await your response at the Palace Examination.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Our sagely progenitor’s way of cultivating himself and establishing good government truly derived from the Great Plan and the Great Learning. This essay develops its subject with proper structure, and its writing is also expansive and profound. Without divination, one can tell that you are an outstanding scholar.

Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: The profundity of our sagely progenitor’s learning and thought, and the thoroughness with which he established laws and bequeathed plans to posterity—this policy essay recounts them without omission. Are you perhaps also someone who aspires to serve the world?

Response: By examining the great essentials of how the kings of successive ages transmitted the Way, one comes to understand…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖學之原觀
一代致治之弘規則知
聖心之用夫學之要原於理治之規本於法者
也是則言之所立雖不能以盡同而理之
所該則不能以獨異規之所制雖不能以
盡一而法之所統則不能以或偏知乎是
可以論斯道矣仰惟我
太祖高皇帝以
天縱之資加
===
日新之學當夫戎馬倥偬而講藝之罔休迨
夫
崇高已極而論道之不怠
思古聖之心則皇皇焉如有求而弗得
圖古聖之治則汲汲焉如有望而未見以帝
王為治之要道莫粹於洪範也則
親御宸翰而詳疏其旨以百聖傳心之要典莫
粹於大學也則揭之
殿廡而時復睇觀是何若是其勤勤也愚嘗
punctuated: 聖學之原，觀一代致治之弘規，則知聖心之用。夫學之要原於理，治之規本於法者也。是則言之所立，雖不能以盡同，而理之所該，則不能以獨異；規之所制，雖不能以盡一，而法之所統，則不能以或偏。知乎是，可以論斯道矣。仰惟我太祖高皇帝，以天縱之資，加日新之學。當夫戎馬倥偬，而講藝之罔休；迨夫崇高已極，而論道之不怠。思古聖之心，則皇皇焉如有求而弗得；圖古聖之治，則汲汲焉如有望而未見。以帝王為治之要道，莫粹於《洪範》也，則親御宸翰而詳疏其旨；以百聖傳心之要典，莫粹於《大學》也，則揭之殿廡而時復睇觀。是何若是其勤勤也？愚嘗
translation_en:
…the source of sagely learning; by contemplating the grand plans through which a dynasty achieves good government, one understands the workings of the sage’s mind. The essentials of learning originate in principle, while the plans of government are rooted in laws. Thus, although what is set forth in words cannot be entirely alike, the principles encompassed cannot be uniquely different; although the provisions of governmental plans cannot be entirely uniform, what the laws govern cannot be partial in any respect. Understanding this, one may discuss this Way.
I reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao combined Heaven-endowed gifts with learning renewed each day. Amid the press of military affairs, he never ceased discussing the classical arts; once he had attained the highest eminence, he remained tireless in discussing the Way. In pondering the minds of the ancient sages, he was restless, as though seeking something he could not obtain; in planning to realize their government, he was eager, as though awaiting something he had yet to see. Believing that no essential teaching on government for emperors and kings was more pure than the Great Plan (Hongfan), he personally took up the imperial brush and expounded its meaning in detail. Believing that no essential classic transmitting the minds of the sages was more pure than the Great Learning (Daxue), he had it displayed in the palace halls and galleries, and repeatedly looked upon it. Why was he so exceedingly diligent? I, in my humble understanding, have once …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
仰窺
聖心之所在矣請以洪範言之初一曰五行次
二曰敬用五事次三曰農用八政次四曰
協用五紀次五曰建用皇極次六曰乂用
三德次七曰明用稽疑次八曰念用庶徵
次九曰嚮用五福威用六極而天人之理
備矣故宋儒蔡沈曰人君治天下之法是
孰有加於此以大學言之一曰格物二曰
致知三曰誠意四曰正心五曰脩身六曰
===
齊家七曰治國八曰平天下而先後之序
悉矣故宋儒朱熹有曰大學如行程謂造
道者用力之途次也我
聖祖知其然潛心體乎此而有以會其要領篤
志察乎此而有以收其實效觀乎遺
東宮
親王有
訓
諭臣民有
punctuated:
仰窺聖心之所在矣。請以《洪範》言之：初一曰五行，次二曰敬用五事，次三曰農用八政，次四曰協用五紀，次五曰建用皇極，次六曰乂用三德，次七曰明用稽疑，次八曰念用庶徵，次九曰嚮用五福、威用六極，而天人之理備矣。故宋儒蔡沈曰：「人君治天下之法，是孰有加於此？」以《大學》言之：一曰格物，二曰致知，三曰誠意，四曰正心，五曰脩身，六曰齊家，七曰治國，八曰平天下，而先後之序悉矣。故宋儒朱熹有曰：「大學如行程。」謂造道者用力之途次也。
我聖祖知其然，潛心體乎此而有以會其要領，篤志察乎此而有以收其實效。觀乎遺東宮、親王有訓，諭臣民有
translation_en:
…reverently discerned where the sagely imperial mind was directed. Allow me to speak first of the Great Plan (Hongfan): first are the Five Phases; second, the reverent use of the five personal faculties; third, the diligent use of the eight affairs of government; fourth, the harmonizing use of the five measures of time; fifth, the establishment of the sovereign’s supreme standard; sixth, governing through the three virtues; seventh, the discerning use of methods for resolving doubts; eighth, attention to the various signs; and ninth, encouragement through the five blessings and deterrence through the six calamities. Thus the principles of Heaven and humanity are fully encompassed. Hence the Song scholar Cai Shen said: “As a method by which a ruler governs all under Heaven, what could surpass this?” To speak of the Great Learning (Daxue): first is investigating things; second, extending knowledge; third, making the intentions sincere; fourth, rectifying the mind; fifth, cultivating oneself; sixth, regulating the family; seventh, governing the state; and eighth, bringing peace to all under Heaven. Thus the sequence of what comes first and what follows is fully set out. Hence the Song scholar Zhu Xi said: “The Great Learning is like the stages of a journey.” He meant the successive stages at which those advancing toward the Way must exert themselves.
Our sagely imperial ancestor understood this. He devoted his mind to embodying these teachings and thereby grasped their essentials; he firmly resolved to examine them and thereby secured their practical results. Consider how, for the Crown Prince and the imperial princes, he left Instructions, and for admonishing his subjects there were…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
誥教民有
令齊民有
律而
大誥一序四民之業極其詳悉而於攸好德
考終命之義特致意焉其所以敘彝倫立
皇極而保萬民者皆本於天道而驗於人
事謂非有得於洪範之奧者乎觀乎因節
用愛人而取孔子之言以明白易知而賛
典謨之旨語善惡則有稂莠害苗之諭語
===
毁譽則辨賢不肖之真尊孟子仁義之說
而黜漢武帝之神仙稱李沆災異之奏而
抑宋真宗之侈大
諭侍臣則曰人民凋弊生息未遂也
諭郡縣則曰天下初定百姓困窮也亢旱爲
災則脩己以答
天甘露獻賀則因瑞而致戒毁鏤金之牀損食
肉之獸謂聲色爲伐性之斧謂技巧爲覆
車之轍
punctuated: 誥，教民有令，齊民有律。而《大誥》一序，四民之業極其詳悉，而於攸好德、考終命之義特致意焉。其所以敘彝倫、立皇極而保萬民者，皆本於天道而驗於人事，謂非有得於《洪範》之奧者乎？觀乎因節用愛人而取孔子之言，以明白易知而賛《典》《謨》之旨，語善惡則有稂莠害苗之諭，語毁譽則辨賢不肖之真。尊孟子仁義之說，而黜漢武帝之神仙；稱李沆災異之奏，而抑宋真宗之侈大。諭侍臣則曰：「人民凋弊，生息未遂也。」諭郡縣則曰：「天下初定，百姓困窮也。」亢旱爲災，則脩己以答天；甘露獻賀，則因瑞而致戒。毁鏤金之牀，損食肉之獸，謂聲色爲伐性之斧，謂技巧爲覆車之轍。
translation_en:
…proclamations; to instruct the people, there were ordinances; to bring the people into order, there were statutes. In the preface to the Great Pronouncements (Da Gao), the occupations of the four classes of people were treated in exhaustive detail, with particular attention to the meanings of “loving virtue” and “completing one’s allotted lifespan.” His means of ordering the constant human relationships, establishing the sovereign standard, and protecting the myriad people were all rooted in the Way of Heaven and tested against human affairs. Could one say that he had not grasped the profound meaning of the Great Plan (Hong Fan)?

Consider how he drew upon Confucius’s words concerning economy in expenditure and care for the people, and elucidated the purport of the Canons and Counsels in language clear and easy to understand. In speaking of good and evil, he offered the analogy of weeds harming grain seedlings; in speaking of blame and praise, he distinguished the true worth of the worthy and the unworthy. He revered Mencius’s teachings on benevolence and righteousness and rejected Emperor Wu of Han’s pursuit of immortals. He commended Li Hang’s memorials on disasters and anomalies and censured Emperor Zhenzong of Song’s extravagance and grandiosity.

When admonishing his attendant officials, he said: “The people are impoverished and exhausted; they have not yet been able to recover and thrive.” When admonishing the prefectures and counties, he said: “All under Heaven has only recently been pacified, and the common people are in distress and poverty.” When prolonged drought brought disaster, he cultivated himself in response to Heaven; when congratulations were presented on the appearance of sweet dew, he took the auspicious sign as an occasion for admonition. He destroyed a bed ornamented with carved gold and reduced the number of meat-eating beasts he kept. He called music and sensual pleasures an axe that cuts down one’s nature, and ingenious craftsmanship the wheel ruts of an overturned carriage.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
無優伶近狎之失無酣歌夜飲之歡
正宫無自縱之權妃嬪無寵恣之幸教
太子則欲其熟聞善言不邇詖行擇臺省都
督府之官以兼
東宫賛輔之職其所以明道術辨人才審治
體察民情崇敬畏戒逸欲嚴
内治定
國本皆由於身心而達於天下謂非有得於
大學之實者乎蓋嘗聞之文中子曰不學
===
書無以議制又嘗聞之西山真氏曰為人
君而不知大學無以清出治之原我
聖祖並用之以收創業之明效而一時輔業之
臣相與都俞咨度以
制定不刊之典為垂範無窮之謀誠以
聖學之源固深
聖心之用則妙上有以接三聖之道統下有以
開萬世之太平所以比隆於唐虞三代者
端在於是而所以示法於
punctuated: 無優伶近狎之失，無酣歌夜飲之歡。正宫無自縱之權，妃嬪無寵恣之幸。教太子，則欲其熟聞善言，不邇詖行；擇臺省都督府之官，以兼東宫賛輔之職。其所以明道術、辨人才、審治體、察民情、崇敬畏、戒逸欲、嚴内治、定國本，皆由於身心而達於天下，謂非有得於《大學》之實者乎？蓋嘗聞之，文中子曰：「不學《書》，無以議制。」又嘗聞之，西山真氏曰：「為人君而不知《大學》，無以清出治之原。」我聖祖並用之，以收創業之明效，而一時輔業之臣，相與都俞咨度，以制定不刊之典，為垂範無窮之謀。誠以聖學之源固深，聖心之用則妙，上有以接三聖之道統，下有以開萬世之太平。所以比隆於唐虞三代者，端在於是，而所以示法於
translation_en:
…He committed no fault of excessive familiarity with entertainers and indulged in no pleasures of drunken singing and nighttime drinking. The empress had no authority to act without restraint, and the consorts enjoyed no license to indulge themselves through imperial favor. In instructing the heir apparent, he wished him to hear good words often and keep away from wayward conduct. He selected officials from the central administrative and censorial offices and the Chief Military Commission to serve concurrently as advisers and assistants to the heir apparent. His efforts to elucidate the Way and its methods, distinguish men of talent, examine the essentials of government, understand the people's circumstances, cultivate reverence and awe, guard against indolence and desire, impose strict order within the palace, and secure the foundation of the state all proceeded from his own person and mind and extended to all under Heaven. Could one say that he had not grasped the substance of the Great Learning?

I have heard that Wenzhongzi said: “Without studying the Book of Documents, one cannot discuss institutions.” I have also heard that Master Zhen of Xishan said: “A ruler who does not understand the Great Learning has no means of purifying the source from which good government proceeds.” Our Sagely Progenitor applied both teachings to achieve conspicuous results in founding the dynasty. The ministers who assisted his enterprise at that time consulted and deliberated together in harmonious accord, establishing enduring statutes and planning to bequeath an example for all time. Truly, the wellspring of his sagely learning was deep, and the workings of his sagely mind were subtle. Looking back, he could carry forward the succession of the Way from the Three Sages; looking ahead, he could inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations. Precisely herein lay the reason his achievement equaled the splendor of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, and the means by which he provided a model for…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖子
神孫者亦無二道矣雖然人主之心斂之足以
妙衆理放之足以舉八埏但他岐之貳外
誘之私後宫盛色之溺讒邪利口之移養
之者無幾而攻之者甚衆夫以無幾之養
奪於甚衆之攻内之所操者無主故外之
作則者無法而欲其政之不紊者難矣是
以高宗之得傅說則望以格心之事成王
之詔羣臣亦期以示德之方卒之成中興
===
之功而光文武之業者良有以也後世願
治之君宜莫如漢之文帝唐之太宗矣蓋
文帝靳百金之費而巳一臺之作示敦朴
之先而簡帷帳之文太宗言及稼穡之艱
難則務遵節儉言及閭閻之疾苦則議息
征徭是故刑措之化貞觀之治三代以下
之所無也然能脩清淨之道而不能不狃
於晁錯之刑名能詢鬼神之理而不能不
惑於新垣平之詭詐能燭譽樹之姦而不
punctuated:
聖子神孫者，亦無二道矣。雖然，人主之心，斂之足以妙衆理，放之足以舉八埏。但他岐之貳、外誘之私、後宫盛色之溺、讒邪利口之移，養之者無幾，而攻之者甚衆。夫以無幾之養，奪於甚衆之攻，内之所操者無主，故外之作則者無法，而欲其政之不紊者難矣。是以高宗之得傅說，則望以格心之事；成王之詔羣臣，亦期以示德之方。卒之成中興之功，而光文武之業者，良有以也。
後世願治之君，宜莫如漢之文帝、唐之太宗矣。蓋文帝靳百金之費，而巳一臺之作；示敦朴之先，而簡帷帳之文。太宗言及稼穡之艱難，則務遵節儉；言及閭閻之疾苦，則議息征徭。是故刑措之化、貞觀之治，三代以下之所無也。然能脩清淨之道，而不能不狃於晁錯之刑名；能詢鬼神之理，而不能不惑於新垣平之詭詐；能燭譽樹之姦，而不
translation_en:
…for his sagely sons and divine grandsons, there was likewise no other way. Nevertheless, when the ruler’s mind is gathered inward, it can comprehend the subtleties of all principles; when extended outward, it can encompass the eight bounds of the world. Yet divergent paths divide it, external temptations turn it toward selfish ends, the alluring beauty of the rear palace immerses it in pleasure, and the glib tongues of slanderers and evildoers sway it. Few things nourish it, while very many assail it. When the nourishment provided by so few is overwhelmed by the assaults of so many, what the ruler holds within has no governing principle, and the example he sets outwardly has no proper standard. To expect his government to remain free of disorder is then difficult indeed. Thus, when Gaozong obtained Fu Yue, he looked to him to rectify his mind; when King Cheng issued instructions to his assembled ministers, he likewise expected them to show him the way of virtue. That they ultimately achieved a dynastic restoration and brought lustre to the accomplishments of Kings Wen and Wu had sound reasons.
Among later rulers who desired good government, surely none surpassed Emperor Wen of the Han and Taizong of the Tang. Emperor Wen begrudged the expense of a hundred units of gold and halted the construction of a terrace; he set an example of earnest simplicity by reducing the ornamentation of his curtains and hangings. When Taizong spoke of the hardships of sowing and reaping, he strove to practise frugality; when he spoke of the sufferings of ordinary households, he considered relieving levies and corvée labour. Thus, the civilizing rule under which punishments could be set aside, and the good government of the Zhenguan era, were unparalleled since the Three Dynasties. Yet although Emperor Wen could cultivate the Way of purity and tranquillity, he could not avoid becoming attached to Chao Cuo’s doctrines of punishments and administrative accountability; although he could inquire into the principles governing ghosts and spirits, he could not avoid being deceived by Xinyuan Ping’s fraud. Although Taizong could discern the treachery in flattery that praised a tree, he could not…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
能不牽於狐媚之愛能抑萬紀之規利而
不能謹於十漸之不終何者天性之仁雖
厚學問之力雖博而正心之實均未切耳
此我
祖訓持守之二言又爲百聖傳心之大要也敢
用爲
今日法
祖正心之獻謹對
第二問
李元陽
同考試官學正方批此策正欲觀士子
事君使民之心志而此篇援古證
今出入帝王之途轍豈布衣而有
天下之慮者乎行將見用執此以
往可也得士如此良慶良慶
考試官教諭周批條答之餘而忠愛
拳拳是可與論世道者
考試官學正季批才氣橫逸識見超
punctuated:
能不牽於狐媚之愛，能抑萬紀之規利，而不能謹於十漸之不終。何者？天性之仁雖厚，學問之力雖博，而正心之實均未切耳。此我祖訓持守之二言，又爲百聖傳心之大要也。敢用爲今日法祖正心之獻。謹對。
第二問
李元陽
同考試官學正方批：此策正欲觀士子事君使民之心志，而此篇援古證今，出入帝王之途轍，豈布衣而有天下之慮者乎？行將見用，執此以往可也。得士如此，良慶良慶！
考試官教諭周批：條答之餘，而忠愛拳拳，是可與論世道者。
考試官學正季批：才氣橫逸，識見超
translation_en:
…could not avoid being swayed by affection for foxlike flattery. He could restrain Wanji’s pursuit of profit, yet could not guard against the failure to persevere described in the “ten gradual failings.” Why was this? Although their innate benevolence was profound and their learning extensive, neither had truly applied himself to rectifying the mind. Thus the two words “maintain” and “preserve” in our ancestral instructions are also the essential principles of the transmission of the mind’s teaching through the hundred sages. I venture to offer this as a contribution toward Your Majesty’s emulating the ancestors and rectifying the mind today. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Policy Question
Li Yuanyang
Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: This policy question was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ intentions in serving their ruler and directing the people. This essay draws upon antiquity to substantiate its discussion of the present and ranges through the courses followed by emperors and kings. Is its author not a man who, though a commoner, concerns himself with all under Heaven? He will soon enter service; he may proceed holding fast to these principles. To obtain a scholar like this is truly cause for rejoicing, truly cause for rejoicing!
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Beyond answering the points in sequence, he displays earnest loyalty and devotion. Here is someone with whom one can discuss the condition of the world.
Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: His talent and spirit range freely; his understanding and insight surpass…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
軼塲中之士少有及之者佳士也
衆之前二塲允稱高薦
天下一氣也而伸縮由於心天下一體也
而動定由於心心也者君是也氣也者臣
是也體也者民是也心以使氣氣以使體
自然之勢也其心正則其氣順其體安此
亦自然之理也心蘊於中正耶邪耶人鮮
得而知也惟其發於言也則其邪正始可
得而見矣傳曰其心明乎正理則其言平
===
正通達此不易之定論也君之運天下也
亦然君正則其臣順而天下之民安且和
矣然人君高拱於穆清之上心之正與邪
焉天下未易測也聽其言也則其撫我虐
我也昭於人目盈於人耳矣孰謂詔令非
所以動天下之大幾也耶請因明問而復
之仰惟我
聖天子屬以倫序入繼
大統奉天即位改元一詔正往昔奸邪之誤
punctuated:
軼，塲中之士少有及之者，佳士也。衆之前二塲，允稱高薦。

天下一氣也，而伸縮由於心；天下一體也，而動定由於心。心也者，君是也；氣也者，臣是也；體也者，民是也。心以使氣，氣以使體，自然之勢也。其心正，則其氣順，其體安，此亦自然之理也。心蘊於中，正耶？邪耶？人鮮得而知也。惟其發於言也，則其邪正始可得而見矣。傳曰：「其心明乎正理，則其言平正通達。」此不易之定論也。君之運天下也亦然。君正，則其臣順，而天下之民安且和矣。然人君高拱於穆清之上，心之正與邪焉，天下未易測也。聽其言也，則其撫我、虐我也，昭於人目，盈於人耳矣。孰謂詔令非所以動天下之大幾也耶？請因明問而復之。仰惟我聖天子，屬以倫序，入繼大統，奉天即位，改元一詔，正往昔奸邪之誤
translation_en:
…surpassing others in discernment; few candidates in the examination can match him. He is an excellent scholar. His work in the preceding two sessions [?] fully merits a high recommendation.

All under Heaven is a single vital force, whose expansion and contraction depend upon the heart; all under Heaven is a single body, whose movement and stillness depend upon the heart. The heart is the ruler; the vital force is his ministers; the body is the people. The heart directs the vital force, and the vital force directs the body: this is the natural course of things. When the heart is upright, the vital force flows harmoniously and the body is at ease. This too is a natural principle. The heart lies concealed within: is it upright or depraved? Few can know. Only when it finds expression in words does its depravity or uprightness become discernible. The Commentary says: “When his heart clearly understands correct principle, his words are balanced, upright, coherent, and lucid.” This is an unalterable judgment. The ruler’s governance of all under Heaven works in the same way. When the ruler is upright, his ministers are obedient, and the people throughout the realm are secure and harmonious. Yet the ruler sits aloft with hands folded in the solemn purity of his palace; whether his heart is upright or depraved is not easily fathomed by those below. When they hear his words, however, whether he cherishes or oppresses them becomes clear to their eyes and fills their ears. Who could say that imperial edicts are not the great pivot by which all under Heaven is moved? Allow me to reply in accordance with your illuminating question.

I reverently consider how our sagely Son of Heaven, by his place in the order of imperial kinship, entered upon succession to the great imperial line. In obedience to Heaven, he ascended the throne and inaugurated a new reign era. A single edict corrected the misguidance wrought in former times by wicked and perverse men …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
主申
祖宗舊章以告民其於諫止
遊巡之臣而被廢者則復其生者之官而加
之顯恤其没者之後而加之贈此非成湯
顯忠遂良之德意也乎其於應濟征伐之
類而被擾者則蠲其往者之逋而不之追
寬其來者之稅而免之半此非武王散財
發粟之遺意也乎民年八十九十者賜予
有差使民知曰
===
朝廷之待老如此我何以不孝且敬乎官年
賜休乞休者存問有禮使民知曰
朝廷之優賢如此我何以不脩爾德乎將由
是而興起於孝將由是而勸勉於德而三
代之俗可跂而待也五帝之化可望而及
也邦其永昌不在于茲乎民生得其所則
元氣固矣傳曰民惟邦本本固邦寧此聖
王之訓也恐奉行者之未至則使風憲官
糾察之孰敢有廢閣者乎慮涖事者之或
punctuated: 主，申祖宗舊章以告民。其於諫止遊巡之臣而被廢者，則復其生者之官而加之顯，恤其没者之後而加之贈。此非成湯顯忠遂良之德意也乎？其於應濟征伐之類而被擾者，則蠲其往者之逋而不之追，寬其來者之稅而免之半。此非武王散財發粟之遺意也乎？民年八十九十者，賜予有差，使民知曰：「朝廷之待老如此，我何以不孝且敬乎？」官年賜休乞休者，存問有禮，使民知曰：「朝廷之優賢如此，我何以不脩爾德乎？」將由是而興起於孝，將由是而勸勉於德，而三代之俗可跂而待也，五帝之化可望而及也。邦其永昌，不在于茲乎？民生得其所，則元氣固矣。傳曰：「民惟邦本，本固邦寧。」此聖王之訓也。恐奉行者之未至，則使風憲官糾察之，孰敢有廢閣者乎？慮涖事者之或
translation_en:
…the ruler, and reaffirmed the ancestors’ established statutes in a proclamation to the people. As for officials dismissed for remonstrating against imperial pleasure tours, those still living were restored to office and granted further distinction; the descendants of those who had died received compassionate care, and the deceased were granted posthumous honors. Is this not the benevolent intent of Cheng Tang in honoring the loyal and advancing the worthy? As for those harassed by demands to supply military campaigns and similar undertakings, their past arrears were remitted without further collection, and their future taxes were reduced by half. Does this not preserve the intent of King Wu in distributing wealth and opening the grain stores?

People aged eighty or ninety received gifts in differing amounts, so that the people would recognize: “The court treats the elderly in this way; how could I fail to be filial and respectful?” Officials granted retirement on account of age [?], or who had requested retirement, received solicitous inquiries with due ceremony, so that the people would recognize: “The court favors the worthy in this way; how could I fail to ‘cultivate your virtue’ [?]?” Through this they would be stirred to filial devotion and encouraged in virtue. The customs of the Three Dynasties could then be eagerly awaited, and the transforming influence of the Five Emperors could be hoped for and attained. Does not the enduring prosperity of the state depend upon this? When the people’s livelihoods are properly secured, the state’s vital energy is firmly established. The transmitted text says: “The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace.” This is the teaching of the sage kings.

Fearing that those charged with carrying out these measures might fall short, he ordered the censors to investigate them. Who would dare leave the measures unimplemented? Concerned that those administering affairs might…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
怠則使分道官考驗之孰敢有不振舉者
乎即是而之焉主之以誠心加之以持久
二帝三王之治可復見也雖典謨之相得
而相告者即此心也商之誓則淺於前日
君民之心矣周之末則詛且盟而怨焉於
是刑之革之矣革且不從而上下之心背
馳矣秦漢而下日趨於非不足論矣是固
時使之然亦敎化不明之過也君有作臣
有守則世有敎化矣有敎化自不患乎世
===
無善治也是故敎化者治之本也君臣者
敎化之本也故曰爲政在人取人以身孔
子之治天下如斯而已矣昔者漢高曰聞
王者莫高於周文覇者莫高於齊桓皆得
賢人而成名賢士大夫有肯從我游者吾
能尊顯之夫是詔也乃諳練閱歷之言不
有是心漢幾何而能成乎天下之士始欣
欣然有詩書禮樂之願而漢之命脉生矣
漢武曰朕即位以來所爲狂悖使天下愁
punctuated:
怠，則使分道官考驗之，孰敢有不振舉者乎？即是而之焉，主之以誠心，加之以持久，二帝三王之治可復見也。雖典謨之相得而相告者，即此心也。商之誓，則淺於前日君民之心矣；周之末，則詛且盟而怨焉，於是刑之、革之矣。革且不從，而上下之心背馳矣。秦漢而下，日趨於非，不足論矣。是固時使之然，亦敎化不明之過也。君有作，臣有守，則世有敎化矣。有敎化，自不患乎世無善治也。是故敎化者，治之本也；君臣者，敎化之本也。故曰：「爲政在人，取人以身。」孔子之治天下，如斯而已矣。
昔者漢高曰：「聞王者莫高於周文，覇者莫高於齊桓，皆得賢人而成名。賢士大夫有肯從我游者，吾能尊顯之。」夫是詔也，乃諳練閱歷之言。不有是心，漢幾何而能成乎？天下之士始欣欣然有詩書禮樂之願，而漢之命脉生矣。漢武曰：「朕即位以來，所爲狂悖，使天下愁
translation_en:
…be remiss, then have the circuit officials examine their performance: who would dare fail to carry out their duties vigorously? Proceed along these lines, taking sincerity as the guiding principle and sustaining the effort, and the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings can be seen again. Even the mutual understanding and counsel recorded in the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents arose from this same disposition. In the Oaths of Shang, however, the bond between ruler and people was already shallower than before. By the end of Zhou, there were curses and covenant oaths, yet resentment persisted; consequently, punishments and measures of reform were applied. Even with reform, people would not obey, and the hearts of those above and below turned in opposite directions. From Qin and Han onward, affairs tended daily toward error and scarcely merit discussion. This was certainly brought about by the times, but it was also the fault of a failure to make moral instruction clear. If the ruler takes the initiative and his ministers uphold it, there will be moral instruction in the world. With moral instruction, there is naturally no need to fear that the world will lack good government. Thus moral instruction is the foundation of government, and ruler and ministers are the foundation of moral instruction. Hence the saying: “The conduct of government depends on men; obtaining such men depends on one's own person.” Confucius's way of governing the world amounted to this alone.
Formerly, Gaozu of Han said: “I have heard that among true kings none surpassed King Wen of Zhou, and among hegemons none surpassed Duke Huan of Qi. Both gained worthy men and thereby achieved renown. If there are worthy scholars and officials willing to associate with me, I can honor them and raise them to prominence.” This edict spoke from practiced understanding and experience. Without such a disposition, what chance would Han have had of establishing itself? Only then did the scholars of the realm joyfully begin to aspire to the Poetry and Documents, rites and music, and the vital pulse of Han came into being. Emperor Wu of Han said: “Since I ascended the throne, my actions have been reckless and perverse, causing the whole realm sorrow…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
苦不可追悔今事有傷害百姓糜費天下
者悉罷之夫是詔也乃悔悟深切之言不
有是言漢幾於不可知也天下之民始帖
帖然無背叛反復之想而漢之肌膚固矣
夫往者鑒式於今者也來者取法於今者
也商書曰事不師古匪說攸聞使傅說而
愚人焉則亦已矣如曰天賚中興之賢佐
則其言固可信矣周書亦曰慎厥麗乃勸
厥民使成湯而庸君焉則亦已矣如曰天
===
錫一代之聖主則其言固可信矣愚也樂
育
明時躬逢
聖主尚當以緝熈
聖敬終始典于學為
獻則德可久業可大而愚芹曝之誠舎此無
敢言者也庶可免隨何遇漢文而不能興
文之誚雖然上有明君則下有良臣臣之
能為臣又在其君致之也玆惟時哉謹對
punctuated:
苦，不可追悔。今事有傷害百姓、糜費天下者，悉罷之。」夫是詔也，乃悔悟深切之言。不有是言，漢幾於不可知也。天下之民始帖帖然，無背叛反復之想，而漢之肌膚固矣。
夫往者鑒式於今者也，來者取法於今者也。《商書》曰：「事不師古，匪說攸聞。」使傅說而愚人焉，則亦已矣；如曰天賚中興之賢佐，則其言固可信矣。《周書》亦曰：「慎厥麗，乃勸厥民。」使成湯而庸君焉，則亦已矣；如曰天錫一代之聖主，則其言固可信矣。
愚也樂育明時，躬逢聖主，尚當以緝熈聖敬、終始典于學為獻，則德可久，業可大，而愚芹曝之誠，舎此無敢言者也。庶可免隨何遇漢文而不能興文之誚。雖然，上有明君，則下有良臣；臣之能為臣，又在其君致之也。玆惟時哉！謹對。
translation_en:
…anguish; regret cannot undo what has happened. Henceforth, abolish every undertaking that harms the common people or squanders the resources of the realm.” This edict expressed profound remorse and awakening. Without these words, the fate of the Han would have been almost beyond knowing. Only then did the people of the realm settle into contentment, abandoning thoughts of rebellion or wavering allegiance, and the flesh and skin of the Han state became secure.
The past provides a mirror and a standard for the present; the future takes its models from the present. The Documents of Shang says: “To conduct affairs without taking antiquity as one's teacher is something I, Yue, have never heard of.” If Fu Yue had been a foolish man, we could leave it at that. But if he was a worthy helper bestowed by Heaven to restore the dynasty, then his words surely deserve belief. The Documents of Zhou also says: “Be careful about those to whom you attach yourself; thereby encourage your people.” If Cheng Tang had been a mediocre ruler, we could leave it at that. But if he was a sage sovereign bestowed by Heaven upon a dynasty, then these words surely deserve belief.
I, ignorant as I am, have been nurtured with care in this enlightened age and have personally encountered a sage sovereign. I should therefore offer this counsel: continually brighten your sagely reverence, and from beginning to end make learning your constant rule. Then your virtue can endure and your achievements become great. In my humble sincerity—like one offering celery or the warmth of the sun—I dare propose nothing beyond this. Perhaps I may thus escape the reproach directed at Sui He for encountering Emperor Wen of Han yet failing to promote cultured governance [?]. Nevertheless, when there is an enlightened ruler above, there are worthy ministers below. A minister's ability to fulfill his role also depends upon his ruler bringing it forth. Now indeed is the time! Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第三問
趙汝濂
同考試官訓導鄭批前輩業儒者兼律
令習之故學爲有用是篇考究詳
明斷制精當推之於政而可行本
之於經而有據非平日諳練世故
决不至此子其有志於致
君堯舜者乎
考試官教諭周批策貴警拔彬蔚如
===
前輩對策何嘗拘拘對偶而文自
可觀此作其庶幾矣
考試官學正季批全篇雖不爲劗刻
斬絶之言而其鋒自不可犯亦可
謂筆底秋霜者
刑以弼教聖人不得已用之也然有法焉
有情焉法固在所當執情亦不可不原雖
有畫一之法每有不一之情情原故誤之
分法歸輕重之等如是或决遣之或收贖
punctuated:
第三問
趙汝濂
同考試官訓導鄭批：前輩業儒者，兼律令習之，故學爲有用。是篇考究詳明，斷制精當，推之於政而可行，本之於經而有據。非平日諳練世故，决不至此。子其有志於致君堯舜者乎？
考試官教諭周批：策貴警拔彬蔚。如前輩對策，何嘗拘拘對偶，而文自可觀。此作其庶幾矣。
考試官學正季批：全篇雖不爲劗刻斬絶之言，而其鋒自不可犯，亦可謂筆底秋霜者。
刑以弼教，聖人不得已用之也。然有法焉，有情焉。法固在所當執，情亦不可不原。雖有畫一之法，每有不一之情。情原故誤之分，法歸輕重之等。如是，或决遣之，或收贖
translation_en:
Third Policy Question
Zhao Rulian

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: Earlier generations of Confucian scholars also studied the statutes and ordinances; thus their learning had practical use. This essay is detailed and lucid in its investigations, precise and appropriate in its judgments. Applied to government, its proposals are practicable; grounded in the classics, they have authoritative support. Without habitual familiarity with worldly affairs, one could certainly not attain this level. Might you aspire to make your ruler the equal of Yao and Shun?

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: A policy essay is valued for striking insight, distinction, refinement, and richness. When earlier scholars answered policy questions, when did they ever fuss over parallel phrasing? Yet their writing was naturally worthy of admiration. This composition comes close to theirs.

Comment by Examiner Ji, School Instructor: Although the essay as a whole avoids minutely chiseled and abruptly cutting language [?], its edge cannot be challenged. One may indeed say that autumn frost lies beneath the writer’s brush.

Punishments serve to support moral instruction; the sages employ them only when compelled by necessity. Yet there is the law, and there are the circumstances of the case. The law must certainly be upheld, but the circumstances must also be examined. Although the law is uniform, circumstances frequently differ. In examining the circumstances, distinguish deliberate wrongdoing from inadvertent error; in applying the law, assign the appropriate degree of severity or leniency. In this way, some offenders are sentenced and dealt with, while others are permitted to redeem their punishments by payment…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之而先王天討之公欽恤之仁兩全而無
害矣嗚呼天地之大德曰生矣然春生秋
殺旣潤之以風雨復鼓之以雷霆何甞專
於生也聖人效法於是乎制刑焉然刑期
無刑辟以止辟而生意亦未甞不存乎其
間也夫刑有五而干犯在所弗宥法之正
也其見之虞典有曰金作贖刑者蔡氏以
爲刑莫輕於鞭扑蓋官府學校之所用耳
於是許贖所以養其愧耻之心也若吕刑
===
贖法蓋五刑之中疑其可赦者不遽赦之
姑取其鍰以示罰耳繼曰閱實其罪則無
可疑者惡能逃乎自是贖罰之途旣開遷
就之謀紛起漢宣帝因討西羌兵食告乏
張敞議令諸州非殺人及盗者皆入穀贖
罪以若所爲免轉輸之勞實邊徼之備亦
何不可而蕭望之以爲如此則富者得生
貧者獨死恐開利路以傷治化是固老臣
經世之慮而事體輕重之間權之熟矣宋
punctuated: 之，而先王天討之公、欽恤之仁，兩全而無害矣。嗚呼！天地之大德曰生矣，然春生秋殺，旣潤之以風雨，復鼓之以雷霆，何甞專於生也？聖人效法於是乎制刑焉，然刑期無刑，辟以止辟，而生意亦未甞不存乎其間也。夫刑有五，而干犯在所弗宥，法之正也。其見之虞典，有曰「金作贖刑」者，蔡氏以爲刑莫輕於鞭扑，蓋官府學校之所用耳。於是許贖，所以養其愧耻之心也。若《吕刑》贖法，蓋五刑之中疑其可赦者，不遽赦之，姑取其鍰以示罰耳。繼曰「閱實其罪」，則無可疑者惡能逃乎？自是贖罰之途旣開，遷就之謀紛起。漢宣帝因討西羌，兵食告乏，張敞議令諸州非殺人及盗者，皆入穀贖罪。以若所爲，免轉輸之勞，實邊徼之備，亦何不可？而蕭望之以爲如此則富者得生，貧者獨死，恐開利路以傷治化。是固老臣經世之慮，而事體輕重之間，權之熟矣。宋
translation_en:
…redeem their punishment, thereby fully preserving both the former kings’ impartiality in executing Heaven’s chastisement and their humane concern and caution in punishment, without detriment to either. Ah! The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life-giving. Yet spring brings life and autumn brings death; having moistened things with wind and rain, they also stir them with thunder. When have they ever been concerned exclusively with giving life? The sages took this as their model in establishing punishments. Yet punishment aims at eliminating punishment, and penalties serve to stop offenses; the life-giving intention has never been absent from them.

There are five punishments, and those who transgress are not to be pardoned: this is the proper rule of law. As for the statement in the Canon of Yu, “Metal payments shall serve to redeem punishments,” Master Cai held that no punishments were lighter than whipping and beating, which were used in government offices and schools. Allowing redemption in these cases served to nurture the offenders’ sense of shame. As for the redemption provisions in the Punishments of Lü, these concerned cases among the five punishments in which there was doubt as to whether pardon was appropriate. Rather than immediately pardoning the offenders, the authorities provisionally exacted a payment in huan, a unit of metal weight, to signify punishment. The text continues, “Examine and establish the facts of their crimes.” How, then, could those whose guilt admitted of no doubt escape?

Once this avenue of redeeming punishment was opened, schemes for accommodating offenders arose in profusion. When Emperor Xuan of the Han campaigned against the Western Qiang, provisions for the troops ran short. Zhang Chang proposed that throughout the provinces, offenders other than murderers and thieves should all be permitted to redeem their offenses by delivering grain. If this relieved the labor of transporting supplies and replenished the stores for frontier defense, what would be objectionable about it? Xiao Wangzhi, however, held that under such an arrangement the rich would live while the poor alone would die. He feared that opening an avenue for profit would harm good government and moral transformation. This was indeed a veteran minister’s concern for governing the realm; he had carefully weighed the relative importance of the considerations involved. In the Song…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
仁宗以先王用法簡約後世刑用滋章令
天下或有冒刑犯禁過誤可憫者以穀麥
錢帛贖焉此詔一下或以為寬慈之仁稀
濶之典可以常行而識者以為富人皆得
贖罪貧者曷能自免豈朝廷用法之意哉
是固大臣體國之忠而舉措得失之辨籌
之審矣夫張敞建議不及賊盜殺人仁宗
詔令止言犯禁過誤而當時臣屬尚以為
非則贖罰一節果無益於世教明矣我
===
太祖高皇帝裁定律令實上稽天理中順時宜
下合人心立萬世之準繩為百王之憲度
者至於贖法雖沿唐舊而就中斟酌事情
權衡輕重實脗合堯舜慎獄好生之意自
制律以來所未有者伏睹
聖祖諭刑部有曰自今十惡非常赦所原者則
云重刑其餘雜犯許聽收贖至
太宗文皇帝又令死罪情重者依律處治情輕
及公罪皆得收贖仰惟
punctuated:
仁宗以先王用法簡約，後世刑用滋章，令天下或有冒刑犯禁、過誤可憫者，以穀麥錢帛贖焉。此詔一下，或以為寬慈之仁、稀濶之典，可以常行，而識者以為富人皆得贖罪，貧者曷能自免？豈朝廷用法之意哉？是固大臣體國之忠，而舉措得失之辨，籌之審矣。夫張敞建議不及賊盜殺人，仁宗詔令止言犯禁過誤，而當時臣屬尚以為非，則贖罰一節果無益於世教明矣。
我太祖高皇帝裁定律令，實上稽天理，中順時宜，下合人心，立萬世之準繩，為百王之憲度者。至於贖法，雖沿唐舊，而就中斟酌事情，權衡輕重，實脗合堯舜慎獄好生之意，自制律以來所未有者。伏睹聖祖諭刑部有曰：「自今十惡非常赦所原者，則云重刑，其餘雜犯，許聽收贖。」至太宗文皇帝，又令死罪情重者依律處治，情輕及公罪皆得收贖。仰惟
translation_en:
…Emperor Renzong, considering that the former kings had applied the law simply and sparingly, whereas later ages had made penal provisions increasingly elaborate, ordered that anyone in the realm who had transgressed the penal laws or violated prohibitions through pitiable error should be allowed to redeem the punishment with grain, wheat, money, or silk. Once this edict was issued, some regarded it as an act of generous compassion and a provision of broad leniency that could be applied permanently. Discerning men, however, held that while the wealthy could all redeem their offenses, how could the poor secure their own release? Could this be the court’s intention in applying the law? This indeed expressed the loyalty of great ministers concerned for the state; they had carefully weighed the merits and faults of such measures. Zhang Chang’s proposal did not extend to robbery, theft, or homicide, and Renzong’s edict spoke only of violations of prohibitions and inadvertent offenses. Yet even then their ministers considered these measures wrong. It is thus clear that redemption of punishment is indeed of no benefit to the moral instruction of the age.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao established the statutes and ordinances by looking upward to heavenly principle, accommodating the needs of the times, and conforming below to the hearts of the people. He established a standard for myriad generations and a model for all succeeding sovereigns. As for redemption, although he followed Tang precedents, he deliberated upon the circumstances of cases and weighed their relative gravity. This accorded fully with Yao and Shun’s concern for caution in adjudication and preservation of life, to a degree unprecedented since the first establishment of penal statutes. I have reverently read the Sacred Founder’s instruction to the Ministry of Justice, which says: “Henceforth, the Ten Abominations, which are not pardoned under ordinary amnesties, shall be termed grave punishments [?]; for other miscellaneous offenses, redemption shall be permitted.” Subsequently, Emperor Taizong Wen also ordered that capital offenses involving grave circumstances be punished according to the statutes, while those involving mitigating circumstances, as well as offenses committed in an official capacity, could all be redeemed. Reverently considering…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
祖宗立法之意止以贖罪待情輕者而重罪未
嘗寬貸奈何在外所司罔思體悉但知儲
蓄不審罪情積財多者爲良吏減罪衆者
爲陰德嗚呼
朝廷何少此毫芒錢穀而翻致干犯愈衆法
梲不行哉先王之制刑與
祖宗之律令果如是乎否也愚聞之書曰天討
有罪又曰天齊于民蓋用刑之權出於天
人君與有司特奉行之耳旣知天法又可
===
任情以高下於其間乎夫有罪不刑雖堯
舜不能以化天下以漢高帝約法三章猶
曰殺人者死若不論情之輕重雖賊盜殺
人以至於罪惡滔天者一槩移情就法以
利贖之則刑不出於天而秪爲姦邪市恩
之具罪不據乎律而翻爲豪强解脫之資
决遣皆貧窮而富饒獲免配沒皆寒苦而
雄黠得安古之狃于姦宄敗常亂俗三細
不宥者後世皆夤緣請託而曲從輕典矣
punctuated:
祖宗立法之意，止以贖罪待情輕者，而重罪未嘗寬貸。奈何在外所司罔思體悉，但知儲蓄，不審罪情，積財多者爲良吏，減罪衆者爲陰德。嗚呼！朝廷何少此毫芒錢穀，而翻致干犯愈衆，法梲不行哉？先王之制刑與祖宗之律令，果如是乎？否也。
愚聞之，《書》曰：「天討有罪。」又曰：「天齊于民。」蓋用刑之權出於天，人君與有司特奉行之耳。旣知天法，又可任情以高下於其間乎？夫有罪不刑，雖堯舜不能以化天下。以漢高帝約法三章，猶曰：「殺人者死。」若不論情之輕重，雖賊盜殺人，以至於罪惡滔天者，一槩移情就法，以利贖之，則刑不出於天，而秪爲姦邪市恩之具；罪不據乎律，而翻爲豪强解脫之資。决遣皆貧窮，而富饒獲免；配沒皆寒苦，而雄黠得安。古之狃于姦宄、敗常亂俗，三細不宥者，後世皆夤緣請託，而曲從輕典矣。
translation_en:
…the intention of the imperial ancestors in establishing the law was to allow redemption of punishment only for those whose offenses involved mitigating circumstances; serious crimes were never treated leniently. How is it that the responsible officials outside the capital give no thought to understanding this intention, knowing only how to accumulate funds and failing to examine the circumstances of offenses? Those who accumulate much wealth are considered good officials, and reducing punishments for many is regarded as hidden moral merit. Alas! How could the court be so short of this paltry amount of money and grain that it instead allows offenses to multiply and the law to go unenforced [?]? Were the punishments instituted by the former kings and the statutes and ordinances of the imperial ancestors really like this? No.
I have heard these words from the Book of Documents: “Heaven punishes the guilty.” It also says: “Heaven brings order to the people.” The authority to impose punishment comes from Heaven; the ruler and the responsible officials merely carry it out.
