Once they recognize Heaven’s law, can they arbitrarily make punishments heavier or lighter? If the guilty are not punished, even Yao and Shun could not transform the world through moral instruction. Even Emperor Gao of Han, who reduced the laws to three articles, still declared: “Those who kill shall die.” If, without considering the gravity of the circumstances, officials indiscriminately reshape the circumstances to fit the law and permit monetary redemption—even for robbers and murderers, and those whose crimes reach to Heaven—then punishment no longer proceeds from Heaven, but becomes merely a means of winning favor for the wicked. The determination of guilt no longer rests on the statutes, but instead becomes a resource through which the powerful obtain release. Those sentenced and dispatched are all poor, while the wealthy escape; those subjected to penal assignment and confiscation are all destitute, while the powerful and cunning remain secure. In antiquity, those habituated to wrongdoing, those who subverted established norms, and those who corrupted customs were not pardoned even for minor offenses in these three categories. In later ages, all such people exploit connections and solicit favors, and the more lenient provisions are perversely applied to them.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
良可慨夫况又所贖之金不資軍國之用
或充貪墨之囊考之周禮貨罰入於司兵
蓋以為治兵之工直也今則皆如是否乎
憲法以止姦刑以繩慝使有罪者皆得以
利免則人皆曰吾金多矣何畏乎官司吾
謀巧矣何憂乎斧鉞汲汲焉惟利之務盈
元姦鉅蠹何憚而不為惡乎此所以犯者
接踵人心弗平而甚失先王明刑弼教之
意也昔人謂何以孝弟為財多而光榮蓋
===
亦有感於是矣然贖法亦律之不廢者若
不失先王制刑之意上體
祖宗欽恤之仁必如何而可也盍考諸書乎舜
典曰宥過無大刑故無小呂刑曰上刑適
輕下服下刑適重上服使法輕而情可惡
矣必寘於罪以為豪横之戒有力不必論
也法重而情可憫矣或令收贖以開自新
之路正典自不廢也如此則咸知有意干
彝者莫能逃利刃無心觸法者亦得以改
punctuated:
良可慨夫！况又所贖之金不資軍國之用，或充貪墨之囊。考之《周禮》，貨罰入於司兵，蓋以為治兵之工直也。今則皆如是否乎？憲法以止姦，刑以繩慝，使有罪者皆得以利免，則人皆曰：「吾金多矣，何畏乎官司？吾謀巧矣，何憂乎斧鉞？」汲汲焉，惟利之務，盈元姦鉅蠹，何憚而不為惡乎？此所以犯者接踵，人心弗平，而甚失先王明刑弼教之意也。昔人謂：「何以孝弟為？財多而光榮。」蓋亦有感於是矣。

然贖法亦律之不廢者，若不失先王制刑之意，上體祖宗欽恤之仁，必如何而可也？盍考諸書乎？《舜典》曰：「宥過無大，刑故無小。」《呂刑》曰：「上刑適輕，下服；下刑適重，上服。」使法輕而情可惡矣，必寘於罪，以為豪横之戒，有力不必論也。法重而情可憫矣，或令收贖，以開自新之路，正典自不廢也。如此，則咸知有意干彝者莫能逃利刃，無心觸法者亦得以改
translation_en:
Truly lamentable! Moreover, the money paid in redemption of punishment does not support military and state expenditure, but may instead fill the purses of corrupt officials. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that monetary penalties were paid to the Director of Weapons, presumably to cover the wages of those who made weapons. Is this how all such funds are used today? Statutes serve to restrain wrongdoing, and punishments to curb wickedness. If all the guilty can purchase exemption, everyone will say: “I have plenty of money—why fear the authorities? My schemes are clever—why worry about the executioner’s axes?” They will pursue profit with relentless urgency; great villains and scourges [?] will have what restraint to keep them from doing evil? This is why offenders follow one another in succession and people feel aggrieved. It gravely betrays the former kings’ intention that clearly established punishments should support moral instruction. Someone in the past said: “What use are filial piety and fraternal respect? Abundant wealth brings glory.” This, too, surely arose from a sense of such abuses.

Yet redemption of punishment is also a provision that the penal code has retained. What, then, must be done to preserve the former kings’ intention in establishing punishments and to embody the imperial ancestors’ benevolence in treating penal matters with reverence and compassion? Why not examine the Documents? The Canon of Shun says: “Pardon inadvertent offenses, however great; punish deliberate offenses, however small.” The Punishments of Lü says: “When an offense carrying a heavier punishment warrants leniency, impose the lighter; when an offense carrying a lighter punishment warrants severity, impose the heavier.” If the statutory penalty is light but the circumstances are abhorrent, the offender must be punished as a warning to the powerful and overbearing; his means need not enter into consideration. If the statutory penalty is heavy but the circumstances merit compassion, redemption may be permitted to open a path to self-renewal. The established law will thereby remain intact. In this way, everyone will know that those who deliberately violate constant norms cannot escape the sharp blade, while those who unwittingly transgress the law may also be allowed to reform…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
絃貧富同刑强弱胥懼人情悉體大法固
存必如此而後謂之明刑必如此而不失
祖宗御世防姦之意抑究而言之又在乎所司
之公明剛正也惟公則輕重適平而自不
偏於私惟明則隱微洞照而自不流於枉
剛則不徇時而徇理之中正則不惟情而
惟法之執否則剖斷未真操持未定縱出
有罪虐入無辜傷天地之和玩經常之典
關係國家誠非細故此書所以簡重司政
===
典獄而惓惓於非佞惟良之訓也嗚呼人
君用人可不慎與愚生章句迂疎罔知刑
律敢掇拾平日所聞以爲明問復諒執事
亦原其未學而不深罪之也
第四問
呂鳯池
考試官教諭周批歷數古人之學如
對面談而商確焉者且歸宿于責
志深得聖賢心事豈亦用心于內
punctuated:
絃，貧富同刑，强弱胥懼，人情悉體，大法固存。必如此而後謂之明刑，必如此而不失祖宗御世防姦之意。抑究而言之，又在乎所司之公明剛正也。惟公則輕重適平，而自不偏於私；惟明則隱微洞照，而自不流於枉；剛則不徇時，而徇理之中；正則不惟情，而惟法之執。否則剖斷未真，操持未定，縱出有罪，虐入無辜，傷天地之和，玩經常之典，關係國家，誠非細故。此《書》所以簡重司政典獄，而惓惓於非佞惟良之訓也。嗚呼！人君用人，可不慎與？愚生章句迂疎，罔知刑律，敢掇拾平日所聞，以爲明問復。諒執事亦原其未學，而不深罪之也。

第四問
呂鳯池

考試官教諭周批：「歷數古人之學，如對面談而商確焉者，且歸宿于責志，深得聖賢心事，豈亦用心于內
translation_en:
…reform their ways. Rich and poor will be subject to the same punishments, and strong and weak alike will stand in fear. Full account will be taken of human circumstances, while the fundamental laws remain firmly intact. Only then can this be called clarity in punishment; only thus can the intent of the imperial ancestors in governing the realm and preventing wrongdoing be preserved. Yet, to investigate the matter further, it also depends upon the impartiality, discernment, firmness, and uprightness of the responsible officials. Only impartiality ensures that the severity of punishment is properly balanced, without bias arising from private interests. Only discernment penetrates hidden details, without lapsing into injustice. Firmness means following what is right in principle rather than yielding to the times; uprightness means holding to the law rather than being guided by personal feelings. Otherwise, judgments will lack accuracy and officials will lack constancy: they will release the guilty through indulgence and condemn the innocent through cruelty, injuring the harmony of Heaven and Earth and treating the enduring statutes lightly. This concerns the state and is certainly no trifling matter. This is why the Book of Documents stresses careful selection of those who administer government and oversee judicial proceedings, and earnestly repeats the injunction to choose good men, not glib speakers. Alas! Can a ruler afford to be careless in employing men? I, an ignorant student, am an impractical and ill-informed student of textual passages and phrases, with no understanding of penal law. I venture to gather what I have heard in the course of ordinary study as a reply to your discerning question. I trust that you, sir, will also pardon my lack of learning and not condemn me too severely.

Fourth Question
Lü Fengchi

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “He recounts the learning of the ancients one by one, as though conversing with them face to face and weighing their ideas together. Moreover, he brings the discussion back to exacting demands upon one's resolve [?], deeply grasping the inner concerns of the sages and worthies. Might he too have applied himself inwardly…”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而有得者乎
考試官學正季　批開闔抑揚若王良
之御見馬而不見路真擅場手也
置之高選良有光于主司
性之囿於氣也其賦同學之變乎氣也其
功大氣者人所賴以生者也而不能無清
濁厚薄之殊性者人所稟以爲人之理也
則固無古今聖愚之異惟其性之同也是
以人皆可以爲堯舜惟其氣之殊也是以
===
===
必資於學焉學也者反其同而變其異之
道也此聖人善憂天下後世而爲之立此
法也粤稽古堯舜孟子所謂性之也其爲
聖之道故不待於學亦未嘗廢學也觀其
曰欽明文思曰允恭克讓此眾人所可見
之德容也然其中心恆如不少間斷雖出
於自然即此便是學之道也自禹湯文武
之爲君皐陶伊傅周召之爲臣則皆孜孜
以學爲言矣曰繇圖曰務成曰甘盤之敷
punctuated:
而有得者乎？

考試官學正季　批：開闔抑揚，若王良之御，見馬而不見路，真擅場手也！置之高選，良有光于主司。

性之囿於氣也，其賦同；學之變乎氣也，其功大。氣者，人所賴以生者也，而不能無清濁厚薄之殊。性者，人所稟以爲人之理也，則固無古今聖愚之異。惟其性之同也，是以人皆可以爲堯舜；惟其氣之殊也，是以必資於學焉。學也者，反其同而變其異之道也。此聖人善憂天下後世，而爲之立此法也。粤稽古堯舜，孟子所謂性之也。其爲聖之道，故不待於學，亦未嘗廢學也。觀其曰「欽明文思」，曰「允恭克讓」，此眾人所可見之德容也。然其中心恆如不少間斷，雖出於自然，即此便是學之道也。自禹湯文武之爲君，皐陶伊傅周召之爲臣，則皆孜孜以學爲言矣。曰繇圖，曰務成，曰甘盤之敷
translation_en:
…and thereby attained insight?

Examiner Ji, School Instructor, comments: “Its opening and closing, restraint and emphasis resemble Wang Liang’s charioteering: he sees the horses but not the road. Truly a master of the field! To place this among the highest selections indeed brings distinction to the presiding examiners.”

Although human nature is confined within material endowment, its bestowal is the same in all; learning’s achievement in transforming material endowment is great. Material endowment is that upon which people depend for life, yet it inevitably differs in clarity and turbidity, richness and thinness. Human nature is the principle people receive that makes them human; fundamentally, it admits no difference between ancient and modern people, sages and fools. Precisely because their nature is the same, everyone can become a Yao or Shun; precisely because their material endowments differ, they must rely upon learning. Learning is the way to return to what is common to all and transform what differs. Thus the sages, thoughtfully concerned for the world and later generations, established this method for them.

Examining antiquity, we find that Yao and Shun were what Mengzi called those who possessed virtue by nature. Their way of becoming sages therefore did not depend upon learning, yet they never abandoned learning. Consider the descriptions “reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful” and “truly respectful and capable of yielding”: these were manifestations of virtue visible to everyone. Within their hearts, however, these qualities remained constant without the slightest interruption. Although this arose spontaneously, it was itself the way of learning. From Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as rulers, and Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao as ministers, all diligently spoke of learning. There are the references to Yaotu [?], to Wucheng, and to Gan Pan’s exposition…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
君子者皆相資以學之人也周衰道廢異
端並興幸而天心篤愛乎斯人神物黙相
乎吾道時則有若孔子之聖者出雖不得
堯舜之位以澤當時然已得堯舜之傳以
澤後世而吾道吾學有主矣春風沂水所
樂者堯舜之氣象秋月尼山所談者堯舜
之文章師友雝雝道義侃侃立正學之髙
壇拓正學之大道揭正學之弘名歸乎此
者曰吾黨之徒也背乎此者曰異端之徒
===
也以此立法猶有異言者有如李斯田子
方之徒皆借名吾道自成一家牢不可破
而吾孔氏之說不能不爲之亂也使天下
貿貿焉卒無所之而吾道隱矣迨夫天運
轉乎上而五星則聚于奎人事恊于下而
諸儒則出乎世濂水之源一開月岩之光
遂揭太極一圖天理明而人事顯矣二程
繼之相與闡明此學清風一嘘率土四應
則吾道之氣復完於天地間矣朱子起焉
punctuated:
君子者，皆相資以學之人也。周衰道廢，異端並興。幸而天心篤愛乎斯人，神物黙相乎吾道，時則有若孔子之聖者出。雖不得堯舜之位以澤當時，然已得堯舜之傳以澤後世，而吾道吾學有主矣。春風沂水，所樂者堯舜之氣象；秋月尼山，所談者堯舜之文章。師友雝雝，道義侃侃，立正學之髙壇，拓正學之大道，揭正學之弘名。歸乎此者，曰吾黨之徒也；背乎此者，曰異端之徒也。以此立法，猶有異言者，有如李斯、田子方之徒，皆借名吾道，自成一家，牢不可破，而吾孔氏之說不能不爲之亂也。使天下貿貿焉，卒無所之，而吾道隱矣。
迨夫天運轉乎上，而五星則聚于奎；人事恊于下，而諸儒則出乎世。濂水之源一開，月岩之光遂揭。太極一圖，天理明而人事顯矣。二程繼之，相與闡明此學，清風一嘘，率土四應，則吾道之氣復完於天地間矣。朱子起焉。
translation_en:
…these gentlemen were all men who aided one another in learning. As the Zhou declined and the Way fell into disuse, heterodox teachings arose together. Fortunately, Heaven's heart deeply cherished these people, and spiritual powers silently aided our Way. At that time a sage such as Confucius appeared. Although he did not obtain the position of Yao and Shun and thereby bring blessings to his own age, he had received their transmitted teaching and thereby brought blessings to later generations. Our Way and our learning thus had a master. Amid spring breezes by the Yi River, what they delighted in was the spirit of Yao and Shun; beneath the autumn moon at Nishan, what they discussed was the cultural legacy of Yao and Shun. Teachers and friends lived in harmony and spoke confidently of the Way and righteousness. They established the lofty platform of orthodox learning, opened its broad road, and proclaimed its great name. Those who adhered to it were called followers of our fellowship; those who turned against it were called followers of heterodoxy. Even with this established as the standard, dissenting voices remained. Such men as Li Si and Tian Zifang borrowed the name of our Way to establish schools of their own, so firmly entrenched that they could not be broken down. The teachings of our Confucius could not escape being confused by them. They left all under Heaven bewildered, ultimately with nowhere to turn, and our Way became obscured.
Then Heaven's cycles turned above, and the five planets gathered in the constellation Kui; human affairs harmonized below, and the Confucian scholars appeared in the world. Once the source of the Lian River opened, the light of Yueyan shone forth. Through the single Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Heaven's principles became clear and human affairs manifest. The two Cheng brothers followed, together elucidating this learning. At one breath of their pure breeze, the whole realm responded from every quarter, and the vital force of our Way was once more restored to wholeness between Heaven and Earth. Master Zhu arose…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以天授頴敏之資天挺豪傑之才聰明始
開即能沙畫八卦端坐黙視此謂非天有
意於吾道而篤生乎斯人不可也位不滿
德潜脩于家得以俯而讀仰而思大究乎
聖言問者師辨者友深明乎正學嘗膺玉
山尹之聘也感其建學延師為之設座開
講首以孔子古之學者為已今之學者為
人為從游者言之以見聖人教人為學非
是使人綴緝言語造化文辭但為科名爵
===
禄之計而已須是格物致知誠意正心脩
身而推之以至於齊家治國平天下方是
正當學問復因程珙之問而為之詳說孔
子言仁孟子兼言仁義使之於身上用力
不可於冊上漫談至於氣質之清濁工夫
之淺深無不並舉而兼教之雖以副邑大
夫建學教人之良意實以廣吾道脩已治
人之正傳也同時有象山陸子靜者少服
父兄師友之訓克勵聖賢道義之心因邵
punctuated:
以天授頴敏之資、天挺豪傑之才，聰明始開，即能沙畫八卦，端坐黙視。此謂非天有意於吾道而篤生乎斯人，不可也。位不滿德，潜脩于家，得以俯而讀、仰而思，大究乎聖言。問者師，辨者友，深明乎正學。嘗膺玉山尹之聘也，感其建學延師，為之設座開講，首以孔子「古之學者為已，今之學者為人」為從游者言之，以見聖人教人為學，非是使人綴緝言語、造化文辭，但為科名爵禄之計而已。須是格物致知、誠意正心、脩身，而推之以至於齊家治國平天下，方是正當學問。復因程珙之問，而為之詳說孔子言仁、孟子兼言仁義，使之於身上用力，不可於冊上漫談。至於氣質之清濁、工夫之淺深，無不並舉而兼教之。雖以副邑大夫建學教人之良意，實以廣吾道脩已治人之正傳也。

同時有象山陸子靜者，少服父兄師友之訓，克勵聖賢道義之心，因邵
translation_en:
…with Heaven-bestowed intelligence and sensitivity, and Heaven-endowed talents of heroic distinction. As soon as his understanding began to develop, he could draw the Eight Trigrams in the sand and sit upright contemplating them in silence. It cannot be said that Heaven, having a purpose for our Way, did not bring forth this man with exceptional gifts. His official station fell short of his virtue. Cultivating himself in retirement at home, he could bend his head to read and raise it to reflect, thoroughly investigating the words of the sages. He treated those whom he questioned as teachers and those with whom he debated as friends, attaining a profound understanding of orthodox learning.

He once accepted an invitation from the Magistrate of Yushan. Moved by the magistrate’s establishment of a school and invitation of teachers, he took his seat and began lecturing. He first addressed those studying with him on Confucius’s saying, “The learners of antiquity studied for themselves; learners today study for others.” This showed that when the sage taught people to learn, he did not mean to have them piece together phrases and fashion literary compositions merely to secure examination honors, official rank, and emoluments. They must investigate things and extend knowledge, make their intentions sincere and rectify their minds, cultivate themselves, and then extend this to ordering their families, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven. Only this constitutes proper learning.

In response to a question from Cheng Gong, he further explained in detail why Confucius spoke of benevolence, while Mencius spoke of both benevolence and righteousness. He directed him to exert himself in his own person, rather than merely discourse loosely on the pages of books. As for the purity or turbidity of one’s psychophysical endowment and the shallowness or depth of one’s efforts at cultivation, he addressed all these together in his teaching. Although this fulfilled the magistrate’s worthy intention of establishing a school and teaching people, it also served to extend the orthodox transmission of our Way: cultivating oneself and governing others.

At the same time there was Lu Zijing, known as Xiangshan, who from youth had followed the instructions of his father, elder brothers, teachers, and friends, and diligently fostered an aspiration toward the Way and righteousness of the sages and worthies. In response to Shao…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
侯之請開白鹿之堂集郡邑羣賢於講筵
揭論語一章之大義其曰君子喻於義謂
君子之志義則所習者必在於義斯曉然
於義也其曰小人喻於利謂小人之志利
則所習者必在於利斯曉然於利也至於
謂科舉取士久矣名儒鉅公皆由於此士
由此而出亦可謂正也但於未得之則不
可以得失為計既得之則不可以祿位為
念但當悉心於國事盡力於民隱能以職
===
業為心便是君子之喻於義若以祿位為
心便是小人之喻於利斯言亦救世之良
劑也朱陸之學昔人辨之詳矣玆其所謂
喻於義者非為己之學歟喻於利者非為
人之學歟何所異哉春秋講義呂東萊之
作也首言學欲切而思欲近春秋夫子筆
也而以深切自命傳經者亦謂撥亂世反
之正莫近於春秋君子將用力於切近之
地置是經其何從降隱迄哀所褒者既往
punctuated:
侯之請，開白鹿之堂，集郡邑羣賢於講筵，揭《論語》一章之大義。其曰「君子喻於義」，謂君子之志義，則所習者必在於義，斯曉然於義也。其曰「小人喻於利」，謂小人之志利，則所習者必在於利，斯曉然於利也。至於謂「科舉取士久矣，名儒鉅公皆由於此，士由此而出，亦可謂正也。但於未得之，則不可以得失為計；既得之，則不可以祿位為念。但當悉心於國事，盡力於民隱，能以職業為心，便是君子之喻於義；若以祿位為心，便是小人之喻於利」，斯言亦救世之良劑也。朱陸之學，昔人辨之詳矣。玆其所謂喻於義者，非為己之學歟？喻於利者，非為人之學歟？何所異哉？
《春秋講義》，呂東萊之作也。首言學欲切而思欲近。《春秋》，夫子筆也，而以深切自命。傳經者亦謂撥亂世反之正，莫近於《春秋》。君子將用力於切近之地，置是經，其何從？降隱迄哀，所褒者既往
translation_en:
…at the lord’s request, he opened the hall at Bailu and assembled the worthy men of the prefecture and its counties for a lecture, expounding the essential meaning of a chapter of the Analects. The statement “The gentleman understands righteousness” means that, because the gentleman directs his aspirations toward righteousness, what he practices must concern righteousness; thus he comes to understand it clearly. The statement “The petty man understands profit” means that, because the petty man directs his aspirations toward profit, what he practices must concern profit; thus he comes to understand it clearly. He went on to say: “The selection of officials through the civil-service examinations has long been established. Renowned scholars and eminent officials have all come through this route, so scholars who advance by it may indeed be said to follow a proper course. But before attaining success, they must not calculate gains and losses; after attaining it, they must not dwell on salary and rank. They should simply devote themselves wholeheartedly to affairs of state and exert themselves to the utmost to relieve the people’s hardships. To set one’s heart on official duties is precisely the gentleman’s understanding of righteousness; to set one’s heart on salary and rank is precisely the petty man’s understanding of profit.” These words, too, are an excellent remedy for saving the world. Earlier writers have distinguished the teachings of Zhu and Lu in detail. Yet is what is called understanding righteousness here not learning for one’s own moral cultivation? And is understanding profit not learning for the sake of others’ approval? What difference is there between them?
Lectures on the Spring and Autumn Annals is the work of Lü Donglai. It begins by saying that learning should bear directly on oneself and reflection should concern what is close at hand. The Spring and Autumn Annals came from the Master’s brush, and he himself characterized it as profound and closely pertinent. Those who transmitted the classic likewise said that nothing approached the Spring and Autumn Annals in bringing order out of a disordered age and restoring what is right. If a gentleman wishes to apply himself to what is directly pertinent and close at hand, what could he follow if he set this classic aside? From Duke Yin down to Duke Ai, what it praises are past …

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之功也所貶者旣往之罪也終日歷數古
人而我無與焉豈所謂切近者哉乾卦講
義黃勉齋之作也首詳元亨利貞四德之
切於人而以孟子人之有是四端於我而
自謂不能者自賊者也謂其君不能者賊
其君者也數言繼之且曰五帝三王載籍
之傳以仁義禮智對立而並言者自孟子
始蓋人受天地之中無非此性雜之以氣
質撓之以習俗不能親師取友以致其學
===
問之功雖有此性亦未免於晦而不明窒
而不通矣呂黃之學源流傳之正矣玆其
所謂切者即四端根於心也所謂近者即
四端備於已也奚有於二哉講於東湖書
院者則道之不行也我知之矣智愚賢不
肖之過不及而指其道為仁敬孝慈信之
在於人者中而已矣過與不及人失之也
講於竹林精舍者教人之方則曰居敬曰
窮理曰力行讀書之法則先大學次論孟
punctuated:
之功也，所貶者旣往之罪也。終日歷數古人，而我無與焉，豈所謂切近者哉？

《乾卦講義》，黃勉齋之作也。首詳元亨利貞四德之切於人，而以孟子「人之有是四端於我，而自謂不能者，自賊者也；謂其君不能者，賊其君者也」數言繼之。且曰：「五帝三王載籍之傳，以仁義禮智對立而並言者，自孟子始。蓋人受天地之中，無非此性；雜之以氣質，撓之以習俗，不能親師取友，以致其學問之功，雖有此性，亦未免於晦而不明，窒而不通矣。」呂黃之學，源流傳之正矣。玆其所謂切者，即四端根於心也；所謂近者，即四端備於已也。奚有於二哉？

講於東湖書院者，則「道之不行也，我知之矣」，智愚賢不肖之過不及，而指其道為仁敬孝慈信之在於人者，中而已矣。過與不及，人失之也。

講於竹林精舍者，教人之方則曰居敬，曰窮理，曰力行；讀書之法則先《大學》，次《論》《孟》
translation_en:
…accomplishments of the past; what it censures are offenses of the past. If one spends all day recounting the deeds of the ancients, yet has no personal involvement in them, can this be what is meant by the immediately relevant and close at hand?

Lectures on the Qian Hexagram is the work of Huang Mianzhai. It begins by explaining in detail how the four virtues—origination, prevalence, benefit, and constancy—bear directly upon human beings, and follows this with these words of Mengzi: “People possess these four beginnings within themselves. Those who nevertheless say they are incapable injure themselves; those who say their ruler is incapable injure their ruler.” It further states: “In the written traditions transmitted from the Five Emperors and Three Kings, it was only with Mengzi that benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom began to be set alongside one another and discussed together. What human beings receive as the balanced endowment of Heaven and Earth is nothing other than this nature. When it is mixed with their psychophysical constitution and disturbed by customary practices, if they cannot draw close to teachers and choose friends so as to bring their learning to fruition, then, although they possess this nature, it inevitably remains obscured rather than clear, blocked rather than freely expressed.” The learning of Lü and Huang derives from orthodox sources and lines of transmission. Here, what they call “immediately relevant” is precisely that the four beginnings are rooted in the heart; what they call “close at hand” is precisely that the four beginnings are fully present in oneself. How could these be two different things?

The lectures at Donghu Academy take up the saying, “I know why the Way is not practiced,” discussing how the wise and the foolish, the worthy and the unworthy, go too far or fall short. They identify this Way as benevolence, reverence, filial devotion, parental kindness, and trustworthiness as present in human beings: it is simply the mean. Going too far or falling short is a failure on the part of human beings.

The lectures at Zhulin Study Retreat describe the methods of instruction as maintaining reverence, investigating principle, and putting learning earnestly into practice. As for the method of reading, they place the Great Learning first, followed by the Analects and the Mengzi…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而終之以中庸勉人以立志則拳拳以去
私慾信道篤爲要言示人以歸宿則切切
以希堯舜學禹湯爲地位陳北溪之講於
嚴陵也其設條目則有曰道學體統曰師
友淵源曰用工節目曰讀書次序蔡久軒
之講於和靖書院也其名義蓋以和靖甫
生爲程門高第其學深有得於大易敬義
之旨以爲終身受用之地此立學之體也
程子謂和靖之學他日必有用於世焉先
===
生之學者亦將以有用於世此行學之用
也體立用行吾道之學備矣以此而用於
世則可以堯舜其君民也以此而用於家
則可以堯舜其倫族也以此而爲人則順
以此而爲己則祥信矣哉聖賢之學不我
欺也然豈強人所不能哉出於人性之固
有求於人力之能爲彼僞學之徒自壞乃
性耳夫豈其性則然哉聞諸李延平曰道
可以治心猶食之充飽衣之禦寒也學也
punctuated: 而終之以《中庸》。勉人以立志，則拳拳以去私慾、信道篤爲要言；示人以歸宿，則切切以希堯舜、學禹湯爲地位。陳北溪之講於嚴陵也，其設條目則有曰道學體統，曰師友淵源，曰用工節目，曰讀書次序。蔡久軒之講於和靖書院也，其名義蓋以和靖甫生爲程門高第，其學深有得於《大易》敬義之旨，以爲終身受用之地，此立學之體也。程子謂和靖之學，他日必有用於世焉。先生之學者亦將以有用於世，此行學之用也。體立用行，吾道之學備矣。以此而用於世，則可以堯舜其君民也；以此而用於家，則可以堯舜其倫族也；以此而爲人則順，以此而爲己則祥。信矣哉！聖賢之學不我欺也。然豈強人所不能哉？出於人性之固有，求於人力之能爲，彼僞學之徒自壞乃性耳，夫豈其性則然哉？聞諸李延平曰：「道可以治心，猶食之充飽、衣之禦寒也。學也
translation_en: …and conclude with the Doctrine of the Mean. In urging people to establish their resolve, he earnestly made eliminating selfish desires and firmly trusting the Way his essential counsel. In showing people their ultimate destination, he insistently set aspiring to Yao and Shun and emulating Yu and Tang as the level to attain. When Chen Beixi lectured at Yanling, he established these headings: the overall structure of Learning of the Way; its transmission through teachers and friends; the stages of practical effort; and the sequence for reading books. When Cai Jiuxuan lectured at Hejing Academy, the significance of its name apparently lay in Master Hejing [?] having been an outstanding disciple of Master Cheng. His learning had deeply grasped the meaning of reverence and righteousness in the Book of Changes, making these the foundation on which he drew throughout his life. This is the substance on which learning is established. Master Cheng said that Hejing’s learning would assuredly be of use to the world one day. Those who study the master’s teachings will likewise seek to be of use to the world: this is the practical application of learning. When its substance is established and its application put into practice, the learning of our Way is complete. Applied in the world, it can make one’s ruler and people like Yao and Shun; applied within the family, it can make one’s kin and clan like Yao and Shun. Acting for others through it brings harmony; acting for oneself through it brings good fortune. How true it is! The learning of the sages and worthies does not deceive us. Yet does it compel people to do what they cannot? It proceeds from what is inherent in human nature and seeks what human effort can accomplish. Those followers of false learning merely ruin their own nature. How could their nature itself be like that? I have heard these words of Li Yanping: “The Way can bring order to the heart, just as food satisfies hunger and clothing wards off cold. Learning…”

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
者耕耨蠶績之功也求其人而證之可乎
伊周孔孟同一學也而伊周遇時故事功
成之於當時孔孟雖不偶於時而其事功
垂之於萬世傳曰脩身人也遇不遇天也
君子知脩吾學而已遇之則當爲伊周不
遇則當爲孔孟是固在我之立志務學如
何
第五問
王璠
===
同考試官訓導張批先有濟世之志而
發之於文庶不泥於古不流於俗
使無定見則惟空言是逞雖華何
益此作參考往迹而昌以正論固
有體而欲達諸用者
考試官教諭周批儒生不達世務者
皆目曰腐此作關係政體曲盡事
情根據舊聞深悉民隱迂腐者能
爲是言乎
punctuated:
者，耕耨蠶績之功也。求其人而證之，可乎？伊周孔孟，同一學也，而伊周遇時，故事功成之於當時；孔孟雖不偶於時，而其事功垂之於萬世。傳曰：「脩身，人也；遇不遇，天也。」君子知脩吾學而已。遇之，則當爲伊周；不遇，則當爲孔孟。是固在我之立志務學如何。
第五問
王璠
同考試官訓導張批：先有濟世之志，而發之於文，庶不泥於古，不流於俗。使無定見，則惟空言是逞，雖華何益？此作參考往迹，而昌以正論，固有體而欲達諸用者。
考試官教諭周批：儒生不達世務者，皆目曰腐。此作關係政體，曲盡事情，根據舊聞，深悉民隱。迂腐者能爲是言乎？
translation_en:
…learning is the work of plowing, hoeing, raising silkworms, and spinning. May we seek out men who exemplify this and thereby verify it? Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius shared the same learning. Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou encountered favorable times, so their achievements were realized in their own age. Although Confucius and Mencius did not meet with favorable times, their achievements have endured for ten thousand generations. A transmitted text says: “Cultivating oneself rests with man; meeting or failing to meet with opportunity rests with Heaven.” The gentleman knows only to cultivate his learning. Given the opportunity, he should become an Yi Yin or a Duke of Zhou; without it, he should become a Confucius or a Mencius. This indeed depends on how we establish our resolve and apply ourselves to learning.
Fifth Question
Wang Fan
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: One must first possess the resolve to aid the world and then express it in writing; only then may one avoid being bound by antiquity or drifting with conventional opinion. Without settled judgment, one merely indulges in empty words. However ornate they may be, what use are they? This essay examines past events and amplifies them through sound argument. It assuredly possesses a foundation and seeks to put it into practical use.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Confucian students who fail to understand worldly affairs are all labeled pedants. This essay addresses the principles of government, fully explores the circumstances of affairs, draws on accounts of the past, and shows a deep understanding of the people's hidden sufferings. Could an impractical pedant speak in this way?

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正季批敘事不遺工詞有
理頓挫起伏而嚴整不亂孰意風
簷寸晷有此作也
民困不可不憫也欲施一念之仁須盡萬
全之慮若徒知益下而無經理周防之術
雖頻蠲屢貸而閭閻之困固自若也如是
則上之所施下之所望不亦兩負也哉嗚
呼仁覆斯民如三代帝王亦云至矣而未
見有所蠲貸者蓋取民雖用田賦而又隨
===
時隨地爲之權衡民皆遵從輸納自不至
於逋負尚何用蠲貸爲哉自是以後賦稅
之額始定額外之征又繁不得不視時之
豐歉民之貧富而時布蠲放之恩亦其勢
然也故逋貸之蠲起於漢武帝逋負之寬
起於吳嘉禾以晉惠帝有戸調絹綿之除
以唐宣宗有度支鹽鐵之免減上供餽運
者始於大中九年也免官司債負和買役
錢者昉於紹興三十二載也是皆有仁民
punctuated:
考試官學正季批：敘事不遺，工詞有理，頓挫起伏而嚴整不亂。孰意風簷寸晷有此作也？

民困不可不憫也。欲施一念之仁，須盡萬全之慮。若徒知益下，而無經理周防之術，雖頻蠲屢貸，而閭閻之困固自若也。如是，則上之所施、下之所望，不亦兩負也哉？嗚呼！仁覆斯民，如三代帝王，亦云至矣，而未見有所蠲貸者。蓋取民雖用田賦，而又隨時隨地爲之權衡，民皆遵從輸納，自不至於逋負，尚何用蠲貸爲哉？自是以後，賦稅之額始定，額外之征又繁，不得不視時之豐歉、民之貧富，而時布蠲放之恩，亦其勢然也。故逋貸之蠲起於漢武帝，逋負之寬起於吳嘉禾，以晉惠帝有戸調絹綿之除，以唐宣宗有度支鹽鐵之免。減上供餽運者，始於大中九年也；免官司債負、和買、役錢者，昉於紹興三十二載也。是皆有仁民
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Ji, Instructor: “The exposition omits nothing; the wording is skillful and the reasoning sound. Its pauses and turns, rises and falls, remain disciplined and orderly. Who would have expected such a composition under wind-swept eaves in the brief time allotted?”

The people’s distress cannot go unpitied. To put a single benevolent intention into effect requires consideration of every precaution. If one knows only how to benefit those below, but lacks methods of administration and comprehensive safeguards, then even repeated remissions and loans will leave the distress of ordinary households unchanged. In this case, would not both the assistance bestowed from above and the hopes entertained below be disappointed? Alas! The benevolence with which the sovereigns of the Three Dynasties sheltered the people may be called supreme, yet we find no instances of their granting remissions or loans. Although they collected revenue from the people through land taxes, they adjusted their demands according to time and place. The people all complied and made their payments, naturally avoiding arrears. What need, then, was there for remissions or loans?

Thereafter, fixed tax quotas began to be established, and additional levies beyond those quotas multiplied. It became necessary to consider whether harvests were abundant or poor and whether the people were impoverished or prosperous, and periodically to bestow the favor of remission. Circumstances themselves made this inevitable. Thus, the cancellation of overdue loans began under Emperor Wu of Han, and relief from arrears began during the Jiahe reign period of Wu. Under Emperor Hui of Jin, household levies of silk cloth and silk floss were abolished; under Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, there were exemptions from fiscal levies on salt and iron [?]. Reductions in supplies remitted to the court and their transport began in the ninth year of Dazhong. The cancellation of debts owed to government offices, compulsory purchases at official prices, and service payments began in the thirty-second year of Shaoxing. These were all instances of having a benevolent concern for the people…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之心者矣然其間又有不盡免而權宜於
其中者考之宋哲宗時令諸路屢年負欠
以十分爲率每年帶納一分似爲便民矣
而蘇東坡訪問濠壽父老有豐年不如凶
年之云者蓋以天災流行民雖乏食縮衣
節口猶可聊生若豐年舉催積欠符檄日
至其門鞭笞日加其身則人皆求死而不
可得反不若凶歲之易過也夫恩典雖厚
奉宣匪人民何由而受惠哉宋自紹興以
===
來邊隅多警役繁賦重極力寬之民病猶
未甦也而朱元晦上封事有遷延一分以
待蠲放之議者蓋宋初舊法凡催理官物
數及九分者諸司即行住催版曹亦置不
問州縣得其贏餘以相補助貧民亦得遷
延以待蠲除恩自朝廷惠及閭里較之虛
文無實所謂黃紙放白紙取者不亦相去
遠哉愚竊聞之天下財賦一歲所入止足
歲之用況又水旱無常虧縮未足若憫
punctuated:
之心者矣。然其間又有不盡免而權宜於其中者。考之宋哲宗時，令諸路屢年負欠，以十分爲率，每年帶納一分，似爲便民矣。而蘇東坡訪問濠壽父老，有「豐年不如凶年」之云者，蓋以天災流行，民雖乏食，縮衣節口，猶可聊生；若豐年舉催積欠，符檄日至其門，鞭笞日加其身，則人皆求死而不可得，反不若凶歲之易過也。夫恩典雖厚，奉宣匪人，民何由而受惠哉？宋自紹興以來，邊隅多警，役繁賦重，極力寬之，民病猶未甦也。而朱元晦上封事，有遷延一分以待蠲放之議者，蓋宋初舊法，凡催理官物，數及九分者，諸司即行住催，版曹亦置不問，州縣得其贏餘以相補助，貧民亦得遷延以待蠲除。恩自朝廷，惠及閭里，較之虛文無實，所謂「黃紙放，白紙取」者，不亦相去遠哉？

愚竊聞之，天下財賦，一歲所入，止足歲之用。況又水旱無常，虧縮未足。若憫
translation_en:
…were all men who had hearts concerned for the people. Yet among these measures were some that did not remit everything, but adopted expedients. Examining the reign of Emperor Zhezong of the Song, we find that the circuits were ordered to divide arrears accumulated over successive years into ten portions and collect one portion each year along with current payments. This would seem to have benefited the people. Yet when Su Dongpo questioned the elders of Haozhou and Shouzhou, some said, “A good harvest year is worse than a bad one.” This was because, when natural disasters struck, the people, though short of food, could still scrape by through economizing on clothing and meals. In a good harvest year, however, all accumulated arrears were pressed for payment: official demands arrived at their doors daily, and beatings were inflicted on their bodies daily. Everyone sought death but could not obtain it; such a year was actually harder to endure than a year of poor harvests. Though acts of imperial grace might be generous, if those charged with carrying them out were unsuitable, how could the people receive their benefits? From the Shaoxing reign onward, the Song faced frequent alarms on its frontiers, onerous labor services, and heavy taxes. Even with every effort to grant relief, the people had still not recovered from their distress. In a sealed memorial, Zhu Yuanhui proposed allowing payment of the remaining tenth to be deferred pending remission. Under an old rule dating from the early Song, whenever collection of government dues reached nine tenths, the various offices immediately ceased pressing for payment, and the Ministry of Revenue likewise left the matter alone. Prefectures and counties could use their surpluses to make up one another’s deficiencies, while poor people could defer payment in anticipation of remission. Grace thus proceeded from the court, and its benefits reached the villages. Was this not far removed from empty paperwork without practical effect—the practice described as “remitting on yellow paper, collecting on white paper”?

I have humbly heard that the empire’s annual fiscal receipts suffice only for that year’s expenditures. Moreover, unpredictable floods and droughts cause shortfalls and leave revenues insufficient. If, out of pity…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
民彫悴舉數年逋負而一旦免之固歡欣
鼓舞於田野矣然大而軍國邊境之需次
而官胥廩祿之費當取辦於何所哉倉庾
儲峙在在空虛如之何其可也是以宋高
宗因湖秀水災欲除下戶積欠慮恐侵損
歲支輒於內庫撥補乃曰內庫所積正備
水旱本是民財却爲民用何所顧惜夫湖
秀一隅侵損未多補給尚易也若舉天下
而出內帑給之勢亦難乎其爲繼愚恐高
===
宗亦末如之何也由是觀之則蠲貸之令
豈可輕舉而無周悉萬全之慮哉昔人謂
赦者小人之幸愚初未敢以爲然今夷考
往迹始知非虛語也盍觀之唐乎玄宗蠲
免七年以前逋負當時稱爲異數而識者
猶有未然蓋寬貸之舉止爲貧民若果貧
民欠負盡數免之以蘇疲困有何不可但
膏脂已竭於貧窮而恩典翻歸於豪猾中
間雖究已收未收之等然亦誰肯自陳其
punctuated: 民彫悴，舉數年逋負而一旦免之，固歡欣鼓舞於田野矣。然大而軍國邊境之需，次而官胥廩祿之費，當取辦於何所哉？倉庾儲峙，在在空虛，如之何其可也？是以宋高宗因湖秀水災，欲除下戶積欠，慮恐侵損歲支，輒於內庫撥補，乃曰：「內庫所積，正備水旱，本是民財，却爲民用，何所顧惜？」夫湖秀一隅，侵損未多，補給尚易也。若舉天下而出內帑給之，勢亦難乎其爲繼，愚恐高宗亦末如之何也。由是觀之，則蠲貸之令，豈可輕舉而無周悉萬全之慮哉？昔人謂「赦者小人之幸」，愚初未敢以爲然，今夷考往迹，始知非虛語也。盍觀之唐乎？玄宗蠲免七年以前逋負，當時稱爲異數，而識者猶有未然。蓋寬貸之舉，止爲貧民，若果貧民欠負，盡數免之，以蘇疲困，有何不可？但膏脂已竭於貧窮，而恩典翻歸於豪猾。中間雖究已收未收之等，然亦誰肯自陳其
translation_en: …the people’s impoverishment and distress, and canceled several years’ arrears at a single stroke, there would certainly be rejoicing throughout the countryside. Yet where would the funds come from for the greater demands of military and state affairs and frontier defense, and, below these, the expense of salaries and grain allowances for officials and clerks? With stores in granaries everywhere empty, how could this be practicable? Thus, when Emperor Gaozong of the Song wished to cancel the accumulated arrears of poorer households following floods in Huzhou and Xiuzhou, he feared that this would diminish the funds available for annual expenditure and accordingly transferred funds from the palace treasury to make up the shortfall. He declared: “What is accumulated in the palace treasury is intended precisely as a reserve against floods and droughts. It was originally the people’s wealth, and now it is used for the people. Why begrudge it?” Huzhou and Xiuzhou were but one corner of the realm: the shortfall was not large, and replacing it was still easy. But if funds were taken from the palace treasury to supply the entire realm, this would be difficult to sustain. I fear that even Gaozong would have been at a loss. Viewed in this light, how could an order granting remission be issued lightly, without thorough consideration and a plan secure in every respect? People of old said, “Pardons are the good fortune of petty men.” At first I did not venture to accept this as true; only now, after carefully examining past events, have I realized that these were no empty words. Why not consider the Tang? Emperor Xuanzong remitted arrears dating from before the seventh year. At the time this was hailed as an extraordinary favor, yet discerning men still had reservations. Such leniency is intended solely for the poor. If the arrears really were owed by poor people, what objection could there be to canceling them in full to relieve their exhaustion and hardship? But the poor had already been drained of their substance, while the imperial favor instead went to the powerful and unscrupulous. Although inquiry was made into such distinctions as whether payments had already been collected or remained uncollected, who would willingly disclose his own…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
弊哉官司欲證其實未免拘集小民里胥
追呼文移煩複農事因之妨廢貪汚緣以
爲姦况又懼包攬之强而俛首認納畏械
繫之苦而依令重陪害及雞豚利歸豺虎
小人之幸良不誣也使當時君臣果知此
弊勿免日前逋負止於次歲量除明開何
等徵需定與減免分數庶窮鄉僻壤盡知
應免應納之數而貪吏豪猾亦難肆重徵
侵尅之姦矣昔宋臣趙善防議稱貧民下
===
戶每歲二稅但有重納未嘗拖欠朝廷蠲
放利歸攬戶鄉胥而小民未嘗霑恩乞明
詔自今郊霈惟減次年賦稅其日前殘零
務依數納足則貧民實被寬恩官賦亦易
催理此誠切要之策而當時未盡舉行良
可惜也嗚呼自昔有天下者欲施不忍之
政而必竭盡心思典法之立非徒然者使
行法得人則蠲減新徵固可也寬貸積逋
亦可也否則德意徒存奉宣未至不但視
punctuated:
弊哉？官司欲證其實，未免拘集小民，里胥追呼，文移煩複，農事因之妨廢，貪汚緣以爲姦。况又懼包攬之强而俛首認納，畏械繫之苦而依令重陪，害及雞豚，利歸豺虎。小人之幸，良不誣也。使當時君臣果知此弊，勿免日前逋負，止於次歲量除，明開何等徵需，定與減免分數，庶窮鄉僻壤盡知應免應納之數，而貪吏豪猾亦難肆重徵侵尅之姦矣。昔宋臣趙善防議稱：「貧民下戶，每歲二稅，但有重納，未嘗拖欠。朝廷蠲放，利歸攬戶鄉胥，而小民未嘗霑恩。乞明詔自今郊霈，惟減次年賦稅，其日前殘零，務依數納足，則貧民實被寬恩，官賦亦易催理。」此誠切要之策，而當時未盡舉行，良可惜也。
嗚呼！自昔有天下者，欲施不忍之政，而必竭盡心思，典法之立非徒然者。使行法得人，則蠲減新徵固可也，寬貸積逋亦可也。否則德意徒存，奉宣未至，不但視
translation_en:
…their malpractices? When the authorities seek to verify the facts, they inevitably summon and detain ordinary people; village clerks hound them, and official correspondence becomes burdensome and repetitive. Farming is consequently disrupted and neglected, while corrupt officials exploit the opportunity for wrongdoing. Moreover, fearing the power of those who undertake tax payments on others’ behalf, the people bow their heads and acknowledge liability; dreading the suffering of shackles and imprisonment, they obey orders and make payment a second time [?]. The harm reaches even their chickens and pigs, while the profits go to jackals and tigers. That this is a boon to petty men is indeed no false assertion. Had the ruler and his ministers at that time truly understood these abuses, they would have refrained from remitting past arrears and instead made measured reductions only in the following year’s taxes. They would have specified clearly which levies were affected and fixed the proportions to be reduced or remitted. Then even people in the poorest and remotest villages would have known exactly how much was exempted and how much remained payable, and corrupt officials and powerful rogues would have found it difficult to perpetrate fraud through duplicate collection and embezzlement.
A Song minister, Zhao Shanfang 趙善防 [?], once argued: “Poor people and households in the lowest assessment categories pay the two annual taxes, sometimes twice over, and never fall into arrears. When the court grants remissions, the profits go to households that undertake tax payments for others and to village clerks; the common people never receive the benefit. I request an explicit edict that henceforth, when acts of grace are proclaimed on the occasion of the suburban sacrifices, only the following year’s taxes be reduced, while all outstanding balances from earlier years must be paid in full. Then the poor will truly receive the benefit of the court’s generosity, and official taxes will also be easier to collect and administer.” This was indeed a policy addressing the essential problem; it is deeply regrettable that it was not fully implemented at the time.
Alas! From ancient times, those who ruled the realm and wished to establish a government unable to bear the people’s suffering had to devote all their thought to the task: the establishment of statutes was no idle undertaking. If the right people are entrusted with enforcing the law, reducing or remitting newly levied taxes is certainly permissible, and granting relief on accumulated arrears is permissible as well. Otherwise, benevolent intentions remain mere intentions, and their implementation falls short; not only are they regarded as…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
爲紙上之文而反重爲閭閻之擾甚至罔
民之愚侵國之用徒知飽煖乎巳不思失
信於民此淳熈州縣之吏不能仰體至懷
而屢詔以督責之也然則赦之布也豈但
豪猾小人之幸亦貪墨之幸耳嗚呼心何
忍哉是以漢時欲安斯民必擇守令而傳
曰文武之政布在方策其人存則其政舉
此雖儒生常談而人君治世之規恐不出
此執事以爲何如惟貸其狂而教之幸也
punctuated: 爲紙上之文，而反重爲閭閻之擾，甚至罔民之愚，侵國之用，徒知飽煖乎巳，不思失信於民。此淳熈州縣之吏不能仰體至懷，而屢詔以督責之也。然則赦之布也，豈但豪猾小人之幸，亦貪墨之幸耳。嗚呼！心何忍哉！是以漢時欲安斯民，必擇守令。而傳曰：「文武之政，布在方策。其人存，則其政舉。」此雖儒生常談，而人君治世之規，恐不出此。執事以爲何如？惟貸其狂而教之，幸也。
translation_en: …as mere words on paper, but instead becomes an additional disturbance to ordinary households. Worse still, officials exploit the people's ignorance and misappropriate state funds, caring only to keep themselves well fed and warm, without considering how they forfeit the people's trust. This is why, during the Chunxi reign period, prefectural and county officials who failed to embody the sovereign's deepest intentions were repeatedly admonished and held to account by imperial edicts. Thus, when an amnesty is proclaimed, how could it benefit only powerful, unscrupulous scoundrels? It also benefits corrupt officials. Alas! How can their hearts bear this? Hence, in Han times, securing the people's peace required careful selection of prefects and magistrates. As the transmitted text says: “The government of Kings Wen and Wu is set forth on wooden tablets and bamboo slips. When the right men are present, their government is put into effect.” Although this is a commonplace among Confucian scholars, I fear that the principles by which a ruler governs the world extend no further than this. What is your judgment, sir? I would count myself fortunate if you would pardon my presumption and instruct me.

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄後序
夫科舉必有錄錄必有序錄
之式載官使以昭事載名氏
以昭賢載文章以昭用序之
式申勸戒以昭義列撫臣藩
臬以昭類列守臣以昭備總
之皆爲貴士設也是之謂制
===
制之行合天下而同也夫合
天下而同於貴士士宜乎軼
前脩而上之矣而顧或不逮
意者勢使然乎是故科舉之
制益飭而有志之士或鬱而
不暢或興而不奮者有矣今
天子以聖神入嗣大歷服躬脩德
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄後序

夫科舉必有錄，錄必有序。錄之式，載官使以昭事，載名氏以昭賢，載文章以昭用；序之式，申勸戒以昭義，列撫臣藩臬以昭類，列守臣以昭備。總之，皆爲貴士設也，是之謂制。

制之行，合天下而同也。夫合天下而同於貴士，士宜乎軼前脩而上之矣，而顧或不逮，意者勢使然乎？是故科舉之制益飭，而有志之士或鬱而不暢，或興而不奮者有矣。今天子以聖神入嗣大歷服，躬脩德
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

Every civil-service examination must have a record, and every record must have a preface. The prescribed form of the record lists the officials and their assignments to make their duties clear, records the candidates’ names to make their worth known, and includes their compositions to demonstrate their usefulness. The prescribed form of the preface reiterates encouragements and admonitions to make their principles clear, lists the grand coordinators, provincial administration commissioners, and surveillance commissioners to show their respective categories, and lists the prefects to show the completeness of the arrangements. In sum, all this is instituted to honor scholars. This is what is meant by the established system.

The implementation of this system is uniform throughout the realm. Since the whole realm is united in honoring scholars, scholars ought to surpass their worthy predecessors and rise above them. Yet some instead fall short: perhaps circumstances make it so? Thus, although the examination system is increasingly well regulated, there are aspiring scholars whose ambitions remain pent up without expression, or who are stirred but fail to exert themselves. Now the Son of Heaven, in his sagely and divine wisdom, has succeeded to the great imperial mandate and personally cultivates virtue…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
教體貌儒臣表忠節登俊良
作士氣以培
國家之元氣於永久凡含生之
類莫不振動抃蹈訖于無外
則夫有司飭制以貴士者皆
聖神精微之所運用已是蓋古聖
賢遑遑終老而不獲見者而
===
况雲貴之遠乎傳曰周之士
也貴此其時矣請與諸士驗
諸今之場屋如監察御史羅
玉之風裁藩臬之慎肅羣司
百執事之恪共道洽而通氣
和而豐祺然韙然罔不心快
目爽於諸士之進曰今科其
punctuated: 教，體貌儒臣，表忠節，登俊良，作士氣，以培國家之元氣於永久。凡含生之類，莫不振動抃蹈，訖于無外。則夫有司飭制以貴士者，皆聖神精微之所運用已。是蓋古聖賢遑遑終老而不獲見者，而况雲貴之遠乎？傳曰：「周之士也貴。」此其時矣！請與諸士驗諸今之場屋：如監察御史羅玉之風裁，藩臬之慎肅，羣司百執事之恪共，道洽而通，氣和而豐，祺然韙然，罔不心快目爽於諸士之進，曰：「今科其
translation_en:
…teaching, treats Confucian officials with ceremonial respect, honors loyalty and integrity, advances men of outstanding worth, and rouses the spirit of scholars, thereby nurturing the vital strength of the state for all time. All living beings are stirred, clapping their hands and dancing for joy; this extends everywhere, leaving none outside its reach. Thus, when the responsible officials put the examination regulations in good order so as to honor scholars, all this is the working of the sage emperor’s subtle and profound wisdom. This is surely what the sages and worthies of antiquity sought anxiously throughout their lives but never lived to see—how much more extraordinary, then, in such distant places as Yunnan and Guizhou!

The Commentary says: “The scholars of Zhou were held in honor.” Now is just such a time! Let me join you scholars in testing this against the present examination arena: consider the bearing and judgment of Investigating Censor Luo Yu, the care and solemnity of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, and the diligence and reverence of all the offices and their functionaries. The Way pervades and flows freely; the vital spirit is harmonious and abundant. All is auspicious and fitting, and everyone feels delight in the heart and refreshment to the eyes at the advancement of you scholars, saying: “This examination, what…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
何時今士其何遇也際千載
難逢之會殆必有千載間出
之士起應之乎如是而諸士
猶踵故常以自居惡在其爲
士也夫士之貴于世者非人
也天也天畀之以聰明靈哲
將使之以是而導人也君人
===
者奉若天道故取而官之使
盡其分有也苟昧於分有以
學則曲以志則溺以才則局
以行則肆以名則忽即不忽
則加之好矣是故曲則失正
溺則失義局則失用肆則失
己忽而好則失實如是則於
punctuated: 何時？今士其何遇也！際千載難逢之會，殆必有千載間出之士起應之乎？如是而諸士猶踵故常以自居，惡在其爲士也？夫士之貴于世者，非人也，天也。天畀之以聰明靈哲，將使之以是而導人也。君人者奉若天道，故取而官之，使盡其分有也。苟昧於分有，以學則曲，以志則溺，以才則局，以行則肆，以名則忽，即不忽則加之好矣。是故曲則失正，溺則失義，局則失用，肆則失己，忽而好則失實。如是則於
translation_en: …What a time this is! What an opportunity the scholars of today have encountered! At such a juncture, scarcely met with in a thousand years, surely scholars who appear but once in a thousand years will arise to answer it? If, under these circumstances, the scholars still follow old routines and remain content with their position, wherein do they deserve to be called scholars? What makes scholars esteemed in the world comes not from men but from Heaven. Heaven endows them with intelligence, discernment, spiritual acuity, and wisdom, intending that they use these gifts to guide others. The ruler reverently follows the Way of Heaven; hence he selects them and appoints them to office, so that they may fully discharge their allotted responsibilities [?]. If they are ignorant of what is allotted to them [?], their learning becomes distorted, their aspirations become mired, their talents become confined, their conduct becomes unrestrained, and they become heedless of their reputation—or, if not heedless, excessively enamored of it. Thus distortion forfeits correctness; becoming mired forfeits righteousness; confinement forfeits usefulness; unrestrained conduct forfeits self-command; and heedlessness or infatuation with reputation forfeits substance. If this is so, then with respect to…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
分所當貴者篾矣士自賤之
誰其貴之而世焉賴之世無
賴於士而天下之事有不僨
乎西漢趙宋之末其士可考
也諸生誦法孔孟學不可謂
不正期在効用志不可謂不
立抱負奇氣才不可謂不達
蒙養童習行不可謂不脩疾
無聞而耻干譽名不可謂不
實所可委之外者惟曰時不
勝道也位不勝用也今遭值
盛時位有待而無可委矣其甚可
畏也哉且雲貴之士校天下
嘗寡至于今則文鳴四方志
punctuated: 分所當貴者篾矣。士自賤之，誰其貴之？而世焉賴之？世無賴於士，而天下之事有不僨乎？西漢、趙宋之末，其士可考也。諸生誦法孔孟，學不可謂不正；期在効用，志不可謂不立；抱負奇氣，才不可謂不達；蒙養童習，行不可謂不脩；疾無聞而耻干譽，名不可謂不實。所可委之外者，惟曰時不勝道也，位不勝用也。今遭值盛時，位有待而無可委矣，其甚可畏也哉！且雲貴之士，校天下嘗寡；至于今，則文鳴四方，志
translation_en:
…what ought to be valued in one’s allotted responsibilities is treated with contempt. If scholars debase themselves, who will esteem them? And how can the world rely upon them? If the world cannot rely upon scholars, how can the affairs of the realm fail to fall into ruin? The scholars of the closing years of the Western Han and the Zhao-Song dynasty furnish examples that may be examined.

You students recite and take as your models Confucius and Mencius: your learning cannot be called incorrect. You aspire to effective service: your resolve cannot be called unestablished. You possess exceptional spirit: your talents cannot be called undeveloped. You have been nurtured and trained from childhood: your conduct cannot be called uncultivated. You deplore remaining unheard of yet are ashamed to court praise: your reputations cannot be called unfounded. The only external circumstances upon which you could lay blame would be that the times cannot accommodate the Way, or that your positions cannot accommodate the exercise of your abilities. Now you have encountered a flourishing age, and positions await you; there is nothing upon which you can lay blame. Is this not truly cause for apprehension!

Moreover, the scholars of Yunnan and Guizhou have hitherto been few compared with those of the realm as a whole. By now, however, their literary accomplishments resound in all directions, and their ambitions…

title: 嘉靖元年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
角天下賢埒諸藩已信乎我
國家覆露之恩乆則無間也然
亦文焉是徵耳要之因才考
行舉學明志而又求以佐其
名雖天下士容敢謂其分之
畢盡乎似於此又不容以多
讓為也忠校文事畢諸士策
===
名于賢科而負時深望故曰
可畏甚而不可以故常自居
也
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學教
諭周忠謹序
punctuated:
角天下，賢埒諸藩。已信乎我國家覆露之恩，乆則無間也。然亦文焉是徵耳。要之，因才考行，舉學明志，而又求以佐其名，雖天下士，容敢謂其分之畢盡乎？似於此又不容以多讓為也。忠校文事畢，諸士策名于賢科，而負時深望，故曰可畏甚，而不可以故常自居也。
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學教諭周忠謹序。
translation_en:
…compete with all under Heaven, and equal the other provinces in worthiness. This indeed confirms that, over time, the sheltering and nurturing bounty of our state leaves none excluded. Yet it is only literary accomplishment that has been assessed here. What matters, ultimately, is to examine conduct in light of talent, advance learning and clarify aspirations, and further seek the substance to sustain one’s reputation. Even among scholars throughout the realm, who would dare claim to have discharged his duty in full? In this, it would seem, there is likewise no room for excessive deference to others.
I, Zhong, have completed the work of examining compositions. These scholars have inscribed their names among those selected for worthiness and bear the great expectations of the age. Thus I say that this is deeply daunting, and that they must not remain content with their accustomed ways.
Preface respectfully written by Zhou Zhong, Instructor of the Confucian School of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang.
